Jira help

This guide holds Atlassian’s own documentation for Jira, gathered on 18 August 2026. The categories are Atlassian’s own, taken from the trail printed above each article.

Jira is used by whole teams, so its documentation covers the person working through a board and the person administering the project in the same estate. Administration material is kept under its own headings rather than left out, so a reader can skip it without losing it.

Add color to work items in your plan

To change the color of your timeline bars:

  • Select which metric you’d like to color using the Color by dropdown menu. To switch back to the default gray, select None. You can color code schedule bars on your timeline bars based on:

Change how your plan sorts your work items

Change how your plan sorts your work items

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

To change how your plan sorts work items:

  • Navigate to the View settings menu on the right side of your screen.
  • Choose from the Sort by dropdown menu. To toggle between ascending and descending order on your roadmap, select the up or down arrow next to the field by which you’d like to sort your plan. If work items are already sorted in ascending or descending order, a reset icon will appear at the top of the Fields column. This icon will revert work items to the default rank order.

By default, work items in a plan are sorted by Ranking. With this method chosen, you can drag and drop your work items into whatever order you’d like.

You can also choose sort work items by Dates, Estimates, Status, Assignees, Teams, and most custom field values configured in your plan. If these are selected, you won’t be able to reorder your work items, since your plan is sorting them based on fixed values.

Filter work items on your plan

Filter work items on your plan

You can search for specific work items on your timeline or narrow the scope of what’s displayed in your plan by filtering them using the Filters menu.

On this page:
  • Filters available on the timeline and list view
  • Filters available on the Program board
  • Filters available on the Calendar view
  • Custom filters
Filters available on the timeline and list view
  • Hierarchy — View work items between two specific hierarchy levels.
  • Work item details — Show work items that contain a keyword or phrase.
  • Releases — See all work items assigned to a specific release.
  • Teams — Filter by teams in the plan.
  • Assignees — Filter by assignees in the plan, as well as users which belong to included teams.
  • Sprints — Show only work items from any sprint included in your plan. You can also filter by sprint state (completed, future, external, etc). Read more about sprints states.
  • Space — Filter top level-work items based on the spaceto which they belong. Child work items from other spaces may still appear if they’re associated with the top-level work item from that space.
  • Goals — Filter by Atlas goals to show links between granular work and outcomes.
  • Priorities — Show only work items of a certain priority level in your plan.
  • Work types — Only show work items of a certain type, based on your plan’s configuration.
  • Components — Filter by components, assuming they’re configured in your plan.
  • Labels — Filter by labels, assuming they’re configured in your plan.
  • Dependencies — Show only work items with dependencies in your plan. The dropdown menu contains the following options:
    • All work items — Show all work items included in the plan, regardless of dependencies.
    • Has dependencies — Show only work items that have dependencies.
    • Overlapping dates — Show only off-track dependencies.
    • Specific work item — Show dependencies related to a specific work item in your plan.
  • Reporter — Filter based on who created the work item.
  • Status — See work items based on their current status.
  • Warnings — Filter work items based on the warnings that apply to them.
  • Date range — Set a start and end date to view a specific time range of your plan. This filter uses the configured date fields of your plan.
Filters available on the Program board
  • Space — Filter top level-work items based on the space to which they belong. Child work items from other spaces may still appear if they’re associated with the top-level work item from that space.
  • Parent work item (such as Epic) — View only work items related to a specific higher-level work item
  • Work type — Only show work items of a certain type, based on your plan’s configuration.
Filters available on the Calendar view

Filter which work items show in the calendar view using the drop-downs at the top of the page. You can filter your work items according to:

  • Space — Filter top level-work items based on the space to which they belong. Child work items from other spaces may still appear if they’re associated with the top-level work item
  • Work type — Only show work items of a certain type, based on your plan’s configuration.
  • Status — See work items based on their current status.
  • Assignees — Filter by assignees in the plan, as well as users which belong to included teams.
  • Custom filters added to your plan
Custom filters

You can filter by custom fields if they’re configured for your plan. Read how to configure custom fields in your plan

Your plan supports five custom field types as filters:

  • single-choice select
  • multiple-choice select
  • checkbox
  • radio button
  • label

Group work items on your plan

Group work items on your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Your plan lets you group work items on your timeline according to assignees, spaces, component, teams, sprints, release, goals and labels. You can also group by custom fields. Find out how to group custom fields that have been added to your plan

To change how work items are grouped:

  • Navigate to the View settings menu of your plan.
  • Find the the dropdown menu labeled Group by, then select how you want to group your work items.
    • If you group by component or label, select + Create group. Enter a name, and then start typing to find the components or labels to add to the group. Before you can group by labels and components, they must be configured by an administrator. Read how to configure custom labels and components.

Any work items that don’t have a value in the selected field (for instance, no team is assigned to a work item, and you group by team) will be in the Unassigned swimlane at the bottom of your plan.

When grouping by sprint

Sprints involving multiple teams have a swimlane for each team. The sprint capacity will display for each team.

When grouping by release

Releases are ordered by release date. Those without dates, are at the bottom of the plan.

When grouping by custom field

The custom field types that can be used when grouping work items on your timeline are:

  • single-select
  • multi-select
  • user picker
  • label

How your plan sorts work items

How your plan sorts work items

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Regardless of how you sort work items in your plan, the following will always be true:

  • The order of work items is determined by the sorting method, and overrules any drag-and-drop adjustments you make to your plan.
  • Work items are sorted based on the highest hierarchy level shown in your timeline. Child work items are grouped under their parent work item.
  • Work items in your plan are sorted by the field of your choice, regardless of changes you make to other fields.
  • Newly created work items are sorted according to your defined sorting rule. Beyond these rules, there are also specific logic that only applies when sorting by certain variables.
Dates

To add custom dates to your plan, they need to be configured in your plan. Change which dates are used in your plan.

There are three dates by which you can sort your work items: target dates, due dates, or custom dates. These different dates are all treated the same way in your plan, so we simply refer to them as dates.

When sorting work items by dates, keep the following rules in mind:

  • Sprint dates will be used if a work item doesn’t have a start or end date but is assigned to a sprint.
  • Adjusting the dates of work items will change how these work items are sorted in your plan.
Estimates

Regardless of whether you’re using story points or time estimates (days and hours), the following rules apply:

  • Work items without an estimate will be sorted as though they have an estimate of zero.
  • Work items that have rolled-up estimate values will be sorted by the total estimate value of a parent work item plus its children.
  • If you change the estimation units of your plan, work items will revert to the default sorting order.
Status

When you sort work items by status, the following rules apply:

  • Work items will be sorted by status within their parent hierarchy level. Work items with the same status type will be ordered alphabetically.
  • Work items created in your plan that haven’t been saved to Jira are sorted above those already saved when in ascending order.
Assignees and teams

Unassigned work items will be grouped together at the top or bottom of your plan, depending on whether you’re using ascending or descending order.

Preconfigured views in your plan

Preconfigured views in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Your plan comes with four views that let you slice and dice your data in a variety of different ways to tell your story through the data. Switch between these views using the view selector dropdown menu next to Filters. They are:

  • Basic view
  • Dependency management view
  • Top-level planning view
  • Sprint capacity management view You can keep these views as is, or you can use the View settings menu to change how your data displays, show or add columns, add colors, change groupings, and more. See all the ways you can change how your plan looks and what it shows.

For each change you make to a view, an EDITED label appears to indicate that this view has been modified but not saved. To recall this edited view later, you’ll need to save it. Find out how to save a new view.

Basic view

Basic view is the default view for new plans.

How to read this view:

  • Columns: Start date and due date fields and status
  • Hierarchy levels set from highest to lowest, per hierarchy configuration
  • Work items sorted by ranking
  • Work items colored by status
  • Timeframe set to Months
Dependency management view

This view focuses only on work items that have dependencies in a plan so you quickly see which ones are blocking the progress of others.

In the screenshot below, some work items don’t match the view’s filters so they appear grayed out in the timeline.

How to read this view:

  • Columns: Dependencies (incoming and outgoing), priority, start and due date, and team
  • Hierarchy set from epic to sub-task and filtered by Work items with dependencies
  • Work items sorted by ranking
  • Work items colored by status
  • Timeframe set to Quarters
Top-level planning view

The top-level planning view gives you a high-level view of how work is progressing by showing work items from highest to lowest hierarchy level. You can also see work items in their hierarchical relationship with each other.

How to read this view:

  • Columns: Progress (work item count), start and due date, release, and component
  • Hierarchy level set from the highest level to story level, per hierarchy configuration
  • Work items grouped by spaces
  • Work items sorted by ranking
  • Work items colored by teams
  • Timeframe set to Quarters
Sprint capacity management view

The Sprint capacity management view shows capacity across work items in a plan so you can optimize sprints or iterations.

How to read this view:

  • Columns: Priority, sprint, story points (estimates), team (collapsed), and release (collapsed)
  • Hierarchy levels set to Story and work items filtered by All future sprints
  • Work items grouped by teams with capacity showing in the timeline
  • Work items sorted by ranking
  • Work items colored by status
  • Timeframe set to Months

Save a new view in your plan

Save a new view in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

When you’re ready to save your changes to a view, open the More on current view menu and select Save current view, as shown below:

Find out how to make your view the default view everyone sees when they load your plan.

Simultaneous edits to a view

If another user is working on the same view as you and makes a change to it before you save, a modal with two options will appear. You can either Overwrite the changes they’ve made which will get rid of their changes in favor of yours. Alternatively, you can Save your changes as a new view which will preserve the other user’s changes and save yours in a new, separate view.

Once you’ve made your decision, select Confirm to continue.

Untitled [Draft] views

You may also see an Untitled [Draft] view while accessing plans in your instance. There are two reasons you’ll see this:

  • You’re accessing an existing plan with work item filters and view settings that were previously configured but not saved. You can finalize this draft by saving it as a new view.
  • Someone else deletes your view as you’re working on it.

Show full hierarchy while filtering work items in your plan

Show full hierarchy while filtering work items in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

When you add filters to your plan, only work items that meet your criteria are shown. However, you can use the Show full hierarchy option in the Filters menu to view all of the child work items that belong to those filtered work items, even if they don’t match your criteria.

For example, you add a filter to only show work items assigned to Release A. Among other work items, your plan contains a parent-level work item (epic by default in software spaces) assigned to that release with four child work items. However, only two of those work items are assigned to Release A.

With Show full hierarchy disabled, you’ll only see the parent-level work item with the two child work items that are assigned to that release.

With it on, you’ll see all four child work items, even though two of them aren’t assigned to that release.

To show full hierarchy when filtering:

  • Open the Filters menu.
  • Toggle the Show full hierarchy checkbox at the bottom.

Show or hide columns in your plan timeline

Show or hide columns in your plan timeline

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Fields from your work items display as columns in your plan. By default, you can view and edit:

  • Start date
  • Due date
  • Status
  • Dependencies (blocked by and blocks)
  • Priority
  • Team
  • Parent
  • Reporter
  • Component

Show or hide columns on your timeline

You can show or hide columns using the Add fields button on your timeline. Once open, you’ll see a list of the current columns visible on your timeline.

Add a field by selecting the Choose fields… dropdown menu. After this, the field will show in the Add fields menu.

You can reorder your columns by re-arranging the list of visible fields, or remove them by selecting the x next to it’s name.

Tips for column management

If you want to add a lot of columns to your timeline, you can drag the left or right edge of the column to resize it. You can also select the column header to collapse (or expand) it.

If you want to replace the timeline bars with more columns, select List next to View settings. More about the list in your plan

What is the calendar view of your plan?

What is the calendar view of your plan?

The Calendar view shows scheduled work in your plan in a calendar format. This view in plans functions very similarly to that of the calendar view in Spaces with a few key changes.

The calendar view shows issues that:

  • have been scheduled using the Start date and Due date fields
  • inherit both dates from a sprint assignment
  • inherit both dates from a release Issues scheduled using rolled-up dates don’t appear on this view.
Schedule issues

You can reschedule issues by dragging and dropping the work item to the new date, or dragging one side of an issue’s bar to change the duration; doing so overwrites any inferred dates. See more about scheduling issues by dates.

View sprints and releases

Sprints and releases show on the calendar view based on their dates. You can select

  • a sprint to view its capacity information
  • a release to view its details The Calendar view in Plans doesn’t support rescheduling sprints or releases unlike the space version of this screen.
View settings

The calendar view focuses on a very specific window of time in your plan. As such, it can only show a limited number of issues at once due to space constraints. If you exceed this number, you’ll see page numbers at the bottom of the view which you can flip through to find the issues you want to see.

Alternatively, you can use the menus at the top of the page to view only specific issues. These filters don’t remove issues from your plan, they just hide them from the view so you can focus on a specific part. See what filters are available on the calendar view.

You can also change how the calendar looks and what information it shows.

What is the list in your plan?

What is the list in your plan?

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

The list in your plan lets you create a view that’s independent of the usual timeline structure. With the timeline bars hidden, you’re free to add more columns to show more detail, or to tell a completely different story with your data.

Because the list hides the timeline bars, certain time-based insights like capacity planning and dependency visualizations won’t show until you toggle the timeline back on. However, changes made in the View settings menu apply to both the timeline and the list versions of your plan.

Since the timeline and the list are independent from each other, columns added to the list won’t show when you go back to the timeline.

To see the list in your plan, select List next to View settings on your plan’s timeline. Use Timeline to go back to the timeline.

What is the summary view of your plan?

What is the summary view of your plan?

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Your plan’s Summary shows key insights to help monitor progress and health of your plans. Work items that have either a starting date or a due date within the selected date range will show on this screen. Use the date selector at the top of the screen to change the timeframe. By default, the Summary shows six weeks of information: two weeks in the past and four weeks into the future from the current date.

At the top of the Summary are four overview cards:

  • unassigned work items
  • high priority work items
  • overdue work items
  • blocked work items Select any one of these to see the work items on your timeline.

Beneath these, you’ll find widgets that dig deeper into the health of your plan.

Status overview

The Status overview widget shows work items in your plan within the date range based on their status category.

This widget shows the rolled-up values of child work items instead of manually set start or end dates to reflect the real state of your plan.

Read more about rollups and how they work

Work item progress

Work item progress shows progress of specific high-level work items in your plan. You can filter by the status of the work item, as well as hierarchy level.

As with the status overview widget, Work item progress also rolls up values reflect the real state of your plan.

Key dependencies

The Key dependencies widget highlights dependencies with the largest impact in your plan. This widget only shows dependencies in your plan that to use the Blocks type, even if they show in other views of your plan.

Dependencies in this widget are broken down into three categories:

  • Overdue work items that are blocking other work are shown in red
    • The lozenge also shows the number of work items that are being held up by it.
  • Work item that are part of a chain of dependencies are shown in yellow
    • A chain means that it’s the first in a series of dependent work items. One of these going off-track can have ripple effects through your plan.
  • Future dependencies are shown in blue
    • These don’t need your attention yet, but they’re important to the health of your plan. Read more about how dependencies work in plans.
Team capacity

The Team capacity widget allows you to view the capacity information of sprints for any scrum or kanban team included in your plan. External teams won’t show in this widget.

In order to see this information, you’ll need to have capacity planning enabled on your plan. View the instructions for tracking capacity in your plan

Team Progress

Similar to the Work item progress widget, the Team progress shows progress of specific high-level work items in your plan except they’re shown based on the team assigned to it.

You can filter by hierarchy level above the Epic level. Each level rolls up values of lower level work items to show you an accurate snapshot of your teams’ progress.

Rovo can give you a quick update on the status of a plan. Open Rovo Chat and enter /summarize-plan along with an optional prompt (for example, “Summarize this plan for engineering leadership”). Rovo will summarize the plan’s scope, health, dependencies, and blockers, and suggest next steps to keep things moving forward.

Collect information for your team with forms

Add or remove fields from your form

Add or remove fields from your form

You have the flexibility to include certain fields in your spaces’ forms.

Add fields to your form

Once you select a work type for your form, the Fields section will display all the fields that are available for that work type. Simply drag and drop the field you’d like to include in your form, and then edit them.

Remove fields from your form

To remove a field from your form:

  • Select a field.
  • Select Remove field (). Or alternatively, you can drag the field back over to the Fields section.
System fields vs custom fields in forms

The following system fields are supported in forms:

  • Summary

  • Description

  • Attachment

  • Due date

  • Priority

  • Labels Custom fields can also be added. These include:

  • Assignee

  • Affected services (software spaces)

  • Category

  • Components (software spaces)

  • Compass components (software spaces)

  • Date picker

  • Date time picker

  • Group picker (single groups)

  • Group picker (multiple groups)

  • Labels

  • Number

  • Parent

  • People (team-managed spaces)

  • Radio buttons

  • Select list (cascading)

  • Select list (multiple choices)

  • Select list (single choice)

  • Sprint (software spaces)

  • Story points (software spaces)

  • Text (multi-line)

  • Text (single line)

  • URL field

  • Versions (software spaces) You may want to include more details in your forms beyond the default fields. A space admin can do this by setting up a new work type scheme and then adding custom fields. More about custom fields

Keyboard shortcuts such as CMD+V are not supported when uploading attachments on public forms.

Restricted fields in public forms

Forms set to public access have some fields that are restricted because they may contain sensitive or confidential data. You won’t be able to add a restricted field to a form with public access, and if you’ve already added a restricted field, it won’t be shown to anyone who views or responds to the form.

Restricted fields include:

  • Assignee
  • People
  • Parent
  • Team
  • Sprint
  • Space
  • Labels
  • Fix versions

Conditionally show form fields

Conditionally show form fields

Show specific questions based on responses to previous questions. Creating conditions allows you to tailor the information you collect from your stakeholders.

Only space admins can create conditions in forms.

Show a form field conditionally

To create conditions on a form:

  • Select Forms from the space navigation.
  • Select an existing form or select + Create form.
  • Add a field that supports conditions to the form builder.
  • Select the field to edit it.
  • Select Add condition to create a condition.
  • Select the field options that need to be chosen for the condition to be met. If the field is a select list (multiple choice) or checkbox, you can choose whether the condition will be met when One of or All of the options are chosen.
  • Drag the fields you want to conditionally show underneath the condition. The condition and any conditionally shown fields will be automatically saved.
  • Select Add condition again to create another condition from the same field. You can nest conditions underneath other conditionally shown fields up to 3 times.
Edit a condition

To edit a form condition:

  • Select Forms from the space navigation.
  • Find the condition you want to edit.
  • Edit any details of the condition. They will be automatically saved.
Delete a condition

To delete a form condition:

  • Select Forms from the space navigation.
  • Find the condition you want to delete.
  • Select Remove () on the condition. This will also delete any conditions and conditionally shown fields nested underneath.
Preview form conditions

Before you share your form, you can preview it to make sure your conditions work as intended.

To preview your form:

  • Select Forms from the space navigation.
  • Select Preview () to see how your form will look.
  • Try selecting different responses to each question in your form to check that the conditions have been set up as you intended.
Fields supported for conditions

You can create conditions based on selections to these fields:

  • Priority
  • Select list (multiple choices)
  • Select list (single choice)
  • Checkbox
  • Radio

Customize your form fields

Customize your form fields

Collect richer information with your form by customizing how fields will appear. How to add fields to your form.

Edit form field name

You can rename each of the field names to suit your form’s purpose.

To rename a form field:

  • Drag and drop the field you’d like to include in your form.
  • Hover over the field you want to rename.
  • Select the current field name.
  • Enter a new name for the field.
  • Press enter or select the confirmation icon (). The new field name will be displayed on the form when shared with other people.

The original field name will remain visible only to you when editing the form. It will also be used in any work items that are created based on responses to the form.

The field will revert to its original name if you drag it back to the Fields section or use it in another form.

Edit form field description

You can add and edit field descriptions to add more instructional details to your form.

To add a form field description:

  • Select Add a description in the field you want to add.
  • Enter a description in text.
  • Press enter or select the confirmation icon (). The new field description will be visible on the form when shared with other people. This will not change the field description in your space settings.
Make form fields required

To make fields required or optional for people submitting responses to the form:

  • Select the field you’d like to update. Options to edit the field will appear.
  • Select the toggle to switch between Required or Optional. Next to the field name, a red asterisk will appear if required, and disappear if optional. You can also make fields required from work type > space settings. If a field is required for the work type, it must be added to a form. If a field is optional for the work type, you can make it required from the form builder.

How secure are public forms?

How secure are public forms?

A public form allows your team to receive work from people who may not have access to your Jira site. You could use public forms to take in requests from other teams in your organization, collect feedback or ideas from customers, or capture tasks from external agencies.

Who can access a public form?

Anyone with a link to a public form can access the form. Public forms override app access and space permissions, meaning people without access to Jira can view and submit a public form. The only exclusion to this is if IP allowlists have been set up by an organization admin to specify who can access content in Jira. In this case, the IP allowlist will dictate who can submit a response to a public form. If someone tries to access a public form from an IP address that is not on the allowlist, they will not be able to view the form. Read more about IP allowlisting.

Who can create public forms?

Space admins can create and manage public forms.

Public access for forms can be turned off in your Jira apps settings by an organization admin, site admin, or Jira admin. There are separate settings for team-managed spaces and company-managed spaces. How to manage form access

What protections are in place to prevent spam?
ReCaptcha protection

Public forms are protected by reCAPTCHA to prevent automated bots from submitting them. If verifying reCAPTCHA fails, the form submitter must complete a manual reCAPTCHA challenge.

Mandatory email addresses

Whenever someone completes a public form and they are not logged in to Jira, the form will display a mandatory field to collect their email address. This email address will be recorded in a comment on the work item so that the source of the work is clear.

Hidden sensitive fields

Some fields will be restricted because they may contain sensitive or confidential data that shouldn’t be shared publicly. Even if these fields are added to the form builder, they will be hidden on the form.

Restricted fields include:

  • Assignee
  • People
  • Parent
  • Team
  • Sprint
  • Space
  • Labels
  • Fix versions You can customize the field names and descriptions that appear to people viewing your form, but field options (such as selections for single-select or multi-select fields) will always appear as they have been set up. How to customize form fields.
Option to deactivate

Space admins can quickly deactivate a form to prevent anyone from viewing or submitting responses to the form.

To deactivate a form:

  • Select Forms from the space navigation.
  • On the form you want to delete, select More actions (), then Deactivate form.
Site settings to turn off public access

An organization admin, site admin, or Jira admin can turn off public access for forms. Separate settings are available for team-managed spaces and company-managed spaces. Turning these settings off will instantly deactivate all public forms on the site.

How to create, edit, save, and delete forms

How to create, edit, save, and delete forms

Only users with space admin permissions can create, edit, or delete forms.

In company-managed spaces, you must also have browse spaces permission.

Create a form

To create forms for your space:

  • Select Forms from the space navigation.
  • Select a template, or select Blank form to create one from scratch.
    • Templates may not be available to all users.
  • If your space has more than one work type, you’ll be prompted to select the type of work.
    • This is how the work will appear in your space (form responses are converted to work items).
    • The fields in the form will differ depending on which work type you select.
  • Reorder fields or edit labels, descriptions, and options as needed.
    • Drag and drop extra fields from the sidebar.
  • Select Preview () to see how your form will look.
  • Your form is now ready to share. How to manage access and share your form.
  • To finish, select Save changes.
Edit a form

To edit a form:

  • Select Forms from the space navigation.
  • Choose the form you’d like to edit.
  • Make your desired changes:
    • Select the title to customize it.
    • Reorder fields or edit labels, descriptions, and options as needed.
      • Drag and drop extra fields from the sidebar.
    • Select the work type at the top-left of your form.
      • This is how the work will appear in your space (form responses are converted to work items).
  • Select Preview () to see how your form will look.
  • Your updated form is now ready to share.
  • To finish, select Save changes. Manage your form fields
Save a form

All changes you make to your form are automatically saved for the next time you return.

Delete a form

To delete a form from your space:

  • Select Forms from the space navigation.
  • On the form you want to delete, select More actions (), then Delete form.
Preview your form

Before you share your form, you can preview it to make sure you’ve captured all the right information.

To preview your form:

  • Select Forms from the space navigation.
  • Select Preview () to see how your form will look. Forms can’t be created, edited, or deleted using the Jira mobile app.

Manage access and share a form

Manage access and share a form

Only people with space admin permissions can create and share forms.

Once you’ve finished creating a form in Jira, it’s time to share it with the right people. You can share a form with specific people or teams that have access to Jira, or you can share it with anyone online. Make sure you’ve set the right access level before you share a form with others.

Manage access to forms

Selecting an access level for your form will determine who can view and submit a response. There are three access levels you can choose from:

  • Limited access: Only people with permission to create work items in your space.

  • Open access: Only people with a Jira license who are able to log in to your Jira site.

  • Public access: Anyone online with the link can submit a response to the form. (This option won’t be available if an admin has disabled public access on your Jira site.) To manage the access level for a form:

  • Select Forms from the space navigation.

  • Select the form you’d like to edit.

  • Select Access ()

  • Select Limited, Open, or Public. If an organization admin has set up IP allowlists to specify who can access content on your Jira site, these restrictions will also apply to public forms. This means that if someone tries to access a public form using an IP that is not on the allowlist, they won’t be able to view the form or submit a response. Read more about IP allowlisting

Share the form

Once you’ve selected an access level for a form, you can go ahead and share it. Whenever somebody submits a response to the form, it will be converted to a work item in your space. The ID of the form will be shown as a label on the work item.

To share a form:

  • Select Forms from the space navigation.
  • Select the form you’d like to share.
  • Select Share ()
  • Enter the email addresses of the people you’d like to share your form with and select Share. Or, select Copy link and paste the link anywhere you’d like to share it. On mobile devices, links to public forms will open in a mobile browser rather than the Jira app.
Public access requirements

When you select public access for a form, you’ll be asked for a few extra details.

  • You must select a default reporter. This person will be the Reporter for any work items created from responses to the form.
  • A mandatory field will be added to your form to collect the Email address of anyone who submits a response. This email address will appear in a comment on the work item, along with a link to the form.
  • Attachments are supported in forms set to public access, with a limit of 100MB per attachment. To view any attachments submitted via a form response, go to the work item created from the form submission.
  • Some fields will be restricted because they may contain sensitive or confidential data. You won’t be able to add a restricted field to a form with public access, and if you’ve already added a restricted field, it won’t be shown to anyone who views or responds to the form. Restricted fields include:
    • Assignee
    • People
    • Parent
    • Team
    • Sprint
    • Space
    • Labels
    • Fix versions
Turn public access on or off

Public access for forms can be turned off by an organization admin, site admin, or Jira admin. There are separate settings for team-managed spaces and company-managed spaces.

To turn off public access:

  • Select Settings () from the top navigation bar in Jira.
  • Select Jira apps.
  • Select Jira configuration from the side menu.
  • Use the toggle for Public forms sharing to turn the feature on or off.

What are forms and what can they do?

What are forms and what can they do?

Forms allow you to collect information and capture work from other teams or stakeholders. You can create different types of forms to receive different types of work from your stakeholders.

Forms can be used to:

  • Help people outside your immediate team send work to your team.
  • Collect the right information from other teams and stakeholders from within your organization.
  • Gather feedback or ideas on your team’s work. You can create as many forms as you like for your space.
View form responses

When someone submit a response to a form, their response will automatically create a work item in the same space where the form lives. The following labels will be added to each work item:

  • Form
  • Form-<unique-form-id> If the user submitting the form doesn’t have permission to create work within your space, the space owner becomes the creator instead.
Selecting the type of work

When you create a form, you need to select which type of work item will be created in your space when a form is submitted (for example, Task).

Each work type includes different form field options, depending on the information you want to collect. You will be able to select any work type from within your space, except for subtasks.

Your space will only show other work types if you have more than one for your space.

Configure a company-managed board

Add a sub-filter to a company-managed kanban board

Add a sub-filter to a company-managed kanban board

If you are using a Kanban board, you can add a sub-filter that refines the issues returned by your board’s filter. For example, you might want to display issues on your board once they’re marked as done, until those issues are released or the sprint is complete.

The sub-filter also allows you to show different data in Reports.

To add a sub-filter to your board:

  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • On the General page under the Filter subheading, find the section labeled Kanban board sub-filter.
  • Select Add sub-filter or hover over the existing query. Edit the field to create a sub-filter using Jira Query Language (JQL). Read more about JQL syntax.
  • Select Update to save your changes.

Change the location of a board

Change the location of a board

Most boards in Jira are located in a space, but you can also have boards that are attached to your profile. When you create a new board, you’re asked to choose either a space or your profile as its location.

To change a board’s location:

  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Under the General settings, select the Location field.
  • Type the name of the space or your name and choose the new location. The board will move to its new location straight away. If a board is attached to an inactive space or user, your space or board admin will need to assign a new location so it’s still accessible.

Find your recent boards quickly. Try any of these.

  • Type / to open quick search (recent boards are shown before you type).
  • Star a board, then quickly find it again by going to For you, then sort by starred boards.
  • If you’re in a space, select the board name below the respective company-managed software space.

Configure columns

Configure columns

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

The vertical columns in the Active sprints view of a scrum board and a kanban board, represent the workflow of your board’s space.

At its most basic, a column describes the current status of a work item. For example, the default columns of a scrum board are To Do, In Progress, and Done. The default columns on a kanban board are Backlog, Selected for Development, In Progress, and Done.

As your team’s workflow matures, you may start to introduce many more statuses to your team’s working process. To help organize and discuss your team’s work, you can assign multiple statuses to a single column, reducing the number of columns your team uses when moving cards across your board.

You can add, delete, rename, or move these columns if you wish. You can also choose which statuses are mapped to specific columns, and whether any constraints apply to each column.

Before you begin

To configure the board and any of its settings, you must be either:

  • a space administrator for the location of the board
  • a board administrator for the board itself More about permissions for company-managed spaces
Edit columns

To edit your board’s columns:

  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Expand the remainder of the menu in the sidebar by selecting Layout.
  • Select Columns.
  • Under Map statuses to columns, you can edit the columns as described in the following table. Add a new column

To the right of the columns, select Add (+). Enter a name for the new column and select its category, then select Add column.

If you’re using the simplified workflow, a new status will automatically be created to match your new column. More about the simplified workflow

Change the name of a column

Select a column’s name to edit, modify the existing name, then press Enter.

Delete a column

Select Delete () at the top of the column.

Any Jira workflow statuses mapped to the deleted column are moved back to the Unmapped statuses panel. What are Jira workflows?

Move a column

Hover over the top of a column, then drag the column left or right to its new position. Drop the column to place it in its new position.

Each column has a gray, blue, or green bar, as shown in the screenshot above.

  • The single left-most column will always be grey, representing items in a new state.
  • The single right-most column will always be green, representing items in a successful state.
  • The middle column (or columns, if you add more) are always blue, representing items in progress. These colors are shown in a number of places in Jira, such as gadgets for Jira apps.
Map statuses to columns

By default, a board’s columns are mapped to the default Jira statuses, as shown in the following tables. You can change this if you wish. For example, if you are using additional, customized Jira statuses, you will probably want to map them to appropriate columns in your board.

If your board’s space is using the default Jira workflow:

Default column

Default mapped statuses

To Do

Open, Reopened

In Progress

In Progress

Done

Resolved, Closed

If your board’s space is using the simplified workflow:

Default column

Default mapped statuses

To Do

To Do

In Progress

In Progress

Done

Done

Edit which statuses are mapped to specific columns
  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Expand the remainder of the menu in the sidebar by selecting Layout.
  • Select Columns.
  • Under Map statuses to columns, you can edit which statuses are mapped to specific columns as described in the following table. Map a status to a column

Drag and drop a status from the Unmapped statuses panel to the appropriate column.

Unmap a status from a column

Drag and drop a status from its current column to the Unmapped statuses panel.

Change which column a status is mapped to

Drag and drop a status from its original column to its new column.

Jira only considers work items in the right-most column of your board as complete. If you have statuses such as Done, Blocked, or Canceled, that represent completed work, make sure they’re mapped to the right-most column in your board settings. When these statuses aren’t mapped correctly, you might not be able to complete a sprint due to “incomplete” work items. Or items in certain statuses (like Blocked or Canceled) might not show up as completed, and they could be carried forward into future sprints.

Note: Some statuses (in particular, custom statuses) may not be available for work items on your board if the workflows used by them do not utilize those statuses. What are Jira workflows?

You can view workflow statuses and transitions in company-managed spaces. Select the status dropdown when viewing a work item and select View workflow.

Add a new status

If your board is using the simplified workflow:

  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.

  • Expand the remainder of the menu in the sidebar by selecting Layout.

  • Select Columns.

  • In the Unmapped statuses panel, select Add status.

  • Enter a name for the new status and select its category, then select Add status. Note: The Add status button is only available if you have the Jira space administrator permission for this board’s space. The Add status button will disappear if you either don’t have the right permissions, or if your space stops using the simplified workflow.

  • More about permissions for company-managed spaces

  • More about the simplified workflow

Delete a status

You can only delete a status if:

  • you are the space administrator for this board’s space(s), and
  • no work items currently have that status. If any other workflows are using this status, then the status will be removed from your workflow, but not deleted.

If your board is using the simplified workflow:

  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Expand the remainder of the menu in the sidebar by selecting Layout.
  • Select Columns.
  • Drag and drop the relevant status to the Unmapped statuses panel.
  • If no work items have the status, you can select Delete () on the status card to delete it. If your board is not using the simplified workflow, statuses can only be deleted by Jira admins in the workflow editor. What are Jira workflows?
Set column constraints

Setting constraints on each workflow state is a crucial part of kanban, so that you can ensure that work is continually flowing through the pipeline. You may also find it handy in Scrum, so that you can see bottlenecks early, and adjust the scope of your sprint. You can specify constraints for all columns, or just some of them.

Constraints trigger a visual indicator when a minimum or maximum number of work items appear in a column. On the board, you’ll notice

On the board view, if a column constraint is exceeded, then the column header will change color, as follows:

  • Red column header — maximum number of work items exceeded
  • Yellow column header — minimum number of work items not met The values of the column constraints will appear at the top of each column you set them for. These values don’t have any impact on the number of work items displayed in the columns.

Column constraints apply to the total number of work items in a column, regardless of whether they are hidden by a quick filter. Configure quick filters

To set column constraints of a board:

  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Expand the remainder of the menu in the sidebar by selecting Layout.
  • Select Columns.
  • Edit the constraints, as described in the following table. Enable column constraints

Under Column constraints, select either Work item count or Work item count, excluding subtasks.

Enabling column constraints will show the work item count in each column. You may want to exclude subtasks (recommended for Scrum teams), so you can constrain the number of stories for your team, rather than the number of individual tasks.

Set a column’s minimum or maximum constraint

Under a column’s name, you can enter a minimum or maximum value.

To remove a constraint, clear the existing value.

Remove constraints for all columns

Under Column constraints, select None.

Configure columns directly on the board

If you’re a space or board admin, and the board uses the simplified workflow, you can configure columns directly on the board:

  • To create a column, select the + icon to the right of all columns.
  • To rename a column, select its name to edit directly.
  • To move a column, select its top, then drag the column to its new position.
  • To set column constraints, right-click its name or hover to select More actions (), then Set column limit.
  • To delete a column, right-click its name or hover to select More actions (), then Delete.
Enable the kanban backlog

You must be a Jira administrator or a board administrator for the board to enable the kanban backlog.

Managing your backlog in the first column of your kanban board is easy to do — as long as there are only a few work items in your backlog. As your backlog grows, viewing and scrolling through these work items can become inefficient.

When you enable the kanban backlog, you’ll get a bigger backlog in a dedicated space where you can create and rank work items for your team. You can also plan story development in the backlog, without distracting your team from their work-in-progress on the kanban board.

To enable the kanban backlog:

  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Expand the remainder of the menu in the sidebar by selecting Layout.
  • Select Columns.
  • Under Map statuses to columns, you’ll notice the kanban backlog panel. To enable the backlog, drag and drop an existing status on the panel. To create a new status instead, select Add status, then drag and drop it on the panel. If the kanban backlog is enabled, you can choose how larger pieces of work are displayed on your board and backlog (by default, this work type is called an epic). They can be displayed as cards, or in the epic panel in the backlog. Managing epics in a kanban space
Troubleshoot work items missing from your board or backlog

If some work items aren’t appearing on your board or in your backlog, this is often caused by board filter settings or backlog configuration problems. Common symptoms include:

  • Newly created work items not showing up in the backlog.
  • Certain statuses or work types missing from the board view.
  • Discrepancies between JQL search results and what appears on your board or backlog.
Potential fixes for missing work items
Check your board filter
  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Select Details and review the filter query.
  • Make sure the filter includes all the work types and statuses you want to see on your board and backlog.
Verify status-to-column mapping
  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Expand the remainder of the menu in the sidebar by selecting Layout.
  • Select Columns.
  • Ensure all statuses you want to appear on the board are mapped to a column.
Enable the backlog feature
  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Features.
  • Make sure the Backlog feature is enabled.
Check status mapping for backlog
  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Expand the remainder of the menu in the sidebar by selecting Layout.
  • Select Columns.
  • Ensure that statuses intended for the backlog are mapped to the “Backlog” column if available. Need help? If you can’t find the answer you need in our documentation, we have other resources available to help you. Get help with Jira Cloud

Configure how your board estimates and tracks work

Configure how your board estimates and tracks work

To configure the board and any of its settings, you must be either:

  • a space administrator for the location of the board
  • a board administrator for the board See Permissions overview for more information.

When configuring a board, you can set whether work items are estimated in story points, time estimate work items, and how progress is tracked throughout your sprint. This process differs for company-managed and team-managed spaces.

To configure space estimates for company-managed space:

This setting can only be changed for company-managed scrum teams.

  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Select Estimation from the left-side menu.
  • Adjust the estimation settings as you desire.
    • Use the Estimation method dropdown to change how work items are estimated on your board.
    • Enable Time tracking if you’d like to use a different method to track progress on your board. It’s common for teams to estimate work then track progress using two different methods.
      • Selecting None uses what you’ve defined as the Estimation method to track progress.
      • Selecting Remaining estimate and time spent tracks progress by subtracting the value from the Time spent field from the original estimate. Find out about logging time to work items. To configure space estimates for team-managed spaces:

Estimation isn’t enabled by default in team-managed spaces. Enabling estimation causes several changes that you should be aware of before doing it. Find out about the changes that happen when enabling estimation in team-managed spaces.

  • Navigate to your relevant team-managed space.
  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Features on the left menu, and turn on Estimation.
  • Select whether to use Story points or Time.

Configure quick filters

Configure quick filters

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

Quick filters let you further filter the collection of work items appearing on a Scrum or Kanban board. Use quick filters to switch between different work types (e.g. show only bugs), or to show team-specific views of a common backlog.

Before you begin

To configure the board and any of its settings, you must be either:

  • a space admin for the location of the board
  • a board admin for the board itself See Permissions overview for more information to configure its quick filters.
About the default quick filters

By default, a board contains two quick filters, called ‘Only My Work items’ and ‘Recently Updated’:

Default quick filter

Default JQL

Notes

Only My Work items

assignee = currentUser()

Displays work items assigned to the person who is currently viewing this board.

Recently Updated

updatedDate >= -1d

Displays work items that have been updated in the last 24 hours.

Manage quick filters

You can create additional quick filters or edit existing quick filters. Any additional quick filters that you create appear in the Quick filters dropdown menu. To display quick filters as buttons, switch on Show quick filters in the dropdown menu.

  • Go to your board, then select more () > Configure board. (NOTE: This requires admin permissions.)
  • Select the Quick Filters tab.
  • Edit the quick filters, as described in the following table. Add a new quick filter

In the blue area, type the Name, JQL, and a Description (optional), then select Add.

Change the name of a quick filter

Click in the Name area of the quick filter, modify the existing name, then select Update.

Change the JQL of a quick filter

Click in the JQL area of the quick filter, modify the existing JQL, then select Update.

See the examples below for some suggestions. For information on JQL syntax, see JQL.

Delete a quick filter

Select the Delete button at the right of the quick filter.

Move a quick filter

Hover over the vertical ‘grid’ icon, then drag and drop the quick filter up or down to its new position.

Sample JQL for quick filters
Show all work items that are assigned to members of the “bugfix” group

assignee in membersOf("bugfix")

Show all work items of type “Bug”

type = "Bug"

Use a work item filter in your quick Filter

savedfilter = "My Filter"

For more JQL guidance, check out:

  • JQL functions
  • JQL fields
  • JQL keywords
  • JQL operators
Save a new search as a filter

To create a new filter, see Save your search as a filter.

Configure swimlanes

Configure swimlanes

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

A swimlane is a horizontal categorization of work items. You can use swimlanes to help you distinguish tasks of different categories, such as work streams, users, or application areas.

Before you begin

To configure the board and any of its settings, you must be either:

  • a space admin for the location of the board
  • a board admin for the board itself See Permissions overview for more information.
Set swimlanes based on a method

You can choose to set up your swimlanes in a variety of ways.

Stories

One parent work item per swimlane containing all of the subtasks, with work items that have no sub-tasks appearing below.

Queries

One JQL query per swimlane (see below for examples). By default, two swimlanes will be created:

  • Expedite — this swimlane is based on the following JQL query: priority = Blocker
  • Everything Else — this swimlane is always at the bottom of the screen, and cannot be deleted. It acts as a “catch-all” for work items that don’t match the JQL of any of the swimlanes above it; hence, it has no JQL specified. You may want to create additional swimlanes that map to other values of your Jira ‘Priority’ field, or use a different field to categorize your swimlanes.
Assignees

One assignee per swimlane, with unassigned work items appearing either above or below the swimlanes (your choice).

Epics

One parent work item (by default, this work type is called an epic) per swimlane. Work items that don’t belong to one of these parent work items are grouped below the swimlanes. Any parent work items that aren’t part of the board’s current filter will be hidden from the board.

If you want to change the order of the swimlanes on your board, navigate to the Backlog of the board, and drag and drop the parent work items (epics by default) as desired.

Spaces

One space for each swimlane, with work items displaying below their respective spaces.

No swimlanes

No horizontal categorization of work items in the Active sprints of a scrum board, or on a kanban board.

Change methods
  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Expand the menu under Layout.
  • Select Swimlanes.
  • In the Select method dropdown, select either Queries, Stories, Assignees, Epics, Spaces or No Swimlanes.
Modifying your query-based swimlanes

If your swimlanes are based on JQL queries (rather than on stories or assignees), you can create, delete, or change them.

  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Expand the menu under Layout.
  • Select Swimlanes.
  • Hover over the existing query to find More actions () then Edit.
  • In the modal, you can edit the name or modify the JQL.
  • To move a swimlane, use the grid icon to drag and drop the swimlane to reorder its new position. Note: The JQL ‘ORDER BY’ clause is not used by the swimlane, as it defaults to order by rank.
Example JQL queries for your swimlanes
Show all work items that belong to a particular component, e.g. ‘User Interface’

space = "coffee hub" AND component = "ui"

Show all work items that are due in the next 24 hours

space = "ios app" "android app" due <= "24h"

Show all work items that have a particular priority

space = "dream team" priority = "Minor"

Show all work items that have a particular priority

space = "pet rescue " priority = "Major"

To learn more about how information is displayed within columns in each swimlane, including mapping multiple statuses to columns, see Configure columns.

Need help? If you can’t find the answer you need in our documentation, we have other resources available to help you. See Getting help.

Configure the work item details

You can customize the work item to show more fields, hide fields, and rearrange the field layout.

Configure the layout of Jira work items to set which fields appear and their order.Open a work item. From the sidebar, select Configure (), then Work item view.To find out more about configuring the layout, check out Configure field layout in the work item.

Before you begin

You must have the following to do the things described on this page.

Role: Space admin

Permission: Administer spaces

Go to Permissions overview for more information.

You can configure the fields to be displayed in the work item on the board configuration screen. The values of some fields are also editable in the work item.

Field

Editable values

Configurable

Description

  • Always displayed and values are always editable

  • Can’t be deleted from the default layout configuration of the work item Estimate

Priority

Component

  • Editable values only if the space has at least one component Labels

  • Always displayed

  • Editable values only if the instance has at least one label Affected versions

  • Always displayed

  • Editable values only if the space has at least one version Fix versions

Parent

  • Use this field to associate a work item with its parent work item at the next level up in the hierarchy (by default, this parent work type is called an epic in software spaces)
  • Company-managed work items can only use parent work items from company-managed spaces, and team-managed work items can only use parent work items from team-managed spaces Reporter

Assignee

Date updated

Work item links

Displayed only if the work item has at least one link

Description

  • Can’t be deleted from the default layout configuration of the work item Comments

Attachments

Subtasks

Some fields may be hidden, depending on the field configuration scheme used for the space’s work types.

Adding, removing, or moving a field
  • Select the Jira icon, then Spaces, then select the relevant space.
  • Choose Settings, then Screens.
  • Expand the relevant scheme by selecting the expand (>).
  • Select the View work item screen.
  • Add or remove the desired fields. Your fields will then appear in the work item. Note that fields will only appear on a work item if they have been associated with the relevant work type, and are not hidden.

Configure working days

Configure working days

The Working days setting for your board is used for different reports and gadgets. You can configure settings on this page to filter out weekends, holidays, and other times your team won’t be working on your board’s spaces.

Working days are reflected in these reports and gadgets:

  • Burndown Chart, Sprint Report, Epic Report, Version Report, Control Chart
  • Sprint Health Gadget, Burndown Gadget
Before you begin

To configure the board and any of its settings, you must be either:

  • a space admin for the location of the board
  • a board administrator for the board itself See Permissions overview for more information.
Configure working days
  • Go to your board, select more (), then Configure board.
  • Select Working days. To change your team’s working days, select the days your team usually work under Standard working days.

To specify holidays or one-off dates your team won’t be working, select a date using the date picker under Non-working days, then select Add date. To remove a non-working day, select the x next to the date.

To change your board’s timezone, select a Region, then Timezone from the dropdowns.

Customize cards

Customize cards

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

Before you begin

To configure the board and any of its settings, you must be either:

  • a space administrator for the location of the board
  • a board administrator for the board itself More about permissions in Jira Cloud.
Why customize cards

By customizing the layout of the cards on your board, you’re bringing just the right level of information to your team’s attention, at a glance. You can:

  • Change the card colors to help your team quickly identify the cards on your board as being of a particular work type, priority, assignee, or anything you choose
  • Add up to three custom fields to display on the cards
The default card layout

Work item cards have three layers of information that are stacked on top of each other following this pattern:

  • The work item summary is always at the top on the board and backlog.
  • Any custom fields added to the card are next.
  • Then details about the work item, including work type, priority, assignee, and estimate. To view all other fields, select a card to open the work item detail view.
Configure card colors

You can base your card colors on work types, priorities, assignees, or JQL. Colors are configured per board (not globally).

To add color:

  • If not already there, navigate to your company-managed software space.
  • Select the Active sprints view (if you use a scrum board) or the Kanban board view (if you use a kanban board).
  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Expand Layout in the sidebar, then select Card Colors.
  • Select method from the drop-down.
  • Select the square in the Color column, and pick a color for the work type, priority, assignee, or query. You can switch between methods, and your settings will be retained. Some colors are no longer available in the new color picker. For assignees and work types, select Remove to update your choice.

Priority colors can be Reset to global color, that are defined in Settings, then select Work items, then Priorities.

To edit or remove colors from a query, select More actions (), then:

  • Edit the card color or update the query.
  • Delete the card color to remove the color and make it usable for other queries. Any work items that used that color will restore to the default when you reload your page.
  • Reorder a card color by dragging and dropping the dotted grid icon () to a new position. For query-based colors, the order is important as each work item will be colored according to the first query it matches.

For example, if your first row has the query “worktype = bug” and is colored red, and your second row has query “assignee = kevin” and is colored green, then bugs assigned to Kevin will appear red.

For each method, you can apply one color for item. For example, pick one color for each work item type, priority, assignee, or query.

The colors display as a thin strip on the left-side of the cards on your board.

Method

How it works

Work types

First create a work item on your board, then pick a color for your work types.

A default color will be allocated to all existing work types. The default work types and colors are:

  • Task = blue
  • Sub-task = light-blue
  • Bug = red
  • Story = purple Priorities

The default priority colors match the default colors for priorities across Jira.

Assignees

First create a work item on your board, then pick a color for your assignees.

A default color will be allocated to every user who’s ever been an assigned a work item on your board.

Queries

You can choose to add a color to any query. Work items that don’t match your JQL queries will be shown in grey. Read more about JQL syntax.

Sample queries
Show all work items that are due in the next 24 hours

due <= "24h"

Show all work items created by a particular user

reporter = "Jane"

Show all work items due by the end of month

duedate > endOfMonth()

Customize card covers

To add or change a work item’s card cover on the board:

  • Hover over a work item.

  • Select More actions ().

  • Select Select cover.

  • Choose a color, gradient, photo by Unsplash, or an image attachment to set it as the cover. To show/hide all card covers on the entire board:

  • On the board, select View settings.

  • In the Show fields section, select (or deselect) Card cover. You can also add card cover images to team-managed software spaces, and business spaces.

Adding fields to cards

You can configure cards on a board to display up to three additional fields. The fields can be different for the backlog and Active sprints, if you are using a Scrum board.

To add fields to cards:

  • If not already there, navigate to your company-managed software space.
  • Select the Active sprints view (if you use a scrum board) or the Kanban board view (if you use a kanban board).
  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Expand Layout in the sidebar, then select Card layout.
  • Add or delete fields as desired. You can also enable Days in column to visually indicate how long a work item’s in a column. This helps identify slow moving work.
Using days in column

This is automatically enabled for kanban boards and disabled for scrum boards.

If you have a large instance (more than 300,000 work items, 100 spaces, 100 boards, or 100 open sprints), we recommend you disable this indicator to improve performance.

When you enable Days in column you’ll see a series of dots on each work items to represent the number of days it’s been in that column (and essentially, status).

This helps you see if work items are stagnating and is particularly useful when your board is displayed as a wallboard.

Dots in cards

Number of days in column

1 day

2 days

3 days

5 days

8 days

12 days

20 or more days

If you move a work item to a column where it’s previously been, the indicator provides the cumulative number of days that the work item has been in that column.

For example, you move a work item to the In progress column, and it stays there for two days.

You then move the work item to the Code review column, and it stays there for one day.

During code review, you receive feedback, which requires more development work. So, you move the work item back to the In progress column, and it stays there for one day.

In this example, the dots will reflect the cumulative value — which was three days — that the work item was in the In progress column.

Customize your view of the board and backlog

Customize your view of the board and backlog

Unless otherwise noted, view settings in software spaces are the same for both company-managed and team-managed spaces.

As the space where your team’s work happens, boards and backlogs get very busy. View settings let you create a more focused view based on the information you need. Turn on the epic and version panels to plan upcoming work, view quick filters as buttons for easy access, or cherry-pick which work item fields are most relevant for you.

Note that view settings are applied per user — any changes you make will apply to your board and backlog, and not anyone else’s.

Epics can be renamed, but the information on this page is relevant, regardless of whether your space uses the name epic or any other name.

Board view settings

You can configure the following view settings on the board by selecting View settings at the top-right of your view:

Setting

Description

Open work items in sidebar

When turned on, work items you select open as a sidebar on the right. When turned off, work items open as a centered dialog.

Quick filters

When turned on, quick filters are displayed as buttons for easy access. How to configure quick filters

Work suggestions

When turned on, you can view automated task recommendations from connected tools. How to use work suggestions

Fields

  • Work type
  • Work item key
  • Epic
  • Linked work items
  • Priority
  • Assignee
  • Card cover
  • Due date (team-managed spaces)
  • Labels (team-managed spaces) Choose to show or hide specific fields on work item cards. Turn on a field’s toggle to show it, and turn it off to hide it.

Swimlanes

  • Expand all Swimlanes
  • Collapse all Swimlanes If you’re using swimlanes to group work items by a certain attribute, select Expand all or Collapse all to show or hide work items. How to configure swimlanes

Use the Group by dropdown to select which attribute swimlanes are grouped by.

Card layout (company-managed spaces)

You can also configure cards on a board to display up to three additional fields. Add more fields to cards

Backlog view settings

You can configure the following view settings on the backlog:

Setting

Description

Version panel

Turn on to open the version panel, and turn off to close it. Use keyboard shortcut V to do it faster. What is a version?

Epic panel

Turn on to open the epic panel, and turn off to close it. Use keyboard shortcut E to do it faster. What is an epic?

Quick filters

When turned on, quick filters are displayed as buttons for easy access. How to configure quick filters

Density

  • Default
  • Compact Choose the density of work items in the backlog. Select Compact to use a more dense view so that a greater number of work items are visible on screen.

Fields

  • Work type
  • Work item key
  • Version
  • Epic
  • Status
  • Priority
  • Assignee
  • Due date (team-managed spaces) Choose to show or hide specific fields on work item cards. Turn on a detail’s toggle to show it, and turn it off to hide it.

Swimlanes

  • Expand all
  • Collapse all Select Expand all to view all subtasks in the backlog, or select Collapse all to view story-level work items only.

Card layout (company-managed spaces)

You can also configure cards on a board to display up to three additional fields. Add more fields to cards

Full screen mode

When you need to minimize distractions and reduce on-screen clutter, use full screen mode to hide Jira’s main navigation and the space sidebar to maximize the number of work items on your screen.

To enter full screen mode on the board or backlog, select Enter full screen at the top right. To exit, select Exit full screen at the top right.

Edit a board filter on a company-managed board

Edit a board filter on a company-managed board

To edit a board filter used by your company-managed board:

  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.

  • On the General page under the Board filter section, select Edit Filter Query.

  • Either edit your JQL query or select Switch to basic to switch to a JQL creation tool.

  • Once you make a change, you’ll then have the option to save your new filter. If you weren’t the original creator of the filter, you’ll only be able to Save as. In which case, you’ll need to give it a new name before saving. Another way you can edit a board filter for your scrum board is by:

  • From the backlog in your scrum board, select More actions () in the top right corner, then Configure board.

  • On the General page under the Board filter section, select Edit Filter Query.

  • Either edit your JQL query or select Switch to basic to switch to a JQL creation tool.

  • Once you make a change, you’ll then have the option to save your new filter. If you weren’t the original creator of the filter, you’ll only be able to Save as. In which case, you’ll need to give it a new name before saving.

Enable ranking

Enable ranking

Enabling ranking allows you to rank work items on a board or list by drag-and-drop, and to create sprints on Scrum boards. It also enables Jira to group subtasks together underneath their parent work item.

By default, ranking is enabled on company-managed boards.

Before you begin

To configure the board and any of its settings, you must be either:

  • a space admin for the location of the board
  • a board admin for the board itself See Permissions overview for more information.
Enable ranking

To enable ranking:

  • Go to your board, then select More actions (), then Configure board.
  • Select the Add Rank button. The filter for your board will be updated to order by Rank. This will affect all boards using this filter.

ORDER BY Rank ASC

You can also rank work items by other work item properties — for example, priority or issuetype:

ORDER BY priority DESC

ORDER BY issuetype DESC

Notes:

  • Jira automatically creates a custom field called Rank, of type Global Rank. Please ensure that your Jira instance contains only one custom field called Rank, and that the Rank field is assigned to the global context (i.e. not to specific work items or spaces).
  • When ranking is enabled for scrum spaces, you can:
    • move work items from your scrum backlog to relevant sprint sections
    • rank work items within currently active sprints and sprints being planned out
  • When ranking is enabled for kanban spaces, you can:
    • move work items from your kanban backlog to your work-in-progress section
    • rank work items within your kanban board and the work-in-progress section in your Kanban backlog
  • When using a ranking setting other than ORDER BY Rank ASC, and moving work items from the backlog to relevant sections, the work items are automatically ranked based on the filter query of your board.
  • The Rank clause is case sensitive. Need help? If you can’t find the answer you need in our documentation, we have other resources available to help you. See Getting help.
