How can I track work progress in Jira?

How can I track work progress in Jira?

You can monitor the progress of a team as they progress through a sprint to ensure that they’re on track using the Time tracking function. By tracking the team’s progress, you can then update the target end date set using the board estimation function as needed. What is estimation in Jira?

Time tracking information can then be funneled into one of several reports that are included with Jira, including a burndown or burnup chart. More about reports in Jira

Jira allows you to use different units of measurements to estimate tasks versus track work across boards. Teams in Jira commonly estimate work items in story points, then track progress on their board using hours. However, not all of these units are intended for both work item estimation and tracking.

How to configure time tracking in Jira

Show or hide work items on your board with quick filters

Show or hide work items on your board with quick filters

As your work grows, use filters to show or hide work items based on certain criteria. These filters only become available in both company-managed and team-managed spaces once they apply to at least one work item in your board. For example, the Label filter only shows if at least one work item in your space has a label.

Enabling a filter won’t remove work items from your board, but rather, allows you to focus on those you want to see.

In team-managed and company-managed spaces, the default filters available are:

  • The Assignee filter, which shows work items that are assigned to specific people in your space. To filter by assignee, select the person’s avatar in the filter bar. You can select more than one person if you need.

  • The Epic or Parent filter, which shows work items that belong to larger pieces of work in your space (by default, this work type is called an epic, but you can rename it). This filter appears after you’ve created your first epic in the space.

  • The Label filter, which shows work items that have been tagged with specific labels in your space. This filter appears after you’ve added a label to at least one work item in your space.

  • The Work type filter, which shows work items based on their work type (for example, Bug or Task). This filter appears after you’ve created more than one type of work item in your space. The following quick filters only appear in company-managed spaces:

  • The Only My issues filter, which shows issues that are assigned to the user whose currently logged in

  • The Recently Updated filter, which shows you issues that were last worked on in your board

Use the simplified workflow

Use the simplified workflow

This is for company-managed software spaces only.

By default, software spaces with a scrum or kanban board use a simplified workflow, rather than a regular Jira workflow. Find out about the differences between simplified workflows and Jira workflow

However, it’s also possible for software spaces to switch to using a regular Jira workflow. If your space is currently using the Jira workflow, you may want to switch it back to the simplified workflow. You will then be able to easily add new statuses from within your software space.

Note that the default steps for the simplified workflow (described in the table above) will not be created when you switch from the Jira workflow. Your existing workflow steps will be included in the workflow instead. The default steps are only created if the simplified workflow is chosen when the board and space are created in your software space.

Before you begin

To configure the board and any of its settings, you must be either:

  • a space administrator for the location of the board
  • a board administrator for the board itself See Permissions overview for more information.
Switch to the simplified workflow

How can I tell if my board is using the simplified workflow?

  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Select Layout to expand the menu, then select Columns.
  • Check what’s described under Workflow type. If you’re using the simplified workflow, you’ll see the words: You’re using the simplified workflow. Otherwise, you’ll see the words: You’re using the Jira workflow.

You’ll also notice that the Add status button is missing if the space is using a Jira workflow.

Space prerequisites

You will only be able to switch to the simplified workflow if:

  • There is only one space being viewed by your board (to check this, look at the board’s filter)

  • That space uses a Jiraworkflow scheme, which only has one workflow for all work types

  • Your workflow only uses post functions, validators, and conditions that are provided by Atlassian — and not any of which provided by add-ons

  • The existing workflow has at least one outgoing transition for each status To switch to the simplified workflow:

  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.

  • Select Layout to expand the menu, then select Columns.

  • Under Workflow type, select the Simplify workflow button. If this button doesn’t display, check that your space meets the prerequisites described above.

  • In the Simplify workflow modal, select which statuses trigger the resolution to be set to Done, then select Next.

  • Review the changes to your workflow, then select Confirm. The Add status button will now be shown in the Unmapped statuses section. You can view workflow statuses and transitions in company-managed spaces. When viewing a work item, select the status dropdown, then View workflow.

Need help? If you can’t find the answer you need in our documentation, we have other resources available to help you. See Getting help.

What are story points?

What are story points?

Story points are a subjective unit of measurement that doesn’t correlate to any amount of time. Instead, story points express the amount of effort needed to complete a task compared to other work in the sprint. For example, assuming a team has 30 story points in an iteration, a small task that can be completed quickly by one person might only be one story point, whereas a task that will consume your team’s entire sprint would consume all 30 story points.

Story points are a core concept in agile planning, and can only be used by those planning for scrum teams. It can be used for both work item estimation and tracking the progress of work on a board.

By default, story points can only be assigned to story or epic-type work items, and not subtasks such as bugs. This can be changed by those with Jira administrator permissions. Learn how administrators can configure custom field contexts.

What are Time estimates (days, hours, minutes)?

What are Time estimates (days, hours, minutes)?

Time estimates do exactly what the label says: a unit of estimation that objectively states “this task should take no more than x hours to complete”. Though scrum teams can also use this, time is the only unit of estimation available to kanban teams.

Time estimates can be used for both work item estimation and time tracking on a board. When tracking progress on a board, Jira looks at the value in the Original Time Estimate field. Learn more about logging time to work items.

By default, time estimates are specified in minutes, but you can use hours, days, or weeks, depending on your Jira system configuration. Learn how to configure time tracking in Jira.

What is a simplified Jira workflow?

What is a simplified Jira workflow?

In most Jira spaces, work items move from To do to Done through a workflow. Each workflow is composed of statuses and transitions that work moves through, usually representing a process in your organization.

When a Software space is created with a Scrum or Kanban board, it uses a simplified workflow instead. Simplified workflows allow workflow management to be delegated to the administrators of the board. For example, board admins can add columns (i.e. statuses) to their board, without needing to contact a Jira admin.

Simplified workflows and Jira workflows compared

Simplified workflow

Jira workflow

Statuses can be edited in Board settings.

  • If the Add status button is missing in Board settings, it’s because your Jira admin has switched the board’s workflow to a Jira workflow. Can only be edited by a Jira admin in Jira settings.

  • Has three default statuses for Scrum boards: To do, In progress, Done

  • Has four default statuses for Kanban boards: Backlog, Selected for development, In progress, Done Has more steps than are typically needed on a board (see the default Jira workflow).

Allows work items to be dragged freely between columns

Has workflow “conditions” that prevent work items from being dragged freely between all columns

Displays no screens on any transitions, all transitions will happen instantly.

Displays screens for Resolve work item, Close work item, and Reopen work item.

Automatically sets a resolution of ‘Done’ when work items are transitioned to the ‘successful’ column, i.e. statuses mapped to the successful column (see Configure columns)

Resolutions aren’t set automatically, but this can be configured. See link

Can be edited via board settings or directly on the board (provided you’re a space admin for the space used by the board, or a board admin for the board itself)

Can only be edited via workflow configuration, see Workflows for more information

What is estimation in Jira?

What is estimation in Jira?

Estimation on a Jira board is a powerful tool to help planners assess the size of a backlog and infer a reasonable due date for a project or initiative. Instead of manually estimating every work item in a backlog, which may span months into the future, this capability uses basic information to project a completion date. It does this by comparing initial work item estimates against the average amount of work the team is currently completing per sprint. This average is referred to as the team’s velocity. How to configure work item estimation

Once work is estimated, you can then track your team’s progress against your target end date. Learn more about tracking the progress of your team’s work. How to track the progress of projects in Jira

What is work item count?

What is work item count?

Work item count divides the total number of work items in your sprint between those that have been complete, those that are in progress, and how many remain to be done. By only tracking the number of work items, it disregards any work item estimates and assumes that they’re all weighted the same. When you’re tracking the progress of a project using this, you won’t be able to set estimates on your work items. The Estimate field on work items will be greyed out and uneditable.

Work item count is only used to track progress of work on a board. Learn how to configure time tracking in Jira.

Work item limits in company-managed spaces

Work item limits in company-managed spaces

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

Jira work items are displayed on your Jira board, in your backlog, and on your timeline – depending on any filters you’ve set up using Jira Query Language (JQL). There’s no limit on the number of work items that can be included in a filter. However, your board, backlog, and timeline can each only show up to 5,000 work items at a time. To avoid performance issues, scope your filter to specific projects or spaces with fewer than 5,000 work items.

To make a board that only shows work items you want included, you can create a board using filters based on a JQL query. For example, you might create a board that includes work items from multiple spaces, one space, or from a particular component of a space. Find out about filters.

To configure a filter on a board, you must be either:

  • a space admin for the location of the board
  • a board admin for the board itself
What happens when the limit is exceeded

When your board or backlog has exceeded the work item limit, it will show the first 5,000 work items according to your board filter settings. This way, your team can still view and edit work items and get on with their work.

If your board or backlog has more than 5,000 work items, your admin will see a warning message with a link to edit the board filter. To resolve this, they can adjust the board filter using JQL to exclude non-critical items. How to edit a board filter on a company-managed board For example, you could use a query like ‘status != Done AND priority = High’ to display only high-priority, incomplete tasks. View more example board JQL queries for board filters.

If you’re not an admin, you’ll still see the message, but you won’t be able to edit the filter. You’ll need to contact your Jira space admin. Select View all spaces from your sidebar to find out who to contact.

If the timeline doesn’t display after you’ve adjusted the board filter, you might need to check whether the filter includes more than one space. Read about the timeline for multiple space.

If you’re a Jira Premium user, you can use the plans feature to display up to 30,000 work items. Get started with plans

Configure columns and statuses in your team-managed sapce

Assign statuses and edit columns in a team-managed space

Assign statuses and edit columns in a team-managed space

This page is for team-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

If you’re in a company-managed space, check out these company-managed space articles instead.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed space.

By default, a board’s columns are assigned the default Jira statuses To do, In progress, and Done. You can change this to suit your way of working.

For example, you may create a custom status to capture work In review, and you’ll probably want to map that status to an appropriate column on your board, too.

All team-managed spaces start out with the Jira default workflow. This means default columns are assigned a default status, like this:

Column

Status

To do

To do

In progress

In progress

Done

Done

Manage how your work flows in Jira team-managed spaces

You must have the administrator role in your space to do the following things described on this page. More about roles in team-managed spaces

You can choose to associate, or map, a specific status to a column.

  • Drag and drop a status from the hidden statuses panel to the appropriate column.
  • Option 2: Go to specific column to add a new status from dropdown.
Configure your columns and statuses

As you advance your team’s way of working, it’s likely you’ll create new, custom statuses and columns. Multiple columns can affect the flow of your board—it might become too busy and tough to navigate.

To free up your board, you can use the Columns and statuses settings and assign multiple statuses to a single column. This is particularly effective when the statuses have something in common and ladder up to a phase or process, which the column can represent.

When a column’s assigned multiple statuses, each status is represented as a “drop zone” on your board’s columns. This lets your team move work to different statuses within the one board column.

To access the Columns and statuses settings:

  • If not already there, navigate to your team-managed software space.
  • From your space’s sidebar, select Space settings, then Board. This will land you directly in the Columns and statuses settings. This is a replica of your board’s columns and their associated statuses, but with advanced configuration options.
Assign an existing status to another column

Consider how you’d like to arrange your board. You may choose to group together common statuses by the stage or step they represent.

Statuses are created and managed in the workflow editor. Learn how to view, add, or remove statuses in your space.

To move a status between columns:

  • If not already there, navigate to your team-managed software space.
  • From your space’s sidebar, select Space settings, then Board.
  • In Columns and statuses, hover over the relevant status. The entire card is interactive.
  • Select, then drag and drop the status onto your chosen column.
  • Once you’re happy, select Save changes. The changes you’ve made will apply to your board.
Unassign an existing status from a column

You can unassign statuses to reduce clutter on your board. This is handy when you use multiple statuses to track your work, but only need certain issues to be visible on the board. If you haven’t assigned a status to a column, any issues with that status won’t be visible on the board and backlog.

To unassign a status from a column:

  • If not already there, navigate to your team-managed software space.
  • From your space’s sidebar, select Space settings, then Board.
  • In Columns and statuses, hover over the relevant status.
  • Select, then drag-and-drop the status to the left panel titled Unassigned statuses.
  • Once you’re happy, select Save changes. The changes you’ve made will apply to your board. When you create a new status in the workflow editor, it’ll be unassigned by default.

Manage columns and statuses in team-managed software spaces

Manage columns and statuses in team-managed software spaces

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

When you first start out, columns and statuses are connected to each other. This means when you create a column, you’re also creating a status. Changes to your columns and statuses can therefore be managed directly on the board.

This changes however when you assign multiple statuses to a single column or give a column and its assigned status unique names. The column and status/es become separate elements, independent of each other.

Columns and their statuses could look a little like this:

Column

Status

To Do

To Do

Gathering Requirements

In Progress

In Progress

In Review

On Hold

Done

Won’t Do

Done

Your board configuration is now separated from your board. To create new columns, or make any changes to your existing columns and statuses, use your Columns and statuses settings.

You must have the following to do the things described on this page.

Role: Space admin

Configure the board in your software space

To access your Columns and statuses settings from your board:

  • If not already there, navigate to your team-managed software space.

  • From your space’s sidebar, select your board beneath its respective space.

  • In the top, far right select More actions (•••), then Configure board. Another way you can configure your board is by accessing the settings:

  • If not already there, navigate to your team-managed software space.

  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings. If you’ve previously changed these settings, you can quickly access them again by selecting Configure board next to the rightmost column on your board.

To access your Columns and statuses settings from anywhere in your space:

  • If not already there, navigate to your team-managed software space.
  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Board.
Add or move a column in your software space’s board

Creating a new column in the Columns and statuses settings won’t create an associated status.

Statuses are instead created and managed in the workflow editor. How to view, add, or remove statuses in your space

To add a new column:

  • If not already there, navigate to your Columns and statuses settings.
  • Select Create column (+) next to the rightmost column.
Rename a column and set limits on your software space’s board

Keep in mind that choosing unique names for a column and the status it’s assigned will impact your ability to edit from your board.

  • If not already there, navigate to your Columns and statuses settings.
  • Hover over the column title. Select Edit column ().
  • Enter a new name for the column.
  • In this modal, you can also set a maximum number of work items. The column changes color when it contains too many work items.
Delete a column on your software space’s board

In your Columns and statuses settings, you can only delete columns. Statuses are independent of columns in these settings. If a status isn’t assigned to a column, any work items with that status won’t be visible on the board.

Statuses are created and managed in the workflow editor.

How to view, add, or remove statuses in your space

  • If not already there, navigate to your Columns and statuses settings.
  • Hover over the column heading. Select Edit column ().
  • Select Delete column in the bottom left. You can continue to configure your board, directly on your board. To do this, revert to the original one-status-per-column state, and make sure the columns and statuses share the same name.

Change financial year dates in your plans

By default, all plans align the financial year with the calendar year beginning in January. You can change this setting so that all plans will automatically calculate and display quarters (3 month intervals) according to your preferred financial year start and end date.

The financial year is named according to the year in which it ends.

To change the financial year start date:

  • Navigate to the Jira admin panel by selecting Settings () in the upper right, then Jira apps.
  • Select Financial year from the left side navigation, then pick your start month and date.

Configure custom hierarchy levels in your plan

Configure custom hierarchy levels in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

The processes described in this section are only possible with Jira administrator permissions.

By default, Jira comes with Epic as a level 1 work type, and Story as a level 0 (subtasks are considered -1 or below Story). While you can rename Epic, which remains at level 1, as part of your Jira Premium and Enterprise subscriptions, you can also add levels above 1 and use these extra levels to track your organization’s larger initiatives in your company-managed projects and plans to unify work across multiple spaces. Some common work types are Legend, Odyssey, or Anthology. Or maybe you wanna go crazy and name your higher hierarchy levels things like Monolith, Deity, or Omnipotence. It’s truly up to you.

Before you can plan with levels above epic, an administrator needs to first associate the hierarchy level in your plan with a Jira work type. This is because your plan uses its own hierarchy structure which correlates to, but is independent from, the order of Jira work types defined in your work type scheme.

Adding a new custom hierarchy level is a three step process. If the work type already exists and is part of your space’s work type scheme, skip to step 3:

Changes to the hierarchy settings will apply to all existing plans and company-managed projects using this work item scheme. These changes can affect existing parent and child work item relationships. Review the impact and use manual updates or bulk edits to correct affected items.

1. Create work type
  • Select Settings (), then Work items.
  • In the left column, go to Work types, then Add work type.
  • Enter a name and description for your new work type.
  • Choose between a standard or sub-task work type.
    • Standard work types are added at the story level, while subtask work types are added underneath the story level (alongside the existing default work type already named subtasks). Jira admins can add standard work types to higher hierarchy levels by configuring the work type hierarchy.
  • Select a work type scheme to associate the new work type (optional).
  • Select Add.
2. Add work type to scheme
  • Select Settings (), then Work items.
  • From the left column, select Work type schemes.
  • Find the relevant work type scheme and select Edit.
  • Edit the name, description, default work type, and selected work types.
    • To add a work type to the scheme, drag it from Available Work Types to Work Types for Current Scheme. The order in which they’re listed in this box represents the hierarchical structure within Jira. For example, if you add the work type bug below story, Jira will consider story to be its parent work type.
  • When you’re done, select Save.
3. Associate the work type to your hierarchy
  • Now that you’ve created the work type and added it to your work type scheme, select Work type hierarchy from the menu on the left.
  • The menu on this screen lets you arrange Jira work types by hierarchy levels. The left column, labeled Level name, is the hierarchy structure in your plan and the right column, labeled Jira work types, are the configured work types in your scheme.
    • To add a new level, select + Create level at the bottom of the menu. Give your new level a name, then use the dropdown in the Jira work types column to associate it with a work type.
    • To reorganize your hierarchy structure, drag and drop the levels into the order you’d like. The order of this list is how your hierarchy levels will show in your plan, and won’t change the structure of your Jira work types as previously configured.
  • Once you’ve configured your level, select Save changes.
  • On your timeline view, open the Filters menu and adjust your hierarchy filters to show this new level on your timeline. In order to see custom hierarchy level relationships in Jira work items, you must add the Parent field to your work items.

See how to add custom fields to your work items in Jira

Configure Dependencies in Jira for your plan

Configure Dependencies in Jira for your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

The processes described in this section are only possible with Jira administrator permissions.

By default, dependencies in your plan treat all work item links as though they have the Blocks work item link type. In order to use custom work item links, they must be created and defined by an administrator.

This is a two step process.

1. Configure your work item link
  • Navigate to the Jira admin panel using the Settings () icon in the upper right and select Work items.
  • In the left hand sidebar, select Work item linking under Work item features.
  • Make sure that work item linking is set to ON. If it’s not, select Activate to enable it.
  • Once activated, you can edit the Name, Outward description, and Inward description of an existing work item link by selecting Edit from the right column. Use Update to save your changes.
    • To add a new link, define the name of your new work item link and the descriptions using the fields under the Add New Link Type header. Use Add to save it. Read more about work item linking.
2. Apply that configuration to your plan
  • Navigate to the Jira admin panel using the icon in the upper right and select Jira apps.
  • Go to Dependencies on the left side nav. Add a work item linking type using the dropdown menu, or remove it with the x that appears in the box. Use Swap on the right side to invert the dependent relationship.
  • Select Save changes. These changes will apply to dependencies in all plans in your instance.

You also have the option of deciding whether your plan uses concurrent or sequential dependencies. With Sequential dependencies selected, work items scheduled to the same sprint show as being off-track dependencies. Read more the differences between sequential and concurrent dependencies.

Manage inherited permissions in plans

Manage inherited permissions in plans

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Users are automatically granted permissions based on their global Jira user group at the time of your site’s creation. It doesn’t automatically update if a group’s global permissions change at a later date, meaning you’ll need to use the instructions on this page to manually revoke a group’s plans permissions.

When your site is created, users with Jira administrator and site administrator access also have Plans administrator access by default, though this can be changed. If your plan includes team-managed spaces, you’ll need Administrator or Editor permissions in those spaces to make changes. If you only have Viewer permissions for a team-managed space, you’ll only be able to read the data from that space.

To add or remove a user group from your plan permissions:

  • From the Jira main navigation, select Settings () then Jira apps in the upper right of your screen.
  • Select Permissions underneath Plans on the left side menu. Read more about the different permission types in plans.

Coordinate and monitor work with sprints

Add work items to an active sprint

Add work items to an active sprint

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

In Scrum, scope creep during a sprint should be avoided. The team is supposed to deliver a working piece of software at the end of the sprint, so when adding work items to a sprint you need to know your team’s capacity for work, as well as the amount of work they are committing to.

Typically, your team estimates work items before adding them to the sprint, so you can see the total estimated work for the sprint (in the sprint footer). You can match this against your team’s capacity for work by looking at past sprints. Tools like the Velocity Chart and Burndown Chart can help you with this. Don’t worry if you don’t have any historical data — you’ll get a good idea of your team’s velocity once they start completing sprints.

To add work items to an active sprint, you must have:

  • Rank work item enabled
  • Schedule work item and Edit work item permissions
Add a work item to an active sprint

If not already there, navigate to your company-managed software space.

Add work items from the backlog to an active sprint
  • From your space navigation, select the Backlog tab.
  • Drag and drop the work items onto the relevant sprint. Tip

To add multiple work items:

  • select the work items (use Shift+Click or Ctrl+Click), right-click, then select the relevant sprint
  • drag the sprint footer down to include work items from the backlog.
Create a work item and add it to an active sprint
  • From your space navigation, select the Active sprints tab.
  • Create a new work item by selecting Create from the top navigation.
  • Fill in the work item details and add the relevant sprint in the Sprint field.
  • Select Create. Tip

To create multiple work items, select the Create another work item checkbox.

Complete a sprint

Complete a sprint

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

To complete a sprint, you must be a Jira Administrator or a user with the Manage Sprints permission.

Before you can complete a sprint, all sub-tasks must be marked as Done. If a parent work item is not marked as Done, it will be moved to a future sprint or to the Backlog when the sprint is completed.

Complete the sprint

Here’s how to complete a sprint in your company-managed space:

  • If not already there, navigate to your company-managed software space.
  • From your space’s sidebar, select Active sprints.
  • If necessary, select the sprint you want to complete from the sprint drop-down.
  • Note that if you have multiple sprints in the Active sprints of your board, the ‘Complete Sprint’ button will not appear until you select one of the sprints.
  • Click Complete Sprint. All completed work items will move out of Active sprints.
  • If the sprint has incomplete work items, select from one of the following:
    • Backlog, to move the work items to the backlog
    • Any future sprint, to move the work items to any future sprint that’s already created
    • New sprint, to create a new sprint and then move the work items to the new sprint Your work items won’t be marked with the date the sprint was closed; however, you can always view the sprint for a work item to find out when the sprint ended.
Marking work items as complete

Work items are considered as complete once they have been moved to the last column on the board. Work items in any other column will be considered incomplete (or “open”).

When a sprint is shared between multiple boards, only work items from the board that is completing the sprint will be carried over to the future sprint or new sprint. Any incomplete work items from other boards will be moved to the Backlog instead.

If you can’t complete a sprint, your board’s filter may be complex, and Jira is unable to determine which spaces will be returned by the query. See Using Manage Sprints permission for advanced cases if you need help.

Sprints only apply to Scrum boards. If you are using a Kanban board, check out Deploying a release instead.

Create sprints in company-managed spaces

Create sprints in company-managed spaces

You can create a sprint for your current iteration, or multiple future sprints if you want to plan several iterations ahead.

Most sprint actions require the Manage Sprints space permission. However, some sprint actions like adding work items to sprints, removing work items from sprints also require the Schedule work items and Edit work items space permissions. More about permissions in Jira

To create a sprint:

  • If not already there, navigate to your company-managed software space.
  • From your space navigation, select the Backlog tab.
  • Scroll down past any currently existing sprints to the section titled Backlog. On the far right of this section, find and select the Create sprint button. Once you have created a sprint, you can add work items to it to start planning your team’s future work.

Delete a sprint

Delete a sprint

When you delete a sprint, the work item it contained are moved to the next sprint in the list. If you delete an active sprint, those work items will keep their status in their new sprint.

The process for deleting completed sprints is different. Learn how to delete a sprint that’s been completed.

To delete a sprint:

  • From your space navigation, select the Backlog tab.
  • Select More actions (), then Delete sprint.

Enable parallel sprints

Enable parallel sprints

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

Use parallel sprints to run multiple active sprints at the same time. This can be useful when your team wants to split their work to focus on different goals while using the same backlog.

For example, part of your team might run a sprint for development, while other team members focus on a separate sprint for design. Both sprints would contain work items from the same backlog, but each sprint can be started and completed independently.

To enable parallel sprints in company-managed spaces:

  • Select Settings (), then Jira apps.
  • Select Jira configuration from the sidebar.
  • Select the toggle next to Parallel sprints for company-managed spaces. The processes on this page require the Administer Jira permission.

If you’ve accidentally moved a work item to a future sprint and you want to move it back to its original sprint (which is now closed), you’ll need to reopen the original sprint. Parallel sprints must be enabled before you do this.

Link a Confluence page to a sprint

Link a Confluence page to a sprint

If you’ve linked your Jira instance to a Confluence instance, you can create and link Confluence pages to your sprints via Jira Software.

For example, you may want to write your team’s retrospective notes in Confluence and link them to the Sprint Report for the completed sprint.

Before you begin
  • These instructions only apply to Scrum boards.
  • Edit work item permission is required to add pages. Read Permissions overview for more information.
Create a new linked Confluence page for a sprint
  • Go to the board that sits below the respective company-managed space in the sidebar.
  • Select Reports, then select Sprint Report.
  • Select the relevant sprint from the sprint dropdown.
  • Select View linked pages above the report chart.
  • Select Create page. The ‘Create’ dialog in Confluence will be displayed.
Link an existing Confluence page to a sprint
  • Go to the board that sits below the respective company-managed space in the sidebar.
  • Select Reports, then select Sprint Report.
  • Select the relevant sprint from the sprint dropdown.
  • Select View linked pages above the report chart.
  • Select Link page, search for the page you want, and select it. Need help? If you can’t find the answer you need in our documentation, we have other resources available to help you. See Getting help.

Monitor the progress of a sprint

Monitor the progress of a sprint

You’ve started a sprint with grand plans. How do you make sure that your team is on track to deliver what they’ve committed to?

Jira provides a number of tools that you can use to monitor the progress of a sprint. If you run into problems or things are just not on track for the target date, Jira can help visualize or highlight problems so your team can take actions to remedy them.

Active sprints

The Active sprints of a Scrum board just may be the central workspace for a sprint that’s in progress. You and your team would usually check Active sprints at least once a day, while a sprint is running — perhaps your team has its daily stand-ups around a monitor displaying Active sprints.

Learn more about using Active sprints

Development panel for work items

If you have Jira connected to your development tools, a ‘Development’ panel is shown on each work item that shows you information about the commits, branches, pull requests, builds, and more, that are related to the work item. This can help you see discrepancies at a glance — for example, work items that have related commits, but are still in the ‘To Do’ status.

Learn more about configuring development tools

Wallboards and gadgets

A wallboard can act as an “information radiator” for your team, letting them know how they are progressing during a sprint, alerting them when builds are broken, reminding them about upcoming team events, and more. You just need to add the desired gadgets to a dashboard, then display it as a wallboard (Tools > View as Wallboard on the dashboard).

Learn more about dashboards in Jira

Burndown Chart

The Burndown Chart shows the work that has been completed in a sprint and estimates how long it will take to complete the remaining work. This can help you determine the likelihood of your team completing a sprint on time — allowing you to visualize or highlight problems so your team can take actions to remedy them.

Learn more about the Burndown Chart

Move or transition work items in an active sprint

Move or transition work items in an active sprint

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

To move or transition work items in an active sprint, you must have:

  • Rank work item enabled
  • Schedule work item and Edit work item permissions More about space permissions
Transition a work item

You can only change the status of multiple work items from the board if you’re in a software space.

Drag and drop a work item between columns to transition it.

To transition multiple work items from the board:

  • Select multiple work items from the board. You can either:
    • hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (Mac) while selecting work items
    • hold the Shift key to select a group of adjacent work items
  • Drag the work items into the column corresponding to the new status. If you are unable to move the work items using this method, complete the following steps.
  • Right-click or select More actions (•••) on one of the selected work items, then select Bulk change.
  • Select Transition work items and then Next.
  • Select the available workflow action. The actions available are dependent on the work items (and their associated workflows) that you have selected. Select Next.
  • Select a value for any required fields for this transition, and if available, decide whether you’d like to send email notifications. Select Next.
  • Review your changes and select Confirm, then Acknowledge.
Move a work item’s position within the column

Drag and drop a work item within a column to rank it. You can also right-click the work item to open a menu that allows you to send it to the top or the bottom of the current column.

Reopen a sprint

Reopen a sprint

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

To reopen a sprint, you must be a Jira administrator or a user with the Manage Sprints space permission. More about permissions in Jira.

If another sprint is already active, you’ll need to enable parallel sprints before reopening a completed sprint.

To reopen a sprint:

  • If not already there, navigate to your spaces.
  • From your space navigation, select the Reports tab.
  • If you’re using a company-managed space, select the Sprint Report. If you’re using a team-managed space, select either the Burnup report or the Sprint burndown chart.
  • Select the relevant sprint from the sprint drop-down.
  • Select More actions (…), then Reopen sprint.
  • Select Reopen. When you reopen a sprint, this event is recorded in the sprint report and the report will use your new end date.

Depending on the state of your team’s work items, and any actions you may have taken when closing the sprint, Jira may change the status of work items as they appear in the sprint report.

Scenarios for reopening sprints

The diagram below shows you the possible flows when you’re reopening sprints, depending on certain scenarios.

In the following sample scenarios listed below, let’s assume the following details:

  • You’ve created a sprint and named it ‘Sprint 1’.
  • You’ve added some work items to Sprint 1, and then started it.
  • Your team is currently working on the work item in Sprint 1.
  • You have a future planned sprint named ‘Sprint 2’.
Simple scenarios

Below are some examples of simple scenarios where you may want to reopen a sprint, and the results you can expect.

Scenario details

Expected results

  • You closed Sprint 1, and there were some completed work items in it.
  • All incomplete work items were moved back to the Backlog.
  • All these incomplete work items are still in the Backlog when you try to reopen Sprint 1.
  • Sprint 1 is reopened successfully.
  • Sprint 1 contains all the completed and incomplete work items that were in Sprint 1 when it was closed.
  • You closed Sprint 1, and there were no completed work items in it.
  • All incomplete work items were moved back to the Backlog.
  • During sprint planning, you moved all of these work items to the future sprint, Sprint 2.
  • You started Sprint 2, and Sprint 2 is a currently active sprint when you try to reopen Sprint 1.
  • The Parallel Sprints feature is enabled. Sprint 1 cannot be reopened because all incomplete work items in Sprint 1 when it was closed are now in the currently active Sprint 2.
Complex scenarios

In some cases, you may be able to reopen a sprint, but the results may not be as what you expect them to be. Or you may not be able to reopen a sprint altogether. Below are some examples of complex scenarios where you may want to reopen a sprint, and the results you can expect.

Scenario details

Expected results

  • You closed Sprint 1, and there were some completed work items in it.

  • All incomplete work items were moved back to the Backlog.

  • During sprint planning, you moved some of these work items to the future sprint, Sprint 2.

  • You started Sprint 2, and Sprint 2 is a currently active sprint when you try to reopen Sprint 1.

  • The Parallel Sprints feature is enabled.

  • Sprint 1 is reopened successfully.

  • Sprint 1 contains all the completed and incomplete work items that were in the Sprint 1 when it was closed.

  • The incomplete work items that were in Sprint 1 when it was closed, but are currently in the active Sprint 2 will remain in Sprint 2. This is because work items in an active sprint are not moved during the reopen sprint process.

  • You closed Sprint 1, and there were some completed work items in it.

  • All incomplete work items were moved back to the Backlog.

  • During sprint planning, you moved some of these work items to the future sprint, Sprint 2.

  • You started Sprint 2, and Sprint 2 is a currently active sprint when you try to reopen Sprint 1.

  • The Parallel Sprints feature is not enabled. Sprint 1 cannot be reopened for the following reasons:

  • There is a currently active sprint, Sprint 2.

  • The Parallel Sprints feature is not enabled.

  • You closed Sprint 1, and there were no completed work items in it.

  • All incomplete work items were moved back to the Backlog.

  • During sprint planning, you moved all of these work items to the future sprint, Sprint 2.

  • You started Sprint 2, and Sprint 2 is a currently active sprint when you try to reopen Sprint 1.

  • The Parallel Sprints feature is enabled. Sprint 1 cannot be reopened because all of its work items are now in the currently active sprint, Sprint 2.

Reorder a sprint in a company-managed space

Reorder a sprint in a company-managed space

You can only reorder planned sprints — not the active sprint or closed sprints. Note that if the same sprints are included on different boards, the sprint order will change on those boards, too.

To move a sprint up or down in your backlog:

  • If not already there, navigate to your company-managed software space.
  • From your space navigation, select the Backlog tab.
  • Select more () then Move sprint up or Move sprint down. You can also move a sprint straight to the top or bottom of your backlog by selecting Move sprint to top or Move sprint to bottom.

Start a sprint in company-managed spaces

Start a sprint in company-managed spaces

To start a sprint in a company-managed space:

  • From your space navigation, select the Backlog tab.
  • Find the sprint that you want to start and select Start sprint.
    • Update the Sprint name.
    • Select the Start date and End date for the sprint.
      • To prevent inaccurate reporting, the planned time and date are replaced by a suggested time and date that match the moment you select Start sprint. This can be changed to suit your team. More about reports in company-managed spaces
    • Add a Sprint goal if desired.
      • This sprint goal is also displayed on the Sprint Report and Burndown Chart.
  • Select Start. After this, you’ll be taken to the Active sprints page that shows issues in your newly started sprint.

You can view your active sprint in the Backlog, and even add and remove issues from it. Be aware that adding and removing an issue from the active sprint is considered to be a scope change and will be reflected in some reports like the Burndown Chart.

When your sprint ends, you’ll be given the option to move any incomplete issues to a new sprint, or your Backlog.

If you want to have more than one active sprint at a time, you’ll need to enable parallel sprints. More about what parallel sprints are, and how to use them

Use active sprints

Use active sprints

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

The Active sprints of a Scrum board displays the work items that your team is currently working on. You can create and update work items, and drag and drop work items to transition them through a workflow.

Before you begin
  • Active sprints are only available on Scrum boards. If you are using a Kanban board, see Monitoring work in a Kanban space instead.
  • Different functions on the Active sprints of a board require different permissions. See Permissions overview for more information.
Use Active sprints in a Scrum board

A work item shows on your active sprints board if it:

  • has a status that maps to one of the board’s columns,
  • is in an active sprint (for Scrum boards), and
  • matches the board’s saved filter Subtasks on the active sprints board are shown slightly indented, with their parent work item key shown above.

Each column maps to one or more Jira statuses. Work items hidden by a quick filter are excluded from the swimlane count.

When the Days in column indicator is enabled, colored dots will show at the bottom of each work item, representing the number of days the work item has been in its current column. Hover over the dots to see the total number of days. Find out about configuring columns

What are parallel sprints?

What are parallel sprints?

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

The Parallel sprints feature lets you enable multiple active sprints that are running in parallel with each other. For example, if you have two teams working from the same backlog, each team can now work on their own active sprint simultaneously.

There are some caveats when using parallel sprints:

  • The Velocity Chart will not show the velocity per team.
  • The current implementation assumes that the teams perform estimation identically, which is unlikely in practice.

What is a sprint?

What is a sprint?

A sprint — also known as an iteration — is a short period in which the development team implements and delivers a discrete and potentially shippable application increment, e.g. a working milestone version. In Jira, sprints are planned from the Backlog tab.

Only Scrum teams can use sprints.

If you haven’t run sprints before, we recommend using a fixed two-week duration for each sprint. It’s long enough to get something accomplished, but not so long that the team isn’t getting regular feedback. Sprints do not apply to Kanban spaces.

In Jira, you view sprints on a board and assign issues to sprints. You can search for issues in upcoming sprints using JQL (Sprint field). You can view the Sprint field on each individual issue as well, to see the sprint that an issue is part of.

Create and configure your work items

Add files, images, and other content to describe a work item

Add files, images, and other content to describe a work item

We’re rolling out some changes to the work item as an open beta. Some documentation may not yet reflect these updates, and the new experience might not be enabled on your site. Read more about the upcoming changes

Once you’ve created a work item, it’s important to add enough detail to it to make sure whoever’s working on it can resolve it as quickly as possible. Images, files, diagrams, support tickets, and other details all help to provide a clear picture of the work that needs to be done.

As you’d expect, you can add content like images and files from your computer, but you can also source and update content from external services via Atlassian Marketplace apps. Here are a few common ways you can add content to work items to create a richer picture for whoever’s working on it.

The Free plans for Jira Cloud and Jira Service Management have a file storage limit of 2GB per app. The Standard plan allows up to 250GB per app, and file storage is unlimited on Premium plans. Read more about Jira Cloud plans.

Add a description

A complete description on a work item can save a lot of time in the long run. If you or a teammate come to a work item, but don’t really understand what it’s about once you’re there, it can mean chasing down the creator and asking lots of questions. A good description means the assignee can start work straight away and get it done faster.

A description can include rich text, code snippets, images, tables, synced blocks, and more. The editor converts things like links, code, and markdown on-the-fly, so you can paste in your content and let the editor do the work.

Common markdown formatting options:
  • ## for H2 style (we support H2–H5)
  • bold for bold
  • italic for italic
  • ``` for a code block
  • this is link text for this is link text
    • for bulleted lists (like this one)
    1. for numbered lists
  • [] for action items
Mention your teammates

If you need someone to know about a work item, but you don’t plan to assign it to them, you can mention them in it. Type @ followed by their name, then choose the right person from the list. The person you mention will be notified and can quickly jump to the work item to see what’s happening.

Add a code snippet

Code snippets let you format source code with numbered rows and syntax highlighting based on the language you choose. In Jira, new code blocks added to descriptions are wrapped by default.

There are several ways to add a code snippet to your work item’s description:

  • Select Code snippet from the main toolbar.
  • Type /code to quickly add the element from the slash command.
  • Type three back ticks (```) to create a code block.
  • Type text between two back ticks (for example,some text) to create inline code. Select a code block to change its appearance and formatting. You can change the auto-detected programming language, unwrap code, and hide or show line numbers.
Add a synced block

You can create a source block in a Jira work item description. You can add this block to other work items, or Confluence live docs and pages as a view-only element.

Synced blocks support text, layouts, tables, images, cards, and just about any other editor element.

  • While editing within a work item description, type /sync or select + on the toolbar.
  • Select Create synced block.
  • Enter anything you want to reuse in other work items.
Improve description using AI (beta)

AI is available and automatically enabled for all apps on Standard, Premium, and Enterprise plans. Organization admins can manage AI preferences by selecting Rovo, then Rovo access in Atlassian Administration.

AI is not available in Atlassian Government organizations. For Sandbox environments, you must manually activate it.

AI can assist in generating work item descriptions when you simply paste Confluence links into Jira. By using the context from the Confluence link placed in the description field of the work item, AI creates structured content to improve the description.

To generate work item descriptions:

  • Paste a Confluence link in a work item’s description field. If a Confluence link is already present, edit the description field.
  • Select Improve description. The improved description will stream directly into your editor and is automatically applied. If you’re not happy with the result, select Undo. You can also use Cmd + Z on Mac or Ctrl + Z on Windows to revert to your original description.
Attach files and images

To attach a file to a work item, open the work item and drop the file on it. Alternatively, from the quick-add buttons under the work item summary, select Add and then Attachment. You can also drop or attach files in comments and other long text fields.

Files, Confluence pages and live docs, and Loom videos all appear together in a single Attachments section. Switch between list and grid views, and filter by type (All, Images, Videos, Documents) to find what you need faster.

To link to files from services like Dropbox and Google Drive, paste a link to the file in the work item description, comments, or any long text field. We’ll add a smart link that’ll always refer to the latest version of the file.

Attached files haves some conditions:

  • File names can’t contain any of these characters: \ / \ " % : $ ? *.
  • By default, the maximum size of any one file is 10MB, but your Jira admin can change this limit. The Free plans for Jira Cloud and Jira Service Management have a file storage limit of 2GB per app. The Standard plan allows up to 250 GB per app, and file storage is unlimited on Premium plans. Find out more
Link to Confluence content or a Loom video

To link a Confluence page or live doc, or add a Loom video, select Add attachment in the Attachments section. From here you can upload a file, link existing 1P content by searching or pasting a URL, or create a new Confluence page/live doc or Loom video.

Find and link related Confluence content using AI

AI is available and automatically enabled for all apps on Standard, Premium, and Enterprise plans. Organization admins can manage AI preferences by selecting Rovo, then Rovo access in Atlassian Administration.

AI is not available in Atlassian Government organizations. For Sandbox environments, you must manually activate it.

Use AI to effortlessly find and link related Confluence content to your work item. This allows you to have all key information at your fingertips and helps you to fully understand the work context needed to make progress.

This feature searches through your site’s Confluence, taking into account all access permissions, and presents a curated list of related content to link to the work item.

To find and link Confluence content using AI:

  • Open a work item.
  • Select Improve work item in the work item’s details section.
  • Select Link Confluence content. AI finds and shows a list of Confluence links.
  • Select Link for individual links or Link all to link all related Confluence content at once.
Link a work item

There may be existing work items that relate to the one you’re working on, and their details can help add more context. When you link two work items together, they each appear on the other’s work item view below the work item description. Linking work items doesn’t change the work items in any other way.

To link a work item:

  • Open a work item and from the quick-add buttons under the work item summary, select Add.
  • Select Linked work item.
  • Choose the relationship (“is blocked by” or “relates to,” for example).
  • Search for and select the work item to link.
  • Choose Link. To create a new linked work item, select + Create linked work item and enter the details of the new work item, including the relationship (“is blocked by” or “relates to,” for example).

Once a work item is linked, it will display in the Linked work items panel on each work item. You can also search for work items that are linked to a particular work item. More about advance searching in Jira.

Link similar work items using AI

AI is available and automatically enabled for all apps on Standard, Premium, and Enterprise plans. Organization admins can manage AI preferences by selecting Rovo, then Rovo access in Atlassian Administration.

AI is not available in Atlassian Government organizations. For Sandbox environments, you must manually activate it.

Use AI to automatically find and surface work items similar to yours from your space, saving you time and effort. Linking similar work items makes it easier for your team to reference prior work, understand complexity, and provide your team with the context they need to plan and code with confidence.

To find and link similar work items using AI:

  • Open the work item.
  • Select Improve task, then Link similar work item.
  • In the Link similar work items panel, select Show results.
  • Select Link as related to link work items with a “relates to” relationship type. You can change the relationship type by selecting the Link as menu. Once a work item is linked, it will display in the Linked work items panel on each work item.
Link to a web URL

Give a work item context from anywhere on the web by linking the URL. Copy and paste any link and you’ll be able to see the work.

To link a web URL:

  • Open a work item and from the quick-add buttons under the work item summary, select Add.
  • Select Web link.
  • Type or copy the web URL and the Link text.
  • Choose Link. You can do this with your keyboard via Jira’s command palette. Use command + K (for Mac) or Ctrl + K (for Windows) to open the command palette while you’re in Jira.More about Jira’s command palette.
Add content from Marketplace apps

If you’re a Jira admin, you can find and try new Atlassian Marketplace apps right from the work item view. Select the Apps quick-add button under the work item summary and choose Add apps.

Work item content helps describe a work item in ways a description and other details can’t. If your Jira site has installed Atlassian Marketplace apps, you can add content via the quick-add buttons under the work item summary. Diagrams and charts are two common types of content that can help describe a work item, but there are many other options on the Marketplace.

More about Atlassian Marketplace apps.

To the right of the Add quick-add button, you’ll find the Apps button, which lists the actions you can take in any of the installed apps you have permission to use. Select Apps and then follow any required steps to add your content.

Once you select the quick-add button, you can add content from the app to your work item. This way, you can ensure everyone’s seeing the latest version of a file.

Choose when subtasks and linked work items have a strikethrough

Choose when subtasks and linked work items have a strikethrough

This page only applies to company-managed spaces.

When does a strikethrough appear on the work item?

A strikethrough will appear across the work item key of child work items (e.g. subtasks) and linked work items when they have a resolution. By default, workflows are set up so that when a work item is moved to a status in the Done category, a resolution is automatically set. This means that moving a work item to Done will make a strikethrough appear on the work item.

Admins can make sure a strikethrough only appears when someone manually sets a resolution.

Ensure a strikethrough only appears when someone manually sets a resolution

You must be an admin to edit a workflow.

To ensure a strikethrough only appears when someone manually sets a resolution:

  • Go to Settings (), then Work items.
  • Select Workflows, then Edit your selected workflow.
  • In the Diagram tab, select a transition to a Done status. Done statuses are green.
  • Select Post Functions.
  • Hover over The Resolution of the work item will be … and select Edit ().
  • For the Field Value, select None.
  • Select Update.
  • Repeat steps 3 to 7 for all transitions to Done statuses.
  • Publish your workflow. Alternatively, you can delete the The Resolution of the work item will be … part of the transition to achieve the same result.

Tip: Clear the resolution when a work item is reopened

You can also set the Resolution to None for To Do and In Progress statuses. This will make sure that your resolution is cleared if your team ever needs to work on a work item again.

Configure field layout in the work item

Configure field layout in the work item

We’re rolling out some changes to the work item as an open beta. Some documentation may not yet reflect these updates, and the new experience might not be enabled on your site. Read more about the upcoming changes

Choosing which fields appear on your team’s work item, and which of those fields are most important, can help your team get more done in less time. The work item design enables great flexibility in where you place your fields. If there are a few fields you fill out for every bug, for example, it makes sense that those fields are always visible and somewhere near the top of the work item. Space admins can set up the work item for spaces to work best with their team.

Work item layout settings are for individual spaces. You can’t share layout settings between spaces right now. But you can copy a work item layout to other spaces that use the same screen. Read more about copying a work item layout to other spaces.

Your Jira admin creates fields across your Jira site. And, they make those fields available to space admins through Jira’s administration settings and space configuration schemes. Read more about how Jira admins create fields.

Space admins can configure how these fields look in their spaces by setting up their layout. When configuring the layout, there are three sections: description fields, context fields, and hidden fields.

Description fields

This section usually appears on the left side of the work item (or at the top in a single-column layout). Since this is the first place users look when they open a work item, put your most important fields here. If your layout’s screen is configured with more than one tab, the other tabs will appear in this section. Only Jira admins can configure tabs (space admins can’t change the order of the fields displayed in the tab). Read more about configuring a screen’s tabs and fields.

Context fields

This section normally appears down the right side of the work item (or at the bottom in a single-column layout) in the Details and More fields groups. Context fields usually contain secondary information that your team might need to sort, filter, or report on work items. Each user can customize context fields to work for them by pinning their most used ones to the top of a work item in the Pinned fields group. Read more about pinning fields.

Hide when empty

The context fields section has a divider you can use to sort always-important fields from sometimes-important ones. Fields above the hide when empty are shown in the Details group and those below the line are hidden under the More fields group when they don’t have a value. When a field in the More fields group has a value, it moves to the Details group.

Hidden fields

This section is for fields that you don’t want to appear on the work item at all. When configuring the layout for a work item type, drag fields to the right side of the screen and drop them in the Hidden fields section.

Configure field layout
  • Open a work item. From the sidebar, select Configure (), then Work item view.
  • Add, remove, and drag fields in the field categories until you’re happy with the setup.
  • Choose Save changes. If a group of work types — tasks and subtasks, for example — use the same view work item screen, which they do by default, you’ll configure the fields for those work types all together as a set.

More about configuring screen schemes for work types

Add fields and create field tabs

Only site admins can do the things described in this section.

The available fields for a work item type are the ones added in the global screen configuration for viewing that work type. To add more existing fields to a work item type, or create and manage field tabs, you need to visit that global configuration screen. More about configuring screens

  • Open a work item. From the sidebar, select Configure (), then Work item view.
  • Select the link to the appropriate screen configuration at the top of the page. (If there are existing tabs in the configuration, you can also select the tab name and then Edit fields & tabs).
  • Add (or remove) the desired fields.
  • Add, remove, and edit the field tabs. Once you have tabs configured, they’ll appear in the description section on the left side of a work item. Select the tab to see its fields.

You can easily add new fields.Open a work item. From the Details section, select Edit fields (), then Create fields.

Copy a work item layout to other spaces

Copy a work item layout to other spaces

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

This feature is currently rolling out and may not be available in your instance yet.

Save time on space configuration by copying a screen’s work item layout to other spaces that use the same screen. For example, if you’ve configured the Customer default screen in one space and want the same layout for the Customer default screen in another space, you can copy the former layout to the latter. Work item layouts can only be copied on a screen-by-screen basis. More about managing screens

Copying a work item layout only copies the layout (which fields are visible, which section of the work item they’re displayed, and what order they’re displayed in). It doesn’t copy the content in any field.

You must be a Jira admin to copy a work item layout to other spaces.

Copying a work item layout will override layouts in the applied spaces.

To copy a work item layout to other spaces:

  • From your space’s sidebar, select Space settings, then Work items, then Layout.
  • Select a work item layout.
  • Select Copy work item layout in the top right. Only Jira admins can see this button.
  • Choose which screen’s layout you want to copy, then the spaces you want to apply it to. The spaces available will be those that use the same screen as the layout to copy.
  • Select Next.
  • Review your selection, then select Copy layout if you want to make the changes. Copying a work item layout doesn’t create a link between layouts. This means that you can always change a space’s individual layouts later without affecting another space that uses the same screen.
