What is work item ranking in your plan?

What is work item ranking in your plan?

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Along with functions like dependencies, you can indicate the order in which your work is to be completed by ranking work items. In order to rerank work items on your timeline, you need to sort work items by Rank. Read more about sorting work items

Your plan displays a work item’s ranking in the Work Item column under #. Ranking only applies to the highest hierarchy level displayed in your plan; child work items are unaffected by this order.

To change the ranking of work items in your plan, move a work item to a new row by either dragging and dropping it to its new place, or by selecting it and choosing Move from the Bulk actions menu that appears. Find out how to edit multiple work items in bulk on your timeline.

Manage and update work in a list

Create and edit work items in your list

Create and edit work items in your list

You must have the following to do the things described on this page.

Permission: Create work items, Edit work items

Create a work item in your list

To create a work item in the list view, you can:

  • Select the + Create button at the bottom of the list.
  • Give your work item a name based on what work needs to be done.
  • Select the work type you’d like to create from the dropdown (if your space has more than one work type). All work types associated with your space will be included, except those that require a parent.
  • Press return (Mac) or Enter (Windows) on your keyboard to finalize. If you have grouping applied when you create your work item, the work item will inherit attributes of the grouping. For example, let’s say you’ve grouped your list by status. When you create a work item with the grouping applied, that work item will have the status of the section you’ve created the work item in.
Quickly edit a work item

In the list view, you can quickly and easily make changes to your work items without having to open them individually.

To edit a work item in your list, select the field you’d like to edit, then:

  • If it’s text, start typing and press return (Mac) or Enter (Windows) when you’re finished.

  • If it’s a selection, select a value from the dropdown menu. Your changes will be applied instantly. To edit a work item using only a keyboard:

  • To enter a value and move focus to the field on the right, press tab.

  • To enter a value and move focus to the field below, press return (Mac) or Enter (Windows). Rovo can action some work item updates for you. For example, you could ask Rovo to update all your assigned work from To Do to In Progress, add comments, or update summaries, descriptions, assignees, and more. Open Rovo Chat and enter /update-work-items to try it out. Some fields may not yet be supported.

View and edit work items in more detail

To view a work item in more detail, select its work item key in the Work column. This appears as a string of letters and numbers, for example, ABC-123.

The work item will open in a preview panel, where you can view its description, status, assignee, and other information in more detail, and make any changes.

Manage child work items in your list

A work item can have child work items that can be assigned and tracked individually. If you have a task with a related subtask, that task would be considered a parent work item while the subtask would be a child work item.

Change the parent of a child work item

From the list, you can change the parent of a child work item by dragging and dropping it underneath a new parent.

Another way to change the parent is to open the child work item, then select the work type icon in the top-left corner next to the work item key of the parent.

In the list view, you can only see up to 500 child work items under a parent. Similarly, if a child work item has a parent that belongs to a different space, it won’t display in the list view.

Customize your list by adding or removing fields

Customize your list by adding or removing fields

Select which fields to display in your list
  • All users with access to the space can select which columns to display in their list.
  • If you add, remove, or rearrange the columns in the list view, these changes aren’t saved if you refresh, your cache expires, or you open the same space in an incognito or private window. Every team has different needs, so you may want to add or remove fields as columns so only the most important information is displayed in your list. You can select other columns you’d like to include in your list. However, you’ll always see the type, key, and summary fields.

The columns are based on your space’s configuration. The columns you choose to display in your list is only visible to you.

To customize the columns you see in your list:

  • In the column header section, select Configure columns ().
  • Choose a field from the dropdown to add it as a column in your list.
    • Company and team managed spaces: if the field is already associated to at least one work type in the space → the field will be added as a column to the work item list view.
    • Team managed spaces only: if the field is not associated to any work types in the space → the field will be added as a column to the list view and automatically associated to all work types in the space.
Remove a column from your list

To remove or hide a column from your list:

  • Hover over the column you want to hide.
  • Select More actions ().
  • Select Remove column.
Add custom fields to your list

You can currently add the following custom fields to your list:

  • Short text
  • Paragraph
  • Labels
  • Number
  • Checkbox
  • Date picker
  • Date time picker
  • Single select
  • Select List (multiple choices)
  • Sprint
  • Story point estimate
  • URL
  • Comments
  • People field (team-managed space only)
  • Formula
  • Single user picker (company-managed space only)
  • Multi user picker (company-managed space only) Find out about adding custom fields to your space

Delete a work item from your list

Delete a work item from your list

You must have the following to do the things described on this page.

Permission: Delete work items

To delete a work item from the list view:

  • Use the checkbox to select the work item you’d like to delete.

  • Select Delete.

  • Select Delete again to confirm. Alternatively, you can:

  • Open the work item you’d like to delete by selecting its key.

  • Select More actions (•••), then Delete.

  • Select Archive if you want to archive the work item, or enter Delete in the text box to confirm that you want to delete it.

  • Select Delete to confirm. You can perform this action with your keyboard via Jira’s command palette. Use command + K (for Mac) or Ctrl + K (for Windows) to open the command palette while you’re in Jira. Read more about Jira’s command palette

Filter, sort, copy, and rank work items in the list

Filter, sort, copy, and rank work items in the list

All users with access to the project can:

  • Filter their work items
  • Copy their work items
  • Change the order of their work items
  • Reorder their list fields
Filter your list view

Use Filter to filter work items in your list view. More about using filters

Sort your list view alphabetically

When you sort your list view, child work items will stay with their parent. The work type icons will be nested below each other, so you can clearly see how the items relate to each other.

To sort the list view alphabetically:

  • Hover over the field (column) header.
  • Select More actions (), then select Summary.
  • Select either Sort A to Z or Sort Z to A.
Reorder the fields in your list

Everyone visualizes their work differently, so you may want to customize the list view. Arrange your list so you can view the information that’s most important to you first.

To reorder the fields in your list:

  • Hover your cursor over the field (column) header.
  • Select More actions ().
    • Select Move column to first position to move it to the first column after the Work column.
    • Select Move column to left to move it one position to the left.
    • Select Move column to right to move it one position to the right.
    • Select Move column to last position to move it to the end. The Work column will always be in the first position and can’t be moved.
Search the list

Use keywords from your work item summary, or description to search in the list view. Enter the keyword and all work items containing those keywords will be shown. You can also search by entering the whole work item key.

Hide work items marked as ‘Done’

Anyone with access to the project can hide work items marked as ‘Done’ or with the done status category:

  • Navigate to the list view in your project.
  • Select More actions () at the top-right of your list view.
  • Switch on the toggle to Hide done items. Once you’ve hidden the done items, it will only appear for you. Those with access to the same project will need to hide it for themselves if they don’t want to see them.
Manually sort your work in the list view

To manually sort and reorder work items in the list view:

  • Set the sort order to Rank in the List view. To do this, open the JQL tab for the List view and update the query to include ORDER BY Rank. In some sites, the Rank field may appear as cf[10019] (a custom field ID for Rank). This ID can be different in your Jira site, so use whichever custom field is configured as your Rank field.
  • After this set-up, you’ll be able to drag to re-order work items in your list. Learn more about ordering by Rank.

How do I view my list?

The list is enabled by default in all spaces.

To view your list (assuming it’s enabled), navigate to your space, then select List in the space navigation.

Only space admins can enable and disable features in a space.

To disable the list:

  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Features.
  • Next to List, select the toggle to enable or disable the feature. You can re-enable the list at any time from Space settings.

Link and unlink goals to work items in your Jira list

Link and unlink goals to work items in your Jira list

To use goals in your Jira space, you’ll need to either have an existing Atlas workspace or sign up to our Platform Experiences early access program (EAP).

You can link goals to work items within Jira spaces and track how your work contributes to your team and organization’s goals.

Create a goal in your list

To link a goal to a work item in your list:

  • Navigate to the list view of your Jira space.
  • Check that you have the Goals field enabled. How to add or remove fields in your list
  • Under the Goals field, select the corresponding cell for the work item you want to create a goal for.
  • Select Add goal then + Create.
  • Give your new goal a name, assign an owner, then select Create.
Link a goal to a work item in your list

To link a goal to a work item in your list:

  • Navigate to the list view of your Jira space.
  • Check that you have the Goals field enabled. How to add or remove fields in your list
  • Under the Goals column, select the corresponding cell for the work item you want to link a goal to.
  • There are two ways to link a goal:
    • Search for a goal, then press Enter on your keyboard.
    • Paste a link to a goal, then select Add.
Unlink a goal from a work item in your list

To unlink a goal from a work item in your list:

  • Navigate to the list view of your Jira space.
  • Under the Goals column, select the corresponding cell for the goal you want to unlink.
  • Hover over the goal then select to unlink it from the work item.

Manage multiple work items in your list

Manage multiple work items in your list

You must have the following to do the things described on this page.

Permission: Edit work items, Delete work items

You can edit and delete multiple work items in the list view at once. Managing your list in a few clicks allows you and your team to work more efficiently.

Edit multiple work items

You can edit up to 1,000 work items at once.

To edit multiple work items in the list view:

  • Select multiple work items in the list. You can either:
    • use the work item checkboxes,
    • hold command (Mac) or Ctrl (Windows) while selecting work items, or
    • hold the Shift key to select a group of adjacent work items.
  • Once you’ve chosen the work items you’d like to edit, select Edit from the toolbar that appears. This will open the bulk edit sidebar.
  • Choose what you’d like to do with the fields shared across the selected work items by clicking into the field and making direct edits. You can also search for additional fields you may want to edit using the search bar. Some fields may require you to choose from a handful of options. The options depend on the type of field, but may include:
    • Keep as is - Make no changes to that field across the selected work items
    • Add new - Add new values to what’s already there across the selected work items
    • Find and remove - Remove a specific value from the field across the selected work items
    • Replace all - Replace the existing content for that field across all selected work items
    • Remove all - Remove all values from the field across the selected work items
  • When you’re done editing, select Next to review your changes on a confirmation screen.
  • Select Confirm to save your edits.
Delete multiple work items

You can delete up to 1,000 work items from the list view at once.

To delete multiple work items:

  • Select multiple work items from the list. You can either:
    • use the work item checkboxes,
    • hold command (Mac) or Ctrl (Windows) while selecting work items, or

Organize your list

Organize your list

  • Anyone with access to the space can group work items in the list view
  • Your grouping and sorting will only be visible to you
  • Your grouping will persist when navigating between views and other spaces You can group the work items in your list by certain attributes to organize and visualize work in the way that suits you best. For example, you can check high-priority tasks to see that nothing is blocked, or see individual team members’ workloads at a glance.

All users are in control of how they want to view their work — so any group you create can only be seen by you. You can group your work by:

  • Assignee
  • Status
  • Sprint
  • Priority
  • Sprint
  • Story points
  • Category
  • Reporter
  • Labels
  • Resolution
  • Work type
  • Version types
  • Select type fields
  • Group picker
  • Goals
Group work items

To group work items in the list view:

  • Select Group at the top of the list.
  • Select the attribute you want to group work items by.
Clear the group

To clear the grouping:

  • Select Group at the top of the list.
  • Select Clear selection.

What is the list?

What is the list?

Jira’s list sorts all your space’s work into a single list that can be quickly scanned and sorted by field. You can also use the list to create, edit, and view work items in your space.

The columns in your list

Understand what each column in your list means:

Type: This column indicates the type of work item in your list. Jira enables you to keep track of different types of work — bugs, tasks, subtasks, etc — by using different work types. The default work types depend on how your space has been set up by your space admin and which Jira template you’re using in your instance. More about work types.

Key: This column gives you a unique work item key. For example, this could look like TBT-12.

Summary: This column shows the summary of the work item in your list. This should provide an overview of the task at hand.

Priority: This column indicate the relative priority of the work item.

Labels: This column indicates additional information that can help categorize work item.

Created: This column shows the date that the work item was first created.

Updated: This column shows the date that anyone last updated the work item.

Status: This column shows what stage each work item is up to in your workflow.

Original estimate: This columns allows you to estimate the amount of time this work item will take to be completed.

Story point estimate: This column shows the amount of effort needed to complete a task compared to other work. More about story points

Sprint: This column shows which sprint the work item is currently in or was completed in. More about sprints

Assignee: This column indicates to whom this work item is assigned.

Team: This column shows which team is assigned to a work item.

Parent: This column shows the parent work item that a child work item lives under.

Due date: This column indicates when the work item is due.

Reporter: This column indicates who has created the work item.

Comments: This column allows you to comment on the work item by opening the comments field in the sidebar. More about comments

Fix version: This column shows the version where you plan on releasing a feature or bug fix. See more about releases and versions

Single version: This column shows which version the work item is in.

Affects version: This column shows the version where a bug or problem was found.

Development: This column shows the development status of the work item, linked from a compatible development tool. See more about development

Goals: This column shows any goal a work item contributes to. How to link and unlink goals to work items

Manage and visualize your software space on the timeline

Add your timeline to a Confluence Cloud page

Add your timeline to a Confluence Cloud page

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

You can add your team’s timeline to a Confluence Cloud page using the Jira Timeline macro. A timeline on a Confluence Cloud page updates in real-time, and users with adequate permissions can interact with it the same way that they interact with it in Jira.

To insert your timeline into a Confluence Cloud page:

  • From your timeline, copy the URL from your browser.
  • Go to the Confluence Cloud page on which you want to add your timeline, and enter edit mode by selecting the Edit icon or using keyboard shortcut E.
  • Paste your link in the place where you want it to appear on your Confluence Cloud page. Confluence Cloud automatically adds the Jira Timeline macro and displays your timeline.
  • Publish your page. Alternatively, you can summon the Jira Timeline plugin in Confluence Cloud using either the keyboard shortcut “/timeline” or by selecting Jira Timeline from the macro menu (+) at the top of the editor. From there, you can manually add the Jira instance URL, then choose your project and board.

Change color of work item schedule bars on your timeline

Change color of work item schedule bars on your timeline

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

On the timeline, you can change the color of parent work item’s schedule bar, which is then applied to all of its child work items. Planners often use this feature to highlight trends or emphasize pieces of work on the timeline. For example, you might want to make regular “Keeping the lights on” tasks a different color from feature work.

To change the color of schedule bars from the sidebar of the work item:

  • Select the work item schedule bar to open the sidebar.

  • Next, select the colored square next to the summary of the work item to open the picker.

  • Choose your color, and your change is automatically applied. To change the color directly from the schedule bar:

  • Right click on the schedule bar (or hold control before clicking).

  • Choose a color from the menu.

Change how many completed work items show on your software space’s timeline

Change how many completed work items show on your software space’s timeline

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

Give your space context by showing work items up to one year old, or show no completed work items to live in the moment. By default, your timeline shows work that’s been completed within the last 12 months.

To change how many completed parent-level work items show on your timeline, go to the View settings menu, then select Show completed. You’ll then have the option to choose the timeframe you’d like to show on your timeline.

This setting only applies to parent-level work items. Story-level work items that are done but belong to an open parent-level work item will still show on your timeline.

How your timeline defines completed work items

Jira looks at two different fields to evaluate whether a work item is done:

  • In company-managed spaces, it looks at the work item’s Resolution field, set via a post function when an work item is moved from an In Progress to Done status. Learn about Jira’s resolution field and configuring post functions.
  • In team-managed spaces, it looks at the category of the work item’s status. Work items are considered resolved when they’re moved from an In Progress to Done status category. Your timeline refers to the Status category change date to define completed work items. This ensures that your plan always refers to the same field and is consistent across multiple workflows.

Create or remove dependencies on your timeline

Create or remove dependencies on your timeline

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

You must have the following to do the things described on this page.

Permission: Link work items

Dependencies, also called Work item links in other parts of Jira, allow you to show the order in which work items need to be done. If there’s a dependency between two work items, one must be finished before the next can begin.

In order to use this feature, a Jira admin needs to enable work item linking. The timeline can only show work items with the Blocks work item link type and link work items from a single space. How to enable work item linking

Create a dependency

To create a dependency directly on your timeline:

  • Hover over the work item’s schedule bar to reveal dots on either side, as shown above.

  • Drag one of the dots to the work item you want to link. The timeline automatically configures the order of the dependency (blocks or is blocked by) based on the order in which work items are scheduled. To create a dependency from the side work item view panel:

  • Highlight a work item on the timeline to open the side info panel.

  • Select the icon to open the link menu, then choose Link work item.

  • Select either blocks or is blocked by, then select the work item to link.

View dependency details

To view dependency details, select the line between dependent items.

Remove a dependency

To remove a dependency between two work items:

  • Select the line linking the work items you want to separate to open the the dependency view window.
  • Select the icon to remove the dependency.

Create work items on the timeline

Create work items on the timeline

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

You must have the following to do the things described on this page.

Permission: Create work items

The timeline view uses your space’s board as its work item source. As you create work items in your space, they’re automatically added to your timeline. You can also make new work items directly on your timeline.

Create a parent work item
  • In software spaces, select Create Epic at the bottom of the work items column. In business spaces, select Create.
  • Give your work item a name.
  • Select the work type you’d like to create from the dropdown (if your space has more than one work type). All work types associated with your space will be included, except those that require a parent.
  • Press return (Mac) or Enter (Windows) on your keyboard to finalize. The default parent work type in Jira is Epic, which is what we use in this documentation. However, this is a dynamic value based on how your administrator configures the parent work item type. For example, if your space uses feature as the parent work type, you’ll see Create Feature.
Insert a work item on the timeline

If you want to place a work item directly between two existing work items on your timeline, hover on the line between them and select the blue + that appears:

Manage child work items on the timeline

A work item can have child work items that can be assigned and tracked individually. If you have a task with a related subtask, that task would be considered a parent work item while the subtask would be a child work item.

Create a child work item

To create a child work item from the timeline view:

  • Hover over the parent work item and select + to create a child work item.
  • Enter a summary of what needs to be done.
  • Press return (Mac) or Enter (Windows) on your keyboard to finalize.
Change the parent of a child work item

From the timeline, you can change the parent of a child work item by dragging and dropping it underneath a new parent.

Another way to change the parent is to open the child work item, then select the work type icon in the top-left corner next to the work item key of the parent.

Enable and disable the timeline

Enable and disable the timeline

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

The timeline view is only available in Jira Cloud. It’s not available in Jira Data Center.

The timeline view is enabled by default in all newly created software spaces. Find out where to find your timeline and how to access it.

If you don’t see a timeline in your space, your administrator needs to enable it. This process varies based on whether you’re working in a company-managed or team-managed space.

To enable or disable the roadmap function in company-managed spaces:

  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.

  • Select Timeline from the list, then turn the toggle off to disable the timeline feature for your space. To enable or disable the timeline function in team-managed spaces:

  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.

  • Select Features.

  • In the Timeline section, turn the toggle off to disable the timeline feature for your space. Another way to enable the timeline view is by:

  • Select Add to navigation (+).

  • Select Timeline.

  • Select the Add to navigation button.

Enable your plan

Your plan is only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

More about Advanced Roadmaps and how to get a free trial of Jira Cloud Premium

Enable planning for child work items on the timeline

Enable planning for child work items on the timeline

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

The ability to plan work using child-level work items (such as stories, bugs, and tasks) is not enabled by default. This is because work items on the timeline are scheduled using the Start date and Due date fields which might not align with everyone’s workflows.

Before enabling this feature, an administrator needs to add the Start date and Due date fields to the work item view for company-managed spaces (they’re shown by default in team-managed spaces). How to add these fields to your work item view.

Once allowed in your site, you can plan work items at the parent level used for larger pieces of work (epic by default in software spaces, level 1) and at the next level down in the hierarchy (often called stories, level 0) on your timeline. The timeline doesn’t show work items at the subtask level (level −1).

To enable planning for child work items on your timeline:

  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings. Alternatively, from your timeline, select More actions (•••), then select Configure Timeline from the upper right of your timeline view (next to view settings).
  • Make sure that Timeline is selected from the list, then toggle the switch for Child level child work item scheduling.
    • Those planning in scrum can also choose whether your timeline shows child child work items based on their sprint dates or using their exact start and end dates by selecting Visualize child child work items by sprints or Schedule child child work items by dates respectively. Once enabled you can now plan child-level child work items on your timeline.

How can I change my timeline view?

How can I change my timeline view?

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

The timeline comes with several built-in viewing options so you can tell (and read) the right story.

Add filters

Filters on your timeline are a handy way to focus on specific work items. You can use them to only show work items that relate to product work, or highlight your team’s “keep the lights on” tasks.

You can find filters at the top of your timeline.

They only show once the field is relevant to the work items in your plan. For example, you’ll only see the Type filter option when more than one work type is added to your plan, and label will only show when you have one or more labels assigned to work items. If a filter doesn’t show at the top of the screen, make sure the field you’re looking for contains a value.

These filters are different from a JQL filter in that they only hide them from the timeline view.

Find out about filters on your timeline.

Change how many completed issues show on your timeline

To change how many completed parent-level work items show on your timeline, go to the View settings menu, then select Show completed. You’ll then have the option to choose the timeframe you’d like to show on your timeline.

This setting only applies to parent-level work items. Story-level work items that are done but belong to an open parent-level work item will still show on your timeline.

Find out how Jira defines completed work items.

Enable dependencies on your timeline

To show or hide dependencies on your timeline:

  • From your timeline, navigate to the View settings menu at the top-right of your view.
  • Under the Visual details heading, enable Dependencies. Find out about dependencies and how they work.
Enable the progress bar on your timeline

Easily monitor the progress of your space from your timeline by enabling the progress bar. The bar that appears beneath the name of a parent work item indicates the progress of child work items. Find out about the progress bar.

To enable or disable the progress bar on your timeline:

  • From your timeline, navigate to the View settings menu at the top-right of your view.
  • Under the Visual details heading, enable Progress.
View sprints on your timeline

Sprints created in your Scrum space are automatically shown on your timeline along the top row. To edit or manage these sprints, navigate to the backlog view.

Define a date range

Use the timeframe selector in the bottom corner to zoom in and out on your timeline to view upcoming Weeks, Months, or Quarters.

Change the color of schedule bars

To change the color of schedule bars from the sidebar of the work item:

  • Select the work item schedule bar to open the sidebar.

  • Next, select the colored square next to the summary of the work item to open the picker.

  • Choose your color, and your change is automatically applied. To change the color directly from the schedule bar:

  • Right click on the schedule bar (or hold control before clicking).

  • Choose a color from the menu. Find out about how you can customize your schedule bars on your timeline.

Roll up dates on your timeline

Roll up dates on your timeline

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

If the Start date and/or Due date fields on a parent work item are empty, the timeline infers its duration based on the dates assigned to child work items. We refer to this as a roll-up. These dates automatically update as those of the child work items change, but are overridden by any manually set dates.

If your timeline is using these rolled-up dates, you’ll see an arrow icon when you hover on the schedule bars:

In order to roll up dates:

  • parent work items can’t have a start and/or end date set. Manually set start and/or due dates override any inferred values. Bear in mind that manually adjusting the length of a schedule bar via drag and drop assigns a date to your work item.
  • all child work items need to be scheduled with either start and end dates or sprints (for scrum teams).
Roll-up values for scrum teams

For scrum teams, you can choose to schedule child work items on your timeline according to the sprint to which they’re assigned or using their start and end dates. Learn how to change which dates your timeline shows child work items.

If you choose to schedule them according to sprint dates, the schedule bars align with the sprints at the top of your timeline.

If you choose to show them using start and end dates, their scheduling bars align with dates at the top of the timeline.

The date of each work item’s assigned sprint is used to roll up dates to parent-level work items. In the example below, the parent-level task Cheddar King infers its dates from the three child work items Fermentation, Develop flavor, and Find your inner cheese. These child work items are scheduled to last two sprints, so the parent work item is begins with the first sprint and the ends after the second.

Roll-up values for kanban teams

Since kanban work items are scheduled using the Start date and Due date fields, a roll-up on the timeline uses the earliest and latest scheduled dates to determine the duration of the parent.

Partial roll-ups

If the start or due date of a parent work item can’t be inferred, its schedule bar fades out in that direction. This is what’s called a partial roll-up, as shown below:

To fix a partial roll-up, make sure that all of your child work items have both start or due dates.

Schedule parent work items on your timeline

Schedule parent work items on your timeline

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

Parent work items on your timeline’s timeline are scheduled using the Start date and Due date, regardless of whether you’re planning for scrum or kanban teams.

Start date and Due date are shown by default in the work item of team-managed spaces, but need to be manually added for company-managed spaces. It’s required when planning for kanban teams, and also is a common cause of completed work items not showing on your timeline. Find out how to add these fields to your work item

When scheduling parent work items, you can manually set dates using either the dates fields or schedule bars. You can also choose to have a parent task inherit the dates of its children.

Schedule work items using the Start date and Due date fields
  • Ensure that the Start date and Due date fields are visible in your work item.
  • Select the work item that you wish to schedule from the Work items column, which will open the side info panel.
  • Find the Start date and Due date fields in the work item panel, and change the dates.
Schedule work items using the schedule bars
  • From your timeline view, place the schedule bar where you’d like. The default duration of work items depends on the timeframe setting on your timeline. If your timeline is set to:
    • Weeks - your work items will be 7 days long.
    • Months - your work items will be 14 days long.
    • Quarters - your work items will be 30 days long.
  • Drag either end of the schedule bar to change the start or end date. Alternatively, you can right-click on the schedule bar to open the Change dates menu, then select Remove start date, Remove due date, or Clear both dates.
Infer dates from child work items

If the Start date and/or Due date fields on a parent work item are empty, the timeline infers its duration based on the dates assigned to child work items. We refer to this as a roll-up. These dates automatically update as those of the child work items change, but are overridden by any manually set dates.

How to roll up dates on the timeline

Schedule work for kanban teams on your timeline

Schedule work for kanban teams on your timeline

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

By default, your timeline doesn’t show schedule bars for child issues when planning in Kanban. In order to use it, an administrator must first enable and configure it. Learn how to enable this feature in your roadmap.

On the timeline, issues belonging to Kanban teams are scheduled using the Start date and Due date fields. The schedule bars align to the dates in those fields, and these dates are also used when rolling up values to parent issues.

You can schedule kanban issues on your timeline in either of the following ways:

Schedule work items using the Start date and Due date fields
  • Ensure that the Start date and Due date fields are visible in your work item.
  • Select the work item that you wish to schedule from the Work items column, which will open the side info panel.
  • Find the Start date and Due date fields in the work item panel, and change the dates.
Schedule work items using the schedule bars
  • From your timeline view, place the schedule bar where you’d like. The default duration of work items depends on the timeframe setting on your timeline. If your timeline is set to:
    • Weeks - your work items will be 7 days long.
    • Months - your work items will be 14 days long.
    • Quarters - your work items will be 30 days long.
  • Drag either end of the schedule bar to change the start or end date. Alternatively, you can right-click on the schedule bar to open the Change dates menu, then select Remove start date, Remove due date, or Clear both dates.
Rearrange work items

To rearrange work items on your timeline view, simply drag and drop them into your desired locations. There are a couple of different reasons you might want to change your work item order:

  • you want to change an work item’s ranking relative to work items of the same type
  • you want to assign a child work item to a new parent These changes in your timeline are saved to your Jira work items in real-time.

Schedule work for scrum teams on your timeline

Schedule work for scrum teams on your timeline

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

For scrum teams, you can choose to schedule child work items on your timeline according to the sprint to which they’re assigned or using their start and end dates. Learn how to change which dates your timeline shows child work items.

If you choose to schedule them according to sprint dates, the schedule bars align with the sprints at the top of your timeline.

If you choose to show them using start and end dates, their scheduling bars align with dates at the top of the timeline.

Before you can use schedule work items by sprint, you first need to create sprints on the board associated with the timeline; you can’t create new sprints from the timeline view. Once created, the sprints appear at the top of your roadmap in chronological order, as shown above.

To schedule scrum child work items according to sprint dates on your timeline:

  • In your space, ensure that you’ve created sprints and assigned them dates. Once you’ve done this, they’ll automatically show on your timeline. Learn how to make sprints.
  • Hover over the timeline section based on when you’d like to schedule the work item. Faint blue drop zones will appear on the timeline, each corresponding to a sprint. If you have overlapping sprints, the work item will be assigned to the one that begins first.
  • Place the schedule bar in a blue drop zone, and Jira assigns the work item to that sprint. To schedule scrum child work items according to start and end dates on your timeline, drag and drop either end of a schedule bar to change its dates.
Change sprint assignment

There are multiple ways to change a work item’s assigned sprint on your timeline:

  • Drag and drop the schedule bar to another sprint zone.
  • Select the schedule bar from the timeline to open the work item, then change the sprint in the Sprint field.
  • Right-click on the child work item’s schedule bar to open the Change sprint menu, then select the parent work item to which you’d like to move it. You can also clear the sprint assignment from this menu.
Rearrange work items

To rearrange work items on your timeline view, simply drag and drop them into your desired locations. There are a couple of different reasons you might want to change your work item order:

  • you want to change an work item’s ranking relative to work items of the same type
  • you want to assign a child work item to a new parent These changes in your timeline are saved to your Jira work items in real-time.

Dependencies, also called Work item links in other parts of Jira, allow you to show the order in which work items need to be done. If there’s a dependency between two work items, one must be finished before the next can begin.

Timeline limits in Jira

Timeline limits in Jira

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

While the timeline view of your space is a useful tool for planning future work, there are limits on what it can show and requirements on how your project must be structured.

Only parent and standard work types show on your timeline

The timeline view in Jira only shows work items of the parent and standard types. Child work items without a parent won’t be shown on your timeline. The default parent work type is epic in software spaces, and the default standard types are story and task. Read about work types in Jira.

Subtasks, which are below standard, and any custom hierarchy levels above parent created by Jira Premium users won’t show on your timeline view. To view them on your timeline and to plan across multiple spaces, you’ll need to use your plan which is included as part of Jira Premium and Enterprise subscriptions. Read about higher hierarchy levels in plans.

All work items need to come from one space

Commonly, teams running a company-managed space create boards with a custom JQL query to monitor work items from multiple spaces. However, the timeline view in Jira only works with work items from the backlog associated with one space. If you’re using a custom JQL filter that draws in work items from multiple boards, adjust it to only include work items from one space. Find out how to adjust your JQL filter.

Cross-space planning is only possible in your plan, which is included with Jira Premium and Enterprise. Read how plans gives an overview of the work of multiple teams and spaces.

A parent-level work type must exist and be included in your space via JQL

Jira comes with a default work item hierarchy structure which includes a parent-level work type for larger pieces of work (epic by default in software spaces). Your administrator can create a custom hierarchy level and name it whatever your organization calls work at that level.

However, if this parent-level work type is hidden from the timeline’s work source, whether through accidentally deleting the work type or it’s filtered out through a JQL filter, you’ll see the same warning as above.

Your timeline cannot exceed 5,000 work items

Your timeline can’t show more than 5,000 work items in total, and the number of parent work items is capped at 500. The timeline won’t load if your space exceeds these limits.

Modify your board JQL to reduce the number of work items that show on your timeline.

Troubleshoot the timeline for company-managed spaces

Troubleshoot the timeline for company-managed spaces

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

This page includes solutions to problems commonly found in company-managed spaces.

Go here to see solutions to common problems related to team-managed spaces.

If you’re working in a company-managed space, here’s some common errors that you might encounter on your timeline:

  • My timeline says “Update your board JQL to continue”. How do I fix this?
  • Board filter exceeds work item limits
  • Your timeline contains corrupt work items
  • No parent work type in space
  • Parent work items don’t display on the timeline (Kanban)
  • My sprints aren’t showing on my timeline
  • Accidentally converted a child work type to a parent work type
  • Recently completed work items not showing on your timeline
  • I can’t see my timeline. Instead, it says “timelines are designed for a single space”
My timeline says “Update your board JQL to continue”. How do I fix this?

We’re making some changes to how JQL functions, which will be announced at a later date. Because of this, some timelines might break if the space isn’t explicitly defined in the board JQL.

This is an easy fix, however: a space admin needs to simply add space = "YourProjectKey" to the board JQL. After which, the timeline will come back.

Those affected will get an error on their timelines – even if the timeline previously worked.

Board filter exceeds work item limits

The timeline view of Jira can only show 5,000 work items at once with no more than 500 being at the parent level.

The timeline automatically excludes work items if they were:

  • moved to the Done status category more than a year ago

  • moved to the Done status category, and it has a due date from more than a year ago To only display work items created within the last year:

  • From your space, select Work items and filters, then Advanced search.

  • In the search bar, enter this query, but replace:

    • NAME with the name of your space
    • DATE with the dates you’d like to focus on space = NAME AND created >= DATE AND created <= DATE
Your timeline contains corrupt work items

A work item is considered corrupt if certain details, like the work type, status, status category, or rank settings are invalid. The details might have been missing when the work item was created or something might have gone wrong with a bulk import.

The timeline won’t display until the details in the corrupt work item are fixed.

To fix a corrupt work item, you must raise a support ticket. Our team will help fix the work item so you can continue using your timeline.

No parent work type in space

In order for a timeline to show, your space needs to have a work item configured as an epic work type. If this work type has been deleted from your space, the timeline won’t show.

To check whether your space has an epic work type configured:

  • Select , then Work items, then select Work types from the left menu.
  • In the Type column in the middle of the page, look for work items that are labeled as Epic.
  • If you don’t find one, you’ll need to configure an epic-type work item. See how to edit and create work types in Jira Alternatively, parent work items could be excluded from your JQL query. To resolve this, your board admin needs to edit the filter query in the Board settings to include parent work items.
Parent work items don’t display on the timeline (Kanban)

The timeline is based on the same JQL filters as your board. If you’re using a Kanban board, it’s likely that your board will have a JQL filter that prevents parent work items from displaying on the board. The query could look like this:

space = FOO and workType != Epic ORDER BY Rank

To display them on your timeline, an admin can remove the JQL query from the board filter, and add it to the Kanban board sub-filter instead.

To adjust your JQL filter:

  • If you’re not already there, navigate to your company-managed space.
  • Next to your board’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Board settings.
  • Select Edit filter query.
  • From your Filters settings, remove workType != Epic. Run the search, then save your changes.
  • Return to the General tab of your board settings. Find Filter, then select Kanban board sub-filter.
  • Edit the query by hovering over the text. Paste and workType != Epic clause into the field.
  • Select Update to save your changes.
My sprints aren’t showing on my Timeline

In order for a sprint to show along the top of your Timeline, it must be from the same backlog or board container as the Timeline. Sprints from other boards won’t show up.

The sprints also need to have dates set (such as closed sprints, active sprints, or a scheduled future sprint) that fall within the previous one year or the next two years. Anything outside this date range won’t be shown.

Accidentally converted a child work type to a parent work type

If you’ve mistakenly converted a standard work type to a parent work type, restore them to their original state with the following steps:

  • Create a new standard-level work type.
  • Delete the ‘wrong’ parent work type (the one that was converted).
  • As part of the work type deletion process, you’ll be asked to which new work type you’d like to move all your work items.
  • Select the new work type you created.
  • Rename this new work type to your old one, if you want to.
Recently completed work items not showing on your timeline

If Due date is hidden from your work items, recently completed work items might not be on your timeline. The first step is to confirm that your work items have the Due date fields enabled:

You must be an admin to use Find your field on the work item.

To find a field on the work item:

  • Open a work item.
  • Select more actions (···), then Find your field.
  • Search for the field you want to find.
  • Select the field. If the field is hidden, Jira generates a warning.

To surface non-default fields in your work items:

  • Navigate to Settings , then Work items.
  • Select Field Configurations from the column on the left, then select Configure.
  • Search for the field you want to add in the search box or find it in the list, then select Show. If it’s already visible in your site, this button will say Hide instead.
  • Finally, select Screens on the line of the field you want to add to your work items, then select the spaces to which you’d like to add this field.
  • When you’re done, scroll to the bottom and select Update.
I can’t see my timeline. Instead, it says “Timelines are designed for a single space”

Commonly, teams running a company-managed space create boards with a custom JQL query to monitor work items from multiple spaces. However, the timeline view in Jira only works with work items from the backlog associated with one space. If you’re using a custom JQL filter that draws in work items from multiple boards, adjust it to only include work items from one space. Find out how to adjust your JQL filter.

Cross-space planning is only possible in your plan, which is included with Jira Premium and Enterprise. Read how plans gives an overview of the work of multiple teams and spaces.

My timeline says “Update this space’s settings to use the timeline”

This happens when the field configuration used by the space doesn’t include the date fields.

Start Date and Due Date fields must be in the field configuration associated to your space.

To edit the field configuration:

  • Next to your space’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (), then Space settings.
  • In the sidebar, expand Work items, then select Fields.
  • Select Edit ().
  • On the field configuration page, select Add field.
  • Find the missing field in the list and select it to add it back to the configuration. How to manage field configurations in work items.

What are filters on the timeline?

What are filters on the timeline?

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

Filters on your timeline are a handy way to focus on specific work items. You can use them to only show work items that relate to product work, or highlight your team’s “keep the lights on” tasks.

You can find filters at the top of your timeline.

They only show once the field is relevant to the work items in your plan. For example, you’ll only see the Type filter option when more than one work type is added to your plan, and label will only show when you have one or more labels assigned to work items. If a filter doesn’t show at the top of the screen, make sure the field you’re looking for contains a value.

These filters are different from a JQL filter in that they only hide them from the timeline view.

You can choose to show or hide work items based on:

  • assignee
  • status
  • versions
  • type
  • label
  • component
  • keyword (using the search box)
  • goals
Custom filters

This feature is currently rolling out to cloud customers. Your site may not reflect these changes, or you might not see it in your site just yet.

You can also create your own filters to use on your timeline.

In company-managed spaces, you can use quick filters from your board to hide work items from your roadmap. Using this filter won’t remove the work items, it just hides them. More about quick filters in Jira Software.

In team-managedspaces, you can do the same thing using custom filters. As with quick filters on company-managed roadmaps, using a custom filter won’t remove the work items, it just hides them. More about custom filters in team-managed spaces.

What does the space timeline show?

What does the space timeline show?

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

The timeline view is valuable for creating and planning long-term projects. It visualizes data from your work items in a Gantt chart so that you can manage your team’s work within a single space.

A Timeline can only show work items from one space

Planning across multiple spaces is only possible in your plan, which is included with Jira Premium and Enterprise.

Find out how to plan work across multiple teams

The column on the left side of your timeline shows the work items in your plan. Parent work items, such as epics, have child work items nested underneath them. You can use the filters at the top of your timeline to show or hide work items based on specific criteria. More about filters.

The default parent work type in Jira is Epic, which is what we use in this documentation. However, this is a dynamic value based on how your administrator configures the parent work item type. For example, if your space uses feature as the parent work type, you’ll see Create Feature.

Each work item on your timeline shows:

  • Work type icon
  • Work item key
  • Work item summary
  • Progress bar (parent work items only). More about the progress bar.
  • Status of child work items (parent work items statuses only show when done)
  • Assignee (if applicable) Your timeline shows bars that represent the duration of scheduled work items. Parent work items are scheduled using dates, either those you manually set or those it infers from its child work items. More about scheduling parent work items on your roadmap.

Child work items in Scrum spaces can be scheduled using the dates of the sprints to which they’re assigned or by Start date and Due date fields. Child work items without a parent won’t appear on your timeline. More about scheduling child work items for Scrum teams.

Work items belonging to Kanban teams are scheduled using the Start date and Due date fields. More about scheduling child work items for Kanban teams.

By default, the top of the timeline shows dates. Use toggle in the bottom right corner to change between Weeks, Months, or Quarters. Along with the dates at the top of your plan, your timeline also shows sprints (scrum teams only) and releases associated with your space. More about releases on your roadmap.

The last two items in this corner of your timeline are theicon which brings up a legend and the icon to make your timeline take up the full screen.

In the example above, there’s lines connecting the timeline bars. These are Dependencies, also called Work item links in other parts of Jira, which allow you to show the order in which work items need to be done. If there’s a dependency between two work items, one must be finished before the next can begin. More about dependencies on your timeline.

Lastly, select a work item on your timeline to open the side panel that allows you to make changes to your work items without leaving the timeline.

Manage capacity in your plans

Capacity in scrum vs. kanban teams in your plan

Capacity in scrum vs. kanban teams in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Capacity for Scrum teams

When scheduling work for Scrum teams, capacity is calculated differently for time-based estimates and story points:

  • If you’re using time-based estimates, the sprint capacity is determined by taking the weekly capacity and multiplying by the number of weeks per iteration. For example, if your team’s capacity is 40 hours and your iterations last two weeks, your team’s sprint capacity will be 80 hours.
  • If you estimate in story points, no conversion is necessary since story points are defined per iteration. The capacity applies to the whole sprint. By default, this is set to 30 story points, though you can adjust this to meet your team’s needs. Find out how to change an iteration’s capacity.
Capacity for Kanban teams

Kanban teams can only use time-based estimates.

For Kanban teams, work is broken down into iterations which each last one week. You can set the weekly capacity of a Kanban team in either days or hours, but the length of the iteration cannot be changed.

Change iteration capacity from your plan

Change iteration capacity from your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

The capacity of your iterations can fluctuate for several reasons. Examples include public holidays, a sick team member, or team members spread across different projects. If you’re using time-based estimates, the default capacity is 200 weekly hours. If you’re using story points, the default setting is 30 story points per iteration.

The default length of iterations in your plan are inherited from each team’s settings. You can keep the sprint (and therefore your plan) accurate by editing its capacity via the sprint details flyout.

To change the capacity of a sprint from your timeline:

  • Enable capacity planning on your timeline.
  • Select a sprint to open the sprint capacity information window.
  • Select the number next to the Sprint capacity field and enter a new value.
  • Use the checkmark to confirm the change. This can be done for active and future sprints.

Enable capacity planning in your plan

Enable capacity planning in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

In order to use capacity planning in your plan:

  • work items need to use story points or hours/days as their estimation units
  • your plan needs to use boards as work sources
    • work drawn from spaces and filters won’t show capacity information
    • if your plan includes team-managed spaces, make sure sprints are turned on in those spaces
  • associate the teams in your plan with a board
  • (optional) create a sprint from your board soyour plan can infer future sprints based on it
    • See what other sprint states are in your plan Once you do that, you can view capacity on your timeline:
  • Navigate the View settings menu and group your work items by Team or Sprint.
  • Select the checkbox next to Show capacity on timeline.
Show capacity on your Program board

Capacity information is enabled by default on the Program board, provided you’ve added your sprints as part of your board’s configuration. See the steps to add sprints to your Program board.

How your plan assigns capacity

How your plan assigns capacity

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

To use capacity planning in your plan, you need to enable it and your plan needs to meet certain criteria.

Find how to enable capacity planning in your plan.

To count against the capacity of an iteration, work items need to have values in all three of these fields:

  • Team
  • Sprint
  • Estimation (hours/days or story points) As you assign estimated work items to a team’s sprints, your plan subtracts the estimation values from the total capacity of the iteration. Find out how to change the capacity of your iterations.
Scheduled work items without a sprint value

Work items assigned to a team and scheduled during their sprint consume capacity regardless of whether you add a value to the Sprint field. The label x work items not assigned to sprint in the sprint capacity detail window refers to these work items. Find out more about the sprint capacity detail window.

Scheduled work items without an estimation

Work items assigned to a team and sprint without an estimation show next to the label x unestimated work items in the sprint capacity detail window. Find out more about the sprint capacity detail window.

How your plan distributes capacity

Your plan assumes that each team member can work on one story-level work item at a time. With that in mind, it distributes a work item’s estimate based on capacity of one team member, which it calculates this using the following equation, assuming the capacity of each team member is equal:

  • [team’s capacity per iteration]/[number of people in a team] = [capacity of one team member] It consumes one team member’s capacity for an iteration, then moves onto the next team member, repeating the process until the work is assigned. If there is still more work to do, a new iteration is started and the process continues until all the work items have been allocated.

For example, if a team of five has a capacity of 20 story points, your plan calculates an individual team member’s capacity to be four points per iteration (20/5=4). With that determined, your plan then distributes a story-level work item with a value of 10 story points over three iterations as follows:

  • iteration 1: four points
  • iteration 2: four points
  • iteration 3: two points However, the capacity distribution algorithm in your plan honors any manually configured end dates that you set for a work item more than capacity. If the scheduled duration of the work item isn’t enough for the individual team member’s capacity to handle, your plan distributes the capacity as outlined above until the iteration where the work item is due. In the last iteration, your plan allocates all remaining estimate values in order to make your deadline.

If the example above was estimated at 16 story points (instead of 10) and had a due date at the end of the third iteration, your plan distributes the capacity as follows:

  • iteration 1: four points
  • iteration 2: four points
  • iteration 3: eight points To change this behavior, revise the end dates of your work items as to not exceed the capacity of your team members, or adjust your work item’s estimate. You might also break down your work into smaller tasks and assign it to multiple people.
How the Auto-scheduler distributes capacity

While these are the base concepts of capacity distribution, the Auto-scheduler has more a complicated logic when planning across multiple iterations. Read more about the Auto-Scheduler.

Capacity on the Timeline

Your plan shows tabs along the top of each team’s swimlane that correspond to an iteration. As issues consume capacity, the green vertical bar rises and turns red when the amount of work assigned exceeds capacity.

The calendar view doesn’t show capacity information; it only shows the sprint’s information.

What are capacity and velocity in your plan?

What are capacity and velocity in your plan?

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Capacity in your plan refers to the number of story points or hours your team can complete in one iteration. For example, a team with a capacity of 30 story points (which is the default setting) can contain six work items that are estimated at five story points each during one iteration.

Velocity, which only exists within your plan, is your team’s average capacity per iteration over time based on past performance. For example, a team with a velocity of 30 story points will require two sprints to complete an epic estimated at 35 story points, assuming no other work was already assigned to those sprints.

Together, these two features ensure that your plan is realistic based on how quickly your teams are able to work.

Find out to turn on capacity planning in your plan.

Manage how work flows in your team-managed space

Add or remove workflow rules in team-managed spaces

Add or remove workflow rules in team-managed spaces

This page is for team-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

If you’re in a company-managed space, check out these company-managed space articles instead.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed space.

Rules help you streamline your team’s process by automatically updating fields when you move work items through your workflow. Workflow rules can automatically update a work item’s fields, or limit the people who can use a certain transition in your workflow, and more. More on workflows in team-managed spaces

Currently, we have the following workflow rules:

  • Assign a work item to someone

  • Update a work item field

  • Restrict who can move a work item

  • Remind people to update empty fields

  • Check that a work item has been through a status For each transition, you can have up to:

  • 10 groups of Restrict transition rules, with 50 rules for each group

  • 50 Validate details rules

  • 50 Perform actions rules More about each rule with examples of how you might use them

You must have the following to do the things described on this page.

Role:Administrator

Permission: Administer spaces

More about team-managed space roles

Add a new rule to a transition

To add a rule to a transition:

  • Next to your space’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings, then Work types.
  • From the sidebar, select the work type you want to edit.
  • Select Edit workflow.
  • From the workflow toolbar, select Rules.
  • Select the rule you want to add from the list, then Select.
  • Select the transition you want to add the rule to from the For transition dropdown.
  • Fill out the required information to set up your rule, and select Add. To see the rule in action, create a test work item and move it through your workflow.

You can add up to 10 rules to each transition.

Take care when using rules to restrict who can transition a work item. If you remove the role associated with the rule, your team may have trouble moving work items through your workflow.

Edit a transition rule

To edit a rule on a transition:

  • Next to your space’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings, then Work types.
  • From the sidebar, select the work type you want to edit.
  • Select Edit workflow. The workflow editor appears.
  • Select the transition in your workflow diagram. The transition details pane appears.
  • Under Rules, select the card for the rule you want to edit.
  • Make your changes and select Update. Your newly edited rules are applied to your software space when you save and exit the workflow editor.
Delete a transition rule

To delete a rule from a transition:

  • Next to your space’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings, then Work types.
  • From the sidebar, select the request type you want to edit.
  • Select Edit workflow.
  • Select the transition in your workflow diagram. The transition details pane appears.
  • Under Rules, select the card for the rule you want to delete.
  • Select Delete rule.
