Manage releases in your plans

Align cross-space release dates in your plan

Align cross-space release dates in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

By default, single-space releases that are contained within a cross-space release can have their own dates. However, if you want all of your single-space releases to converge or begin at the same time,your plan lets you align releases using either the start or end dates.

Cross-space releases are only used for planning purposes inside your plan. They can’t be viewed or edited in spaces.

To align the dates of single-space releases in a cross-space release:

  • Navigate to the Releases view from the left side navigation, and find the cross-space release whose release dates you want to align.
  • Select More actions (), then Align dates.
  • Choose how you want to align the start and/or end dates.
  • When you’re done, select Set dates to update the dates in your plan.
Release start date options:

As early as possible - The release will start as soon as there are available teams to work on the issues in the release. This is mostly only used when auto-scheduling issues.

Fixed date - Set a date

Relative to previous release date - Automatically trigger a new release a certain amount of time after the previous release finishes. For example, you can start work on the beta release one day after work for the alpha is completed.

Release date end options:

After all issues are completed - The release date is flexible and doesn’t display in the plan.

Fixed date - The release will happen on this chosen date, overriding the capacity and velocity settings. The release icons on the timeline will turn red for overbooked releases.

As early as possible - The release will start as soon as there are available teams to work on the issues in the release. This is mostly only used when auto-scheduling issues.

Release date end options:

Fixed date - The release will happen on this chosen date, overriding the capacity and velocity settings. The release icons on the timeline will turn red for overbooked releases.

You can ask Rovo to create a release in your plan using natural language. Open Rovo Chat and enter /create-plan-release, followed by a description of the release. For example, “Create a new release called Q3 starting today and ending in one month, with the description March release”.

How do single-space and cross-space releases differ?

How do single-space and cross-space releases differ?

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Plans in Jira can use two different types of releases: single-space and cross-space.

Single-space releases are the same as those found in spaces outside of your plan. In order to use releases from team-managed spaces in your plan, they need to be enabled first.

Plans also has cross-space releases which align multiple single-space releases in your plan to one unified date, but can’t be saved outside of your plan.

A cross-space release lets you align and track several single-space releases as one release across different work streams. Cross-space releases appear on your timeline in the same way as single-space releases.

Cross-space releases are only used for planning purposes inside your plan. They can’t be viewed or edited in spaces.

Remove releases in your plan

Remove releases in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

When you no longer want to include a release, you can either remove or delete it, depending on whether it’s been saved outside your plan.

  • You can remove a release when it’s been saved to a space. Removed release are no longer shown in your plan, but remain untouched the your space.
  • You can delete a release if it hasn’t been saved or is a cross-space release (which can’t be saved outside your plan). Though the steps are the same, deleted releases can’t be recovered. See how release types differ in plans

To remove or delete a release from your plan:

  • In the Releases tab, find the release you want to remove from your plan.
  • Select More actions () then Remove (or Delete). Confirm your decision in the modal that opens.

Track releases in your plan

Track releases in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Once you add a release to your plan, it shows on your plan.

  • Releases on your timeline
    • Track cross-space releases
  • Releases on your calendar
On your timeline

To view releases on your plan, you need to have the timeline bars showing on your plan or have the Releases column visible. Find out how to show or hide your timeline bars.

Releases on your timeline are indicated by small icons along the top of the timeline bar section. If:

  • you have multiple releases happening at once, your plan adds a number above the icon
  • the icon is green, that release is On-track
  • the icon is red, that release is Off-track
    • Releases that contain issues scheduled by sprint dates will show as off-track if the sprint ends after the release date. Select a release icon above your timeline to see you a high-level overview of that release. In this window, you can select:
  • the Highlight on timeline check box to extend either a red or green line down your timeline
  • Filter by issues included in this release
  • View in Jira Use the left or right arrow at the top of the window to toggle through releases.
Track cross-space releases

When your plan shows a cross-space release on your timeline, it will always have a number displayed above it because, according to your plan, there are two releases scheduled on that date: the cross-space release and the final single-space release.

For this reason, when you select the release icon to open a flyout window, you’ll see both the cross-space release as well as any single-space releases:

On your calendar

Releases show on your calendar as bars according to the Release date. If a release has a red icon, that release is Off-track.

Selecting a release on your calendar shows the following window:

Turn releases in your plan on or off

Turn releases in your plan on or off

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Releases (also known as Fix versions) are commonly used by development teams as deadlines for sections (or versions) of work. Those planning work for non-software teams can choose to hide all information related to releases.

This feature only hides releases from your plan and hides release-related tools. It doesn’t impact releases in your spaces.

This feature is currently rolling out to cloud customers. Your site may not reflect these changes, or you might not see it in your site just yet.

When you turn releases off in your plan, you’ll no longer see:

  • the Releases tab

  • the Releases field from the timeline as well as any filters that use it

  • release markers on the timeline, calendar, and program board

  • the option to group work items by assigned releases in the View settings menu

  • any rolled up dates based on releases If you’re using release data to schedule work or define plan scope:

  • work items scheduled using the dates of assigned releases will instead use dates from sprints

  • if you’ve removed work from your plan based on their release, those work items will be re-added to your plan Save all changes related to releases before you turn them off in your plan

Before turning off releases, save any unsaved changes related to the above features, such as changes to release dates or work item release assignments. Unsaved data related to releases will be discarded and it can’t be recovered.

How to save changes made in your plan

To turn releases on or off in your plan:

  • Next to your plan’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Plan settings.
  • Select Features, then toggle Releases. If you have unsaved changes related to releases, you’ll be asked to confirm that you want to discard these changes.
  • In the modal that opens, confirm your choice. You can use Rovo to enable or disable releases without going into your plan settings. Just open Rovo Chat and enter /manage-plan-featuresfollowed by an instruction (for example, “Enable releases for this plan”).

What are releases in your plan?

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Releases in your plan are referred to as Fix versions in Jira. Read more about versions in Jira Software.

Releases are commonly used by development teams as deadlines for sections (or versions) of work. In the rest of Jira, these are also referred to as Fix versions.

You can schedule releases to end on a date of your choosing or once all of the work items it contains have been completed. If you choose the second option, the end date of the release in your space appears blank.

View, add, and create new releases in your plan by navigating to the Releases tab in your plan.

You can plan using two types of releases: single-space releases and cross-space releases.

  • Single-space releases are the same as those found in space outside of your plan. In order to use releases from team-managed spaces in your plan, they need to be enabled first.
  • Alternatively, you can use cross-space releases to align and track several single-space releases as one release. More about single-space and cross-space releases

Create a new team from your plan

Create a new team from your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

When creating a team, you can choose to add a team that’ll be visible across your organization, or one that lives entirely in your plan. Plan-only teams can be shared across your entire organization later on.

Once a team is made public, it can’t be un-shared. Find out more about the types of teams in your plan.

To create a team in your plan:

  • In the Teams view, navigate to + Add team
  • Select Create a new team, and choose the type of team you’d like to create. You can create a team that’s Available across organization (also known as an Atlassian team) or a team that’s Plan only. From here, the process differs slightly.
For Atlassian teams:
  • On the screen that pops up, enter you team name and add members.
  • When you’re ready, select Create team, and this new team is now available across your organization. On this confirmation dialogue, you can use View your plan to begin planning with this team, or configure it further using Configure team.
  • After you select Configure team, you’ll be able to add planning information such as:
    • Work source
    • Planning style (Scrum or Kanban)
      • if your plan estimates work items in Story points, you’ll only be able to create a Scrum team
    • Sprint length (Scrum only; Kanban assumes an iteration length of one week)
    • Capacity
  • Select Done to save your changes.
  • To configure a managed team, follow this process.
For plan-only teams:
  • On the screen that pops up, enter the following information:
    • Team name
    • Team members
    • Work source
    • Planning style (Scrum or Kanban)
      • if your plan estimates work items in Story points, you’ll only be able to create a Scrum team
    • Sprint length (Scrum only; Kanban assumes an iteration length of one week)
    • Capacity
  • When you’re happy with your team, select Create. Your team will now be available in your plan. When you’re ready, you can convert it to an Atlassian team, which is visible across your organization. See how to convert a plan-only team to an Atlassian team.

To change values associated with your teams, start by finding the team you want to edit in the Teams tab, and select ••• > Team settings.

From here, the process differs slightly.

For an Atlassian team

    • Work item source

      • if your plan estimates work items in Story points, you’ll only be able to create a Scrum team
    • Sprint length (Scrum only; Kanban assumes an iteration length of one week)
    • Capacity
  • When you’re done, select Save.

How do I use teams in plans?

How do I use teams in plans?

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

The work in your plan needs to be completed by someone, and Teams are how you designate who will do what. You can assign work to teams, monitor their capacity and velocity, and show or hide work based on team assignments.

To view the teams in your plan, select the Teams tab from the plan navigation.

Your plan uses two types of teams:

  • Atlassian teams are available across either your whole site or your entire organization. Anyone can add an Atlassian team to their plan, and model future work based on capacity, overall availability, and the members of the team. Read more about Atlassian teams
  • Plan-only teams live within the plan in which they were created. Any work item assignments or changes to work you’ve made in your plan can’t be saved until you convert it to an Atlassian team. Find out how to convert plan-only team to an Atlassian team. Read how to view and edit teams in your plan.
External teams

If you remove a team from your plan, work items still assigned to them have the EXT. TEAM lozenge next to the team name. This indicates that this team isn’t represented in your plan and that this work item represents an external dependency.

You can fix this by adding the team back to your plan or reassigning the work items.

Limitations of teams in open planning sites

Limitations of teams in open planning sites

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

An open site is site that anyone can access without administrator approval – including those outside your organization. Sometimes, this is done intentionally, or it can be a result of misconfigured site access settings. Find out how to restrict access to your site.

Depending on how your administrator configures them, teams in your Jira site can either be a global entity that can be used and viewed across all of your organization’s other Atlassian sites or restricted to only specific Jira sites.

To protect sensitive team data (e.g. - team names), users viewing an open Jira site can only see these organization-wide teams if they also have access to a restricted site in the same organization. Conversely, users that can only access open sites won’t be able to see teams or assign issues to a team; they’ll only be able to see and assign issues to plan-only teams. See what information is available on unrestricted sites.

Remove and delete teams from your plan

Remove and delete teams from your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

When a team is no longer needed, you can remove them from your plan.

If you’re using an Atlassian team, you can simply remove it from your plan and the team entity still exists across your organization. However, if you remove a plan-only team, it ceases to exist elsewhere and can’t be recovered.

To remove an Atlassian team:

  • In the Teams view, find the team you want to remove, and select more (•••) > Remove. This removes the team from your plan, and adds the change to your list of changes in the Review changes modal.
  • Use the Review changes button to save your changes to your plan. You can’t fully delete an Atlassian team from your plan. Find out how to delete an Atlassian team.

To delete a plan-only team:

  • In the Teams view, find the team you want to remove, and select more (•••) > Delete.
  • Confirm you want to delete the team. This change is applied right away.

Manage your user profile

Allow OAuth access

Allow OAuth access

About OAuth access tokens

OAuth access tokens allow you to:

  • Use a Jira gadget on an external, OAuth-compliant web app or website (also known as a consumer)
  • Grant this gadget access to Jira data which is restricted or privy to your Jira user account.
Before you begin

Your Jira administrator must establish an OAuth relationship with this external web app or instance by approving it as an OAuth consumer. For example, if you want to add a Jira gadget to your Bamboo homepage and allow this gadget to access your restricted Jira data, then your Jira administrator must first approve Bamboo as an OAuth consumer.

The Jira gadget on the consumer is granted access to your Jira data via an OAuth access token, which acts as a type of key. As long as the consumer is in possession of this access token, the Jira gadget will be able to access Jira data that is both publicly available and privy to your Jira user account. You can revoke this access token at any time from your Jira user account, otherwise, all access tokens expire after seven days. Once the access token is revoked or has expired, the Jira gadget will only have access to publicly available data on your Jira instance.

An OAuth access token will only appear in your user profile if the following conditions have been met:

  • Your Jira Administrator has established an app link using OAuth between your Jira instance and the consumer. Jira Administrators should refer to Using AppLinks to link to other apps.
  • You have accessed a Jira gadget on a consumer and have allowed this gadget access to your Jira data. (More on this step in the next section.)
Issuing OAuth access tokens

An OAuth access token is issued by Jira to provide one of its gadgets on a consumer, access to your Jira data (that is, data which is restricted to your Jira user account).

  • When you are using a Jira gadget on a consumer (such as Bamboo) and this gadget requires access to your Jira data, you will first be prompted to log in to Jira (if you have not already done so).
  • Once you have logged in to Jira, you will be prompted with a Request for access message.
  • At this point, Jira is preparing to issue the Jira gadget (on the consumer) with an OAuth access token.
  • To grant the gadget access to your Jira data, select Approve access. The consumer app will receive the OAuth access token from your Jira instance. This access token is specific to this gadget and as long as the token resides with the gadget, your gadget will have access to your Jira data.
Revoking OAuth access tokens

You can revoke an OAuth access token to deny a Jira gadget on a consumer access to Jira data which is restricted to your Jira user account. You can only revoke OAuth access tokens that you have allowed Jira to issue previously.

  • Select Your profile and settings, then Personal settings.
  • Choose Manage apps in the Connected apps section at the bottom of the page.
  • Your list of OAuth access tokens is presented in a table, with each access token presented in separate rows and each property of these tokens presented in a separate column. Refer to the OAuth access token table details section.
  • Locate the Jira gadget and its associated consumer app whose OAuth access token you wish to revoke and select its Revoke OAuth access token link in the Actions column.
  • You may be prompted to confirm this action. If so, select OK. The gadget’s access token is revoked and the Jira gadget on the consumer will only have access to publicly available Jira data.
OAuth access token table details

Column name

Description

Consumer

The name of the Jira gadget that was added on the consumer.

Consumer description

A description of this consumer app. This information would have been obtained from the consumer’s own OAuth settings when an OAuth relationship was established between Jira and that consumer. If the consumer is another Atlassian app, this information is obtained from the Consumer Info tab’s Description field of the OAuth Administration settings. The app’s administrator can customize this Consumer Info detail.

Issued On

The date on which the OAuth access token was issued to the consumer by Jira. This would have occurred immediately after you approved this gadget access to your Jira data (privy to your Jira user account).

Expires On

The date when the OAuth access token expires. This is seven days after the Issued On date. When this date is reached, the access token will be automatically removed from this list.

Actions

The functionality for revoking the access token.

Manage your Jira personal settings

Manage your Jira personal settings

To manage your personal settings, you must log into your Jira site. Public and anonymous users inherit the site’s default user preferences.

Your personal settings let you customize some elements of Jira to your liking, including language, timezone, watch settings, and email type. For other settings, like your full name, avatar, password, and email address, see Managing your user profile.

To access your personal settings:

  • From the top right of your screen, select Settings ().

  • Under Personal Jira settings, select General settings. You can update the following settings:

  • Language – Change your Jira app language to one of the available options.

  • Your timezone – The timezone used for date and time information across your Jira apps. If the timezone you select doesn’t match your computer’s timezone, you’ll have the option to automatically update this preference.

  • Watch your work items – With this enabled, you become a watcher of any work item that you create or comment on. This means you’ll get an email when someone updates or comments on the work item. Rovo can help you get to the right settings to make the changes you need. Open Rovo Chat and enter /find-jira-settings, then tell Rovo what you’re looking for. Rovo will provide a link to the most relevant settings page, along with a rundown on what you can do once you get there.

Manage notifications

To access your notification settings:

  • From the top right of your screen, select Settings ().
  • Under Personal Jira settings, select Notification settings. You can choose what notifications you’d like to receive from a variety of work item activity.

You can choose to receive (or not receive) notifications in-app or by email by using the checkboxes.

Use the Customize space notifications section to set specific notifications for different spaces. You can customize notifications for up to 50 spaces.

All your notification settings (default or custom) act like a filter on top of the notification settings configured by your admin. If your admin has turned off a particular notification, you may not receive it even if you’ve chosen to receive that kind of notification in your settings.

Choose email notifications for work item activity in Jira Cloud

Your Jira admin sets up your default notifications. Depending on the space, you may get notifications when someone adds a comment on a work item or someone completes a work log entry. These actions tend to happen in short bursts, with a few small, individual changes added to a work item within minutes of each other.

Instead of sending one email per change, Jira will consolidate individual updates into a single summary email. To make sure relevant updates are batched together, notifications could be delayed by up to 10 minutes.

Important notifications will come through immediately, like mentions, alerts, SLA notifications, and newly assigned work items.

You can override and control some of these notifications to reduce the amount of email you receive from Jira.

Outside of these settings, you may receive other email notifications including:

  • Announcements and updates about your Jira site
  • Updates for work item filter subscriptions if you’ve set them up
  • Notifications for activity outside of Jira, including those regarding your Atlassian account
Limit email notifications for work item activity

By default, you receive the notifications configured by your Jira admin.

To choose not to receive email notifications for specific types of work item activity, or all work item activity in general:

  • From the top right of your screen, select Settings ().

  • Under Personal Jira settings, select Notification settings.

  • If not already there, select Spaces and work items in the side navigation.

  • Switch the toggle off for Send me emails for work item activity, or select the relevant checkboxes for email notifications you want to receive. You can choose whether you receive email notifications for issue activity when:

  • You’re watching the work item

  • You’re the reporter

  • You’re the assignee of the work item

  • Someone mentions you

  • You make changes to a work item Even if you clear all checkboxes, you may still receive other email notifications configured by your Jira admin.

Filter emails in your inbox

Summary emails have variable From fields, depending on who’s adding updates to a work item:

  • The From field will be the actioner’s name, if only one person added the updates presented in the email.
  • The From field will be Jira, if multiple people added the updates presented in the email. The sender’s email will always be jira@.atlassian.net.
Manage connected apps

You can view and manage apps with access to your Jira account via the Personal settings page. These apps use OAuth access tokens issued by Jira to give them access to restricted data on an external, OAuth-compliant web application or website (also known as a “consumer”).

To view and manage apps:

  • From the top right of your screen, select Settings ().
  • Under Personal Jira settings, select General settings.
  • Select Manage apps in the Connected apps section at the bottom of the page. Check out Allowing OAuth access for more information on when to issue or revoke OAuth access tokens.

View and update your profile

View and update your profile

To view and edit your profile:

  • From the top right of your screen, select your avatar or profile picture.

  • Select Profile, then Edit profile.

  • Update the relevant details, then select Save. From your profile, you can view and change your:

  • Full name

  • Nickname

  • Job title

  • Department

  • Organization

  • Location

  • Timezone

Manage other profile details

Account details like your avatar, profile picture, email address, and password are managed through your Atlassian account. To change these details:

  • From the top right of your screen, select your avatar or profile picture.
  • Select Profile, then Manage your account.
  • Update the relevant details. Your changes will be saved automatically.

Add a child work item with your keyboard

Add a child work item with your keyboard

To add a child work item with the command palette:

  • Open the command palette.
    • If you’re a Mac user, press command + K to open the command palette.
    • If you’re a windows user, press Ctrl + K to open the command palette.
  • Search for the command Add child.
  • Enter a name for the child work item and select enter on your keyboard.

Change the status of a work item with your keyboard

Change the status of a work item with your keyboard

You can move a work item through the workflow (also known as transitioning a work item) by changing its status in the command palette. For example, you could change the status from To do to In progress.

To change an work item’s status with the command palette:

  • Make sure you’re viewing a work item either in the side bar or in full screen.
  • Open the command palette.
    • If you’re a Mac user, press command + K to open the command palette.
    • If you’re a windows user, press Ctrl + K to open the command palette.
  • Search for the command Change status.
  • Select the desired status.
    • If there are any transition requirements for the status you select, the transition work item window will open so you can complete the action.

Edit components of a work item with your keyboard

Edit components of a work item with your keyboard

You can edit components of a work item using only your keyboard via the command palette.

Create a component

To create a component with the command palette:

  • Make sure you’re viewing a work item either in the side bar or in full screen.
  • Open the command palette.
    • If you’re a Mac user, press command + K to open the command palette.
    • If you’re a windows user, press Ctrl + K to open the command palette.
  • Search for the command Add components, or Edit components if your work item already has components.
  • Enter a name for the component and select Create new component. This will take you to a separate page to create your component.
Add or edit a component

To add or edit a component with the command palette:

  • Make sure you’re viewing a work item either in the side bar or in full screen.
  • Open the command palette.
    • If you’re a Mac user, press command + K to open the command palette.
    • If you’re a windows user, press Ctrl + K to open the command palette.
  • Search for the command Add components, or Edit components if your work item already has components.
  • Search for the component you’d like to add to the work item or locate it in the dropdown list, then select enter on your keyboard.
Remove a component

To remove a component with the command palette:

  • Make sure you’re viewing a work item either in the side bar or in full screen.
  • Open the command palette.
    • If you’re a Mac user, press command + K to open the command palette.
    • If you’re a windows user, press Ctrl + K to open the command palette.
  • Search for the command Edit components.
  • Locate the component you want to remove in the dropdown list, then select enter on your keyboard.

    • Search for the person you’d like to assign to the work item. Select the person by hitting enter, this will close the command palette and assign the work item.

Search work items, projects, and more with your keyboard

Search work items, projects, and more with your keyboard

You can use a forward slash / in the command palette search bar to find:

  • Work items

  • Projects

  • Boards

  • Filters To search for work items, projects, and more in the command palette:

  • Open the command palette.

    • If you’re a Mac user, press command :command: + K to open the command palette.
    • If you’re a windows user, press Ctrl + K to open the command palette.

  • Type a forward slash / or press the down key and select the top command Search work items, projects, and more

  • Type keywords into the search bar to find what you’re looking for.

  • The forward slash in the search bar indicates you are not searching for commands, you’re instead searching for work items, projects, boards, and filters.

  • Labels separate different types of results.

  • Work item results show:

    • The work item type icon
    • The work item key, e.g. TR-35.
    • The work item summary, e.g. “Editable fields”.
    • The project where the work item lives, e.g. “Team Rocket”.

  • If you don’t see what you’re looking for straight away, you can select View all results. It will take you to another page with all the relevant search results.

Use keyboard shortcuts

Use keyboard shortcuts

Keyboard shortcuts are a great way for you to speed up editing, navigating, and performing actions without having to navigate away from the keyboard.

Some keyboard shortcuts require additional permissions or applications. These shortcuts rely on the way permissions are configured for your account and which applications are installed. Keyboard shortcuts for third-party apps may not integrate with Jira. Check out their support docs to see what’s possible.

View keyboard shortcuts

You can open the keyboard shortcuts dialog using either of the following methods:

  • Select Help then Keyboard shortcuts.

  • Press the ? on your keyboard from any page (Shift + / ). The keyboard shortcuts dialog shows commands for the operating system and browser that you’re using. The dialog is divided into sections for the following information:

  • Global shortcuts — shortcuts that can be used in any part of Jira.

  • Navigating work items — shortcuts for navigating through work items.

  • Work item actions — shortcuts for working with work items.

  • App-specific — any shortcuts that are specific to an application and won’t work anywhere else.

Keyboard shortcuts in team-managed spaces

In team-managed software spaces, the keyboard shortcut dialog is divided into the following sections:

  • Essentials — common and frequently used shortcuts that can be used when you’re in a space, on a board, in the backlog, or using filters or a dashboard.
  • Board and backlog — shortcuts that can be used on the board or backlog.
  • Navigate spaces — shortcuts that can be used to switch views in a space.
  • Navigate work items — shortcuts that make it easier to find and browse work items.
  • Work item actions — shortcuts for working with work items.
Create a work item with your keyboard

Press C to create a new work item.

Update work items with your keyboard

Work items support a limited set of keyboard shortcuts for editing and updating work items:

  • Press O to open the selected work item

  • Press A to assign the work item to someone

  • Press I to assign a work item to yourself

  • Press M to quickly add a comment) You can also navigate the work item with keyboard shortcuts:

  • Press J to go down

  • Press K to go up

  • Press N to go to the next column

  • Press P to go to the previous column

Turn off keyboard shortcuts

If you’d prefer to turn keyboard shortcuts off, you can do so via the keyboard shortcuts dialog:

  • Select Help then Keyboard shortcuts.
  • Switch off Keyboard shortcuts are enabled.
Modifier keys

Some keyboard shortcuts require modifier keys to be pressed simultaneously, along with a single ‘action’ key. Modifier keys may differ, depending on your combination of operating system and web browser.

The following identifies the modifier keys for some supported web browsers and operating systems:

Chrome
  • Windows: Alt + Shift
  • macOS: Ctrl + Alt/Option
  • Linux/Solaris: Alt + Shift
Firefox
  • Windows: Alt + Shift
  • macOS: Ctrl
  • Linux/Solaris: Alt + Shift In Firefox, it’s possible to customize ‘modifier key shortcuts’. See Mozilla’s documentation for more information.
Safari
  • Windows: Ctrl
  • macOS: Ctrl + Alt/Option
Internet Explorer
  • Windows: Alt Typing a ‘modifier key shortcut’ that leads to a link requires you to press Enter to complete the action.

What is the command palette?

What is the command palette?

The command palette lets you seamlessly work in Jira with just your keyboard. Use the command palette to find work, perform actions on work items, and navigate to key places in Jira.

Open the command palette
  • If you’re a Mac user, press command + K to open the command palette.
  • If you’re a Windows user, press Ctrl + K to open the command palette. The command palette won’t open if it looks like you’re trying to edit or type something so make sure you haven’t clicked into a field (like a search bar, or the priority field of a work item).

What about the shortcut to add a link?

If you’re editing something in a free text field (like description, comment, etc.), the command palette will not open and that shortcut will instead allow you to add a link.

Using command palette
  • Search for commands using the search bar.
  • Use a forward slash / in the search bar to search for:
    • Work items
    • Spaces
    • Boards
    • Filters
  • A chevron ( > ) on the far right of a command indicates that, when you hit enter, you’ll stay in the command palette to perform that action. If there is no chevron, the command palette will simply close and perform the selected action.
  • If there is a keyboard shortcut already associated with a command, we’ll show it in the command palette. Keyboard shortcuts work in Jira without needing to open the command palette. In the example above, you can just press 1 to navigate to the backlog in your space at any time. Find out about keyboard shortcuts
  • Give feedback on your experience using the command palette to help us continually improve the feature and make it the best it can be.

Plan your next quarter using a Program board

Add and change sprints on the Program board in your plan

Add and change sprints on the Program board in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

When you create your Program board, it automatically creates six columns and assigns start and end dates to them each lasting two weeks based on the start date of your board. If your scrum teams use sprints, you can associate the columns to sprints, then schedule work items to them. How does the Program board schedule work items once I add sprints?

Because sprints are a scrum-only concept, only teams that use a scrum board as their work source can plan using sprints.

To add a team’s sprints to your Program board:

  • Associate the teams on your board with a scrum board. How do I associate teams with work sources?
  • Select Add sprints next to the team’s name. In the modal that opens, choose which sprints belong to which columns on the board.
    • When you add a team’s sprints to your board, you’ll need to add all sprints for that team at one time. You won’t be able to add three then come back later to add the rest. For this reason, we recommend creating all of a team’s sprints in their backlog to prepare for your planning session.
  • Select Add when you’re done. Any work items already in a column will be assigned to the sprint.

Change work item info from the Program board in your plan

Change work item info from the Program board in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

The Program board lets you make common adjustments when planning across multiple sprints, such as:

Re-parent work items

To assign an work item to a parent work item, select the More actions [•••] menu on the child work item’s card, then choose the work item to which you want to link it.

If a child work item already has a parent work item, select the status lozenge on the card to change or remove the link.

This only works with story-level work items. Parent work items can’t be reparented to a higher hierarchy level from the Program board.

Assign a work item to a different team

When you move a work item to a new team, it inherits the scheduling information of that column (sprint of dates). You may need to reschedule it based on the new teams’ information.

To move a work item to a new team, either:

  • select the More actions [•••] menu on the work item, then Change team.
  • drag the work item to the new team’s swimlane
Add a Dependency

To create a dependency between two work items, select the ••• menu on the work item, then Add dependency. In the modal that appears, select which dependency type you want, then select the other work item in the relationship. You can only link work items included in your plan.

Create a new Program board in your plan

Create a new Program board in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

For a smoother experience, we recommend that you do some preparations before creating your Program board.

To create a new board:

  • Select Program from the top nav.
  • From the dropdown menu next to the search bar, select Create a new Program board.
  • Name your board, choose a start date, and then set the Column duration and Number of columns. Your board can span to between 7 and 16 weeks.
  • Choose what work items you want to include in this view.
    • If you’ve groomed your work items and marked them with a field or a label, select that field and value to only bring in work items that match.
    • If you leave this empty, your board adds all work items in your plan with To do or In progress statuses.
  • When you’re ready, select Create. Try using Rovo to create your next program board. Open Rovo Chat and enter /create-program-board, then briefly describe how you want the program board to work (for example, “Create a program board called FY26 with 2 columns, each 5 weeks starting from tomorrow”). Rovo will suggest a program board structure for you to review and create directly in your plan.
How the Program board sorts work items

When you first open your Program board, work items appear in the Drag issues to schedule column if:

  • they have no scheduling information or

  • are currently scheduled outside the scope of your board Work items with partial information are automatically placed them in the columns it thinks are most appropriate:

  • If you link sprints to your Program board, work items assigned to those sprints are placed in the corresponding column

  • If you don’t link your sprints and your work items have an end date (or you’re inferring sprint dates on your timeline), your board moves these work items based on the date at the top of the column If your partially filled work items don’t meet either of these cases, they’ll show in the Drag work items to schedule column.

Recommended preparations before using the Program board

Recommended preparations before using the Program board

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

The Program board is designed to be used for Program Increment Planning rituals as part of the SAFe planning methodology. Before you start planning work on your Program board, the plan owner should prepare for the upcoming planning session.

Want to see the Program board in action? Watch a video tutorial of how to set up and use the Program board in Plans.

Groom your work before planning

By default, your program board includes all work in your plan with To do or In progress statuses. To focus their program board on the most relevant work, planners can tag work (both parent and child work items) they want to include using either of the following:

  • a single-select or multi-select field or
  • the Label field You can use this field as a filter when you create your program board or update the filter of an existing program board.
Create teams and configure them in your plan

The program board plans work based on Teams. Before you start your quarterly planning ritual, you need to add teams to your plan.

Once your plan includes Teams, you need to associate teams with work sources to use capacity planning.

If you don’t associate Teams with a work item source, any work items from scrum boards will be scheduled according to the dates at the top of the column and not the team’s sprints, even if the sprint happens over the same timeframe.

Create sprints for the coming quarter for all of your scrum teams

Sprints can only be used by Scrum teams.

As a planner, you can schedule work items on the Program board in one of two ways:

  • assign work items directly to a team’s sprint or
  • schedule work items using the dates at the top of the columns We recommend that you create all of the sprints you’ll need before you set up your Program board. When you add a team’s sprints to your board, you’ll need to add a team’s sprints to all of the columns at one time. You won’t be able to add three then come back later to add the rest.

Find out how to add sprints to your Program board.

Schedule work items from the Program board in your plan

Schedule work items from the Program board in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

To schedule or reschedule work items on your Program board, select and move the cards between the columns. Alternatively, select the More menu [•••] on the work item and choose which column you want to move it to. To unschedule work, move it back to the column on the left by either dragging it or using the same menu as before.

The program board focuses on when the work is expected to be delivered, not started. For this reason, place work items on your board based on when you expect the work to be completed. See how the Program board sorts scheduled work items when you create your board.

By default, the Program board schedules work items by dates. To schedule work by sprints, you need to add sprints to your Program board.

If your plan uses sequential dependencies, linked work items in the same column show as off-track. To allow dependencies in the same column, change your plan to use concurrent dependencies.

Using dates on your Program board

When you move a work item, your board schedules it based on the start and end dates at the top of the column.

If you move a parent-level work item to a column, only the end date is assigned; you’ll need to add a start date manually.

All parent-level work items (work items Level 1 such as Epics or Features) are scheduled using dates on the Program board. This way, the timeline view shows the full length of the parent-level work item when roll-ups are enabled. What are rollups in Plans?

Using sprints on your Program board

If you’ve added sprints to your Program board, your board updates the Sprint field when you drag it to a new column. From here, it’s scheduled according to the dates of the sprint.

Update and remove Program boards in your plan

Update and remove Program boards in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

To view your program board’s settings

  • Next to your plan’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Plan settings.

  • Select Program board From this screen you can:

  • update your program board’s filter by selecting either Change filter or Add filter next to the board you want to update. More about adding filters to a program board

  • rename a program board by selecting the name of the Program board, entering a new name, then using the checkmark to save.

  • delete a program board by selecting Delete [] next to the plan you want to delete. This action can’t be reversed. Rovo can delete a program board on your behalf. Open Rovo Chat and enter /delete-program-board, then tell Rovo which board you want to delete.

View and manage dependencies on the Program board

View and manage dependencies on the Program board

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

This feature is currently rolling out to cloud customers. Your site may not reflect these changes, or you might not see it in your site just yet.

The Program board lets you create, view, and edit dependencies while planning upcoming work. When a work item is part of a dependency, a chain icon appears in the bottom corner of the card. If the dependency falls off-track, the icon turns red.

If your plan uses sequential dependencies, linked work items in the same column show as off-track. To allow dependencies in the same column, change your plan to use concurrent dependencies.

View dependencies by work item

To investigate dependencies related to a work item in deeper detail, select the chain icon on the card. From this window, you can:

  • draw lines to show all of the dependencies related to this work item
  • see a list of dependent work items
  • open the Dependencies tab of your plan focusing on this work item
  • create a new dependency starting from this work item - see how easy it is to create dependencies
View dependencies across your board

As well as viewing individual dependencies, you can view the broader impact of dependencies across your board.

Inside the View settings menu are two settings that show how dependencies ripple out across your plan:

  • Add a work item in the Show lines for dependencies linked to field to focus on dependencies for up to 10 work items at once. Lines are only drawn once work items have been scheduled, so lines to unscheduled work items won’t show.
  • View all of the off-track dependencies in your plan by selecting Show lines for all off-track dependencies. Lastly, you can filter work items on your board to only show those with off-track dependencies using the Dependencies filter at the top of your plan.

What does the Program board show?

What does the Program board show?

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

After you create your Program board, you’ll see the following:

  • The column labeled Drag work items to schedule shows your as-of-yet unplanned work based on the team assigned to each work item. Peterman and Associates team is set up to use their planned sprints for the coming quarter, while Junior Mints team isn’t. How do I add sprints to my Program board?.
  • Filter the work that shows on your board based on filters like Parent work item (such as Epic), Work type, and the Space it’s from. This filter doesn’t remove them from your board but hides them from the view for easier planning. Filter options only appear once they’re relevant to your plan.
  • Adjust what information shows on your Program board using the View settings menu. Find out what View settings options you have on your Program board.

What is the Program board in my plan?

What is the Program board in my plan?

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

The Program board interface gives planners visibility into the work, priorities, and dependencies of multiple teams so they can plan for multiple iterations at once. It can be used by all planners, but it’s been optimized to support Program Increment Planning rituals (also called Program planning or Quarterly planning), which are an essential part of the SAFe planning methodology.

Want to see the Program board in action? Watch a video tutorial of how to set up and use the Program board in Plans.

This view focuses on work items at the level 1 and level 0 hierarchy levels (commonly referred to as the Epic and Story levels). Any hierarchy levels above or below these – such as Initiative or Subtasks – won’t show on this view. Read more about hierarchy levels in Jira.

Each plan can have two active program boards at any time. A Program board is considered active if its end date is in the future. Once a Program board’s end date passes, the board is completed and no longer counts against your allotment of active boards.

The Program Board isn’t designed for real-time collaborative planning sessions such as Big Room Planning. For now, we recommend using a whiteboarding tool alongside the Program board to accommodate the large number of inputs needed for a collaborative planning session.

To get started with your Program board, select Program from the left side navigation then select Create program board. See what the Program board shows.

Release your team’s work in versions

Check the progress of a version

Check the progress of a version

You’ve been monitoring the progress of your sprints and keeping your team on track for each iteration. How do know if you are on track to deliver the version?

Jira provides a number of tools that you can use to monitor the progress of a version. These tools can help you see problems early, as well as determine the likelihood of releasing a version on time.

Release page

The release page helps you understand the status of work for your version at a point in time. It shows a summary and breakdown of the work items in the version.

To view a version, select Releases in your space sidebar, then select your version from the list.

If you have connected Jira to your development tools, the release page will show development information about pull requests, commits, builds, and deployments associated with your work items.

Depending on which development tools are connected, warnings can also appear when your work item data is potentially out of sync with your development data. These include warnings about work items that are marked as done but have open pull requests or unreviewed code.

Find out about checking the progress of a version on the release page

Release burndown report

The release burndown report helps you understand how your team is progressing towards the completion of the version. The report shows your team’s velocity (relative to the current version), how scope changes have affected progress, and the estimated number of sprints needed to complete the remaining work.

Find out about the release burndown report

Check the release status of a version

Check the release status of a version

Since a version has many moving parts, you need to be sure that everything is ready before you can release a particular version — work items are complete, code is committed, reviewed, and merged, builds are passing, etc. The Release hub in software spaces can help you stay on top of everything when it’s time to release a version. Work items in Jira also have a development panel that help you see the development status at a glance.

Before you begin

To configure the board and any of its settings, you must be either:

  • a space administrator for the location of the board
  • a board administrator for the board itself More about permissions in Jira Cloud.
Use the release hub

The release hub is useful for seeing the status of a version at a point in time. It shows a summary and a breakdown of the work items in the version so you can see if there’s any remaining work for the release.

To view a version, select Releases from your navigation, then select your version from the list.

Depending on which development tools are connected to Jira, warnings can also appear when your work item data is potentially out of sync with your development data. These include warnings about work items that are marked as done but have open pull requests or unreviewed code.

More about warnings on the release page

Check the development status of an work item

If you need to deep dive into individual work items, the development panel on each work item will show you its development status. This includes commits, builds, branches, pull requests, and more.

More about viewing development information for a work item

Create a version

Create a version

Versions represent points in time for your space. They can be used to schedule how features are rolled out to your customers, or as a way to organize work that has been completed for the space.

Enable releases

You must have Space admin permissions to enable features. More about space permissions

In Jira, you create versions using the releases feature. If the releases feature isn’t enabled in your space yet, you can turn it on.

To enable the releases feature:

  • Navigate to your software space.

  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.

  • Select Features.

  • Enable the Releases feature. Another way you can enable reports is by:

  • Select Add to navigation (+).

  • Select Releases, then Add to navigation. The releases tab will now be accessible from your space navigation.

Create a version

You must have Space admin or Manage versions permissions to create a version.

  • From your space navigation, select Releases.

  • Select Create version. When you create a version, you can enter the:

  • Name: choose a name that’s easily identifiable for your teammates so they can recognise the version.

  • Start date: the date work on the version will start.

  • Release date: the planned release date for the version.

  • Description: more information about what you plan to release in the version.

  • Driver: someone in your team with administrator permissions who’s responsible for coordinating the release from start to finish (by default, it’s the person who creates the version).

Add a custom section with rich text

To add custom text, you must have permission to resolve work items and edit work items.

Customize your release by adding a section of your own text. You can add rich text, lists, hyperlinks, dates, and emojis; and you can format the text with bold, italics, and colors.

To add rich text to your release:

  • From your space navigation, select Releases.
  • Select your release from the list.
  • Select “Give this section a name” and enter a heading.
  • Select “Add your own text here…” and enter some body text.
Add other work related to your version

To add related work, you must have permission to resolve work items and edit work items.

Add related work to your version so team members and stakeholders can easily find it. This can include things like release notes, analytics dashboards, designs, support documentation, and more.

To add related work to your version:

  • From your space navigation, select Releases, then select your version.
  • Select Add… in the Related work section.
  • Enter the URL for the related work, a description, or both.
  • Choose a category and select Save. Once you’ve added related work, select the menu icon () next to an item and select Edit to update it, or Remove to delete it.

If your related work items are not ready yet, you can create a placeholder and add the URL later when the work is available.

If you need someone to work on an item for your release, link a work item to the related work and assign it to them. To link a new work item, hover over the related work item and select Create work item, or select Link work item to link an existing work item.

Add an approver to a version

Make sure the right team members sign off on your release by adding them as an approver. Approvers can approve or decline a release, and add a reason to a decline so the team knows what has to change.

  • From your space navigation, go to Releases.
  • Select a release from the list.
  • In the Approvers section, select Add approver ().
  • Select an approver from the list of space members, and add an optional description to let them know what they are approving.

Release a version

Release a version

It’s time to turn your team’s hard work into a software release.

Use the release page to check the progress of your version and verify that:

  • work items are complete
  • code is checked in, reviewed, and merged
  • builds are passing
  • work items have been deployed to the correct environment
  • any related work is complete
  • any warnings are addressed More about checking the release status of your version
Release a version

You must have Space admin permissions to enable the releases feature for your space. Enable releases and versions

You must have Space admin or Manage versions permissions to create or edit a version. More about space permissions

  • From your space navigation, select the Releases tab. If Releases doesn’t appear in your navigation, see how to enable the releases feature.
  • Select the version from the list.
  • In the top-right, select the version’s current status (for example, Unreleased) and then select Release.
  • Choose what to do with any unresolved work items, and enter a release date.
  • Select Release.
Kanban boards in company-managed spaces

If you are using kanban in a company-managed space, you can release a version via the kanban board. Select the Release menu above your board to see a list of unreleased versions. The list will only include versions that have been assigned to one or more of the work items in the ‘Done’ column on your board. Select a version to release, enter the details in the release dialog, and then select ‘Release’. Work items will disappear from the board once all their fix versions have been released.

More about managing a release.

Use the release page to check the progress of a version

Use the release page to check the progress of a version

Versions represent points in time for your space. They can be used to schedule how features are rolled out to your customers, or as a way to organize work that has been completed for the space.

Versions in Jira Software are managed using the releases feature. How to enable the releases feature

To check the progress of a version:

  • From your space navigation, select Releases.
  • Select your version from the list.
  • Check the progress of your work items and related work in the Progress section. Using the progress bar, you can see a summary of work item status (done, complete, warnings) and related work status (added, placeholder).
Approve or decline the work in a version

If you’ve been added as an approver, you can approve or decline the work in the release.

Approval indicates you’re happy for the release to go ahead, and declining means you think changes are needed first.

  • From your space navigation, select Releases.
  • Select a release from the list.
  • Find your name in the Approvers section, and select Waiting.
  • Select either Approve or Decline (and add an optional reason if you decline). Your approval status will now be updated in the approval section, and you can update it again by selecting it.
View warnings

Warnings appear when your work item data is potentially out of sync with your development data.

Warnings appear if:

  • Jira Software is connected to your development tools (like Bitbucket, GitHub, GitLab, or Jenkins).

  • Find out about integrating with development tools

  • You have the View development tools permission.

  • Find out about Jira permissions

  • Warnings are enabled. To view the warning types that are enabled, go to the Work items section of your version, select the actions icon () on the right, then the settings icon (). You must be a space admin to do this. Depending on which development tools are connected to Jira Software, you can view different warning types:

  • Open pull requests (a work item is marked as done, but it has an open pull request).

  • Unreviewed code (a work item is marked as done, but its commits aren’t part of a pull request or code review).

  • Failing builds (a work item is marked as done but it’s linked to a failing build).

  • Open reviews (a work item is marked as done but it has open reviews).

  • Open review warnings will only appear if you are using a Fisheye-Crucible integration with Jira Software.

View development information on the release page

The release page will display the commits, branches, pull requests, builds, and deployments related to each work item in your version, provided that:

  • Jira Software is connected to your development tools, and
  • your team includes work item keys in their branch names, commit messages, and pull requests.
Commits, branches, and pull requests

If you’ve connected a source code management (SCM) tool like Bitbucket or GitHub, you can view the number of commits, branches, and pull requests associated with each work item in the Work items section.

We’ll also show the pull request status (e.g. open, merged, or declined). Select a piece of dev info to view a detailed dialog with links to the commits, branches, or pull requests in your SCM tool.

Builds

If you’ve connected a build tool like Bitbucket, GitHub, or GitLab, you’ll see the build status for each work item in your version in the Work items section.

We’ll show an icon to indicate whether the build was successful , failed, or unknown. Click on a build icon to view a detailed dialog with links to the associated pipelines in your build tool.

Deployments

If you’ve connected a CI/CD tool like Bitbucket Pipelines, GitHub, GitLab, or Jenkins, you’ll see the deployment status of each work item in your version in the Work items section.

We’ll show an icon to indicate whether a work item has been deployed successfully and a label to tell you what environment it’s been deployed to. Click on a deployment status to view a detailed dialog with links to the associated pipelines in your CI/CD tool.

Feature flags

If you’ve connected a feature management tool like LaunchDarkly or Split, you’ll see a flag icon and a percentage in the Work items section.

The icon indicates whether a flag is enabled or disabled, and the percentage shows the current rollout of a particular flag. If you have more than one feature flag linked to a work item, the number of flags linked will be shown instead of a rollout percentage. Hover over the icon to see quick info about connected flags, and select it to view full details.

Release a version

You must have space admin permissions to release a version.

To release a version:

  • From your space navigation, select Releases.
  • Select the version from the list.
  • Select the version’s current status (for example, Unreleased) and then select Release.
  • Confirm what to do with any unresolved work items, and enter a release date.
  • Select Release.

Resolve warnings in your plans

Troubleshoot warnings on your timeline in your plan

Troubleshoot warnings on your timeline in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

As you schedule work for your teams, your plan warns you of any scheduling errors which are referred to as off-track dependencies. This page discusses common causes of warnings and how to resolve them.

Child work item starts before parent work item (or ends after)

If your plan is set to roll up dates, the parent work item automatically updates. But if you don’t, and you manually set dates for child work items which don’t align with the dates of their parent, your plan generates a warning to highlight the conflict. This also applies when using sprint dates to schedule work items.

To resolve this:

  • reschedule child work items so they occur within the dates of the parent
  • change the dates of the parent work item to reflect that of the child issue or
  • roll-up dates in your plan
Work item starts or ends after its due date

When scheduling work items, your plan uses the Due date field by default, though you can change which dates your plan uses to schedule work items. If an issue source in your plan uses a different date field, and you then schedule a work item to end after the date in that field, you’ll see this warning to alert you of the conflicting date fields.

To resolve this:

  • add a column to your plan to show the date field configured on your work items
  • open the work item and change the date field on the work item directly
  • reschedule work item on your plan to align with the date in the second date field
Open work item has passed its inferred/assigned end date

This warning tells you that you have open work items that are past their due date in your plan. The only difference between these two warnings is that one refers to work items using inferred rolled-up dates, and the other refers to those using manually set dates.

To resolve this:

  • change the work item status to DONE
  • move the work item to a different sprint
  • change the work item’s end date
Work item scheduled outside of its assigned sprint

You’ll only see this warning if you have

  • work items with a sprint assignment and manually set dates, and

  • those dates fall outside the dates of the assigned sprint To resolve this:

  • move the work item to a different sprint

  • change the work item’s dates to align with the sprint

Kanban work item assigned to a sprint

Sprints are only used by teams that plan work using the Scrum method of work planning. So you’ll see this warning if you assign a work item from a Kanban board to a sprint.

To resolve this:

  • remove any sprint assignment from Kanban work items

Save changes made in a plan

Save changes made in a plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

To save the changes made in your plan, you’ll need the Plans administrator permission as well as permission to edit the space in Jira.

As you build your plan, changes to work items or Teams are in a draft state until you’re ready to save them. This allows you to explore different planning outcomes without effecting existing work items. When you’re ready, you can save edits made in your plan so they update within the space. Jump to the list of changes you might see in the Unsaved changes modal.

Changes are listed by title. If there’s multiple updates to a work item, the number of changes shows in the What changed column. Select the field in this column to view all of the changes made to that work item.

To save work done to date, select the changes you’d like to save and click the Save changes button. You can also filter changes in the Unsaved changes modal. Changes will update in the background as you continue working on the plan.

Changes remains visible in the Unsaved changes modal until you:

  • Save changes
  • discard, by selecting the change, then Discard selected changes You can also send notifications to those watching work items by using the Send update notifications checkbox in the lower left corner.
Changes you can find in this modal

The Unsaved changes modal will display following change types made inyour plan:

Unless you’re planning with multiple scenarios, the changes below marked with an * have no impact outside of your plan. You can save them to get rid of the unsaved changes markers in your plan, or ignore them. Changes will remain in the Review changes modal until they are saved or discarded.

If you are planning with multiple scenarios, these changes will be applied to all scenarios in your plan.

Updates to work items
  • create a work item in your plan
  • change a work item:
    • estimate
    • team assignment
    • summary
    • scheduled dates or sprint assignment
    • value in a custom field
  • remove a work item from your plan*
Updates to teams
Atlassian teams

Atlassian teams can be used outside of your plan as soon as they’re created. The changes related to them that appear in the Review changes modal are only important if you’re planning with multiple scenarios.

  • create or add a new team in your plan*
  • change an existing team’s name, sprint capacity, or sprint length*
  • remove a team from your plan*
Plan-only teams
  • create a plan-only team in your plan
    • Plan-only teams need to be saved using the Review changes modal in order to promote them to Atlassian teams.
  • edit team membership*
  • change an existing team’s name, sprint capacity, or sprint length*
  • deleting a plan-only team*
Updates to releases
  • editing a release’s
    • name
    • description
    • dates
  • creating a new single-space release
  • creating a new cross-space release*
  • removing a single-space release*
    • To delete a single-space release, you’ll need to go to the space in which it was created.
  • deleting a cross-space*

Troubleshoot warnings in Unsaved changes modal

Troubleshoot warnings in Unsaved changes modal

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

In the Unsaved changes modal, you may see warning icons in the far left column. We recommend resolving before saving changes to Jira Software.

This work item has been added to an active sprint

If you add or remove a work item from an active sprint, you’ll see a warning in the Unsaved changes modal informing you that this will change the scope of the sprint.

There’s no resolving this work item as it won’t break your plan, but it’s a heads up that sprint capacity will be affected.

Required custom fields in Jira Software work items

If your Jira Software work items have required custom fields, but these fields weren’t added to your plan, you’ll see a warning. Since these fields are required, you’ll need to either add them to your plan or turn off the required field in Jira Software.

Custom fields not supported for work types or spaces in plan

If you set a value for a custom field that hasn’t yet been set up in Jira Software, you won’t be able to save this change from your plan. If you need this change to be saved, ask your Jira Software admin to configure this custom field in your instance.

Child work items not saved to Jira Software

If you’ve created child work items in your plan, the parent work item needs to be saved in Jira Software as well. Since the child work item is dependent on values inherited from the parent, the child work item can’t be saved on its own.

The work item can’t be updated due to the field association

“Some fields no longer apply to its space, or work type, and need to be added again. Discard the change if it’s no longer required.”

When you see this error message, it indicates that some changes can not be saved because the field is no longer valid for this space or work type. This can happen if the field configuration has changed.

Read more about field configuration.
