Use Jira business projects for finance projects

Use Jira business projects for finance projects

This page is for business spaces

To check whether you’re in a business or software space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

Finance teams are responsible for a lot. They manage company finances, reconcile invoices and payments, and keep the books balanced.

One area that business spaces can help with is the tracking of internal purchases. When there are other departments involved in requests, business spaces can help centralize everything for better control.

Check out How do I build the workflow I want? to find out more about updating workflows.

Track all your equipment

Create a work item for each purchase request, or for each item or service being purchased (if they are large). Your board will always give you a clear view of where something is in the purchasing process, and lets you see what’s coming up.

Manage your purchase paperwork

Attach quotes, diagrams, photos, and other relevant documents to each work item.

Purchase tracking

Some other suggestions for tracking purchases:

  • Use labels on each work item to track the location of large items that are tracked as assets. Labels can help you filter work items later.
  • Set due dates to review service agreements and claim upgrades.
  • Use components to track by department, so you can see where the main volume of requests is coming from.

Use Jira business projects for marketing projects

Use Jira business projects for marketing projects

This page is for business spaces

To check whether you’re in a business or software space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

Marketing teams do a huge range of activities within a business, from basic promotion planning to executing large multi-channel campaigns, and everything in between.

Often, these activities involve developing content for the business.

Jira business spaces come with a content management project template, with a workflow to help you develop marketing assets and copy.

Track all content types

You can treat each item in your business spaces as one piece of content (like a marketing email), or you can use one item to track content activity (a website update, for example).

All your content is trackable on the board, so you can easily see what’s in progress, in review, and queued up for approval.

Modify to suit your process

Depending on how you manage content in your business, you may want to change this workflow to include additional steps. For example, you may want to add a pre-publishing process.

Capture your assets

You can easily attach drafts and review copies to each work item representing your content. You will still need to version control, but with a full history of activities and dates, keeping track is so much easier.

Use due dates

To avoid missing publishing deadlines, set due dates on your work items. You can set a due date per item, or, to manage all the lead-up activity, set due dates on any subtasks as well.

Use Jira for HR projects

Use Jira for HR projects

Jira comes packed with useful templates for a wide range of work tracking, and lets you update them to suit your needs. The recruitment project template helps you track candidates through your HR recruitment process.

Keep track of candidates

Create a work item for each candidate you’re considering hiring, then track the progress of their recruitment on the board. Get a quick overview of who’s been interviewed, who’s been screened, and more.

Manage all the files

Open the candidate’s work item, then select the paperclip icon to attach relevant documents. This might include a resume, references, cover letter, and their portfolio. You can also use internal comments to make notes about interviews and other details.

Make it work for you

Not all recruitment processes are the same. Here are some common ways to make it fit your process:

  • Customize the workflow to suit your recruitment process. For example, you may want to record three rounds of interviews — pre-screening, general, and shortlist. See Customize your project.
  • Create a work item for each role, then use subtasks to track candidates. This might be useful if you frequently have open roles and want to track overall recruiting in one place. See Create and work with issues.
  • Modify the board. Use the board to create the view you want of your recruitment stream. See Working with boards.

Use Jira for operations spaces

Use Jira for operations spaces

This page is for business spaces

To check whether you’re in a business or software space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

Operations teams do all kinds of projects, ranging from office moves to site audits.

The project management template in Jira business projects is an ideal base for managing short-term and delivery-based projects.

About the template
  • Ideal for projects of any size, any duration, and for any deliverable
  • Can be used to track milestones and set time limits for activities
  • Easily customized to include additional steps, such as review, blocked, etc.
Stay on top of everything

You’re able to view the status of every work item on the board, including who’s working on what, and if it’s overdue.

Add milestones using versions

Projects often have ‘checkpoints’ or milestones that need to be reached in order to keep the broader project on track. In business spaces you can use versions as milestones. Once you have versions set up, you can organize work into different versions.

See Organizing work with versions.

Report back to management

Projects are usually made up of well-defined, specific, measurable activities that have one major deliverable or goal. This makes project reporting even more critical to ensuring things get delivered on time. Jira business spaces include built-in reporting, but you can also use your dashboard and custom filters based on your searches to monitor activities.

Customize

Jira is highly customizable. Some common customizations include:

  • Adding additional steps to the workflow (such as approvals) to fit the way a project works
  • Changing the layout of work items to capture specific information
  • Use labels to track groups of work items related to project phases or workstreams

Business spaces in Jira are packed with useful templates for a wide range of work tracking, and lets you update them to suit your needs. The lead tracking space template helps your sales team track leads through to closing.

Keep track of opportunities

Set up approvals in Jira

Set up approval steps

Set up approval steps

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

Adding an approval step to a workflow means that specific team members must approve work items before they move along to the next status in that workflow.

To require approval for a work item, you first need to ensure the right fields are available, and then you must add an approval step to the relevant workflow status.

Create the right fields for entering approvers

Some projects come with an Approvers field for adding individual approvers, and an Approver groups field for adding groups of approvers. If your project doesn’t already have these fields, you’ll need to add them as custom fields. You might also want to create more custom fields if your workflow has more than one approval step, or if you want the field to have a different name in the work item view.

You must have the following to do the things described in this section.

Role: Site admin

To add a new custom field for approvals:

  • Select Settings (), then Work items.
  • Select Fields, then Create field.
  • In the Field type dropdown:
    • To add individual approvers, select User Picker (single user or multiple users).
    • To add groups of approvers, select Group Picker (multiple groups).
  • Name your field and add a description (optional).
  • Select Create.
  • Find your new field in the list of fields and select More actions (), then select Add field to screen.
  • Select the screens where you want the field to be displayed, then select Update. What are work item screens?
Add an approval step to a workflow status

When you add an approval step to a workflow status, you can choose:

  • When a work item requires approval,
  • Who needs to approve the work item, and who can’t approve it, and
  • What happens when the work item is approved or declined. You must have the following to do the things described in this section:

Role: Site admin (if the workflow is shared with other projects), or

Permissions: Edit workflows (if the workflow is not shared across other projects)

To add an approval step to a workflow:

  • Next to your project’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (), then Project settings.
  • Select Workflows from the sidebar.
  • Select Edit workflow next to the workflow you want to add an approval to.
  • Select the status you want to add an approval step to.
  • Select Add () next to Approvals.
  • Select an Approver source. If you don’t see the custom field you want to get approvers from, make sure its Applicable context is set to Global. Edit the context of a custom field.
  • Select More options:
    • Choose a Number of approvers. You can set this up so that approval is required from everyone in a group (or everyone assigned as an approver), or from a specific number of people.
    • Under Exclude approvers from, select the fields you want to exclude approvers from. Any users who appear in the fields you select here will not be able to approve work items that use this workflow.
  • Select what statuses the work item should transition to if it’s approved or declined.
  • Select Save.
  • Select Publish draft. You must use the new workflow editor to add an approval step to a workflow status. What’s the new workflow editor?
Enable the approver field for work items

You must have the following to do the things described in this section:

Role: Site admin (if the screen is shared with other projects), or

Permissions: Manage work item layout (if the screen is not shared across other projects)

Before you can add approvers to work items, you must add the approvers field to the work item type’s screen. Find out more about screens.

You can do this by adding the approver field to the work item layout. Here’s how:

  • Next to the name of your project in the sidebar, select More actions (), then Project settings.
  • Select Work items, then Layout.
  • Find the work type(s) whose layout you want to view and select Edit work item layout.
  • Drag and drop fields to add the field to both the layout and the screen.
  • Select Save changes. Read more about configuring the layout of work item.

What are approvals?

What are approvals?

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

Approvals allow you to manage work items that need to be approved before they can move to the next status in their workflow.

This can be useful for various types of work, including the following:

  • Marketing content might need to be approved by brand and legal teams before publication.
  • Multiple stakeholders, including the technical lead, product manager, and security team, might need to approve software changes of a certain complexity.
  • Project deliverables may need to be approved by the client stakeholder before being marked as complete. You can add an approval step to any status in a company-managed project’s workflow. How to manage workflows in Jira
How approvals work

You must be an admin to set up approvals in Jira. Here’s what happens once you’ve added an approval step to a workflow status:

  • A team member creates a work item.
  • The work item transitions to a status that has an approval step.
  • The designated approvers are notified via email that they need to approve or decline the work item.
  • The approvers approve or decline the work item directly within Jira, adding any necessary comments or feedback.
  • The work item transitions to the next status in the workflow, and the person who created the work item is notified of any comments that the approver added. The approvals feature is only available on Premium editions in Jira.

Set up Jira Cloud

Automate what build and deployment events are sent from Jenkins to Jira

Automate what build and deployment events are sent from Jenkins to Jira

This topic details an optional step in the process of connecting a Jenkins server to a Jira Cloud site using Jenkins for Jira. This step is not necessary to complete a connection and get data flowing, and relies on a good working knowledge of how Jenkins pipelines are made. Some teams may find it useful when setting up a connection to a Jenkins server running a large number of pipelines.

When using the Jenkins for Jira app to send build and deployment events from a Jenkins server to Jira, the Atlassian Jira Cloud plugin on your Jenkins server will look for explicit instructions in your server pipelines to send data to Jira. Specifically, it will look for these instructions in the Jenkinsfiles that define those pipelines.

These instructions are detailed in the set up guide generated in Jira when you connect to a Jenkins server.

In addition, when setting up the Atlassian Jira Cloud plugin on your Jenkins server, a Jenkins admin can opt to enable the following advanced options:

  • Send builds automatically
  • Send deployments automatically When these options are selected, the Atlassian Jira Cloud plugin will look for explicit instructions in your pipelines Jenkinsfiles, as well as particular naming conventions for build and deployment stages in those. If it finds either of these, it will send data to connected Jira sites. For more information see How Jenkins for Jira works.
Is automation appropriate for your team?

Some teams, which use a consistent naming convention for build and deployment stages when writing their Jenkinsfiles, may find using stage names more convenient that writing specific instructions into each build and deployment stage, especially if their Jira spaces utilize a large number of Jenkins pipelines.

To find out if this is an appropriate option for your team, reach out to your developers and ask:

  • Who maintains the Jenkinsfiles relevant to each Jira space?
  • Does your team want:
    • Granular control of each pipeline that sends data to Jira, or
    • Jenkins to send build and deployment updates to Jira every time it runs a pipeline. Once you know who maintains the Jenkinsfiles for each Jira space, ask those team members:
  • When writing Jenkinsfiles, do you have a consistent naming structure for build and deployment stages?
    • For example:
      • Are all build stages named stage('build')?
      • Are all deployment stages named stage('deploy to staging'), stage('deploy to prod'), and so on
  • If so, what are those naming structures?
Setup options

Depending on your team’s answers to the questions above, here’s whether enabling these options is appropriate to your team:

Send build data automatically

This setting covers how Jenkins sends build events to Jira.

Based on how your team uses Jenkins, here’s what to select:

If your team:

  • Wants Jenkins to send build updates to Jira every time it runs a pipeline.

  • Has a consistent naming structure for build stages when writing Jenkinsfiles.

    • For example, if every build stage is called stage('build') You or your Jenkins admin should:

  • Enable this option

  • Enter a regular expression filter matching your team’s build stage name structure

    • For example:
      • If every build stage is called stage('build')
      • Enter the regular expression ^build$ If your team:

  • Want Jenkins to send build and deployment updates to Jira every time it runs a pipeline.

  • Do not have a consistent naming structure for build stages when writing Jenkinsfiles. You or your Jenkins admin should:

  • Enable this option

  • Leave the regular expression filter field empty If your team:

  • Want granular control of each pipeline that sends data to Jira You or your Jenkins admin should:

  • Disable this option

Send deployment data automatically

This setting covers how Jenkins sends deployment events to Jira.

Based on how your team uses Jenkins, here’s what to tell your Jenkins admin:

If your team:

  • Have a consistent naming structure for deployment stages when writing Jenkinsfiles.

    • For example, if every deployment stage is called stage('deploy to staging'), stage('deploy to prod'), and so on

  • Want every pipeline to send deployment data to Jira You or your Jenkins admin should:

  • Enable this option

  • Enter a regular expression filter matching the names your teams use for deployment stages

    • For example:
      • If every deployment stage is called stage('deploy to staging'), stage('deploy to prod'), and so on
      • Enter the regular expression^deploy to (?<envName>.*)$
        • Use (?<envName>.*) in place of specific stage names like ‘staging’ or ‘prod’ to let Jenkins extract environment names and display these in Jira If your team:

  • Does not have a consistent naming structure for deployment stages when writing Jenkinsfiles, or

  • Want granular control of each pipeline that sends data to Jira You or your Jenkins admin should:

  • Disable this option

Quick space creation with bundles

Quick space creation with bundles

With bundles, you can now effortlessly create between 2 to 6 spaces at once, streamlining your space creation process and minimizing the need for repetitive manual tasks. Whether you’re working in Jira or Jira Service Management, bundles guarantee a smooth space creation experience.

Choose from two pre-set bundles: the Marketing team or the IT team bundle. But if these don’t fit your requirements, you have the flexibility to customize and create your own bundle.

Create a bundle

There are a few ways you can create a bundle, one way is to:

  • Next to Spaces in the sidebar, select Create space ().

  • Select Bundles. Another way to create a bundle is to:

  • Next to Spaces in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Manage spaces.

  • Select Templates, then More templates.

  • Select Bundles.

Use preset bundles

The management type and access you applies to all of the spaces in your bundle. The management type can’t be changed later (but everything else can!). If you wish to do so, you’ll need to create a new space. More about management types and changing management types

  • Next to Spaces in the sidebar, select Create space ().
  • On the Review spaces in your bundle screen
    • Rename a space, select Edit.
    • Choose their management type, and update the access settings.
  • Select Create 3 spaces.
  • Leave the page open — it should only take a couple of minutes. Once creates, we’ll take you to the board view of your first space.
Build a custom bundle
  • Next to Spaces in the sidebar, select Create space ().
  • Select Build a bundle.
  • Use the Select space templates button to choose 2-6 space templates for your custom bundle.
  • Use the template selector to search, select, and remove templates from your bundle. Once selected, hit Confirm.
  • Next, add names for spaces, choose their management type, and update the access settings.
    • To rename a space, select Edit.
    • Choose their management type, and update the access settings.
  • Select Create spaces.
  • Leave the page open — it should only take a couple of minutes. Once creates, we’ll take you to the board view of your first space.
Get the most out of bundles
Invite people to spaces relevant to them

Avoid clutter and maintain efficient collaboration by inviting team members to spaces that align with their roles and responsibilities. This helps improve focus, engagement, and overall productivity on spaces across your organisation.

Navigate effectively across spaces in your bundle

To make things easier for you, we’ll add all the spaces in your bundles to the Shortcuts view in the horizontal navigation.

Use these shortcuts to quickly navigate between spaces within your bundle, without losing momentum. More about shortcuts.

Set up your plan and change its settings

Add or remove fields from your plan

Add or remove fields from your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Users need Plan administrator permissions to add fields to a plan.

Along with the columns available by default in your plan, you can also show associated fields from any of your plan’s work sources.

To add columns to your plan based on fields from your work sources:

  • Next to your plan’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Plan settings.
  • Select Timeline, then add a field on the table labeled Fields added on the timeline.
  • Use Add fields to select the field you want to add, then select Add to finalize your choice. Remove fields from your plan using the icon on this page. When you remove it, any unsaved changes to this field are discarded.

You can’t remove a field that’s being used to schedule work items in your plan. First, you’ll need to select a different date field in Plan settings.

Field association with spaces and work types

To display and edit a field in your plan, the field must be associated with both the space and the work type. You can manage these associations in Jira by updating your field configurations and field configuration schemes.

Fields in team-managed spaces can only be used for work items within the same space. Read more about team-managed space limitations in plans

To check which fields are available for your plan:

  • Next to your plan’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (), then Plan settings.

  • Select Timeline.

  • Look for the column called Applies to work items in. This shows the number of spaces available for each field.

  • Select the number in this column to see a list of spaces where the field is available. If a field isn’t available for a space, it will appear as disabled in your plan and you won’t be able to edit it. When you hover over a disabled field, you’ll see a tooltip with one of the following explanations:

  • “This field has not been associated with this space” - This means the field isn’t included in the field configuration scheme used by the space.

  • “This field is not used in this space for this work type” - This means the field isn’t available for the specific work type in the space’s field configuration scheme. To make a field available, you’ll need to update the field configuration.

Change how work is estimated in your plan

Change how work is estimated in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

You can choose whether your plan estimates work items using:

  • hours
  • days
  • story points Story points can only be selected if all teams in your plan are scrum teams. If your plan includes a kanban team, the option for story points won’t appear. What are story points?

Story points and time-based estimates (hours and days) are not interchangeable. Changing from one to the other erases any unsaved work item estimations.

To change the estimation units in your plan:

  • Next to your plan’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Plan settings.
  • On the Estimation and scheduling page, select whether you’d like your plan to be estimated in Hours, Days, or Story Points.
  • If you haven’t already, add the field that your work items use to estimate work to your plan. Add fields to your plan

Change how your plan handles dependencies in the same iteration

Change how your plan handles dependencies in the same iteration

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Planners have the option to change whether dependent work items that have been scheduled to the same iteration show as off-track dependencies. This applies when scheduling work by sprints on the timeline and in the program board.

Most planners won’t need to touch this setting. However, we recommend turning this setting off if you’re using the auto-scheduler.

To change how concurrent dependencies are displayed in your plan:

  • Next to your plan’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Plan settings.
  • On the Estimation and scheduling page, use the checkbox next to Dependent work items can be scheduled to the same iteration.

Change the date field used to schedule work items in your plan

Change the date field used to schedule work items in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

By default, your plan uses the Due dates field when scheduling work items. You can choose to replace this with any date field that’s been added to your plan.

Looking at your timeline, the date fields that are used to schedule work items are marked with a D in the Date column. If your dates have an S next to them, then your plan is scheduling work based based on sprint dates. If your dates have an R next to them, then your plan is scheduling work based on release dates.

To change which date field your plan uses:

  • Next to your plan’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Plan settings.
  • On the Estimation and scheduling page, use the drop down menus to select the fields you want to use to schedule the start and end dates of your work items.

Configure the auto-scheduler in your plan

Configure the auto-scheduler in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Those with the Plan Edit permission can configure which fields the auto-scheduler has permission to overwrite. The auto-scheduler can overwrite values in the Releases, Teams, and Sprint fields, though it won’t overwrite any data for issues in an active sprint.

To change the auto-scheduler settings:

  • Next to your plan’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Plan settings. Then choose Auto-scheduler.
    • If you don’t see Auto-scheduler listed in the side nav, you’ll need to turn the auto-scheduler on using the Features page.
  • Adjust what you would like the Auto-scheduler to include or exclude from your plan.
  • When you’re ready, use Preview results to begin the auto-scheduling process. Read more about using the auto-scheduling tool.

Delete or archive your plan

Delete or archive your plan

When you’re done with a plan, you can delete or archive it.

Archive a plan

Archive a plan you’ve completed to remove it from your active plans. Once archived, your plan won’t show in the Plans dropdown menu and can’t be edited. They won’t be scheduled for deletion, and can be restored at any point.

To archive a plan, select the next to your plan name then choose Archive.

Delete a plan

If you don’t want to keep a completed plan, you can move it to the trash. Like archived plans, plans in the trash plans won’t show in the Plans dropdown menu and can’t be edited. However, plans in the trash are automatically deleted after 60 days. Until that point, they can be restored.

To delete a plan, select the next to your plan name then choose Move to trash.

Restore deleted or archived plans

All of the processes described in this section require the Plans Administrator permission.

You can restore archived plans or plans that were deleted fewer than 60 days ago. Once restored, they can be edited and shared like a normal plan.

To restore a deleted or archived plan:

  • Navigate to the Jira admin panel using the icon in the upper right of your screen and select Jira apps. Then:
    • to restore an archived plan, select Archive.
    • to restore a deleted plan, select Trash.
  • Select the next to the plan name you want to restore, then choose Restore.

Duplicate your plan

Duplicate your plan

Instead of creating a new plan from scratch, you can duplicate an existing plan.

To duplicate the plan you’re currently on:

  • From the Roadmap view, navigate to settings using the next to your plan name > Duplicate.
  • Choose your new plan’s name, then select Confirm. You can also duplicate a different plan from the View all plans page by selecting the on the right side of the screen.

This new plan inherits the following:

  • plan settings, such as:
    • work sources
    • exclusion rules
    • scheduling configurations
    • permissions
    • custom fields
  • view settings, such as:
    • how work items are grouped
    • any dependency settings
    • any coloring options
  • any custom saved views created in your original plan
  • all filters currently applied to your plan.

How your plan handles timezones

How your plan handles timezones

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

In your plan, target start dates and target end dates are independent from local timezone settings. However, in Jira, due dates and custom dates are adjusted based on the local timezone settings of the user. This means that users looking at the same issues in your plan and Jira may see different date values based on their timezone settings.

Limitations of team-managed spaces in your plan

Limitations of team-managed spaces in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

You can add team-managed spaces to your plan like you would any other work source, though there’s a few differences to keep in mind as you’re planning.

Fields made in team-managed spaces can only be applied to work items from the same space

If you want to use a field made in a team-managed space across multiple spaces, we recommend having your Jira administrator convert it to a field that can be shared.

Work items from team-managed spaces need to stay in the space in which they were created

You can’t move a level 0 work item (such as a task or story) from a team-managed space to a parent in a company-managed space.

Rules that remove work items from your plan don’t apply to team-managed spaces

When tailoring your plan scope, you can automatically remove work items from your plan based on criteria like status, work item type and more. Read how to refine your plan scope

These rules don’t apply to work items in team-managed spaces. Statuses and work types from team-managed spaces, even if they’re the same as their company-managed counterparts, won’t appear in the search box.

Limits on plan size

Limits on plan size

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

To prevent Jira from timing out, there are limits on how how much data your plan can include. Some limits can’t be exceeded, like the work item limits, while others negatively impact your plan’s performance or usability. Read how to improve the performance of your plans.

Work item limits

A single plan can load up to 10,000 work items. At that point, you’ll begin to see warnings that your plan performance will be affected.

For larger projects, consider spreading the work across multiple plans.

Team limits

While there is no enforced limit on the number of teams that can be included in your plan, we recommend adding no more than 50 teams. If you add more, some teams won’t display on the Teams tab and you’ll need to enter the team name in the search box.

Limits on work sources

Your plan can handle up to four work sources with no problems. The impact of work sources beyond this depends on their complexity. However, your plan can only span 100 Jira spaces, including those that are pulled in as part of boards and filters.

If you hit the space limit in your plan, try adjusting your board or filter’s JQL to include fewer spaces. Alternatively, if you only need a handful of work items from a work source, consider moving those work items to a different space or using exclusion rules to only pull in the relevant work items.

Performance recommendations for your plan

Performance recommendations for your plan

Your plan loads in three steps:

  • Jira reads the data stored in your work items.
  • It compares that data to any unsaved changes held in your plan.
  • Then it runs calculations (such as capacity planning and dependencies) to generate your plan. The larger and more complex your plan is, the more effort it takes to load your plan. So while we’re constantly optimizing the load times of plans, the best way to speed up your plan’s performance is to keep it as focused as possible.
Optimize your JQL

All JQL queries are not created equal. JQL uses a strict logic that does exactly what you tell it to do, whether or not it’s the most efficient way. These inefficiencies can add up, causing performance issues in your plans.

If you’re using a JQL query as part of your plan (whether it’s as part of a filter or custom field), make sure that it’s written in a way that’s not causing more churn in your plans. Find out about how to optimize your JQL queries.

Remove work item sources

Your plan can handle up to four work item sources with no problems. The impact of issues sources beyond this depends on their complexity. Alternatively, if you only need a handful of issues from an issue source, consider moving those issues to a different space or using exclusion rules to only pull in the relevant issues.

Find out how to add or remove work item sources from your plan.

Limits on number of work items

All plans have a soft limit of 5,000 work items. You can exceed this number, but the performance of your plan will begin to suffer. For this reason, we recommend that you remove unnecessary work items, or consider breaking larger roadmaps into two separate plans.

Learn how to set an exclusion rule on your plan.

Remove work items belonging to old releases

By default, your plan adds all releases and fix versions in a space regardless of when they’re scheduled to happen. These extra releases might technically be relevant to your plan, but realistically slow down your plan’s performance. This is why we recommend that you either delete old releases in Jira, or use exclusion rules to focus on work items belonging to specific releases in your plan.

Find out how to set an exclusion rule on your plan.

Remove excess sprints

As mentioned at the start of the page, capacity planning calculations are done entirely in your plan when you load it. The more sprints that are included in your plan, the more effort required, leading to longer load times.

To remove old sprints from your plan, use the Exclude any completed work items after field in the exclusion rules, or delete old sprints from your boards in Jira.

Remove individual work items from your plan

Remove individual work items from your plan

By default, your plan contains all work items from the spaces in your plan scope. Along with using rules to remove work items, users can remove individual work items using Bulk actions menu on your timeline. Edit multiple work items at once

Work that’s been removed this way can be re-added by plan admins from the Work in your plan page. To view and re-add these work items to your plan:

  • Next to your plan’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Plan settings.
  • Go to the Work in your plan page, then select the Removed work items tab.
  • Select the work you want to re-add, then select Save.
Can’t find a work item in your plan?

If you can’t find a work item in your plan, you can search for it using the search box on the Work in your plan page.

Enter the missing work item’s entire key to see if it’s:

  • in your plan scope
  • removed by a rule or user or
  • included in your plan but hidden by a timeline filter This search requires the full work item key. Partial matches won’t work.

Remove work items from your plan using rules

Remove work items from your plan using rules

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

By default, your plan contains all work items from the spaces in your plan scope. You can create rules to remove work items based on:

  • work type (Story, Bug etc)
  • work status
  • the number of days since it was moved to a Done status
    • your plan defines completed work items differently than the rest of Jira
  • the releases to which they’re assigned Plans users can also remove work items individually from the timeline.

To remove work items in your plan using rules:

These rules only apply to work items from company-managed spaces.

  • Next to your plan’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Plan settings.
  • Go to the Work in your plan page, then select the Removed work items tab. To remove work items based on:
    • work type, status, or number of days since it was marked Done, select View rules. In the panel that opens, choose the criteria by which you want to remove work items from your plan.
    • their assigned release, select View releases. The releases selected on this view have been removed from your plan. Select a release to remove it, or deselect one to add it back. If releases have been turned off in your plan, you won’t see this option.
  • When you’re ready, select Save.
Can’t find a work item in your plan?

If you can’t find a work item in your plan, you can search for it using the search box on the Work in your plan page.

Enter the missing work item’s entire key to see if it’s:

  • in your plan scope
  • removed by a rule or user or
  • included in your plan but hidden by a timeline filter This search requires the full work item key. Partial matches won’t work.

By default, work items will be removed once they have been marked as Done for more than 30 days. To update this:

  • Next to your plan’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Plan settings.
  • Select Work in your plan, then select Removed work items.
  • Select View rules.
  • In the panel that opens, select the box under Remove work marked DONE more than and enter your preferred number of days.
  • Select Save.

Types of permissions in your plan

Types of permissions in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Plans has a separate permissions model from that found in the rest of Jira. However, administrators can automatically grant plans permissions to users based on their Jira global permissions. Find out how to change permissions in your plan based on Jira permissions.

To change who can view and edit this plan, you must have the GLOBAL_BROWSE_USERS permission. Read more about global permissions in Jira.

The levels of access for plans are:

  • Plans administrator

  • Plans shared team management

  • Plans user

  • Plans viewer Things to note:

  • To set up the above levels of access for plans for your users, navigate to Jira admin settings, then Plans, and then Permissions and add the appropriate permission groups. More about default groups

  • Additionally, users must also have the necessary ‘Browse spaces’ permissions to access plans. More about space access and configuration permissions

  • In order to edit work items in plans, users need to have space permissions as well. See limit who can view your plan based on individual users or user groups.

Plans administrator

Users with this permission can perform all administrative functions in plans, including accessing any private plans.

By default, Jira administrators are automatically given Plans administrator access.

Shared team management

Users with this permission can access global team management and edit teams that are shared across plans. This permission is being made redundant with the introduction of our new Teams platform. Read more about these changes.

Plans user

Users with this permission can create plans and view plans they have access to. For plans they can access, they can also edit their work item sources, edit any work items in the plans, and save these edited work item details in Jira. This is the minimum permission level required to share a plan as an image, a .csv, or as an embedded element.

It’s possible for a user to have the Plans user permission, but lack the permission to edit a space included in the plan. If this is the case, the user won’t be able to save their changes using the Review changes button.

Plans viewer

Users with this permission can browse and view plans in read-only mode, but can’t update or change any plan details. They also can’t access to export a plan to an image, .csv, or as an embedded element.

View and change the scope of work in your plan

View and change the scope of work in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

To add or change the work in your plan:

  • Next to your plan’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Plan settings.
  • Go to the Work in your plan page, and select Edit plan scope. Use the menus on this page to add a space, board, or filter that contains the work items you want to see in your plan.
  • When you’re done, select Save to update your plan scope. By default, all work items from these sources are included in your plan. After the plan is created, you can remove work items individually from your timeline or based on rules. How to trim your plan scope
As you add or change what’s in your plan, remember to:
  • use boards if you intend to use capacity planning
  • make sure that the plan owner has permission to edit work items in all work sources You can use Rovo to add a space or board to a plan. Open Rovo Chat and enter /add-plan-work-source, followed by an instruction like “Add the Marketing board to this plan”.

Similarly, you can use Rovo to remove a space or board from your plan by entering /remove-plan-work-source and telling Rovo which space or board to remove.

Share and export your plan

Create a static image of your plan

Create a static image of your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Create a flat image of your timeline to include in presentations or emails. All images include a legend that tells viewers how to read your plan, making it ideal for sharing with those who aren’t familiar with Jira.

This option is only available on the timeline view of your plan.

Before creating the plan timeline image, adjust your filters and view settings to show the issues and details on your timeline that you want to include. Only the data visible on your timeline will be included in the exported image.

You can export up to 500 issues in one image. For larger data sets, we recommend either exporting your data as a .csv file, or creating multiple images of your plan. Find out how to export your data in .csv format.

To export or share your plan, you need to have Plans administrator or Plan user permissions. Read more about plan permissions.

To create a static image of your plan:

  • From your plan, select Share , then choose Export.
  • Select Export an image of your timeline view (.png).
  • Use the menus at the top of the modal to decide
    • how wide you want your timeline to be
    • the date range you want to include
  • When you’re happy with your image, select Export to generate an image of what’s visible on your plan.

Embed your plan using an iFrame

Embed your plan using an iFrame

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

To export or share your plan, you need to have Plans administrator or Plan user permissions. Read more about plan permissions.

Embed a view of your plan in places that don’t support smart links, such as an internal wiki or reports, by adding an iFrame component to your page’s HTML. While it can be embedded in any page, viewers still need to have the permissions described below to view your plan.

This option is only available on the timeline view of your plan.

If you’re embedding your plan in a Confluence page or other Atlassian app, you can embed it using only the link.

When you share your plan, access is granted to viewers based on their global Jira permissions. For users to see your plan, they need:

  • access to your site or app
  • permission to view your plan as granted by the plan owner, who can limit access to their plans
  • the Plans viewer global permission
  • permissions to view the spaces and boards included in your plan Lacking these, those given the link won’t be able to access your plan, and embedded plans appear empty.

To create an <iframe> element of your plan:

  • In your plan, select Share (), then select iFrame.
  • Copy the generated iFrame using the Copy button.
  • Add this to the page’s HTML code.

Share and embed your plan in Atlassian apps

Share and embed your plan in Atlassian apps

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

The easiest way to share or embed your plan is to select Share from any view of your plan. From here, you can:

  • share your plan with other users in Jira or through Slack (if connected)

  • get a link that you can share with anyone

  • embed your plan in Atlassian apps

  • create an iFrame element that you can embed in an HTML page (from the timeline only)

  • create an image of your plan (from the timeline only)

  • export your plan data as a .csv file (from the timeline only) When you share your plan, access is granted to viewers based on their global Jira permissions. For users to see your plan, they need:

  • access to your site or app

  • the Plans viewer global permission

  • permissions to view the spaces and boards included in your plan Lacking these, those given the link won’t be able to access your plan, and embedded plans appear empty.

To export or share your plan, you need to have Plans administrator or Plan user permissions. Read more about plan permissions.

Share a link to your plan

To get a link you can share with anyone, select Copy link to copy the URL to your clipboard.

To share with other Jira users or Slack users:

  • From Share , select:
    • Share timeline to share your plan with other Jira users. Add the name of the person/people with whom you want to share your plan.
    • Share in Slack - to share your plan via Slack (if configured). Select the workspace and the channel or person to whom you want to send your plan.
  • Add an encouraging message to them.
  • Use Share to invite them to your plan.
Embed your plan

To embed your plan in an Atlassian app, such as Confluence, or a third-party app that is compatible with Smart links:

This process replaces the Jira Premium Plan macro in Confluence Cloud. Existing uses of the macro are still visible, but can’t be edited.

  • Save any changes you’ve made to your view. Any view changes that aren’t saved won’t show when you embed your plan.
  • From Share , select Copy link.
  • With the link in hand, navigate to the page in which you want to add your plan, and paste the link into the body section.
  • Select the link and choose the Embed view, then drag the vertical bars on either side of the window outward to expand it to the full width of the page. How to embed smart links in Confluence. Plans from Jira Cloud can no longer be shared in Confluence Data Center

Sharing a Plan from a Jira Cloud site on Confluence Data Center instances is no longer possible due to recent updates.

If this feature is something your site needs, register your interest on the public Feature Request ticket.

Create a board based on filters

Create a board based on filters

Jira allows you to create a company-managed board that displays work items from multiple spaces. Before you begin, you must have access to at least one saved work item filter — either your own filter, or one that someone else has shared with you. If you don’t, you need to create and save a new work item filter first. More about creating a filter using JQL.

If you’re working with a team-managed project, this is the required method for creating additional boards. Team-managed projects don’t support creating extra boards directly from within the project.

To create a board from an existing filter:

  • From the top navigation at the top of the page, select the search field (or press /) and select Go to all: Boards. Then select Create board in the upper right of the screen.

  • In the modal that appears, choose to either Create a Scrum board or Create a Kanban board, then choose Board from an existing Saved Filter.

  • Give your board a name, and choose which filter you want to use. This new board will be available to all users who have access to your chosen filter.

  • When you’re ready, select Create board. Another way you can create a board using an existing filter is by:

  • Hover your cursor over the company-managed software space in the sidebar until a plus icon () shows up next to the space name.

  • Select Create board (), then select what type of board you’d like to create.

  • Enter a name for your board.

  • Choose what to include in the board from the dropdown, then select Advanced.

  • Select which saved filter you’d like to use from the dropdown.

  • Select Create. Your new board is now ready to use!

Create a Kanban board based on spaces

Create a Kanban board based on spaces

If you’re setting up Jira for the first time, follow the prompts to create a space. A new board may already be selected for your space by default. You can change which board is associated with your space using by selecting Change to view all options.

If you’ve already set up Jira, follow these instructions to create a Kanban board using work items from a space.

  • From the top navigation at the top of the page, select the search field (or press /) and select Go to all: Boards. Then select Create board in the upper right of the screen.

  • In the modal that pops up, choose Create a Kanban board.

  • Select whether to base your board on a new software space or one or more existing spaces (you need the Browse spaces permission for both options).

  • Follow the prompts to set up your board. Another way you can create a kanban board is by:

  • Hover your cursor over the company-managed software space in the sidebar until a plus icon () shows up next to the space name.

  • Select Create board (), then select Kanban.

  • Enter a name for your board.

  • Choose what to include in the board from the dropdown.

  • Select Create. Your new board is now ready to use! At the top is a link that you may want to send to other people so that they can use it too.

If you’re basing your board on one or more existing spaces, this will create a pre-configured board that contains all the work items in your chosen space. Your board will have a work item filter with the following query:

space = "[YOUR SPACE]" ORDER BY Rank ASC

Find out about other JQL queries you can use in your board.

Create a new space

Create a new space

Jira apps come with many different space templates created to suit your team’s needs and workflow. For example, you can create spaces optimized for scrum or kanban methodologies, or for tracking tasks in business teams like marketing, legal, and HR.

Jira admins can create spaces from any template, including company-managed and team-managed spaces. Any user can create their own team-managed space unless a Jira admin changes this in global permissions. More about global permissions

Create a space

To create a space:

  • Hover over Spaces in the side navigation, then select Create space ().
  • Select a category or app from the template library. Templates are grouped by use case or by Jira Cloud app.
  • Find the template you’d like to use, and select Use template.
  • Give your space a name.
  • Select either Company-managed or Team-managed. What’s the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces?
  • If you’re creating a space using the team-managed Kanban or Scrum templates, these include recommended defaults for work types, statuses, and views. You can adjust these options and preview the setup before creating your space.
  • Select Create. Jira will generate a space key when you create the space, and you’ll be set as the space owner by default.

To change these details:

  • From your space sidebar, select Space settings.
  • Select Details. Jira will remember your template choice and use it as the default the next time you create a space.
Create a space with Rovo

You can create a new Jira space from scratch using Rovo, or use your existing work as a starting point. To get started, link documents, upload local files, or select suggested work from your Teamwork Graph. You can also choose from a range of prompts or describe what you want to do in your own words.

To create a space with Rovo:

  • Hover over Spaces in the side navigation, then select Create space ().
  • Under Space templates, select Create with Rovo.
  • Enter a prompt describing the space you’d like to create. You can also add links to Confluence pages and Loom videos, or upload files (like CSVs, images, or PDFs) to provide more context.
  • Review the suggested configuration, including the space name, key, work types, statuses, and views. You can also choose whether to enable sprints.
  • Select Next.
  • While your space is being set up, you can invite your teammates to join, or select I’ll do this later.
  • Select Next again to view your new space.
Create a space that shares its configuration with another space

Only Jira admins can create spaces with a shared configuration. This setting isn’t available on the Free plan.

Spaces with a shared configuration share:

  • work types
  • workflows
  • screens
  • fields
  • permissions
  • notifications If you change the configuration in one space, it affects all other spaces sharing that setup. We’ll notify you if a setting is shared.

To create a space with a shared configuration:

  • Hover over Spaces in the side navigation, then select Create space ().
  • Select a category or app from the template library.
  • Review the available templates and, when you find the right one, select Use template.
  • Select Company-managed.
  • Give your space a name.
  • Select the Share settings with an existing space checkbox.
  • Select the space you want to share settings from in the Choose space dropdown.
  • Select Create.

Edit a space’s details

Edit a space’s details

As an admin, you can edit your space’s:

  • Name — appears when people in your Jira site search, browse directories, or use the space switcher

  • Space key — typically the shorthand version of the space’s name

  • URL

  • Description

  • Category — helps larger organizations label and filter similar spaces in directories

  • Avatar — helps teams across your Jira site visually identify your space

  • Space owner — usually the space’s administrator

  • Default assignee — a role to which all work items created in the space are assigned

  • Space background

  • Card covers To edit a space’s details:

  • Open the space you want to change.

  • From your space’s sidebar, select Space settings, then Details.

  • Edit the relevant details and select Save details. If you change the name of your space, the new name will automatically update in any filters on your Jira site.

Change a space’s key

Only organization, site, and Jira admins can edit a space key.

Space keys provide a shorthand for the work items in your space. Together with a work item’s sequential number, they form a unique identifier called a work item key. More about work item keys

To change your space key:

  • Next to your space’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Details.
  • In the Space key field, enter your desired space key. It must:
    • be at least two characters long
    • start with an uppercase letter
    • contain only uppercase letters or numbers
  • Select Save.
Things to consider before changing a space key
  • Before making any significant changes, it’s a good idea to back up your Jira site to ensure important information isn’t lost.
  • You won’t be able to create a new space with the old space key. The old space key will only be available if you delete the space it was previously associated with.
  • If you use Confluence with Jira, the Jira work item macros in Confluence will continue to work. If you don’t see the change straight away, allow some time for the cache to refresh.
  • Links containing the old space key will continue to work, since link aliases won’t be updated with the new key.
    • For example, if you have a link to a work item EXAMPLE-1 in the description of a work item, and you change the space key EXAMPLE to DEMO, then the alias EXAMPLE-1 won’t be updated to DEMO-1. The link will still direct you to DEMO-1.
  • After you change a key, we recommend communicating the change to your users. You’ll need to update board filters, dashboard filter gadgets, and any other global queries with the new key.
Delete a previous space key

Only organization, site, and Jira admins can delete a space key.

Whenever you change your space key, we automatically save your previous space keys. This ensures that any links, filters, and queries using your previous key continue working.

In some cases, you may need to delete a previous space key from its associated space so you can use it for a new space. Deleting a previous space key can impact anything that is still using that space key, including:

  • links
  • board filters
  • dashboard filter gadgets
  • JQL queries We recommend letting users know before you delete your previous space key so that they can update any links, filters, or queries using the previous space key.

To delete a previous space key:

  • Next to your space’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Details.
  • In the Previous space keys field, delete the relevant space key.
  • Select Save.
Link to more space details with a space URL

Space URLs are only available in company-managed spaces.

You can link team members and viewers to an external site by adding a space URL. The space URL displays in the Spaces directory of your site.

Most teams supply an address to documentation about the space, roadmaps, or other important content outside of their Jira site. If you use Confluence to collaborate, we recommend adding a link to your team’s space.

To change your space’s URL:

  • Next to your space’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Details.
  • In the URL field, enter your link.
  • Select Save details.
Add a space description

Administrators can view the description in the Summary section of your space’s settings.

To add or edit your space’s description:

  • Next to your space’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Details.
  • In the Description field, enter a summary of important details about the space.
  • Select Save details.
Edit a space’s category

Your Jira admin may add space categories to help manage spaces across your Jira site.

If you’re using a company-managed space, contact a Jira admin to assign your space to one of those categories.

If you’re using a team-managed space, here’s how to assign or change your space’s category:

  • Next to your space’s name in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Details.
  • Under Category, use the dropdown to assign your space a category.
  • Select Save.
Change the type of space

You can’t directly change from a software space to a business space, and vice versa, but you can create a new space and move all of the work items into it.

For example, you can create a software space and move all of the work items over from a business space to get finer control over your space’s workflow, board settings, and more.

The difference between a software and business space is in the way your users work in the space.

Change your space’s avatar

Avatars help give a face to your space’s name. They appear in the space sidebar and in your site’s list of space.

To change your space’s avatar:

  • Next to the relevant space in your sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Details.
  • Under your space’s current avatar, select Change icon.
  • Choose from a default icon or upload your own, then use Select to save your choice.
Change the space owner

A space owner is usually the space administrator, who controls and manages a space’s settings.

You may want to change the space owner as people move in and out of your team.

To change the space owner:

  • Next to the relevant space in your sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Details.
  • In the Space owner field, select the person who’ll own the space.
  • Select Save.
Add or change your space’s default assignee

When work items are created in your space, you can set a default assignee. This is useful for open spaces where everyone on the site can report tasks to your space.

The default assignee is typically a team member who prioritizes or validates that reported work items are meant for their team and distributes these tasks to their team members accordingly. By default, they receive a notification when someone creates a work item in the space.

To change your space’s default assignee:

  • Next to the relevant space in your sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Details.
  • In the Default assignee field, select the relevant person.
  • Select Save. Note that the default assignee can only be either Unassigned, or the Space owner. If you want a specific person to be the default assignee, you’ll need to change the Space owner (described above).

Example JQL queries for board filters

Example JQL queries for board filters

We’re updating terminology in Jira, moving from “issue” to “work item”, and “project” to “space”.

As we roll out these changes, some JQL entries using the new terms may not work yet. If you come across this, try using the old term instead.

There are no changes to existing JQL queries.

You can use a JQL filter to make a board that shows the relevant work items based on whatever criteria you want. JQL is a flexible yet robust logic that can be used in a variety of different ways. Learn more about the power of JQL queries.

When constructing your JQL query, it’s important to tell Jira where it should search for work items by including or excluding specific spaces or boards.

When a query has to search through fewer work items, results load faster.

Let’s say you want to view all the work assigned to you using a JQL filter. However, you only work on two spaces within your entire organization.

This query works:

assignee is currentUser()

But this one is better:

space in (The Big Cheese, Project Kanban) and assignee is currentUser()

Why?

The first query searches through all of the work items in your site to find the ones assigned to you. The second query is more focused on your spaces.

If your site has 10,000 work items Jira can look at the 500 work items in those spaces and can ignore the remaining 9,500. Fewer work items to sort through, the quicker the query can run, even though the results are the same.

Here’s some other queries to help get you started
Show work items in different lifecycles

space in (LIFE) and status in ("In Progress", "To do") ORDER BY Rank ASC

Select all work items you are interested in

space in (LIFE) AND (assignee = currentUser() or reporter = currentUser()) AND (fixVersion in unreleasedVersions() OR fixVersion is empty)

Show all work items for a team (using a label custom field named “team”)

space in (LIFE) AND (team = ateam or team = dreamteam OR team = engineroom) AND (fixVersion in unreleasedVersions() OR fixVersion is empty)

Create a seperate board for completed work items

space in (LIFE) and status in (Done, Duplicate) and statusCategory = Done ORDER BY assignee

Use labels to organize by specific work streams

space in (LIFE) and labels in (ui-only, android-app) ORDER BY Rank ASC

Only show your bugs in a bug fix team
space in (LIFE) AND team = bugfix AND workType = bug AND (fixVersion in unreleasedVersions() OR fixVersion is empty)
Show all work items that are unscheduled or in an unreleased fix version

space in (LIFE) AND (fixVersion in unreleasedVersions() OR fixVersion is empty

Show all work items in the next fix version to be released

space in (LIFE) AND fixVersion = earliestUnreleasedVersion(SPACE KEY)

What are Jira workflows?

What are Jira workflows?

All Jira spaces contain work items that your team can view, work on, and transition through different stages — from creation to completion. The path that your work items take is called a workflow. Each Jira workflow is composed of a set of statuses and transitions that a work item moves through during its lifecycle, and typically represents processes within your organization.

Company-managed space workflows

In company-managed spaces, Jira uses workflow schemes to define the relationship between work types and workflows. Workflow schemes are associated with a space, and make it possible to use a different workflow for different combinations of space and work types. If you need to edit or create a more advanced workflow to match how your team or organization works, you can log in as a Jira administrator with global permission to access and create your workflow.

To keep things simple, use the default workflows that come with the space type you select in Jira. You can always modify or create new workflows later.

Team-managed space workflows

Space admins can create, edit, or delete space workflows in team-managed spaces. You can start off by using the default workflows that come with the template that you selected when you created a space. You can always modify or create new workflows later. You can have multiple workflows in each space through assigning workflow to specific work types.

What are the space templates?

What are the space templates?

When you create a space in Jira, you will do so from a template library where you can browse a variety of different templates across all the Jira Cloud products you own: Jira and Jira Service Management. In the template library, the information and best practices of each template help you select the optimal template that is best suited for your new space.

Jira comes with a variety of space templates to help teams get set up quickly by creating spaces tailored to a specific team or use. These templates include pre-configured work types, workflows and other features relevant to their type. Find out about creating a space using templates

  • Kanban visualizes and advances your space forward using work items on a powerful board. It’s designed for teams that control work volume from a backlog or connect work across their tools. Find out about kanban features
  • Scrum sprints toward your space goals with a board, backlog, and roadmap. It’s best suited for teams that deliver work on a regular cadence or connect work across their tools. Find out about scrum features
  • Bug tracking manages a list of development tasks and bugs. It’s best suited for teams that are capturing, tracking, and resolving bugs. Find out about bug tracking features
Kanban

Choose the kanban template to help teams visualize their work, limit work currently in progress, and maximize efficiency. Work is continuously delivered in kanban, and your team pulls single pieces of work from the backlog, and then moves them to done.

Track work using a simple board

Work items are represented visually on your kanban board, allowing teams to track the status of work at any time. Find out about kanban boards

Improve team focus by using the board to limit work in progress

Set the maximum amount of work that can exist in each status with work in progress (WIP) limits. Find out about WIP limits

Continuously improve with agile reports

Like the cumulative flow diagram, help ensure your teams are consistently delivering maximum value back to your business. Find out about agile metrics

Scrum

Choose the scrum template to build your product in a series of fixed-length iterations (sprints) that give teams a framework for shipping on a regular cadence.

Plan upcoming work in a backlog

Prioritize and plan your team’s work on the backlog. Break down work from your roadmap, and order work items so your team knows what to deliver first. Find out about the backlog

Organize cycles of work into sprints

Use sprints to drive incremental delivery, allow your team to ship high-quality work and deliver value faster. Find out about sprints

Understand your team’s velocity and capacity

Improve predictability on planning and delivery with out-of-the-box reports, including the sprint report and velocity chart. Find out about agile metrics

Bug tracking

Choose the bug tracking template to capture, track and resolve bugs and work items throughout your entire development process.

Identify and capture bugs

See all your bugs in one place. Once you’ve identified a bug, capture its details by creating a work item from anywhere in your space. Each unique work type can have its own custom workflow.

Assign and prioritize

Once captured, bugs can be ranked and prioritized based on importance, urgency, and your team’s workload capacity.

What is a board in software spaces?

What is a board in software spaces?

This page is for software spaces

To check whether you’re in a software or business space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

What is a board?

A board displays your team’s work as cards you can move between columns. In Jira, cards and the tasks they represent are called “work items”.

Usually, your board reflects your team’s process, tracking the status of work as it makes its way through your team’s process.

The columns on your board represent the status of your team’s work items. This visual representation of your team’s work helps you discuss and track the progress of your space from start to finish.

While the timeline can help you plan and track large initiatives over weeks, months, and quarters, the board is more tactical. It gives you a status of the work your team is currently carrying out, usually over the next week or two. Note that a board can display up to 5,000 work items at a time.

Your board comes with the following default status columns:

  • To Do — the first column on the board
  • In Progress
  • Done — the last column on the board
Cards on the board

Cards in the first column on your board view (from left to right) are always categorized as to do, meaning no progress has started on carrying out the task.

Cards in the last column of your board view are always categorized as done, meaning all work has been completed and the task has been carried out. If you’ve enabled the sprints feature, these work items won’t return to the backlog when you complete your sprint. If you don’t have the sprints feature enabled, these work items are automatically removed from the board after 14 days.

What is a Jira space?

What is a Jira space?

A Jira space is a collection of related work items that helps your team organize, track, and manage work. You can use a space to manage work for a product, project, team, or service in Jira Cloud.

What’s in a space?

A space groups work items together and provides views like boards, backlogs, and timelines to visualize and track progress. Each space has a space key (for example, “GDT”) that prefixes all its work items (GDT-1, GDT-2, etc.).

Spaces come pre-configured with work types, workflows, screens, and fields, but these can all be customized to fit your team’s way of working. You can also set up components, permissions, and boards. How to create a new space.

Team-managed vs. company-managed spaces

There are two ways a space can be managed.

  • Team-managed: Simple to set up, controlled by individual teams, and each space’s settings don’t affect other spaces. Anyone can create these.
  • Company-managed: Uses shared, standardized configuration set by Jira admins. Only Jira admins can create these.
Software spaces vs. business spaces

There are two types of spaces in Jira.

  • Software spaces: Designed for development teams. Choose from scrum, kanban, or bug tracking templates to suit your way of working. Read more about kanban vs scrum.
  • Business spaces: Designed for non-technical teams (HR, marketing, finance, etc.) to track tasks, assets, approvals, and more.
Who can create a space?
  • Team-managed: Anyone can create team-managed spaces, even non-admins. How to manage and configure a team-managed space.
  • Company-managed: Only Jira admins can create company-managed spaces. Read more about Jira admin permissions.
What are space templates?

Jira space templates are pre-configured setups that define the structure, work types, workflows, and features of a new space. When you create a space, select a template that matches your team’s way of working. Or, you can create a blank space without any pre-configuration. See what space templates are available.
