What is advanced search in Jira Cloud?

What is advanced search in Jira Cloud?

The advanced search allows you to build structured queries using the Jira Query Language (JQL) to search for work items. You can specify criteria that you can’t define in the quick or basic searches. For example, you can use the ORDER BY clause in JQL when you’re searching for work items. JQL can help gain key space insights and help you find not just work items but also important information in spaces.

If you don’t have complex search criteria, try quick search instead.

JQL is not a database query language, even though it uses SQL-like syntax. In advanced search, you can use queries to find your work items. Queries are a series of elements or parts, like fields, operators, and values, that are strung together to form a structure. More about constructing JQL queries

Using JQL, you could search for all work items in your space “Assassin’s Guild” that:

  • have “weaponry” in a text field, and
  • are ordered by when they were created in ascending or descending order.
  • Switch between Basic and JQL
  • JQL editor
  • Expand or Collapse editor
  • Syntax help
  • Search button
  • Line numbers when your JQL query is longer than a line
  • Autocomplete suggestions based on context
Perform advanced searching with JQL queries

The syntax-powered advanced search or JQL is a powerful tool for getting specific information from spaces.

To use advanced search or JQL to find your work items:

  • Select Search 🔍 in the top navigation (or press / on your keyboard). Alternatively, select Filters in the sidebar.
  • Select View all work items.
    • If the basic search is shown instead of the advanced search, select JQL (next to the 🔍 icon). If advanced or JQL search is already enabled, you’ll see the option to switch to basic.
  • Enter your JQL query.
  • Press Enter or select 🔍 to run your query. Your search results will be displayed based on the criteria in your JQL query. As you type, Jira will offer a list of “autocomplete” suggestions based on the context of your query. Note, autocomplete suggestions only include the first 15 matches, displayed alphabetically, so you may need to enter more text if you can’t find a match.
Construct JQL queries

Get the most out of advanced searching by learning how to structure your JQL query. A simple query in JQL (also known as a ‘clause’) consists of a field, followed by an operator, followed by one or more values or functions.

Description

Fields

A field in JQL is a word that represents a Jira field (or a custom field that has already been defined in Jira). More about using fields for advanced searching.

Operators

An operator in JQL is one or more symbols or words that compare the value of a field on its left with one or more values (or functions) on its right, such that only true results are retrieved by the clause. Some operators may use the NOT keyword. More about using operators for advanced searching.

Keywords

A keyword in JQL is a word or phrase that does (or is) any of the following:

  • joins two or more clauses together to form a complex JQL query
  • alters the logic of one or more clauses
  • alters the logic of operators
  • has an explicit definition in a JQL query
  • performs a specific function that alters the results of a JQL query. More about using keywords for advanced searching.

Functions

A function in JQL appears as a word followed by parentheses, which may contain one or more explicit values or Jira fields.

A function performs a calculation on either specific Jira data or the function’s content in parentheses, such that only true results are retrieved by the function, and then again by the clause in which the function is used.

More about using functions for advanced searching.

For example:

project = "TEST"

This query will find all work items in the “TEST” project. It uses the “project” field, the EQUALS operator, and the value "TEST".

A more complex query might look like this:

project = "TEST" AND assignee = currentuser()

This query will find all work items in the “TEST” project where the assignee is the currently logged in user. It uses the “project” field, the EQUALS operator, the value "TEST",the “AND” keyword and the “currentuser()” function.

Set the precedence of operators

You can use parentheses in complex JQL statements to enforce the precedence of operators.

For example, if you want to find all resolved work items in the ‘SysAdmin’ project, as well as all work items (any status, any project) currently assigned to the system administrator (bobsmith), you can use parentheses to enforce the precedence of the boolean operators in your query, i.e.

(status=resolved AND project=SysAdmin) OR assignee=bobsmith

Note that if you do not use parentheses, the statement will be evaluated left-to-right.

You can also use parentheses to group clauses, so that you can apply the NOT operator to the group.

Restricted words and characters
Special characters

In general, non-alphanumeric characters, such as + . , * / % ^ $ # @ [ ], aren’t indexed for search and are ignored in queries. Exceptions include email addresses and URLs.

When building queries, make sure to surround phrases with special characters or spaces with single ' or double " quotation marks, for example: field ~ "email@atlassian.com". Additionally, some characters may need to be preceded by two backslashes \\, for example, field ~ "\\(text".

Reserved words

JQL also has a list of reserved words. These words need to be surrounded by quotation marks (single or double) if you wish to use them in queries:

“a”, “an”, “abort”, “access”, “add”, “after”, “alias”, “all”, “alter”, “and”, “any”, “are”, “as”, “asc”, “at”, “audit”, “avg”, “be”, “before”, “begin”, “between”, “boolean”, “break”, “but”, “by”, “byte”, “catch”, “cf”, “char”, “character”, “check”, “checkpoint”, “collate”, “collation”, “column”, “commit”, “connect”, “continue”, “count”, “create”, “current”, “date”, “decimal”, “declare”, “decrement”, “default”, “defaults”, “define”, “delete”, “delimiter”, “desc”, “difference”, “distinct”, “divide”, “do”, “double”, “drop”, “else”, “empty”, “encoding”, “end”, “equals”, “escape”, “exclusive”, “exec”, “execute”, “exists”, “explain”, “false”, “fetch”, “file”, “field”, “first”, “float”, “for”, “from”, “function”, “go”, “goto”, “grant”, “greater”, “group”, “having”, “identified”, “if”, “immediate”, “in”, “increment”, “index”, “initial”, “inner”, “inout”, “input”, “insert”, “int”, “integer”, “intersect”, “intersection”, “into”, “is”, “isempty”, “isnull”, “it”, “join”, “last”, “left”, “less”, “like”, “limit”, “lock”, “long”, “max”, “min”, “minus”, “mode”, “modify”, “modulo”, “more”, “multiply”, “next”, “no”, “noaudit”, “not”, “notin”, “nowait”, “null”, “number”, “object”, “of”, “on”, “option”, “or”, “order”, “outer”, “output”, “power”, “previous”, “prior”, “privileges”, “public”, “raise”, “raw”, “remainder”, “rename”, “resource”, “return”, “returns”, “revoke”, “right”, “row”, “rowid”, “rownum”, “rows”, “select”, “session”, “set”, “share”, “size”, “sqrt”, “start”, “strict”, “string”, “subtract”, “such”, “sum”, “synonym”, “table”, “that”, “the”, “their”, “then”, “there”, “these”, “they”, “this”, “to”, “trans”, “transaction”, “trigger”, “true”, “uid”, “union”, “unique”, “update”, “user”, “validate”, “values”, “view”, “was”, “when”, “whenever”, “where”, “while”, “will”, “with”

Types of JQL
Bounded JQL query

A bounded JQL is a JQL that requires a search restriction. The JQL must have at least one condition with field on the left side followed by an operator and then by one or more values (or functions). Here are some examples of bounded queries:

  • project = TEST order by key; here, project = TEST is a search restriction in the JQL query.
  • reporter = currentUser(); here, reporter = currentUser() is a search restriction in the JQL query.
  • status IN ("To Do", "IN PROGRESS") AND priority >= Medium ORDER BY created; here status IN ("To Do", "IN PROGRESS") and priority >= Medium are the search restrictions in the JQL query.
Unbounded JQL query

On the other hand, unbounded JQL is a JQL that doesn’t have any search restrictions. They can be an empty query or one that solely lists order by clauses, such as:

  • order by createdDate
  • order by key
Perform a text search

You can use text-searching features when performing searches on the following fields, using the CONTAINS operator:

Summary, Description, Environment, Comments, and custom fields that use the “Free Text Searcher”

The custom fields that use the “Free Text Searcher” are built-in custom field types, like Free Text Field, Text Field, Read-only Text Field.

More about using search syntax for text fields

Troubleshooting in advanced search
Why can’t I switch between basic and advanced search?

In general, a query created using the basic search can be translated to advanced JQL search, and back again. However, a complex query created using advanced JQL criteria may not be translated to basic search, particularly if:

  • the query contains an OR operator. Instead, you can use an IN operator and it will be translated. For example: project in (A, B)
  • the query contains a NOT operator
  • the query contains an EMPTY operator
  • the query contains any of the comparison operators: !=, IS, IS NOT, >, >=, <, <=
  • the query specifies a field and value that is related to a space (e.g. version, component, custom fields) and the space is not explicitly included in the query (e.g. fixVersion = "4.0", without the AND project=JRA). This is especially tricky with custom fields since they can be configured on a Space/Work Type basis. The general rule of thumb is that if the query cannot be created in the basic search form, then it will not be able to be translated from advanced search to basic search.
Why can’t I see autocomplete suggestions?
  • Your administrator may have disabled the “JQL Auto-complete” feature for your Jira instance.
  • Auto-complete suggestions are not offered for function parameters.
  • Auto-complete suggestions are not offered for all fields. Check the fields reference to see which fields support autocomplete.
Where can I see the error in my JQL query?

While typing, you can hover over the invalid text of your query to know more about the JQL error. Alternatively, if your JQL query has an error, you can hit search and Jira will display the specifics of the error below the JQL editor, along with the line and character number of the invalid text in the query.

How can I fix the error in my JQL query?

Run your query and check for any error messages below the JQL editor. You can fix the JQL errors:

  • manually by identifying and correcting issues like missing fields, incorrect operators, or typos
  • by reviewing the AI-generated, error-free query suggestion, and selecting Accept to apply it instantly AI is available and automatically enabled for all apps on Standard, Premium, and Enterprise plans. Organization admins can manage AI preferences by selecting Rovo, then Rovo access in Atlassian Administration.

AI is not available in Atlassian Government organizations. For Sandbox environments, you must manually activate it.

Use custom space templates

Create a custom space template

Create a custom space template

Custom space templates are an exclusive Enterprise plan feature

Custom space templates let Jira admins save time by reusing settings from existing spaces, so every new space starts with the right configuration.

Create a template from any space to share its workflows, boards, navigation, and shortcuts with others across your site.

To create a custom space template:

  • Start in the space you want to reuse.
  • Next to your space’s name in the header or the sidebar, select More actions (), then Save as space template.
  • Enter a name and description for your custom template. These details appear in the space templates screen, and help your teams know when to use this template.
  • Select the template icon if you’d like to upload a custom icon for your template.
  • Use the rich text editor in the Template overview section to add details about what you can do with the template and why it works, then select Next.
  • In the next screen, select the users or groups you want to allow to create spaces from this template.
  • For company-managed spaces, use the checkboxes to choose whether new spaces created with this template should copy workflows and screens from the source space.
  • Select Save. Once your template is saved, return to the source space and select More actions () to edit the template name or description. You can also delete the template from the edit screen.

Enable users and groups to create spaces with custom templates

Enable users and groups to create spaces with custom templates

Jira admins can create a custom template, which allows approved users and groups to create their own spaces in Jira.

Allow users to create spaces with an existing template
  • Go to the template’s source space and select More actions (•••).
  • Select Edit template.
  • From the template name and description screen, select Next.
  • Add the users and groups you wish to create new spaces from the template.
Allow users to create spaces with a new template
  • Go to the space you wish to make a template of and select More actions (•••).
  • Select Save as template.
  • Follow the prompts provided in-product to create the template.
  • Add the users and groups you wish to create new spaces from the template.
Where can approved users and groups view custom templates?

Custom templates created by your organisation will be available for approved users and groups in the template gallery, which is visible to them after they select Create space.

Use a custom template to create a new space

Use a custom template to create a new space

Custom space templates are an exclusive Enterprise plan feature

The following roles and permissions can create a space using custom templates:

  • Jira administrators can create a space from both team‑managed and company‑managed space custom templates.
  • Users with the “Can create team-managed spaces” global permission can create a space from team‑managed space custom templates.
  • Any groups or users enabled by a Jira admin can also create a space from a custom template.
Create a new space with custom template
  • In the main navigation, go to the Spaces menu.
  • Select Create space.
  • On the templates screen, select Custom templates.
  • Choose the template you wish to use and select the Use template button.
  • Complete the space setup screens to start working on your space.
Manage spaces created from templates

Anyone creating a new space from a team-managed space template becomes a project owner and can configure their own space settings.

For a company-managed space:

  • Users and groups will need permissions via the source space to access and configure space settings for a new space created with the template.
  • Changes made to space settings will apply to any space created with the template, unless the template settings are customized and copied. Read more about permission schemes and permissions

Use Docs in Jira Cloud

Set up Docs in Jira

Set up Docs in Jira

We’re currently updating the Pages experience and renaming it to “Docs”. There might be a temporary difference between the information below and what you see in Jira.

The Docs feature helps your team keep track of your documentation in Confluence Cloud. Connect Confluence to your Jira space to give your team direct access to your project documentation, without having to go to Confluence.

Confluence spaces are like Jira spaces. They’re used by your team to store information. But while Jira spaces store work items, Confluence spaces store pages, whiteboards, and other types of content.

Add the Docs tab

Only space admins can add new tabs via the space navigation.

To add the Docs tab to your Jira space:

  • In the space navigation, select Add to navigation (+).
  • Select Docs. A new menu item, Docs, will be added to the horizontal menu.
Connect your Jira space to Confluence

If you don’t already have access to Confluence Cloud, you can sign up for a free trial from your Jira space

Create a new Confluence space for your team

When you sign up to Confluence via Docs, you will have to select a Confluence space to join or create a new one. If you want to create a new one via Jira, you’ll need to:

  • Navigate to your Jira space.
  • In the space navigation, select Docs.
  • Select Create a new Confluence space.
  • Enter a name for the new space, then select Create space to create a new Confluence space that will be automatically connected to Jira.
Connect your team’s existing Confluence content to your Jira space

To connect an existing Confluence space, folder, or page from Docs in Jira, you’ll need to:

  • Navigate to your Jira space.
  • In the space navigation, select Docs.
  • Select Link existing Confluence spaces or content.
  • Select a Confluence space, folder, or page, or search to find one.
  • Select Connect and your Confluence content will be connected to your Jira space.
Connect to different Confluence content

Jira spaces can only be connected to one Confluence space, folder, or page at a time. When you connect a Confluence space, folder, or page, all its child pages will be visible in Jira. If a page is restricted in Confluence, the same permission settings apply in Jira.

To change which Confluence content is connected to your Jira space:

  • Navigate to your Jira space.
  • In the space navigation, select Docs.
  • Select Manage connection.
  • Select an existing Confluence space, folder, or page or search to find one. You can also create a new one and connect to it by selecting Create new space.
  • Select Connect and your selected Confluence space, folder or page will be connected to your Jira space.
How users get access to Confluence via Docs

Once you have Docs set up, Jira users will be able to see the Docs tab in the space navigation. If a user selects Docs and they don’t have access to the connected Confluence space, they’ll see a prompt to try out Confluence or learn more about how it works.

If the user is on an approved domain, they can select the “Join Confluence” button to start using Docs right away. Users that join Confluence this way will get default app access.

If the user isn’t on an approved domain, they’ll have to request access. They won’t be able to use Docs or Confluence until they’re approved by a site admin.

If a page is restricted in Confluence, the same permission settings apply to Docs in Jira.

What is the Docs feature?

What is the Docs feature?

The Docs feature helps your team stay aligned and collaborate more effectively by linking your Confluence content to your Jira space.

Track work and view documents in one place

Connect a Confluence space, folder, or page so everyone can easily view, edit, and create docs from Jira. No need to switch between tools.

Get started with the Docs feature

To use Docs in Jira, you’ll need to add the feature and then connect a Confluence space, folder, or page. How to set up the Docs feature

Once you’ve connected a Confluence space, you can view all its folders and pages on the Docs tab in your Jira space.

Search and filter docs in Jira

You can find content by typing in the search bar, or using the following options:

  • Type: Filter the content to show pages and live docs, whiteboards, or folders.
  • Sort: Arrange content alphabetically, or match the default order. Select a content item to open it in a preview panel where you can edit, add comments, share, or open in a new tab.
Create content via Docs in Jira

You can create new content items in Confluence via the Docs feature in Jira:

  • Select Create at the bottom of the list of content, or hover over a content item and select Create child item (+).
  • Select a content type: Live Doc, Page, or Whiteboard.
  • Enter a title and add some content to the body.
  • Select Open in Confluence if you’d prefer to continue creating in a new tab. Tip: Try using a Confluence template to create what you need faster. Read more about templates

Use Jira Cloud with other apps

Configure collaboration tools

Configure collaboration tools

Integrating collaboration tools with Jira can help you plan and run your project more efficiently. By connecting to collaboration tools like Confluence, and Team Calendars for Confluence, you can:

  • Link project documentation to your team’s work across Jira, Confluence, and Team Calendars for Confluence
  • Centralize your team leaves in Team Calendar for Confluence Connect to Confluence (wiki), or Team Calendars for Confluence to get work item notifications in your chat rooms, link project documentation to work items, centralize your team leave, and more.
Connecting Jira to your collaboration tools

Follow the instructions on Integrating with collaboration tools (Jira admin documentation) to connect Jira to Confluence.

Note that you need to be a Jira administrator to connect Jira to Confluence. You will need to be an administrator for Confluence as well.

Feature overview

If you have Jira Software, Confluence, and Team Calendars for Confluence, you can use them together to build stronger user stories and better plans for sprints or releases, while streamlining your team’s work. Create meeting notes on the fly, wrap up a sprint with a retrospective report, and more.

Here are some of the features that you’ll unlock by integrating Jira and Confluence. For a full feature overview, see Using Jira apps with Confluence.

Plan larger pieces of work

If you have linked your Jira instance to a Confluence instance, you can create and link Confluence pages to your parent-level work items. For example, you may want to link an epic to a specification or design document in Confluence.

How to link a Confluence page to a parent-level work item

Plan sprints

Team Calendars for Confluence acts as your single source of truth for managing team leaves, tracking projects, and planning events. If you have Team Calendars installed in Confluence, planning your sprints around leaves and events is even easier. Add a sprint event to your team’s calendar in Confluence, and as you plan your sprints, you will be able to see whether team leaves or events will impact your work.

Manage sprints

If you have linked your Jira instance to a Confluence instance, you can create and link Confluence pages to your sprints via Jira. For example, you may want to write up the sprint meeting notes in Confluence and link them to the sprint. You may also want to write your team’s retrospective notes in Confluence and link them to the Sprint Report for the completed sprint.

How to link a Confluence page to a sprint

Manage releases

With releases ongoing, you can update your stakeholders on the release progress by creating Jira status reports in Confluence. The Jira status report provides a snapshot of a release at a point in time. Stakeholders can monitor progress, even if they don’t have access to Jira.

Need help? If you can’t find the answer you need in our documentation, we have other resources available to help you. See Getting help.

Configure development tools

Configure development tools

Jira can be connected to a range of development tools to help keep your space tracking in sync with your development work.

Connect to source code management tools, like Bitbucket or GitHub, where you can:

  • configure work items to automatically transition when certain events occur in your repository, such as commits and branches created, pull requests merged and declined, and more

  • create branches, pull requests, and commits directly from work items in Jira

  • see every work item with its related commits, branches, builds, and pull requests in Jira

  • see your deployments (if you have enabled Bitbucket Pipelines) Connect to Crucible for code reviews, where you can:

  • configure work items to automatically transition when a review changes status

  • see every work item with its related reviews in Jira Connect to Bamboo, and you can see every work item with its related builds and deployments in Jira.

Connecting Jira to your development tools

Make sure that you have the right permissions. You need to be a Jira administrator to connect Jira to another app. You also need to be an administrator for your development tool.

Bitbucket isn’t available in the Atlassian Government environment.

Follow the instructions on Integrating with development tools (Jira admin documentation) to connect Jira to your development tools.

Configuring Jira and your development tools

Some features will be automatically enabled when you connect Jira to your development tools. Others require some additional configuration. Each feature is listed below, including the configuration work required to set it up.

Development panel on work items

The Development panel is shown on every work item, and helps you to evaluate the development status of a work item at a glance. If you need to investigate further, click any item to display more details, or drill down into the development tool.

You don’t need to do any further configuration once you have connected Jira to your development tools. However, your team will need to know how to reference work items in their development work.

Learn more: Referencing work items in your development work

We’re gradually rolling out a work item, which you may see on your boards and in your backlog. The work item detail view will look a little different and some procedures will change slightly. Take a look at our info page to see what’s changed and get the latest updates.

View development information on the Jira board

Once you’ve connected your development tools and your team is using work item keys in branch names, commit messages, and pull requests, you’ll start seeing development information on your Jira board. Work item cards will display development icons to indicate when they have pull requests, branches, commits, or deployments associated with them, so you can see at a glance how work is progressing. You can hover over the icons to view the details of the development activity, and click through to go to your connected development tool.

Development icons will show on your Jira board as long as:

  • At least one of the work items on your board has development data linked to it.
  • Your board contains less than 100 work items.
View development information on the Development page

Once you’ve connected your development tools to Jira and your team is using work item keys in branch names, commit messages, and pull requests, you’ll start seeing development information on the Development page.

Once set up, you’ll see:

  • Key metrics like pull request cycle time and deployment frequency, showing your team’s delivery health.
  • Related work like pull requests, vulnerabilities, and deployments from apps connected to Jira—so you can view details, see who’s working on what, and jump straight into code.
  • Work suggestions with proactive, actionable recommendations to resolve blockers and boost your team’s progress. Read more information about Development in Jira.
View work item information in your developer tools

If you have connected Jira to one of the supported developer tools, like Bitbucket, GitHub, GitLab, Fisheye/Crucible, or any other source code tools available on the Marketplace, you will be able to view information about the work items in those tools. For example, in Bitbucket, you’ll be able to see the work items that were referenced in a changeset; in Bamboo, you’ll be able to see the work items linked to a plan’s builds.

Here’s an example of a work item key (MSP-15) in a commit message in Bitbucket:

When you click the work item key in Bitbucket, you’ll see the work item view:

Learn more: Bitbucket Cloud, GitHub, Bamboo, Fisheye, Crucible

Create branches, commits and pull requests from a work item

If you’ve connected a source code management tool like Bitbucket or GitHub, you can create branches directly from work items in Jira via the Create branch link in the Development panel. The link will open your connected code tool and launch the process of creating a branch for you. If you have multiple tools connected, you can choose where you’d like to create the branch.

Once a branch is created and linked to a work item, you can also create commits and pull requests via the Development panel on a Jira work item.

Workflow triggers

You can configure triggers in workflows that respond to events in your linked development tools. This helps your team keep their work item statuses in sync with their development work, rather than lagging behind. For example, when a developer creates a branch in Bitbucket to start work on a work item, they can reference the work item in the branch name, and the work item will automatically be transitioned from ‘Open’ to ‘In progress’.

You’ll need to add triggers to your workflow(s) after connecting Jira to your development tools. We recommend that you read our guide on configuring workflow triggers.

Learn more about configuring workflow triggers (Jira admin documentation)

Development information on the release page

If you’ve enabled the Releases feature in Jira and you’re using versions to organize your team’s work, you can use the release page to view the progress of a version and determine what is likely to ship, at a glance. You can see all of the work items in the version, broken down by status category, as well as potential problems that could affect the release of the version (e.g. work item that should be in the release but are part of unmerged pulled requests, work items that haven’t had code reviews, or broken builds).

To view development information on the release page:

  • Log in to Jira and go to your space.
  • Select Releases in the space menu.
  • Select a version from the list.
  • Look for the Development column in the table of work items. Once you have connected Jira to your development tools, you don’t need to do any further configuration to see development information on the release page. However, your team will need to know how to reference work items in their development work.

Learn more: Referencing work items in your development work

Need help? If you can’t find the answer you need in our documentation, we have other resources available to help you. See Getting help.

Integrate Jira Cloud with Gmail

Integrate Jira Cloud with Gmail

The Jira Cloud for Gmail app helps you manage Jira work items without leaving Gmail. Effortlessly create work items from emails, view detailed information on hyperlinked work items, and edit or comment on them - all within your inbox. These features will help you transform email conversations into actionable tasks without context switching between apps.

Top features

Install the Jira Cloud for Gmail app to access the following features:

  • Create work items using details from an email or with Atlassian Intelligence (AI)*
  • View details of work items hyperlinked in an email.
  • Edit and comment on work items within Gmail.
  • Attach emails as comments to existing work items.
  • *Atlassian Intelligence (AI) will need to be enabled for Jira sites and spaces for users to have access to this feature. Users should be mindful when sharing sensitive data or information with the app when using generative AI to create work item summary and description fields.
Before you begin

To use the Jira Cloud for Gmail app, you need:

  • A Jira Cloud account
  • Access to a Jira site
  • A Gmail account (personal* or Google Workspace)
  • The Jira Cloud for Gmail app installed from the Google Workspace Marketplace
  • *Note to admins: Atlassian permits users to link their personal email accounts to the Atlassian platform.
Install the Jira Cloud for Gmail app
  • Open Gmail in your browser and select the + icon in the right side panel.
  • Enter Atlassian in the Google Workspace Marketplace search bar.
  • Find the Atlassian app, select Install and follow the permission prompts.
  • Once installed, open any email and select the Atlassian icon in the sidebar.
  • Sign in with your Atlassian account to connect Gmail with your Jira site.
Create a work item from an email
  • Open an email in your Gmail inbox.
  • Select the Atlassian icon in the right vertical sidebar.
  • Select Create in the app side panel.
  • Select Use email body as description to include the email subject as the work item summary and email body content as the description
  • Or, select Use AI to generate description to create the work item summary and description fields with generative AI based on the email content.
  • Edit and review the work item fields then select Create in the pop-up window.
  • Work items created using the app will be automatically attached to the source email. This means the app will detect and display any work items attached to an email in the app panel.
Edit or comment on a work item in Gmail
  • Open an email in your Gmail inbox.
  • To find existing work items select Find in the app side panel.
  • Paste a link to a Jira work item in the input field and select Find.
  • The work item will appear in the app side panel.
  • Select Edit to update and comment on the work item in the pop-up window.
  • Hyperlinked work items will automatically appear in the app side panel. Select a work item and follow step five to edit it.
Attach an email to an existing work item
  • Open an email in your Gmail inbox.
  • To find existing work items select Find in the app side panel.
  • Paste a link to a Jira work item in the input field and select Find.
  • The work item will appear in the app side panel.
  • Select Attach email.
  • Select Attach to include the email content as a comment to the work item. The comment field can’t be edited.
Uninstall the Jira Cloud for Gmail app
  • Open Gmail in your browser and select the + icon in the right side panel.
  • Enter Atlassian in the Google Workspace Marketplace search bar.
  • Find the Atlassian app and select Uninstall to remove the app.

Integrate Jira Cloud with Microsoft Teams

Integrate Jira Cloud with Microsoft Teams

Jira Cloud for Microsoft Teams gives your team a shared view of Jira spaces so you can collaborate on and action work items without leaving Teams. Streamline your workflow with custom notifications, link previews, and the functionality to create, search, and update Jira work items—all within Teams.

Jira Cloud features

Install the Jira Cloud app in Teams chats to access the following features:

  • Space notifications - Customize your notifications to get instant updates.
  • Link previews - View real-time information and status updates.
  • Action Jira work items - View, assign, comment on, and watch work items directly in Teams.
  • Quick commands - Find work items, configure notifications, and request support using prompts.
Install the Jira Cloud app
  • Select Apps from the left vertical toolbar in Teams.
  • Enter Jira Cloud in the Apps search bar.
  • Find the Jira Cloud app and select Add.
  • Select Add for me from the drop-down menu in the app modal.
  • Follow the sign in prompts to complete your installation.
Setup personal notifications
  • Select Jira Cloud from the left vertical toolbar in Teams.
  • Enter Notifications in the Jira Cloud chat.
  • Jira Cloud will automatically setup default personal notifications.
  • Select Change notifications to adjust your notification preferences.
  • Select Save notifications. Once you’ve setup personal notifications in Teams, you can turn off or adjust email notifications in Jira from your browser.

Navigate to your avatar on the top left menu in Jira and select Notifications and then Space and work item notifications to adjust your email notification preferences.

Add a Jira Cloud tab to a team or channel chat
  • Select the + icon on the top right of the chat menu.
  • Search and select Jira Cloud.
  • Select your Jira Cloud site from the drop-down menu.
  • Select your saved filter from the drop-down menu.
  • Select Save. You’ll see a Jira Cloud tab appear in the chat menu. In this tab view, you can access Jira work items you’ve recently viewed, worked on, or been assigned to.
Add Jira Cloud to a meeting
  • Select Calendar on the left toolbar, then select + New meeting.
  • Enter your meeting details and select Send.
  • Open the meeting and select the + icon from the menu.
  • Search and select Jira Cloud.
  • Select your Jira Cloud site, then select Save. You’ll see a Jira Cloud tab appear in the meeting invite and chat menu. In this tab view, you can access Jira work items you’ve recently viewed, worked on, or been assigned to.
Setup notifications in a team, channel or meeting chat
  • Add Jira Cloud to the team, channel or meeting chat.
  • Enter @Jira Cloud, select Jira Cloud from suggestions then enter Notifications.
  • This command will trigger the setup for channel notifications.
  • Follow the prompts to select your site and space to adjust your notifications preferences. Once you’ve setup personal notifications in Teams, you can turn off or adjust email notifications in Jira from your browser.

Navigate to your avatar on the top left menu in Jira and select Notifications and then Space and work item notifications. Scroll down and select Add space notifications to select your space and adjust your notification preferences.

Create and search for work items in Teams
  • Navigate to your team, channel or meeting chat.
  • Select the Jira Cloud tab on the top right of the chat menu.
  • Select Create and follow the prompts to create a work item.
  • Enter a search phrase or work item key into the search bar to find a work item.
Create work items using Rovo

AI is available and automatically enabled for all apps on Standard, Premium, and Enterprise plans. Organization admins can manage AI preferences by selecting Rovo, then Rovo access in Atlassian Administration.

AI is not available in Atlassian Government organizations. For Sandbox environments, you must manually activate it.

Use Rovo to create Jira work items straight from messages in Teams chats. AI analyzes your chat context to swiftly generate detailed, structured work items, saving you time.

Descriptions follow a predefined format based on the work type for consistency, and the content is automatically localized to match your Microsoft Teams language settings. Using AI is the default creation method, but you can turn it off anytime while creating work items.

To create work items from messages in Teams chats:

  • Navigate to your team, channel, or meeting chat.
  • Find the message you want to create a work item from and select More options (···).
  • Select Create work item in Jira.
  • Choose a Jira site and space.
  • If not already selected, select Use Rovo to generate the summary and description to allow AI to generate the work item details.
    • The app remembers your previous selection and applies it each time until you decide to change it.
  • Fill in any additional details as required.
  • Select Create to create the work item. Rovo gathers context only from the selected message in your team, channel, or meeting chats. It doesn’t have access to the message threads in chats.
Preview and action work items in Teams
  • Share a link to a work item in a team, channel or meeting chat.
  • Sign in to your Atlassian account to view the full link preview.
  • The link will display the status, type, assignee and priority of the work item.
  • Select Comment, Edit or Open in Jira to action the work item in Teams. For a seamless experience, Jira Cloud installs in chats and channels when someone shares a preview link.

Turn off the auto-installation feature when sharing a Jira link by selecting x when the preview of the link is displayed. You’ll now be able to share a Jira link without triggering auto-installation in the chat.

Quick commands for Jira Cloud in Teams

Use these commands with Jira Cloud to streamline your workflow in Teams.

Personal chat - Enter the Command directly into the chat to trigger the action.

Team/channel/meeting chat - Enter @Jira Cloud, select Jira Cloud from suggestions then enter a Command.

Command

Action

Configure

Connect to your Jira Cloud instance

Notifications

Setup your personal notifications in Teams

Find

Search for Jira work items using a search phrase or work item key

Support

Create a ticket to request support

Help

View a list of quick commands for Teams

Feedback

Submit feedback to the Atlassian App Integrations team

Tour

Find out about the top Jira Cloud features for Teams

Sign out

Sign out of your Atlassian account

Uninstall the Jira Cloud app
  • Find Jira Cloud in the left vertical toolbar in Teams.
  • Secondary click on the Jira Cloud icon.
  • Select Uninstall.
  • Select Remove to uninstall Jira Cloud.
Privacy considerations

Your data and personal information are encrypted for added security. Jira Cloud is activated only with the @Jira Cloud prompt followed by a Command.

Integrate the Jira Cloud plugin for Copilot in Microsoft Teams

Integrate the Jira Cloud plugin for Copilot in Microsoft Teams

Use the AI capabilities of the Jira Cloud plugin for Microsoft Copilot to boost your productivity and streamline team project management. This powerful integration brings the robust features of Jira Cloud directly into Microsoft Teams, allowing you to track your work seamlessly. Enhance your workflow using natural language prompts to search for Jira tickets, create and update tasks, add comments, and more—all within a Teams chat.

Prerequisites

Before you install the Jira Cloud plugin for Copilot in Teams, you must have:

  • A license for Copilot for Microsoft 365.
  • Extensions enabled by default in all Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed tenants.
  • An Atlassian account to sign in to your Jira Cloud instance.
Install Microsoft Copilot in Teams
  • Select Apps from the left vertical toolbar in Teams.
  • Enter Copilot for M365 in the Apps search bar.
  • Select Add and follow the prompts to complete the installation.
Install the Jira Cloud plugin in Copilot
  • Select Copilot from the left vertical toolbar in Teams.
  • Enter Jira Cloud plugin in the search bar.
  • Find the Jira Cloud plugin and select Add.
  • Follow the prompts to complete the installation.
  • Turn on the toggle next to Jira Cloud in the plugin popup.
Prompt the Jira Cloud plugin

Use clear, plain language prompts to tell Copilot to perform a task for you.

You can use prompts to help you:

  • Find all tickets assigned to a teammate.
  • Summarize your tasks for the week.
  • Create an email to communicate an update.
  • Search and manage open Jira tickets. Learn: How to write effective prompts

Watch: How to use the Jira Cloud plugin in Copilot

Troubleshoot Copilot in Teams

If you need help using Copilot to find information on your Jira tickets, follow these steps:

  • Sign in: Check you are signed in to the Jira Cloud app in Microsoft Teams.

  • Enable plugin: Check that the toggle for Jira Cloud is turned on in the Copilot plugin popup.

  • Permission: Check you have access to the Jira board you are trying to view. If none of the previous steps work, follow these additional steps:

  • Sign out of and uninstall the Jira Cloud app.

  • Sign out of and close Teams.

  • Reopen and sign in to Teams.

  • Reinstall and sign in to the Jira Cloud app.

  • Turn on the toggle for Jira Cloud in the Copilot plugin popup.

Need help?

Visit the Microsoft Copilot support page for help with Copilot, or contact your admin.

Contact Atlassian at support@atlassian.com for help with the Jira Cloud plugin.

Use Jira Cloud for Sheets

Use Jira Cloud for Sheets

Jira Cloud for Sheets enables you to import Jira data into your spreadsheets with Jira filters or JQL (Jira Query Language).

Your G Suite admin must enable access to Google Sheets add-ons for all users to use the integration. Find out about turning on a G Suite Marketplace app for all users.

Add the Jira Cloud add-on to Google Sheets

To add the Jira Cloud add-on to Google Sheets:

  • Go to a Google Sheets spreadsheet.
  • Select Add-ons then Get add-ons.
  • Search for Jira Cloud for Sheets.
  • Hover the app and then click +Free.
  • Follow the prompts to give add-on access to your Google Sheets spreadsheet.
Connect your Jira Cloud site with Google Sheets

To connect your Jira Cloud site with Google Sheets:

  • Go to a Google Sheets spreadsheet.
  • Select Add-ons, then Jira Cloud for Sheets, then Open….
  • Select CONNECT. This will open a new browser window.
  • Select the site you want to add from the list of available sites.
  • Select Accept.
Import data from Jira

Import work items to your spreadsheet with the following methods.

To import data from Jira using JQL
  • Go to a Google Sheets spreadsheet.
  • Select on Add-ons, then Jira Cloud for Sheets, then Open …, then Get data from Jira.
  • Specify the JQL for the query you want to run. You can select on the OPEN IN JIRA link to open and test the JQL query in Jira. If you don’t write a specific JQL query the system will import all work items on your site.
  • Select GET DATA.
To import data from Jira using filters

Your filter must be a Starred Filter to import to a spreadsheet.

  • Go to a Google Sheets spreadsheet.
  • Select on Add-ons, then Jira Cloud for Sheets, then Open …, then Get data from Jira.
  • Select the FILTERS tab.
  • Choose your filter from the list of available filters.
  • Select GET DATA. You can restrict the number of rows returned with Max Rows.
JIRA() custom function with JQL

Only owners of the document can enable the JIRA() custom function with JQL. When enabled, this function uses the document owner’s configured site and Jira account to query Jira.

Anyone who can edit the document can use the function to import Jira data using the document owner’s Jira account.

To import data from Jira using the JIRA() custom function with JQL:

  • Go to a Google Sheets spreadsheet.
  • Select Add-ons, then Jira Cloud for Sheets, then Open…, then Settings
  • Select Enable = JIRA() function for users of this sheet.
  • Read the warning and accept.
Troubleshooting and workarounds
I enabled the =JIRA() function and it’s still showing me an error.

Clear the value of the cell where you are using the =JIRA() function, press enter. Enter the query again and it should now work. You will only need to do this once (we’re working on fixing a bug causing this behavior).

The add-on returns an error when I want to query a large number of work items.

The add-on should work fine with queries of up to 10,000 work items. If you need to return more work items, you should use the =JIRA() function which lets you paginate through results. Make sure to sort the results in the query.

For example, to return 20000 work items, put this on one cell to return the first 10,000 work items:

=JIRA("space = ProjA order by updated desc", "", 0, 10000)

And this in another cell to return the following 10,000 work items:

=JIRA("space = ProjA order by updated desc", "", 10000, 10000

The add-on returns a generic error when importing work items.

Hmmm ... looks like we stumbled a bit, please try again or contact Atlassian support if the issue persists.

If you encounter the above error when importing work items:

  • Review the log for any authentication failures. If there are failures, reattempt the import process using valid authentication credentials..
  • The error may be due to attempting to import a large number of rows. If this is the case, retry the import with a reduced number of rows (e.g. 1000 to 2000 rows in batches)
  • Disconnect and then reconnect your Jira Cloud site through the add-on.
  • If the above steps do not resolve the error, uninstall and then reinstall the add-on to establish a new connection.
The add-on returns a ‘no Jira auth’ error when importing work items.

If you’re receiving a Jira authentication error when trying to fetch work items into Sheets:

  • Uninstall and then reinstall the add-on to establish a new connection.
  • Disconnect and then reconnect your Jira Cloud site through the add-on.
  • Create a new Google Sheet, paste the function in this new sheet, and reattempt the import.
  • Create a copy of the Google Sheet, and reattempt the import. If none of the above steps resolve the error, try revoking access in both your Atlassian account settings and on your Google account. Then, remove the add-on from Google Sheets, and try reauthorizing it again.
The add-on returns empty cells for user data.

The add-on respects individual users’ privacy settings for profile data. If a user has made their profile information private then the add-on will return a blank value for this user in columns like assignee or reporter.

What functionality does Jira Cloud for Sheets provide?

Jira Cloud for Sheets is an add-on you can use within Google spreadsheets to import data from Jira Cloud sites:

  • based on a JQL (Jira Query Language)
  • based on starred/pre-defined filters on Jira Cloud
How do I specify which columns are populated in the spreadsheet?

The add-on uses your column settings on Jira Cloud while importing data. You can have different column settings for your account and also for filters. If there are no user/filter specific columns configured on Jira Cloud, the add-on uses the default system columns.

You can specify different columns by using the =JIRA() function, for example:

=JIRA("space=MYP","workType,reporter,another column")

For advanced use cases

You can also extract subfields if you know the structure of the data returned by Jira Cloud API. For example, if you are interested only in importing the work items ID and the reporter’s display name, you can use the following arguments to the JIRA() custom function.

=JIRA("space=MYP","workType.id,reporter.displayName")

How do I uninstall this add-on?

You can uninstall the add-on by click on Add-ons > Manage Add-ons > Manage > Remove.

Can I use this add-on if I don’t have a licensed Atlassian Product?

No, you need a license/subscription for Jira Cloud to use this add-on.

Can I use this add-on with Jira Server?

No, the add-on only works with Jira Cloud sites for Jira Work Management, Jira Software and Jira Service Management. Check with your Jira administrator if you are not sure about cloud vs server.

How do I disconnect the spreadsheet from any connected Jira Cloud instance(s)?

You can disconnect all your configured Jira Cloud sites from the add-on. From a spreadsheet:

  • Select on Add-ons, then Jira Cloud for Sheets, then Open…
  • Select on on the Disconnect site button
  • this will redirect you to your Atlassian Identity profile page where you can disconnect the add-on/app by selecting Remove access.
Is this add-on GDPR compliant?

Yes. We also don’t store any personal user information. Read more in our migration guide.

What is the space toolchain in Jira?

The toolchain page makes it easy to discover, configure, and manage all the tool-based apps your team uses for a space.

Discover and integrate apps

Find the best DevOps apps for your team. Discover new apps and tools by browsing the categories on the page, and get tailored recommendations from Atlassian.

Discover our DevOps integrations

Using the toolchain page
  • To add an app, select Install next to an app.

  • To remove an app, select Apps, then select Manage apps in the global navigation. You must have site admin permissions to do this. To view the toolchain page, go to Space settings, then Toolchain. You must be a space admin to access this page.

Use Jira Cloud with Bitbucket

Use Jira Cloud with Bitbucket

Enjoy the seamless integration of work items and code by connecting Jira Cloud and Bitbucket Cloud.

Once connected, all you need to do is add a Jira work item key to a branch name, commit message, or pull request title to access key details and information. You can even create new branches and pull requests directly from a work item.

And on the other side, you can get core details from a Jira work item, without leaving Bitbucket. Simply select the linked work item wherever it’s been added in Bitbucket.

Connect Jira Cloud to Bitbucket Cloud | More on referencing work items in dev tools.

In company-managed software spaces, use the Releases view to display the state of all work items in the coming release, or, the releases panel to show how the deployment actually went.

More about tracking versions in the release view.

Bitbucket isn’t available in Atlassian Government environments.

Automate Jira workflows

Sync pull requests, commits, and branches to your Jira Cloud workflow so details update automatically. Use Smart Commit messages to process Jira Cloud work items.

Invite other workspace members

Make it easy for new members to find your repos in a workspace. More on how to automate team invitations.

Troubleshoot your connection

If you’re having problems, troubleshoot your connection with Jira Cloud.

Use Jira Cloud with Confluence

Use Jira Cloud with Confluence

To add Confluence to Jira, go to Switch sites or apps (), then More Atlassian apps to begin your free trial. You can cancel at any time via Manage applications.

What is Confluence?

Confluence is a content creation and collaboration platform that connects teams with the content, knowledge, and coworkers they need to get work done, faster. Confluence spaces are great for creating and organizing rich content related to Jira spaces using Confluence pages – meeting notes, project plans, requirement documents, release notes, roadmaps, and more.

Why use Confluence with Jira

Here are some of the reasons we think you might like to add Confluence to your Jira instance:

For bugs

Create a knowledge base article to document a workaround for a bug.

For new features

Create a product requirements document for a new feature.

For general use-cases

Document and collaborate with your team on a work item in Confluence.

What Confluence can do

Here are just a few of the things Confluence allows you to do:

  • Collaborative commenting, especially through the use of @mentions
  • Share pages
  • Watch pages
  • Form a ‘team’ network and let them know what you are doing via a status update
  • Add images, picture galleries, videos, and more
  • Enable various content macros
Confluence features for Jira users

Create a space in Confluence to give your team a central location for all relevant information, like:

  • product requirements
  • meeting notes
  • decision logs
  • retrospectives You can even display the open work items of your Jira space in your Confluence homepage. More about space blueprints
Define product requirements

Many of our customers write product requirements documents using Confluence to plan new product features. The Product Requirements Blueprint helps development teams collaboratively create, discuss, and organize their product requirements. It’s easy to link your product requirements in Confluence to work items in Jira.

More about Blueprints. Or, watch this 5-minute introduction.

  • Define the properties of the document, which are then indicated on any page with the Page Properties Report macro.
  • Communicate the status of your product requirements with the status macro.
  • Use @mentions to automatically notify key stakeholders.
Team Calendars for Confluence: Your birds-eye-view of Jira

Surface everything your development team is working on in Jira to the teams that live in Confluence with Team Calendars.

  • Timeline calendar: View plans 3 months ahead of time
  • JQL support: Track your versions, work items, and agile sprints
  • Date ranges: Visualize work items over time to understand the upcoming workload Read more about Team Calendars for Confluence
Insert work items on any Confluence page using the Jira work items macro

Any Jira search result can be embedded in a Confluence page using the Jira work items macro with your choice of included fields and field ordering. With the Jira work items macro, you can:

  • Display a table of work items on your page, based on the results of a search using Jira Query Language (JQL) syntax or a Jira URL.
  • Display a single work item from the Jira site, or a subset of selected work items from your Jira search results.
  • Display a count of work items from the Jira site.
  • Create a new work item on the Jira site and display that work item on your page.
Auto-convert pasted work item links

Auto-convert makes producing reports of work items, backlogs, and tasks as easy as copy and paste. With Jira and Confluence connected, you can paste individual work items or Jira query URLs into the editor and watch them immediately transform into the Jira work items macro.

Automatic links

Whenever a work item is mentioned in a Confluence page using the Jira work items macro, Jira will create a work item link to that page for you, automatically. Product requirements to work items, knowledge base articles to support tickets, project outlines to tasks—it all works.

Gadgets

You can embed a Confluence activity stream or a Confluence page in Jira’s dashboard. Likewise, Jira gadgets can be rendered on a Confluence page. More about Confluence Cloud gadgets.

Use Jira Cloud with Slack

Create and update Jira work from Slack

Create and update Jira work from Slack

With the Jira Cloud for Slack app installed, you can create a Jira work item from a Slack message using the message action menu. This flow is available with or without Rovo. If Rovo is available, it can pre-fill the summary and description from the thread context. If Rovo isn’t available, you can enter those fields manually.

Create a work item from Slack
  • Hover over any message in a channel or thread.
  • Select More actions ().
  • Select Create work item from Jira Cloud.
    • If Rovo is available, toggle Use Rovo to generate the summary and description on. The app remembers your preference for next time.
  • Review the auto-filled summary and description, or fill them in yourself if you didn’t use Rovo.
  • Fill in any remaining fields (space, work type, etc.).
  • Select Submit to create the work item. When Rovo is enabled, it can access the full thread context in channels, giving it the entire conversation to work with. In direct messages, it can only use a single selected message. The Rovo auto-fill is only available through the message action menu; it does not run when using the /jira create slash command.
View work items in link preview cards

Whenever anyone pastes a Jira work item link into a Slack channel, the Jira Cloud for Slack app automatically unfurls it into a link preview card. This card always shows the latest data from the work item.

And, if you type a work item key from a particular space (e.g. MSD-19) in a channel that’s connected to the same Jira space, Slack will automatically detect it and show the preview card. Make sure you type the work item key in uppercase letters.

From the preview card, you can:

  • See all key fields: Status, priority, assignee, labels, description.
  • Edit any field inline.
  • Summarize the work item: Rovo AI generates a quick summary you can share with the team.
  • Refresh: Select refresh on any card to pull the latest data from Jira.
  • Watch the work item to get updates in that channel.
  • Sync the thread: Push all replies in the thread as comments to Jira.
  • Add to work item: Share any Slack message to an existing Jira work item as a comment.

Get Jira notifications in Slack

Get Jira notifications in Slack

The Jira Cloud for Slack app can send Jira notifications directly in Slack, either as direct messages or as updates in a channel. You can configure which events trigger notifications, filter by space or priority, and take action on work items directly from the notification card.

Receive personal notifications in Slack

Personal notifications appear as direct messages from @Jira in Slack. You can control exactly what triggers a notification, so you only hear about what’s relevant to you. Personal notifications are on by default once you connect your account.

Set up personal notifications

Here’s how to set up, or update, your personal Jira notifications in Slack:

  • Open a DM with @Jira in Slack (or any channel the Jira bot is in).

  • Type /jira notify.

  • Choose your notification triggers: Essentials (recommended) or All.

  • Add optional filters: by space, work type, or priority.

  • Select Submit When you select Essentials notifications, you’ll receive notifications about the following:

  • work items assigned to you

  • mentions

  • comments on your work items

  • status changes on work items you’re watching

Turn off email notifications

Once you’ve set up personal notifications in Slack, you might want to disable email notifications so that you’re not receiving duplicate messages.

  • Select Settings (), then select Notification settings.
  • Use the toggle next to Send me emails for work item activity to disable email notifications.
View a personal notification in Slack

Each notification card shows you the work item title, current status, priority, assignee, and a summary of what changed. You can act on it directly - you don’t need to go to Jira.

Receive channel notifications in Slack

Subscribe a Slack channel to a Jira space so the whole team gets notified about relevant work items. There are a few different ways to connect your Jira space to the right Slack channel.

Connect a Jira space using the slash command in Slack
  • Go to the Slack channel you want to receive updates in.
  • Type /jira connect.
  • Select your Jira site and space.
  • Set your notification filters (work item type, priority, event type).
  • Select Confirm.
Connect a Jira Space from your Jira space settings

You can also set up Slack notifications from inside Jira.

  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Under Notifications in the sidebar, select Notifications.
  • Under Connect to Slack, select Get started, then connect a Slack channel. Space admins can configure notification filters, choose between a basic or extended format, and use JQL-based advanced filtering.
Manage your channel subscriptions

To see and manage all subscriptions in a channel, type /jira manage. From here, you can update filters, pause notifications, or disconnect a space.

Take action from a channel notification

Every notification card has contextual actions built in. Depending on the type of update, you may see the option to add a comment directly to the Jira work item.

You might see an option to transition the work item’s status (for example, from In Progress to Done).

You might also see the option to assign the work item to yourself or someone else, or to start or stop watching to control future notifications.

Get started with Jira Cloud and Slack

Get started with Jira Cloud and Slack

The Jira app is located in the Apps section of your Slack sidebar, alongside your channels and DMs. The Home tab shows the following sections:

  • Assigned to me: All open work items currently assigned to you.

  • Watching: Work items you’re following for visibility. For any work item listed on the Home tab, you can select More actions () to do any of the following:

  • Start or stop watching the work item

  • Assign it to yourself or someone else

  • Transition its status (for example, from To Do to In Progress to Done)

  • Comment on it directly

Invite your teammates

The Jira Cloud for Slack app allows you to invite your teammates without leaving your workspace.

Invite a teammate from Slack

If you add a Jira link to a Slack channel where one or more users don’t have Jira access, the app will prompt you to either invite them directly (if you can) or send a request to an admin to grant them access. Admins can review these requests in Atlassian Administration or directly in Slack.

If you receive a Jira link but don’t have access to Jira, the app lets you request access from Slack. Admins can review and approve the request in Atlassian Administration or directly in Slack.

Invite a teammate from Jira

When inviting users to Jira from Jira, you can invite teammates directly from your Slack workspace. Go to People, then select Invite a teammate, then Connect teammates from, then select Slack.

Integrate Jira Cloud and Slack

Integrate Jira Cloud and Slack

The Jira Cloud for Slack app brings your Jira work into Slack, so you can create work items, get notifications, and take action without ever leaving your conversations. Whether you’re triaging a bug in a thread, assigning a ticket to a teammate, or just checking the status of a work item, it’s all available right from Slack.

To get started, install the Jira Cloud for Slack app.

You can use the Jira app for Slack to create, update, and assign Jira work items using natural language, directly from any Slack channel or DM.

Before you begin
  • The Jira Cloud for Slack app must be installed on your Slack workspace. You can install it from the Slack App Directory.
  • After installing, you’ll be guided to log in to your Atlassian account to link Slack and Jira. This takes about a minute.
  • Once connected, you’ll get a direct message from the Jira Cloud app in Slack.
  • If you want Jira to work in a private channel, you must first invite @Jira to that channel.
  • If your organization has multiple Jira Cloud sites, you’ll be asked to select a site when connecting spaces or setting up notifications. Your Jira site administrator must enable the Slack integration at https://<your-instance>.atlassian.net/plugins/servlet/ac/jira-slack-integration/addon-config-page before anyone can connect. If you see a message like “Connecting with this Jira Cloud instance was disabled by administrator”, ask your admin to enable it first.

Slack workspaces are given a “Needs review” status until they’re approved by a site admin. You can still configure and use Jira from Slack until the site admin approves the relevant workspace.

What you can do from Slack

Feature

What it does

Home tab

See all work items assigned to you and ones you’re watching. Take quick actions.

Quick actions with AI

Use natural language to create, update, and assign Jira work items directly from any Slack conversation.

Create via action menu

Turn any Slack message into a Jira work item with a single click. Rovo AI pre-fills the details.

Thread to Jira sync

Sync a Slack thread as comments on a Jira work item.

Link preview cards

Paste a Jira link or just type a work item key (e.g. MSD-19) to get a live, editable card showing all key fields.

Personal notifications

Get notified about your work items directly in Slack DMs.

Inline actions

Comment, transition status, or assign a work item directly from a notification card.

Channel space subscriptions

Subscribe a Slack channel to a Jira space so the right team gets the right updates at the right time.

Slash commands

Create, search, and manage Jira from anywhere in Slack using /jira commands.

Invite teammates to Jira

Invite Slack teammates to Jira, or request access on their behalf, without leaving Slack.

Available slash commands

Type /jira help in any channel to see all available commands. Here are the most useful ones:

Command

What it does

/jira connect

Subscribe a channel to a Jira space.

/jira manage

View and manage channel subscriptions.

/jira notify

Set up or change your personal notification preferences.

/jira create

Create a new Jira work item directly from Slack. This opens a dialog where you can select a space and work type, then enter a summary and description.

/jira agent

Configure or update the @Jira settings for the current channel.

/jira [work item key]

Get information about a specific Jira Cloud work item. Note that this information will only be visible the person who uses the command.

/jira feedback

Give feedback about the Jira Cloud for Slack app.

/jira unsubscribe

Stop receiving notifications you no longer want.

/jira logout

Log out of your Atlassian ID. Your Atlassian ID is used to retrieve the list of sites to connect to or create Jira work items from. Logging out will not remove or suspend any of your previously set up subscriptions.

/jira help

See all available commands and what they do.

Security controls
Jira permissions are respected

The app respects existing Jira permissions at both the work item and administration levels. You’ll only ever see and interact with work items you have permission to access in Jira.

Work item-level security

If your Jira site uses work-item-level security schemes, Slack notifications will not be sent for work items with security restrictions applied. Read more about work item security schemes

Mention Jira in Slack to manage work

Mention Jira in Slack to manage work

You can use @Jira in any Slack conversation to create work items, update fields, and assign tasks in plain language, without leaving the thread.

An organization administrator must activate Rovo in Atlassian Administration before you can use this feature.

Set up Jira mentions in a channel
  • Go to any Slack channel (public or private) and type @Jira.
  • If the Jira app hasn’t been added to the channel yet, follow the prompt to invite it.
  • On first use, you’ll be prompted to configure how Jira works in this channel:
    • Select the Jira site you want to use in this channel.
    • Select a default space for the channel.
  • Select Save to confirm your configuration. Once configured, you’re good to go. You can update the configuration at any time by typing /jira agent
Where you can use @Jira

Surface

How to use it

Public channels

Use @Jira to add the app to the channel and start talking to it.

Private channels

Use @Jira to add the app and start talking to it.

Jira app Home tab

Use @Jirawithin the Jira app home to get started.

The Jira app must be added to the channel before initiating conversation. This is a Slack platform requirement.

Create work items

To create a work item, use @Jira in a channel or thread and describe what you need. For example:

  • @Jira create a bug for the login issue discussed in this thread

  • @Jira create a task with the summary “Update API documentation” Jira uses the context of your conversation to automatically fill in fields like space, work type, summary, and description. The context depends on where you @mention it:

  • If mentioned within a thread, Jira uses the full thread as context.

  • If mentioned outside a thread, Jira looks at the last 15 messages in the channel for context. If all required fields can be determined from context, the work item is created immediately, and a confirmation with a link is posted in the thread. If anything’s missing, Jira will ask you to fill in the gaps before creating the work item.

You can also ask Jira to summarize a thread into multiple work items at once. For bulk actions affecting more than 10 work items, you’ll be asked to confirm before proceeding.

Update work items

You can update existing Jira work items by using @Jira and describing the change. For example:

  • @Jira assign PROJ-123 to Sarah
  • @Jira change the priority of PROJ-456 to High
  • @Jira add a comment on PROJ-789 saying “Fixed in latest deploy” Jira links Slack users to their Atlassian accounts when assigning or mentioning team members. If a user can’t be found or doesn’t have access to the space, you’ll be notified.

For bulk updates affecting more than 10 work items, you’ll be asked to confirm before changes are made.

Follow up in a thread

After a work item is created or updated, you can continue the conversation in the same thread to request further actions. Use @Jira for each follow-up request. For example:

  • @Jira assign this to the QA team
  • @Jira change the priority to High
  • @Jira add a label “urgent” Jira maintains context within the thread, so it knows which work item you’re referring to.
Assign work items to agents

You can assign work items to coding agents directly from Slack. For example:

  • @Jira assign this to the coding agent
  • @Jira assign PROJ-123 to the QA agent You can do this as part of the initial creation request or as a follow-up in the thread after the work item has been created.
Manage channel configuration

To view or update how @Jira works in a channel:

  • Type /jira agent in the channel.
  • Update the site, space, or custom instructions as needed.
  • Select Save. The custom instructions field lets you guide Jira on your team’s conventions — like preferred work types, naming patterns, or default field values.

Migrate from the Jira Server integration for Slack

Migrate from the Jira Server integration for Slack

If you’ve already set up the legacy Jira Server integration (webhook-based) for your Jira Cloud site and want to switch to the modern Jira Cloud for Slack app, follow these steps:

  • Go to your-slack-team.slack.com/apps/manage and select Jira Server.
  • For each configuration you want to remove, select the pencil icon and then select Disable or Remove in the top-right corner.
  • Go to slack.atlassian.com and select Add to Slack to install the new Jira Cloud for Slack app.
  • Follow the installation instructions to set up the new app.
  • Once you’ve confirmed your Jira Cloud site, you can reconfigure your channel subscriptions and notification preferences in the new app to match your previous setup. The new Jira Cloud for Slack app is built on the modern Atlassian Connect platform and gives you access to features that aren’t available in the legacy Server integration, including the link preview cards, thread sync, and Rovo-powered work item creation.

Sync your Slack threads with Jira work items

Sync your Slack threads with Jira work items

Thread sync adds the messages from a Slack thread as comments on a Jira work item. This keeps the conversation context attached to the work item and makes it searchable in Jira

When you sync a thread, all previous messages are synced, not just new ones. Any new replies added after syncing will continue to appear as comments on the Jira work item automatically.

Sync a thread
  • In a channel where you’ve pasted a Jira link, select Sync with thread on the link preview card.
  • Select Confirm for all thread replies (including previous messages) to be added as comments to the Jira work item.
Unsync a thread

If you no longer want new Slack messages syncing to Jira, you can unsync the thread at any time:

  • Select More actions () on the link preview card in the thread.
  • Select Unsync thread. Messages already synced will remain as comments on the Jira work item. Only new replies will stop syncing.

When you create a single work item using the Jira app, the Slack thread is automatically synced with that work item’s comments. Synced threads are not enabled by default when multiple work items are created simultaneously in the same thread.

View and manage dependencies in your plans

Add a dependency in your plan

Add a dependency in your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

There’s a few different ways to add a dependency to work items in your plan.

Create a dependency on your timeline

The quickest way to create a dependency is using the drag and drop method. With your timeline visible, select a work item’s dependency badge icon next to its timeline bar, and drag it to the schedule bar of the work item to which you want to link it, as shown in the picture below.

Alternatively, select the dependency badge icon to open a menu that allows you to manually create the dependency.

Use Rovo Chat to add dependencies between work items in your plan. Enter /add-work-dependency, followed by a prompt like “ABC-1 should be blocked by ABC-4”. Rovo will suggest a dependency link for you to review and create without needing to go to the timeline, the program board, or the dependencies view.

Create a dependency on the Program board

From your Program board, select More (•••) on a work item, and select Add dependency. In the window that opens, select the type of relationship you want to create, and nominate the other work item. Use Add to save your dependency.

Create a dependency in the Dependency report

You can also create a dependency from the Dependency report view of your plan.

Choose the Add dependency button beneath the Review changes button, and configure your dependency in the menu that appears. When you’re done, select Add.

Change how your plan timeline displays dependencies

Change how your plan timeline displays dependencies

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

To change how your plan displays dependencies on your timeline:

  • From the timeline view of your plan, select to the View settings .
  • Use the Dependency style dropdown to choose your dependency style.
Dependency display options

If you’re looking at the list of your plan, you’ll only be able to see the Incoming dependencies and Outgoing dependencies columns. Find out how to show or hide your timeline bars.

When looking at the timeline, you can choose from either of the following options:

  • Badges adds a badge icon to either end of your schedule bar to show that a dependency is linked to that work item.
    • You can add the number of dependencies to badges using the Show number of dependencies checkbox underneath the Dependency style dropdown menu. This option is only available when you have badges selected. To view this number while viewing lines, hover over the schedule bar and the number will appear.
  • Lines connects dependent work items on your timeline with lines.
    • If your plan can’t display a line between two dependent work items, or if the dependency connects to a work item not included in your plan, a badge icon will be shown instead. To view the number of dependencies, hover over the schedule bar.
    • The line will turn red if there are conflicting dates. To resolve this, change the start or end date associated with the dependency.
    • If the dependency connects to a work item not included in your plan, or if the line can’t be displayed for any other reason, your plan will show the icon instead.
