Refine the dependencies view of your plan

Refine the dependencies view of your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

In the Dependencies view of your plan, you can choose which work items show and how they appear.

Parent work item and child work item are relative terms used to refer to higher-level work items that contain smaller tasks. This concept scales to any hierarchy level:

  • an initiative (parent work item) that contains epics (child work item)
  • an epic (parent work item) that contains stories (child work item)
  • a story (parent work item) that contains subtasks (child work item) In this documentation, we use initiative, epic, and story in examples to refer to hierarchy levels based on Agile best practices. However, in Jira these labels can be configured by your administrator.
Filter work items

Show or hide work items from your Dependencies view based on:

  • the space they’re in
  • sprint assignment
  • a specific work item
  • work item link type (if configured by your administrator)
Roll-up to

Choose at which hierarchy level you would like to see your dependencies – whether you’d like to see the individual story-level work items, or how this relationship impacts the parent work items.

If you choose to view your dependencies up to levels above the dependent work items, it shows as a dotted line to indicate that the dependency being referenced is not of the same hierarchy level as your current view. Select the x links text above the dotted arrow to reveal the specific work items which are dependent on each other.

Group by

You can group dependencies based on:

  • Team
  • Sprint
  • Space
  • Parent-level work items (such as Epic)
    • You can only group by the parent-level work items above story in your site. For example, if your Stories roll into Epics which roll into Initiatives, you’ll only be able to group by Epics. When grouping by the parent-level task, subtasks are automatically rolled up into the Story-type level.

View all of a work item’s dependencies on your plan

View all of a work item’s dependencies on your plan

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

With the timeline section of your plan visible, select the dependency icon on either side of the schedule bar to show all of the dependencies attached to that work item. When your plan is set to show Badges, these icons are always visible on your timeline. If you have your plan set to show dependencies as Lines, they only show when you hover over the schedule bar.

Regardless of how you get there, selecting the icon will bring up a window. In it, you’ll find the following information:

  • Type - “is blocked by” denotes an incoming dependency while “blocks” denotes outgoing
  • Work item - Work item details of the dependent work item
  • Status
  • Assignee
  • Lead time - The number of days between the dependent work items
  • Filter by dependencies - Hides other work items on your timeline to highlight this dependent chain You can also dependencies from the Summary tab on the left side navigation. Learn more about the Summary page.

What are dependencies in your plan?

What are dependencies in your plan?

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

Dependencies in your plan indicate work items that are reliant on others being completed first. Your administrator can configure other work item link types to show in your plan, but they’re all treated as through they’re of the Blocks type meaning that the first work item must end before the second one can begin.

On your timeline, dependent work items are either connected by a line or numbered badges at either end of the schedule bar to indicate the direction of the relationship (whether it blocks a work item or it’s blocked by a work item). Change how your plan shows dependencies.

Off-track dependencies

Dependencies in your plan turn red to indicate when the lead-in work item is putting the second work item at risk. This is referred to as being off-track, and helps identify potential scheduling problems with your plan.

The plan owner can also choose to show dependencies in the same iteration as off-track.

What is the dependencies view in your plan?

What is the dependencies view in your plan?

This page refers to the advanced planning features that are only available as part of Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise.

The Dependencies tab in your plan displays work items as tiles with arrows to illustrate which work items are dependent on others. To open this view, select Dependencies from the navigation.

The Dependencies view only shows work items in your plan that have dependencies, either incoming or outgoing; the arrow between work items indicates the direction of their relationship. If the arrow turns red, this indicates that the dependency is off-track.

To resolve an off-track dependency, select on the work items tile, then choose Locate work item in timeline. Read more about off-track dependencies.

Using the filters at the top of the page, you can change how they’re grouped, filter out work items, and more to focus on the work items you want to see. Find out how to refine the dependencies view

View and understand insights in team-managed spaces

Configure insight settings in a team-managed project

Configure insight settings in a team-managed project

We’re in the process of removing insight settings from software projects. Insights will continue to show as normal, but admins won’t be able to enable or disable specific insights, and any insights that were previously disabled will now be enabled.

To send us feedback about this change:

  • In your Jira software project, select Board or Backlog.
  • Select Insights.
  • Scroll to the bottom of your Insights and select Give feedback. This page is for team-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

If you’re in a company-managed space, check out these company-managed space articles instead.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed space.

Configure your sprint insight settings

On your board’s sprint insight settings page, find all the insights that can easily be enabled or disabled. Set the toggle to enable if you want the insight to show up on your board’s insights panel, or set it to disable if you prefer not to show a specific insight. Sprint insight settings are board scoped and visible to anyone in the team with access to the board.

  • Open the Insights panel on your board and select settings ().

  • All insights are enabled by default, select the toggle to disable the insights you don’t want to show on your board’s insights panel. or

  • Select Project settings from the project sidebar > Board.

  • Select Insights from the board settings menu. All insights are enabled by default, select the toggle to disable the insights you don’t want to show on your board’s insights panel. You can change this at any time, simply come back to this page and set the toggle to enable if you want an insight to show on the panel.

To configure the insight settings for your board or backlog, you must be either:

  • a project admin for the location of the board
  • a board admin for the board See Permissions overview for more information.
Configure your backlog insight settings

On the backlog insight settings page, find all the insights that can easily be enabled or disabled. Set the toggle to enable if you want the insight to show up on your backlog insight panel, or set it to disable if you prefer not to show a specific insight. Backlog insight settings are visible to anyone in the team who has access to the backlog.

  • Open the Insights panel on your backlog and select settings ().

  • All insights are enabled by default, select the toggle to disable the insights you don’t want to show on your backlog’s insights panel. or

  • Select Project settings from the side panel > Board.

  • Select Insights from the board settings menu; first, you’ll find the board insights. Select the Backlog tab. All insights are enabled by default, select the toggle to disable the insights you don’t want to show on your board’s insights panel. You can change this at any time, simply come back to this page and set the toggle to enable if you want an insight to show on the panel.

Understand insights on the backlog in team-managed projects

Understand insights on the backlog in team-managed projects

The following information only applies to team-managed, scrum projects.

To check your project type, look at the bottom of your project’s left-hand sidebar. If you don’t see an icon stating You’re in a team-managed project, then you’re in a company-managed project. Check out our company-managed project documentation.

Insights on the backlog provide support for you and your team during sprint planning sessions and retrospectives.

Sprint commitment

Review your previous sprint commitments during your sprint planning sessions to get an idea of past trends. Look for your ideal range, and aim to assign the target amount of story points, work items or time.

The sprint commitment insight looks at the average story points completed, work items completed, or time logged in the last five sprints to recommend a target range for future sprints. The insight respects the estimation statistic that’s enabled for your project; story points, work item count or time.

Learn how to enable estimation in a team-managed project.

As you plan, the story points, time or work items you commit to the sprint will be tallied and compared to your target. Recommendations are automatically calculated if your commitment falls outside the target range, making it easy for you to adjust your scope as you plan.

Access your commitment metrics from your previous or current sprints by selecting the bars on the chart. If you select the current sprint you’re planning the insight will expand to show you the number of points or hours you’ve committed. You can also view the recommended range of points or hours to help you plan for the best outcome.

When selecting a previous sprint, the insight will expand to show your completed points or hours, incomplete work and the total percentage of work completed.

Work type breakdown

Use the work type breakdown for sprint planning sessions. Assess the balance of work from previous sprints to adjust, or maintain, your focus next time around.

See the work type breakdown for your sprint. As work is assigned, the visualization and callout adjust, so you can understand the balance of different work types. The insight only displays the work types allocated to that specific sprint.

The callout lets you know which work type appears the most in the sprint. This is useful during retrospectives, so you can reflect on recurring, time-consuming work types.

During planning sessions, assess your top work type to make sure your team isn’t heavily focused on bugs and tech debts. Too many bugs and a hefty tech debt could be a cue for your team to focus on quality or block out time to resolve debts.

Hover over the bar associated with each work type to see the exact number of work items allocated to the sprint, and the percentage it contributes overall.

Understand insights on the board in a team-managed project

Understand insights on the board in a team-managed project

Insights use the latest browser-features. Check which browsers we currently support.

Sprint progress

Hit every daily scrum meeting with a dose of insights. As you run through your board, see how your sprint’s tracking to understand the likelihood of completion.

Understand exactly how your sprint’s progressing across each status category, making it easier for you and your team to pivot, set expectations, or see work through.

The bar is split by the number of story points, work items, or time assigned to each status category. If your project has story points enabled, the progress bar will update when points are added to each work item.

So, at a glance, you can understand the portion (and percentage) of work that hasn’t been started, is in progress, or done.

Hover over each status category section to see a breakdown by story point, work item count or time estimate.

Sprint burndown

Keep an eye on your team’s sprint progress as it’s happening. By frequently tracking your output against your goal, you can shift focus, maintain momentum, or take a moment to revel at your pace.

The Y-axis represents the total amount of work committed to a sprint. As work’s completed, the percentage and corresponding blue line reduce, indicating how much work remains.

The grey horizontal line acts as a guide. It indicates roughly what percentage you’d expect to see at that point in time, in order to reach 0% by the end of your sprint.

Find your scope change information underneath the Burndown chart when you add, remove or modify work items after the sprint has started.

This expansion of the insight gives you more transparency over unplanned work. Scope change information will equip you with the right amount of detail to manage your team’s priorities effectively.

Hover over the sprint scope changes to reveal a tooltip with the most recent scope changes. You can also select these data points to see a list of affected work in a separate tab.

Overall, you’ll be able to track exactly how much work remains compared to how much work was planned. This helps you manage and pace effort gives you adequate time to respond to trends and allows faster decision-making to help your team achieve their sprint goals.

Work items for attention

Stay on top of flagged or blocked work items in your sprint or on your Kanban board. This will help you assess impact, pivot priorities, and continue to move work forward.

The work items for attention insight surfaces stuck work items, work items that are blocked by their dependencies, and flagged work items. This makes it easier to address high-priority work within your current sprint or on your board.

Select the Insights button to view the Work items for attention insight

  • The All tab is the default view and offers a list with all work items for attention. This list may include stuck, blocked or flagged work items. Work items in this list may also be a combination of stuck, flagged or blocked.
  • Work items that take too long to progress will be marked as “stuck”. We consider a work item as “stuck” when it spends a longer time in a particular status than is expected compared to your other work items. Select the Stuck tab to view a list of these work items.
  • Blocked work items are under the Blocked tab. This list contains all work items that are blocked by other dependencies.
  • For flagged work items, check the Flagged tab. Work items are ordered by set priority or due date, which makes it easier to know what to pay attention to next. The description underneath the tabs changes with what work items are showing up, and this offers information at a glance of the work items for attention you’ll find in the list. Select the work item to expand its view and see more detail.

You might have Prev and Next buttons at the bottom of the insight. This means that there were too many work items to display in one list. Select Next to view the remaining work items under the tab, or select Prev to go back a step.

A work item can be flagged via the More menu found in the top right corner of the work item. Blocked work items are linked to their dependencies using the Blocked by link, found in the quick-add button. Stuck work items are automatically labelled as stuck when the work item exceeds the 85th percentile for their current status.

Work progress

Keep an eye on your priorities and stay on track to achieve your goals by seeing how your sprints contribute to larger pieces of work.

Epics can be renamed, and the default name can vary in business spaces. The information on this page is relevant, regardless of whether your space uses the name epic, workstream, or any other name.

Epics will often represent a big goal, project, or outcome. Instead of tackling everything all at once, Scrum teams often break down big goals into smaller pieces of work that then get added to a time-boxed sprint.

The work progress insight helps you connect the work you’re doing in your sprint to that larger goal or outcome. This could mean your sprint only contains work items working towards one epic, such as your launch plan. Or, maybe your team choose to divide and conquer and add work to a sprint that helps to progress multiple outcomes

The insight also indicates when the work items in your sprint aren’t working towards any epics. This might be because your work items haven’t been assigned to an epic or workstream. If the work has been assigned to an epic, and it’s still not showing up in the insight, check your estimation statistic. Right now, insights support story points, time estimation, and work item count.

Insights, and other combined metrics, are sourced from various sets of project-level data. That data is rolled up into a summarized figure to represent an aggregated view of a single metric.

Use insights with a board or backlog backed by a filter

Insights use the latest browser-features. Check which browsers we currently support.

You can use a JQL filter to define which work items appear on your board or backlog.

Although insights live on your board and backlog (and deployments view), they surface project-level data. This is what gives you a holistic view of your efforts and possible areas for improvement.

The insight feature won’t display unless your filter includes a specific project. This includes filters based on a work type, such as a Bug, or an assignee, as well as user-owned boards.

A project admin can see if your board or backlog is based on a JQL filter.

Work in Jira business spaces

Add, edit, or delete a shortcut

Add, edit, or delete a shortcut

You can add shortcuts to the space navigation to link to information you think your team may find useful. When you add a link, it’s available to all users who can access the space.

To add, delete or edit a link, you must have the Jira Administrator permission or the Space Administrator permission. When adding or editing a link, you need to have the full web address, and you must give it a name that will show in the Shortcuts menu. Naming the shortcut makes it easier to identify where the link will take you.

Add a shortcut
  • Select Spaces, then select a starred or recent space, or choose View all spaces and select a space.
  • Select Shortcuts in the space navigation.
  • Enter the web address and name for your shortcut and select Add shortcut. You must enter a valid web address that is recognized by Jira. These must be prefixed with a valid scheme (or URI scheme).

Valid schemes (or URI schemes) for shortcuts are:

http://, https://, mailto:, skype:, callto:, facetime:, git:, irc:, irc6:, news:, nntp:, feed:, cvs:, svn:, mvn:, ssh:, itms:, notes:, smb:, hipchat:

Edit or delete a shortcut
  • Select Shortcuts in the space navigation.
  • Select Edit shortcut () next to the shortcut you want to edit.
  • Do either of the following:
    • Edit the link details and select Update; or
    • Select Remove shortcut.

Add, rename, or delete a column in team-managed business spaces

Add, rename, or delete a column in team-managed business spaces

This page is for business spaces

To check whether you’re in a business or software space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

If you’re using a team-managed business space, you can make updates to your space’s workflow directly on the board, without needing to navigate to the space settings.

Columns on the board are controlled by your space’s workflow, so updates made to your board’s columns will be reflected in your workflow.

  • Work items on the board must be grouped by status (which is the default) to add, edit, or delete columns from the board.
  • You can only add, edit, or delete columns on the board if your space uses a single workflow. You must have the following to do the things described on this page.

Role:

  • a space administrator for the location of the board
  • a board administrator for the board itself Go to permissions overview for more information.

By default, a board’s columns are assigned the default Jira statuses To do, In progress, and Done. You can change this to suit your way of working.

For example, you may create a custom status to capture work In review, and you’ll probably want to map that status to an appropriate column on your board, too.

All team-managed spaces start out with the Jira default workflow. This means default columns are assigned a default status, like this:

Column

Status

To do

To do

In progress

In progress

Done

Done

More about how your work flows in Jira team-managed spaces.

Add a column in your business space’s board

Creating a new column on the Board will create an associated status. The newly added column will contain a status in the status category you select (To do, In progress, or Done).

To add a column to your board:

  • Select Create status () next to the rightmost column.
  • Give your status a name.
  • Select Submit to create the new column and associated status. You can rearrange columns to suit how you’d like them to be ordered in the workflow. How to rearrange columns on the board

To change the status, or statuses, associated with specific column, you could either:

  • From your board, go to More actions (), then select Configure columns.

  • Select (drag and drop) a status from an existing column, or from the Hidden statuses panel, and pop it in it’s new column. Or,

  • Navigate to a specific column. From More actions (), select Add a new status from dropdown.

Rename a column in your business space’s board

To rename a column on your board:

  • Select the text in the column you want to rename. Alternatively, select More actions (•••), then Rename.
  • Enter a new name for the column.
  • Select the tick symbol or press return (Mac) or Enter (Windows) on your keyboard.
Delete a column in your business space’s board

To delete a column from your board:

  • Select More actions (•••) in the top-right corner of the column you want to delete.
  • Select Delete.

Alternatively, hover over the value of each row and select Edit or Delete when they appear.

Create a business space

Create a business space

Jira spaces represent shared containers for you and your team’s work. When creating a new space in Jira, you can select from a variety of pre-configured templates designed to accommodate different ways of working. For example, if you’re coordinating a go-to-market launch for your product or business, select the Go-to-Market template to create a space with a pre-configured workflow that follows this process. Learn more about the templates available when creating a new space in Jira.

Jira admins can create any kind of space using any template. By default, any user with access to the site can create a space using a team-managed template. This setting can be changed in Jira’s global permissions.

There are a few ways you can create a new space, one way is to:

  • Select the plus icon + in the space sidebar.

  • Choose from the dropdown which template you’d like to use.

  • Give your space a name and review the details of your space. Depending on the template and space type selected, you may also be asked to set additional settings, such as the access level of your space. You can change these details later in your Space settings.

  • Select Create space. Another way to create a space is to:

  • Select Spaces > Create space in the top navigation bar.

  • Browse the space templates available by category or product. Select a template to view more information, including the template’s default work types and workflow.

  • Once you’ve chosen a template, select Use template.

  • Give your space a name and review its details. Depending on the template and space type selected, you may also be asked to set additional settings, such as the access level of your space. You can change these details later in your Space settings.

  • Select Create space. A space key will automatically be created. Now that your space has been created, you can configure its settings and begin adding your team.

Space names are unique in Jira. They are always visible to Jira administrators and anyone with the Administer Jira global permission. Avoid using confidential or sensitive terms in your space’s name. If you need to label a space with confidential or sensitive information, we recommend using a codename, instead.

Create a company-managed space that shares its settings with another space

Only Jira admins can create company-managed spaces (spaces with shared settings).

When creating a new space in Jira, you can choose to share its settings with another existing space. This means that if a change is made to one space, it will be reflected in all spaces that share this setting.

These settings that can be shared across spaces include:

  • Work types

  • Workflows

  • Screens

  • Fields

  • Permissions

  • Notifications To share a new space’s settings with an existing space, follow the steps above to choose a template and fill in the details of your space. On the Create space screen:

  • Select the Share settings with an existing space checkbox. The Choose space dropdown will appear.

  • Choose the space that you want to share your new space’s configuration with.

  • Select Create.

Customize cards on your business space’s board

This page is for business spaces

To check whether you’re in a business or software space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

You can customize the cards shown on your board to see the information that’s most important to you. You can choose to see as much or as little information on the cards of your work items on the board.

You can customize the board cards to see the following fields, and any supported custom fields you’ve set up for your space:

  • Key

  • Type

  • Assignee

  • Reporter

  • Due date

  • Start date

  • Updated (last updated)

  • Subtasks (if your space has subtasks as a work type)

  • Priority

  • Labels

  • Created

  • Confluence items (if your license includes Confluence)

  • Linked work items

  • Category

  • Card cover The supported custom field available are:

  • Short text

  • Date picker

  • Date time picker

  • Single select

  • Select List (multiple choices)

  • Number

  • People field (team-managed space only)

  • Single user picker (company-managed space only)

  • Multi user picker (company-managed space only) To adjust what information you view for the cards on the board, you can:

  • On the board, select View settings.

  • In the Show fields section, choose what fields you’d like to be visible on your cards by enabling or disabling the field toggles. The fields of the cards will automatically adjust on your board.

Customize card covers

To add or change a work item’s card cover on the board:

  • Hover over a work item.

  • Select More actions ().

  • Select Select cover.

  • Choose a color, gradient, photo by Unsplash, or an image attachment to set it as the cover. To hide all card covers on the entire board:

  • On the board, select View settings.

  • In the Show fields section, select (or deselect) Card cover.

Edit and reorder work items on the timeline

Edit and reorder work items on the timeline

This page is for business spaces

To check whether you’re in a business or software space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

You must have the following to do the things described on this page.

Permission: Edit work items

View and edit work items in detail from the timeline

To view a work item in more detail, select its key on the left of the timeline. This appears as a string of letters and numbers. For example, ABC-123.

The work item will open, where you can view its description, status, assignee, and other information in more detail. Learn more about editing work items

Reorder work items on the timeline

Select the work item name and drag it up or down to reorder it. If the work item has child items, they’ll remain with their parent. Your changes will be reflected in the board and list views as well.

Add or adjust start and due dates on the timeline

To reschedule a work item, select the entire schedule bar and drag it forwards or backwards. If the work item has child items, they’ll move with it.

To change the duration of a work item, select and drag the handles at either end of the schedule bar.

If your work item doesn’t have a start or due date yet, you can add the dates directly to the timeline. Hover your cursor over the timeline until you see the correct start date, then click to add a schedule bar.

Filter work items

Filter work items

You can filter work items in your list, board, calendar, and timeline view. Filtering helps you focus on specific details in your spaces to find important information without having to scroll through your entire team’s work. You can check high-priority tasks to see that nothing is blocked or see individual team members’ workloads at a glance.

  • All users can use the filter in these views.
  • Your filter will only be visible to you.
  • Your filter will persist when when navigating between views and different spaces
Filter work items

Filter the work items you’re searching for by selecting Filter at the top of the list view. You can either apply quick filters or other filters but not both at once.

Apply quick filters

You can apply one or more of the following quick filters:

  • Assigned to me
  • Due this week
  • Done work items You can also create your own quick filters which allow you to save, reuse and access them later with just one click. Saving your filters will let you see the most important information first. You can also view saved filters created by your teammates.
Apply other filters

You can also apply the following filters to view specific work items:

  • Date range: You can filter work items by a specific date range by selecting the Start date and Due date
  • Assignee: You can filter work items by selecting the avatar or by searching the name of the assignees. You can select Unassigned to view work items that don’t have an assignee
  • Category: You can filter work items by the categories added to your space. You can select No category to view work items that don’t have a category assigned
  • Goals: You can filter work items based on the goal it contributes to.
  • Work type: You can filter work items based on their work type. For example, you may only want to filter by subtask. You can filter your work items based on whether they are tasks or subtasks.
  • Labels: You can filter work items by selecting a label added to your space. You can select No label to view work items that don’t have a label assigned
  • Parent: You can filter work items based on it’s respective parent item.
  • Priority: You can filter work items based on priority such as blocked, highest, high, medium, low, and lowest
  • Reporter: You can filter work items by selecting the avatar or searching the name of the reporter
  • Status: You can filter work items based on status, for example, to do, in progress and done
  • Team: You can filter work items based on which team is assigned.
Clear filters

To clear your filters:

  • Select Filter from the top of your screen.
  • Select Clear selection. You can also select ( x ) next to the fields to clear the applied filter.

When cleared, the board, list, calendar, or timeline reverts to the default view, showing all work items.

Filter by assignee using avatars

To see the work items assigned to a particular team member, select their avatar at the top left of your preferred view and you will see all the work items filtered by that assignee.

Child work items when a filter is applied

When filtering work items you’ll still see both parent work items and subtasks if they match your filter. However, child work items will not be nested under their parent.

Currently, the board view does not support filtering by subtasks.

Filter by custom fields

You can filter by the following types of custom fields in the list, board, calendar, and timeline view of your space:

  • Single select
  • Multi-select
  • Multi-checkboxes
  • User picker (company-managed spaces only)
  • People field (team-managed spaces only)
  • Custom date More about custom fields

How to manage approvers

How to manage approvers

This page refers to approvals, which is a feature in team-managed business spaces that’s only available for:

  • Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise licenses
  • Jira Service Management Cloud Premium and Enterprise licenses You can define preset approvers in your approval process. That means that when a work item reaches a status that triggers an approval, the preset approvers will be automatically added as approvers to that work item. You can always modify these approvers in the work item later if you choose.
Manage approvers for a specific work item

To add or change approvers on a specific work item:

  • Select the work item you’d like to add more or different approvers to and open it up in the work item dialog.
  • Select Add approvers below the list of approvers to the right of the work item dialog.
Remove existing approvers

To remove approvers on a specific work item:

  • Select the work item you’d like to remove approvers from and open it up in the work item dialog.
  • Hover your cursor over the approvers you’d like to remove, and select the trash icon to finalize.
Manage preset approvers

To manage the preset approvers in an approval step in your workflow, you can:

  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Approvals.
  • Select the edit icon under Actions in the table and you’ll be taken to the approval configuration in the workflow editor.
  • Manage the preset approvers field by entering a name or removing an approver.
  • Select Save.
  • Select Update workflow at the top-right of the workflow editor to apply your approval and any changes to your workflow. Once all of the approvers listed on the work item have signed off, the work item will be transitioned through to the approved transition. If one of the approvers decline, the work item will go through the declined transition.

Save your filters in business spaces

Save your filters in business spaces

This page is for business spaces

To check whether you’re in a business or software space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

If you use filters frequently in your business space, saving filters will allow you to save, reuse, and easily access them later. Saving your filters across your board, list, timeline, and calendar will let you see the most important information first. You can also view saved filters created by your teammates.

Create a saved filter

To create a saved filter:

  • Select Filter at the top of your board, list, calendar, or timeline view.

  • Apply all the filters you want to save.

  • Select Save filter on the top right of the Filter dropdown.

  • Name your saved filter.

  • Select Save filter. Your saved filter will be at the top of the Filters dropdown of whichever view you’re in.

  • You can create multiple saved filters for your space but you can only apply one at a time.

  • Your saved filters are specific to the space you create them in.

Apply a saved filter

You can apply a saved filter by either selecting it or searching for it from More actions (…) in the Filter dropdown. All the filtered fields are highlighted when you apply a saved filter.

Edit a saved filter

Currently, you can only edit the name of your saved filter. If you want to edit the attributes in the saved filter, you’ll need to create a new one and delete the existing.

Only you can edit the name of a saved filter you’ve created. Here’s how you can edit the name of a saved filter that was created by you:

  • Select Filter at the top of your board, list, calendar, or timeline view.
  • Hover over the saved filter.
  • Select Edit ().
  • Enter a new name for your saved filter.
  • Select Save.
Star a saved filter

You can star the saved filters created by you and your team.

To star a saved filter:

  • Select Filter at the top of your board, list, calendar, or timeline view.
  • Hover over the saved filter.
  • Select the star icon (). When you star a filter, it appears at the top your Filter menu so you can easily use it.

There is no limit on the number of saved filters you can star.

Search for a filter

You can search saved filters created by you and your team and apply them to your spaces. This search will also include your starred filters.

To search for a saved filter:

  • Select Filter at the top of your board, list, calendar, or timeline view.
  • Select More in the Filters dropdown
  • Enter the name of the saved filter in the search bar
  • Select the filter you want to apply.
Delete a saved filter

You can delete any saved filter that you’ve created.

To delete a saved filter:

  • Select Filter at the top of your board, list, calendar, or timeline view.
  • Hover over the saved filter.
  • Select Delete (). The saved filter will be removed from your space.

Set up approvals in your business space

Set up approvals in your business space

This page refers to approvals, which is a feature in team-managed business spaces that’s only available for:

  • Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise licenses
  • Jira Service Management Cloud Premium and Enterprise licenses Before you add an approval step to a workflow

Make sure:

  • You have space admin permissions to add an approval step to a workflow.
  • You have transitions set up for your workflow. How to set up transitions There are two ways you can set up an approval. You can set up approvals through the workflow editor or the approvals view for your business space. Setting up an approval process can help your team standardize and adhere to effective governance to minimize risk when delivering work.

Your team may need approval for work items as part of your business process before they can move to the next status in their workflow.

Before you can set up approvals, you’ll need to have transitions set for each status. How to set up transitions

Set up approvals from the approvals tab

Here’s one way you can set up approvals for your business space:

  • Select Approvals in your space navigation, then select Approvals.
    • If you’ve never used approvals in your business space before, you’ll need to add it to your navigation first. In your space navigation, select add to navigation (), then select Approvals.
    • Select Add to navigation.
  • Select Set up approvals.
  • Select which workflow to apply an approval to. Some space may only have one workflow — in which case, you’ll set up an approval process for that one workflow. If you have multiple workflows, you’ll need to choose which workflow and associated work types to apply an approval process to.
  • Choose a status from your workflow to trigger an approval from.
  • Select Continue.
  • Select who you’d like to nominate as preset approvers. Preset approvers will be automatically added when the work item reaches the status you’re triggering an approval from. You can always modify the list of approvers in a work item later.
  • Give the approver field a name. This is a custom user picker field that contains the people you want to approve the work item.
  • Choose a transition for when the work item is approved.
  • Choose a transition for when the work item is declined.
  • Select Save.
  • Select Update workflow at the top-right of the workflow editor to apply your approval and any changes to your workflow.
Set up approvals through your space settings

Here’s another way you can set up approvals for your business space:

  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Work types from the sidebar navigation on the left.
  • Choose which work type’s workflow you would like to edit, then select Edit workflow of that work type’s screen.
  • Select the status you want to add an approval step to.
  • Select the plus symbol next to Approvals in the right sidebar to open up the approvals setup screen.
  • Select who you would like to nominate as preset approvers. Preset approvers will be automatically added when the work item reaches the status you’re triggering an approval from. You can always go back and modify the list of approvers in a work item later.
  • Give the approver field a name. This is a user picker field that contains the people you want to approve the work item.
  • Choose a transition for when the work item is approved.
  • Choose a transition for when the work item is declined.
  • Select Save.
  • Select Update workflow at the top-right of the workflow editor to apply your approval and any changes to your workflow.
Troubleshoot setting up your approval

For further support when setting up approvals for your space, see more about troubleshooting your approval setup.

Important to note once your approval process is set up

When you set up approvals for your space, approvals will not be retrospectively applied to existing work items that are already at the status you’re triggering an approval from. The approval process will only be applied to new work items that go through the workflow.

Show software releases in a business team calendar

To check whether you’re in a business or software space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

You must have the following to do the things described on this page.

Role: Space admin

Here’s how to show software release dates in a business teams’ calendar.

Stay up to date with a software teams’ release dates, and better plan your marketing campaigns or customer-related tasks.

If you’re using a software space, see Manage releases in your calendar.

This feature isn’t currently supported for cross-space views.

Show and hide software release dates
  • Navigate to the calendar view in your business space.

    • Premium users can select up to 5 spaces.

View the Releases panel

The Release panel in your calendar will show the following:

    • UNRELEASED indicates the release has not been shipped
    • RELEASED indicates the release has been shipped
    • OVERDUE indicates the release has passed its due date
  • The progress of work items in the release:
    • TO DO, IN PROGRESS and DONE
  • The start and release dates
  • The software space selected

Sign off and approve work

Sign off and approve work

This page refers to approvals, which is a feature in team-managed business spaces that’s only available for:

  • Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise licenses
  • Jira Service Management Cloud Premium and Enterprise licenses There are a few different ways that you can sign off and approve work if an approval has been set up for your space.
Sign off through the approvals view

To view work items pending your approval:

  • Select Approvals in your space navigation.
  • Select Pending your approval at the top-right of your approval view. This is where you’ll see all work items that are pending your approval.
  • Select either the tick or cross icon under Action to approve or decline the work. Another way you can approve work is by opening the work item, and selecting Approve or Decline in the right section of the dialog.
Approval notifications

When your approval is required, you’ll receive a notification and an email. The notification and email will link you directly to the work item, where you can view more information, and approve or decline the work.

Troubleshoot approvals in business projects

Troubleshoot approvals in business projects

This page refers to approvals, which is a feature in team-managed business projects that’s only available for:

  • Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise licenses
  • Jira Service Management Cloud Premium and Enterprise licenses If you’re having problems setting up approvals for your team-managed business project, this page can help you troubleshoot the setup process.
Set up transitions for your workflow before you can set up approvals

You’ll need to set up transitions for your statuses for approvals to work properly. The reason this needs to be set up correctly is so you can identify a status destination for when a work item is approved or declined.

Ideally, your approved transition progresses the work item to the next stage in the workflow or Done. The declined transition destination should go back to a status so that the assignee (or person who has requested approval) can review why the work has been declined.

Once you’ve set up transitions for your workflow, you’ll need to:

  • Select the status you’re triggering an approval from in the workflow.
  • Select the plus icon next to the approvals section in the right sidebar.
When ‘any status’ is applied to your approval status

You can still set up your approval and apply it to your workflow, however if you have the ‘any status’ transition applied to the status your work item will move to once approved, your approval process can be bypassed. It means that you can move a work item from any status to the approved status, bypassing the entire approval process.

To make sure that you don’t skip any steps in the workflow and that work doesn’t proceed without approval, you need to set up proper transitions between your statuses. How to manage work item transitions

Be sure to remove ‘any status’ transition applied to the status you’re triggering an approval from to avoid it from making your approval process redundant. There are a few ways to remove the ‘any status’ from a status:

  • Select the ‘any status’ lozenge in your workflow and select the Delete transition button at the bottom right of the screen, or press delete or backspace on your keyboard.
  • Select the status your work item will move to once approved, then in the right sidebar, deselect ‘Allow work items in any status to move to this one’.
Approver fields

The approver field needs a different name for each approval process that’s set up.

The field is a multi-select user field that stores the list of approvers and responses. If you have multiple approval steps in a workflow, you cannot share the same field. For each approval step, you’ll need a distinct name so the field can store the list of approvers and their response for each step.

Give each approval that you’re setting up a unique name. In workflows with multiple approval steps, you’ll need a distinct name for each step so the field can store the distinct respective approvers and their responses.

Preset approvers can be changed by those with edit access to the work item

Anyone in the project with Edit any work item access can manage preset approvers from the work item. How to manage approvers

View all attachments in a business project

View all attachments in a business project

This page is for business spaces

To check whether you’re in a business or software space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

Add attachments to work items and provide additional context to your team’s work. Images, documents, videos, spreadsheets and PDFs are supported as attachments.

View all attachments in a project

To view all attachments in a project, select Attachments from the project navigation. Any attachment that has been added to a work item in your project will appear here. This means you won’t need to search through work items to find a specific attachment.

Use filters to find a specific attachment

In Attachments, you can use the following filters to find a specific attachment more easily:

  • Added by: Filter attachments by the people who added them to a work item.
  • Attachment type: Filter attachments by the type of attachment, for example, an image or document.
  • Date added: Filter attachments by the date they were added to a work item.
Add an attachment

If you don’t have permission to add attachments, contact your admin.

To add an attachment to a work item.

  • Open the relevant work item.
  • Drag and drop the attachment onto the work item. You can also select Attach and upload your attachment.
Download attachments
Download a single attachment

To download an attachment from a work item:

  • Open the relevant work item.

  • Hover over the relevant attachment and select Download (). If attachments are displayed in a list, Download () will appear to the right of the attachment. If you don’t know which work item an attachment belongs to, you can download the attachment from the Attachments view:

  • Select Attachments in the project navigation.

  • Hover over the relevant attachment and select Download ().

Download multiple attachments

To download multiple attachments from a work item:

  • Open the relevant work item.
  • Select More actions (•••) above the attachments, then Download all.
Delete an attachment

If you don’t see Delete () when hovering over an attachment, the attachment might have been uploaded in the description or in a comment in the work item. To delete the attachment, navigate to the work item and edit the description or comment.

If the attachment isn’t in the description or a comment and you still can’t see Delete (), you may not have permission to delete it. If this happens, contact your admin or find out who added the attachment.

Delete a single attachment

To delete an attachment from a work item:

  • Open the relevant work item.

  • Hover over the relevant attachment and select Delete (). If attachments are displayed in a list, Delete () will appear to the right of the attachment. Alternatively, you can delete an attachment from the Attachments view (this is helpful if you don’t know which work item the attachment belongs to):

  • Select Attachments in the project navigation.

  • Hover over the relevant attachment and select Delete ().

Delete multiple attachments

To delete multiple attachments from a work item:

  • Open the relevant work item.
  • Select More actions (•••) above the attachments, then Delete all.

View and manage versions in business projects

View and manage versions in business projects

This page is for business spaces

To check whether you’re in a business or software space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

This page is for company-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed spaces.

Versions are points-in-time for a project. They help you schedule and organize your releases. Once a version is created and work items are assigned to it, you can use the version to filter information in various reports. If you’ve integrated Jira with Bamboo, you can start a build automatically.

You must have the following to do the things described on this page.

Role: Space admin

Permission: Administer spaces, Manage versions

Manage a project’s versions

You can manage versions in your project’s settings:

  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Versions from the project settings sidebar. The Versions or Releases page is displayed, showing a list of versions and each version’s status. From here you can manage the project’s versions as described on this page.
Version status

Each version can have any of the following the statuses:

  • Released — a bundled package
  • Unreleased — an open package
  • Archived — a historical snapshot of a package Versions that include end dates can indicate when a release is overdue. The release date appears in red for unreleased versions that have passed their planned release date.

The status affects where the version appears in drop-down lists for version-related work item fields, for example Fix version.

Add a new version

You can create as many versions as you want to represent a package you intend to release.

To create a version:

  • On the Releases or Versions screen, select Create version.
  • Give the version a name. You might organize versions by number, for example “3” or “3.2.2”. Or you might use code names, for example “Corvette” or “DeLorean”.
  • Optionally, add a start and release date, and a description.
  • Select Save. You can rearrange versions by dragging and dropping them in the table.
Add a work item to a release version

If your project has a backlog:

  • Go to the Backlog view, then select the Versions panel on the left.

  • Drag work items to the appropriate version If your project doesn’t have a backlog:

  • Open a work item you want to add to a version

  • Locate the Fix versions field and enter the version to add the work item to The work item is added to the version you entered. If you can’t see the Fix versions field on your work item, make sure to click the Show more option below the last field on the work item. If you still don’t see it, take a look at Defining a screen to add the field to your screen.

Fix versions vs Affects versions fields

Jira has both Fix versions and Affects versions fields. So what’s the difference?

Fix versions shows the version that the work on the work item is released in. If you fix a bug in and the fix is released in version 3.6.2, the Fix version should be 3.6.2. Entering a version in the Fix versions field adds the work item to the release version.

Affects versions details the versions of your product that a work item—a bug, for example—affects. You may find the bug in several previous versions, and you can add those versions to the Affects versions field. Entering a version in the Affects versions field on a work item does not add the work item to the version, but using the field enables you to search for work items that affect particular versions.

Add a version start date

If specified, the Start date is used by the Version Report. This gives you a more accurate report in cases where you might plan a version many weeks (or even months) in advance, but not actually commence work until closer to the release date.

Release a version

Marking a version as released will affect some changes in some reports and some work item fields’ drop-downs. If you have integrated Jira with Bamboo, you can trigger a Bamboo build to run automatically when releasing a version in Jira. The version will only be released if the build is successful. For more information, see Running a Bamboo build when releasing a version.

  • On the Releases or Versions screen, find the version you want to release.
  • Select the More actions (), then select Release. To revert the release of a version, simply select Unrelease from the More actions menu ().
Archive a version

To archive a version (and hide it from reports or other parts of your project):

  • On the Releases or Versions screen, find the version you want to archive.
  • Select More actions (), then Archive. To revert the release of a version, simply select Unarchive from the More actions menu ().
Merge versions

You can merge one version into another and move its work items to the desired version.

To merge versions:

  • On the Releases or Versions screen, find the version you want to merge into another.
  • Select More actions (), then Merge.
  • In the dropdown, select the version you want to merge to.
  • Select the Merge button.
Edit a version’s details
  • On the Releases or Versions screen, find the version you want to edit.
  • Select More actions (), then Edit.
  • Edit the version’s name, start and release date, and description.
  • Select the Save button to save your changes.
Delete a version
  • On the Releases or Versions screen, find the version you want to edit.
  • Select More actions (), then Delete. From here, you can specify the actions to be taken for work items associated with the version. You can either move these work items to another version, or simply remove references to the version you want to delete.
Reschedule a version

Rescheduling a version changes its place in the order of versions. On the Releases or Versions screen, drag and drop versions into the release order you prefer.

What are approvals in business spaces?

What are approvals in business spaces?

This page refers to approvals, which is a feature in team-managed business spaces that’s only available for:

  • Jira Cloud Premium and Enterprise licenses
  • Jira Service Management Cloud Premium and Enterprise licenses Simplify your approval process using Jira business spaces instead of chasing people up via email or instant message. Having an approval process is a key component of effective governance and can play a critical role in helping teams and organizations achieve their goals while minimizing risk along the way.

Approvals are embedded into your space’s workflow to save you time following up with stakeholders. You can customize your approval process to have multiple approval steps to match how your team operates.

Here are some examples how approvals can be used:

  • A copywriter needs the legal team to sign off on content they have written for a new webpage for a marketing campaign.
  • A technical writer has written hardware documentation for their team’s product that a compliance team needs to approve.
  • An event coordinator is organizing an end of year party for their team, and needs to expense certain costs. Before they can expense these costs, they need approval from management for the budget.
  • A designer creates a new experience for the homepage of an app that is being developed. Before the software developers start their work on this, a design manager need to review and approve this work before it can move to the next status in the workflow.

What is the timeline view and how do I use it?

What is the timeline view and how do I use it?

This page is for business spaces

To check whether you’re in a business or software space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

The timeline view helps visualize the timing, duration, and dependencies of work items in your space. Easily view how long tasks take to complete and when things will land. It gives a general overview of the status of your work, making it well suited for sharing progress with leaders, stakeholders, or just within the team.

To start using the timeline, open your space and select Timeline in the space navigation. You can only use the timeline view if you are in a business space. If you still can’t see it, your admin may have removed the timeline view from your space.

How to use the timeline view

Your space’s timeline is a Gantt chart view that can be used to visualize and plan the timing and sequence of individual work items. The schedule bars on the timeline represent the start date and due date of each work item in your space. Schedule bar colors represent the status of each work item.

  • Hover over a horizontal line and select a work item to set a start and due date.
  • Move the schedule bar to adjust the start and due date of the work item or change the duration by dragging the handles of each bar.
  • Drag the schedule bar to reschedule a work item. If the work item has any subtasks, they’ll be moved as well.
  • Select the name and drag up or down to reorder the work items in your timeline
  • Link work items in the timeline that are contingent on others being completed first.
  • View which work items may be blocked due to a certain issue.
  • Change how much time you’re viewing with the button in the bottom right: Weeks, Months, or Quarters.
  • Select the Today button at the top right to go back to today’s date (which is marked with an orange vertical line).
  • Select Filter to filter work items on your timeline.
  • Use keywords from your work item summary or description to search in the timeline view. Enter the keyword and all work containing those keywords will be shown. You can also search by entering the whole work item key.
  • Add important key fields like assignee and status as columns on your timeline so that you track work quickly without opening each work item. These fields are now inline editable in the timeline.
How roll-up works on the timeline

On the timeline, parent items (like epics) can automatically reflect dates and progress based on their child work items.

  • The parent start date is the earliest start date of its child items.
  • The parent end date is the latest due date of its child items.
  • The parent’s progress reflects the statuses of its child items. This helps you quickly see if a parent item is realistically scoped and how it’s tracking without opening each child work item.

Roll-up might not apply in some situations:

  • No child items: If a parent item has no child work items, its dates won’t be rolled up from anything else — you can set and adjust them manually.
  • Filtered timeline view: When your timeline is showing items as a flat list, roll-up can be turned off so you only see each item’s own dates.
  • Space with more than 10,000 work items: In very large spaces, we may turn off automatic roll-ups to help keep the timeline fast and responsive. In that case, parent items won’t automatically calculate dates from their child items

Work with boards in business spaces

Work with boards in business spaces

This page is for business spaces

To check whether you’re in a business or software space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

Jira business boards are designed to give you an easy and clear way to visualize work. You get a snapshot of your team’s progress, including what work is yet to be started, what’s currently being worked on, and what’s been completed.

To start using boards, open your space and select Board in the navigation. A few things to know about your board:

  • Ranking: By default, work items are ordered by their rank. You can change an item’s rank by dragging and dropping it relative to others on the board or in other Jira views.
  • Infinite board capacity: The board displays all work items in your space. To view more items in a column, scroll to the bottom of the list and additional items will load automatically.
  • Hide done work items after: You can choose to have work items in a Done status category clear from your board after a certain period of time (7, 14, 30, or 60 days), or select Never to keep them on your board indefinitely. From your board, select View settings, then select Hide done work items after to pick your preference.
Board actions
Track work progress

As you start new tasks or finish something, move it along your workflow from one status to the next. Select a work item, then drag and drop as it progresses.

Rank and prioritize work

You can manually sort and rank work items in each column to suit how your team picks up work. Moving an item up or down will change its rank across all views (not just on the board).

Group work items

By default, work items are organized into columns by Status. To organize work further, use the Group menu to add swimlanes to your board.

You can group work items into swimlanes by:

• Priority

• Category

• Assignee

Rearrange columns (space admins only)

Space admins can reorder columns on the board and change the column status mapping. These changes apply to every user of the board.

For more detail about rearranging columns, see Workflows and statuses for boards in business spaces.

Save board defaults (space admins only)

Space admins can set a default column order and view for everyone using the board:

  • Update the board (columns, card fields and applied filters) to achieve your desired layout.
  • Select Save or reset view settings, then select Save board.
  • Once saved, this layout will become the default view for all users.
Card fields

You can customize which information is visible on your work item cards. This includes default system fields and specific custom fields.

To change which fields appear on your cards, select View settings, then select Show fields and toggle your preferred options. See card customization options

Expand or collapse board columns

In the column you’d like to expand or collapse, select the expand () or collapse () icon next to the column heading.

Complete a work item

Select a work item to open its detailed view. From there you can update fields, like the description, assignee, and due date; comment or watch the work item; and add attachments, linked work items, and sub-tasks.

A work item includes:

  • Quick-add buttons: Add attachments, subtasks, linked work items, and content from Atlassian Marketplace.
  • Transition work items: Quickly get from To do to Done, and any status or workflow step in between.
  • Watch and more actions: Watch the work item, and perform other actions like move and clone.
  • Work item details: Assignee, labels, components, time tracking, custom fields, and more. Choose Show more to view all fields.
  • Configure work item layout: Move and hide fields in the work item view.
Board columns and your workflow

There’s a correlation between your space’s workflow and the columns on your board.

They don’t have to be in the exact same order, but a step in the workflow will be represented as a column on your board, and a column on your board will show in your workflow.

Workflow steps:

To add or rename columns, you need to edit the workflow. For more information, see How do I build the workflow I want?

Manage column mapping (space admins only)

To change which statuses are mapped to specific columns, select More actions (•••), then select Configure columns. From here, you can:

  • Create and rename columns: Organize your board layout to match your team’s process.
  • Map multiple statuses to a single column: Combine different workflow steps into one visual column to simplify your board.
  • Hide statuses from the board: Move a status into the Unmapped statuses section to hide work items in that status from the board entirely. Note: When a space admin saves changes to the status column mapping, any personal column-based customizations previously made by other users will be reset to the new admin default.
View work items in specific workflow

By default, your board will show work items from all workflows. To view work items from a specific workflow, you’ll need to create a new board for each workflow

To filter by work type on your board:

  • From your Jira business board, select Filter.

  • Navigate to the Work types section, then select which work types you’d like to show for that workflow.

  • If your board is too busy, select Collapse () to minimise a column. To manage a workflow for a specific work type:

  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.

  • Go to Work types, then select the work type you’d like to edit.

  • Select Edit workflow, make your changes, then Update workflow.

Workflows and statuses for boards in business spaces

Workflows and statuses for boards in business spaces

This page is for business spaces

To check whether you’re in a business or software space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

Statuses and transitions

Two concepts define a workflow:

  • Statuses: the steps in your team’s working process that describe the state of a piece of work.
    • Status categories: Jira lets you collect many statuses under a To do, In Progress, or Done category. These categories help you sort, filter, and report on your work. For example, you might have a Backlog To do status and a Waiting for approval To do status. Or, you might have a Developing In Progress status and an In review In Progress status.
  • Transitions: This is how a piece of work can move between statuses. In order for a work item to move between two statuses, a transition must exist. A transition is a one-way link, so if a work item needs to move back and forth between two statuses, two transitions need to be created. The available workflow transitions are listed on the work item at the top-right corner in a dropdown.
    • Global transitions: Global transitions allow any status in a workflow to transition to a particular status. For example, you can drag a work item from the To do column directly to the Done column if the Done status has a global transition. More about global transitions
Workflows

Each workflow is composed of a set of statuses and transitions that your work item moves through during its lifecycle, and typically represents work processes within your organization. The path that your work items take is called a workflow. More about workflows

Different work types in your business space can have different workflows. For example, you may want to define a particular workflow or set of steps for a bug to pass through, compared to a task.

For team-managed spaces

Only space admins can edit workflows for your team-managed space. View more about how to manage workflows in a team-managed space

For company-managed spaces

Only Jira admins can edit workflows for your company-managed space. View more about how to manage workflows for a company-managed space

Statuses

The board is a visual way to view the status of your work items. The status for each work item can be determined by which column it’s in if your board is grouped by status. More about grouping on the board

If your work item is sitting in the To do column, then that’s the status of the work item. You can also view the status by opening the work item, and viewing the status at the top right corner.

Your board’s statuses (in the columns) may differ depending on the template that you’re using or how your admin has configured the workflow. So, depending on which template you’re using for your business space, your board’s statuses may look different across your spaces.

You can hide done work items after 7, 14, 30, or 60 days via your board’s View settings. (By default, this is set to “never”, meaning done work items will stay on the board indefinitely.) Work items will still appear in the list, timeline, and calendar views, even if they’ve been hidden from the board.

Multiple workflows on your board

If your business space contains multiple work types with different workflows, your board will show work items from all workflows by default. To view work items from a specific workflow, you’ll need to create a new board for each workflow.

First, create a new board:

  • In your space navigation, select Add to navigation ()

  • Select Board, then select Add to navigation.

  • Enter a name for your new board. Then, filter by work type on the new board:

  • From your Jira business board, select Filter.

  • Navigate to the Work types section, then select which work types you’d like to show for that workflow.

  • If your board is too busy, select Collapse () to minimise a column.

Rearrange the columns in your board

Only Jira and space admins can rearrange the columns in your business space’s board.

To rearrange columns in your board:

  • In the top right corner of your board, select More actions (•••).
  • Select Configure columns.
  • Drag and drop columns to reorder them. For example, you may want to move your in-progress column first so you can easily see what’s in flight.
  • Select Publish to save your changes. Space admins can also rearrange columns by dragging them directly on the board, or by selecting More actions (•••) on a column header.

The column order applies to every user of the board.

Add custom fields to your space

Add custom fields to your space

In addition to the default fields that exist in your space, you can create other fields you’d like to include in your space.

Users can create fields in two ways:

  • In company-managed spaces, Jira admins can create fields in their settings.
  • In team-managed spaces, they can do the above plus create fields while on list view.
Custom fields in a company-managed space

Only Jira admins can set up custom fields that can be used in your list view for company-managed spaces.

You’ll need to add custom fields to your company-managed space to be able to view them in your space. How to create custom fields for your company-managed space

You can currently add the following custom fields to your space:

  • Date picker
  • Date time picker
  • Number field
  • Select field (single select)
  • Select field (multi-select)
  • Text field (single line)
  • Text fields (multi-line)
  • URL field
  • Labels
  • Checkbox
  • User picker (single and multi-user)
Custom fields in a team-managed space

Only space admins can set up custom fields that can be used for team-managed spaces.

You’ll need to add custom fields to your team-managed space to be able to view them in your list. How to create custom fields in team-managed spaces

More custom fields will be added over time to give you and your team more flexibility in viewing specific information in your list.

Filter by custom fields

You can also filter by the following types of custom fields in your space:

  • Single select
  • Checkbox
  • Multi-select
  • User picker (company-managed spaces only)
  • People field (team-managed spaces only)
  • Custom date
  • Formula More about filtering items in your space

Confluence signup from Jira

Confluence signup from Jira

When you enable the Confluence integration in Jira, users can create Confluence content without leaving Jira. Users who only have Jira can request access directly from a few locations in the Jira interface, including in the Add menu in a work item and after they complete a sprint.

Enable Confluence signup in Jira

Jira admins can turn each of the three create content options on or off for users who only have Jira. This prevents users from starting the Confluence signup process from within Jira.

Turning this off will not remove any previously linked content or block users from linking existing Confluence content.

Admins can go to Product settings → Integrations → Confluence to change these settings.

Users without a Confluence account

When a user who only has Jira and not Confluence tries to create new content, they will be invited to join Confluence according to the organization’s account sign-up settings.

Users with a Confluence account

Users who already have both Jira and Confluence access can create new content in three areas:

  • After a sprint: When completing a sprint, users can create a Confluence page or whiteboard with a retrospective template.
  • From the work item view toolbar: Select the Add dropdown to create a new page, whiteboard, or database that will be linked to the work item.
  • In the Confluence linked content section: When users select the plus icon (+) in the Confluence content section, they can create a new content item that will be automatically linked to the work item.
  • From linked content: Users without Confluence access can see if content is already linked to the work item. Selecting the content items will let users start the signup process. Confluence content in Jira respects Confluence’s space and content permissions. If a user doesn’t have access to a content item that’s linked to a Jira work item, they won’t be able to open it or see the title. When they select an item, they will be able to request access from the content’s owner.

Connect Cisco to Jira

Connect Cisco to Jira

The incidents feature in Jira allows you to view, triage, and track incidents from Cisco Cloud Observability products. Using this feature, your development team can:

  • View incidents impacting the services they manage
  • Create Jira issues automatically populated with incident details
  • Create post-incident reviews (PIRs) to get to root cause and prevent incidents from recurring
Before you begin

To install the New Relic for Jira app, you need:

  • Site admin permissions for your Jira site

  • Admin role permissions your Cisco Cloud Observability product

  • A Cisco clientID, and secret key created by a Cisco admin For some organizations, the task of connecting Cisco to Jira might involve multiple team members with different role permissions:

  • A Jira site admin to install the Cisco Cloud Observability for Jira app

  • A Cisco admin to create and provide a secret key

Install Cisco Cloud Observability for Jira app
  • In Jira, select Apps, then Explore more apps.
  • Search for Cisco Cloud Observability for Jira, then select it from the results.
  • Select Get app, then Get it now.
Connect Cisco Cloud Observability for Jira
  • After the app is installed, select Get started. If the app is already installed on your Jira site, you can find this section by selecting Apps, then Manage your apps, and then Cisco Cloud Observability for Jira.
  • Select Set up.
  • Select Continue.
  • Paste your Cisco API token, then select Connect.
Connect Cisco Cloud Observability services

If your team’s service aren’t connected, go the incidents feature:

  • Select Connect services.

  • Search or select the services your team manages.

  • After you have selected services, select Connect. How to use the incidents feature:

  • Connect New Relic to Jira

  • Connect and remove services in Jira
