Connect Jira Service Management services to Jira Software

When you connect a Jira Service Management service to Jira Software, incidents and post-incident reviews (PIRs) associated with that service will appear in the incidents feature. Once you remove one, the incidents and PIRs associated with the service will no longer appear.

Once you’ve connected services your team owns, you can add more or remove connected services.

Connect and remove services in Jira

You need access to Jira Service Management to connect services to a space.

To connect services if none are connected:

  • From your space’s sidebar, select Incidents.

  • Select Connect services.

  • Search for or select services from the list, then Connect.

  • Once services are connected, select Manage services to add more. To remove connected services:

  • Go to Manage services.

  • Select the more actions icon () next to the service you want to remove.

  • Select Remove connection.

  • The incidents page will refresh to exclude the removed service. Read about the incidents feature

Create a chart showing data from your work items

Create a chart showing data from your work items

Using charts to visualize data in Jira can give you fast insights about your team’s work, helping you make decisions, progress individual items, and spot potential problems quickly.

Create a chart

You can create a chart from the List view in your Jira Cloud space:

  • From your space navigation, select List.
  • Select More actions (), then View work items as a chart.
  • In the dropdown, select the column you’d like to see in a chart.
  • Select your preferred chart type. The chart will show all the filtered work items from your current settings in the List view For example, if you’ve filtered the list of work items to show “Done” items, and then you create a chart based on the “Assignees” column, the chart will show the number of “Done” work items belonging to each assignee.

If you can’t see a particular field in the Column dropdown, try adding it as a new column in the List view.

Organize your board

  • Select the Group by drop-down at the top-right of the board
  • Select Clear.

Save and share views in Jira

Save and share views in Jira

Saved views give teams a consistent way to look at work in a space. Space admins can create shared views so everyone starts from the same setup, while individual users can adjust a view for their own work without affecting the rest of the team.

A saved view stores a snapshot of a view’s configuration. It isn’t a live link to a saved filter or to another user’s personal changes.

What are saved views?

A saved view is a reusable space view that captures how work is displayed in Jira. It can include things like filters, visible columns, grouping, and other view settings, depending on the experience in which the view is used.

Saved views help teams switch between common ways of viewing work, such as:

  • a planning view for upcoming work
  • a delivery view focused on in-progress items
  • a reporting view grouped by owner, status, or another field Because saved views belong to the space, they help teams work from the same starting point without requiring everyone to recreate the same setup manually.
Create a saved view

If you have space admin permissions, you can create a saved view from the list or timeline in Jira.

Create a saved view from the list
  • Start in a Jira space and select List from the space navigation.
  • Use filters and grouping options to refine your list.
  • Select Configure columns if you want to add or remove columns, then drag and drop to change the order of columns.
  • Select More actions () for other view options, like hiding Done work items or showing the work item hierarchy in the list.
  • Select Save or reset view settings (), then select Save list.
Create a saved view from the timeline
  • Start in a Jira space and select Timeline from the space navigation.
  • Use filters to adjust the timeline view according to your preferences. Select the View settings icon for additional options.
  • Select Save view settings () then select Save view.
Who can manage saved views?

Saved views have different capabilities for space admins and regular space members.

Space admins

Space admins control the shared version of a saved view. They can:

  • create a new saved view
  • save changes to a view for everyone in the space
  • rename or reorder a saved view
  • set a default saved view
  • delete a saved view When a space admin saves a view, that configuration becomes the team’s shared version.
Space members

Regular space members can use saved views, but they can’t control the shared version. They can:

  • open and switch between saved views
  • change the view for their own use
  • reset their personal changes back to the admin-saved version When a regular user makes changes to a view, those changes only affect that user’s experience. They don’t update the shared space view for anyone else.

This table shows a summary of what actions can be performed by space admins compared to regular users:

Action

Space admin

Regular user

Create a saved view

Yes

No

Save changes for the whole space

Yes

No

Make personal changes to a view

Yes

Yes

Reset to the admin-saved version

Yes

Yes

Rename, reorder, set default, or delete a saved view

Yes

No

What a saved view includes

A saved view generally stores settings that affect how work is displayed. This can include:

  • filters applied to the view
  • visible fields or columns
  • grouping or hierarchy settings
  • display preferences A saved view preserves the context for how results are presented, providing more than just a query.
Saved views compared to saved filters

Saved views and saved filters solve different problems. This table shows a summary of the key differences between these two features:

Feature

Saved view

Saved filter

Purpose

Saves how work is displayed in a space view

Saves a reusable work item query

Scope

Shared in the space experience

Reusable across supported Jira experiences

Includes layout settings

Yes

No

Can be updated for everyone by regular users

No

No, unless they own or can manage the filter

A saved filter focuses on which work items appear. A saved view goes further by capturing how those work items are arranged and shown in context.

How shared and personal changes work

Each saved view has a shared version managed by space admins, and a personal working state for individual users.

This gives teams a balance between consistency and flexibility:

  • Admins provide a stable default view for the team.
  • Users can temporarily tailor that view to suit their own work.
  • Users can select Reset to return to the admin-saved version. This model helps keep shared views reliable while still letting individuals work in the way that suits them best.
When to use saved views

Use saved views when your team needs different, easy-to-access ways to look at the same space data. For example, a team might use one saved view for weekly planning and another for reviewing daily progress.

Share a Jira board or backlog in Confluence

Share a Jira board or backlog in Confluence

Share your team’s Jira board or backlog in Confluence using Smart Links. You can add Jira Smart Links to the content tree in the left-side navigation area or embed them in another content type.

Sharing a board

Select the share icon () in the backlog’s top section, then select Copy link. This copies a web address (known as a URL) to your clipboard. That URL links back to Jira.

Share it in the content tree

There are two ways to add a Smart Link to the content tree.

  • Select Create in the main navigation, then Smart Link. This will create in the space you are currently in or will default to your personal space/whichever space you have edit permissions.
  • Select the plus icon () in the Content section of the space sidebar, then Smart Link. This will create the Smart Link in the content tree directly where you want it. After selecting Smart Link, you’ll be prompted for a URL. Paste the Jira link and select Add Smart Link to finish.
Share it in a page, blogpost, whiteboard, or database

Create a new content item or edit an existing item.

Paste the link you copied from the board. It will render as a Smart Link in embed view.

Sharing a backlog

In addition to boards, Jira software projects also display issues in a backlog view.

Select the share icon () in the backlog’s top section, then select Copy link. This copies a web address (known as a URL) to your clipboard. That URL links back to Jira.

Share it in the content tree

There are two ways to add a Smart Link to the content tree.

  • Select Create in the main navigation, then Smart Link. This will create in the space you are currently in or will default to your personal space/whichever space you have edit permissions.
  • Select the plus icon () in the Content section of the space sidebar, then Smart Link. This will create the Smart Link in the content tree directly where you want it. After selecting Smart Link, you’ll be prompted for a URL. Paste the Jira link and select Add Smart Link to finish.
Share it in a page, blogpost, whiteboard, or database

Create a new content item or edit an existing item.

Paste the link you copied from the board. It will render as a Smart Link in embed view.

Use smart replies in work item comments

Use smart replies in work item comments

To use smart replies

  • Select a work item.
  • Scroll down to the comment box.
  • Select one of the smart replies to auto-add it to the comment box. (Scroll sideways to view any additional smart reply options.)
  • Either type more information within the comment box, or select Save to publish the comment to the work item. Premium and Enterprise Customers

If you’re a Premium or Enterprise customer utilizing Jira’s AI feature, you’ll experience AI-powered smart replies. The smart reply buttons act as prompts for AI to draft more detailed comments and conversation-starters for you, rather than simple, pre-populated comments.

To disable smart replies

If you don’t want to use a smart reply, simply start typing in the work item’s comment box, and the smart replies will disappear.

To disable* the feature (affecting everyone in your Jira instance):

  • Go to (settings).
  • Select System settings.
  • Select Edit settings.
  • Next to Smart replies, select Off. *Admin permissions required

View your work suggestions in Jira

View your work suggestions in Jira

What are Jira work suggestions?

Jira work suggestions provide automated task recommendations generated from multiple connected tools to help you decide which task to complete next.

Knowing what to work on next can be challenging as you navigate several tasks during your work day. When managed with several tools in your toolchain, it’s especially easy to lose sight of ad-hoc tasks, such as reviewing pull requests or resolving critical vulnerabilities. You and your team can eliminate bottlenecks and maintain daily work momentum with contextual, timely, and actionable work suggestions. You can see information about the task at a glance, making it easy to plan your work and stay ahead of what needs to be done.

Work suggestions are available on scrum and kanban boards in Jira.

Types of work suggestions

You’ll see customized work suggestions for you when:

  • you’re added as a reviewer on an open pull request
  • you’re added as a reviewer on a draft pull request
  • your pull request has changes requested
  • your pull request is ready to merge
  • there hasn’t been any activity on your pull request for more than five days
  • deployments related to work items currently assigned to you have failed
  • builds related to work items currently assigned to you have failed
  • there are critical security vulnerabilities related to work items in your sprint
  • a work item assigned to you in the current sprint blocks other work items
  • a work item assigned to you in the space blocks other work items You may get some or all of these work suggestions depending on the source code management tool you’re using and its connection with Jira, as well as the specific type of Jira board in use, whether it’s an agile or a scrum board.
View your work suggestions

Jira work suggestions are enabled by default for you. You’ll see the work suggestions panel on your Jira board only when suggestions are customized for the context of your work are available and you haven’t previously disabled work suggestions.

To view your work suggestions:

  • Go to your Jira board and select your avatar to open the work suggestions panel.
  • Hover on or select a suggestion to view more information about the task and take action.
  • Hover on a suggestion and select Snooze for 24 hours or Remove suggestion to permanently remove the suggestion from your work suggestions list. Your suggestions are only visible to you and won’t be visible to other team members or admins.
Close the work suggestions panel

To temporarily close the work suggestions panel, select Close () on it.

The panel will open again when you select your avatar on the Jira board, provided suggestions are available for you, and you haven’t turned off work suggestions.

Turn off work suggestions

If you don’t want to get any work suggestions, you can turn it off altogether. Once turned off, the work suggestions panel won’t open when you select your avatar on the Jira board.

  • Go to your Jira board.
  • Select View settings at the top-right of your active sprints view, turn the Work suggestions toggle off. You can always turn Work suggestions on at any time to start getting suggestions again.

What is the summary view?

What is the summary view?

The summary view helps you monitor the progress of your space by giving you a high-level overview of your team’s work. It includes a snapshot summary of your space’s status, priorities, workload distribution across team members, and progress across your team’s larger pieces of work.

Enable the space summary

The summary view is enabled by default in all spaces. To view your space summary (assuming it’s enabled), navigate to your space, then select Summary.

To disable the summary in a software space:

  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Features.
  • Select the toggle to the right of Summary. You can re-enable the summary at any time from Space settings.

Only space admins can enable and disable features on a space.

View the space summary

Keep reading to discover what each section means in your space’s summary.

Overview cards

At the top of your summary, there are four overview cards. These four sections provide an overview of recent activity within the space by displaying the number of work items that have been completed, updated, and created in the last seven days, as well as the number of items due in the next seven days.

Status overview

Here’s where you can view your space’s overall progress on work items, based on the statuses in your workflow. Only items that have been completed in the last two weeks will appear in Done. If you don’t have any work items in your space, you’ll need to create some to get the most value out of this section. Read more about workflows

Recent activity

Stay up to date with what’s happening across your software space. Scroll through the feed to view recent activity and select a link to the relevant activity you’d like to review.

Priority breakdown

Here’s where you can get a holistic view of how work is prioritized within your software space, to make sure that your team is focusing on the most important work first. The priority breakdown will only display if you have selected a priority for each work item in your space. How to define priorities

Types of work

Get a breakdown of your space’s work items by their type. In this list, you can check out the work types linked to your space, as well as how the work items are distributed across each type. Read more about work types

Team workload

Here’s where you can view your team’s current workload at a glance. Making sure work is equally and correctly distributed across your team will ensure your space is properly resourced.

You can assign work to the correct team member by editing the assignee field in the list view. How to edit work items in the list view

Work progress (for software spaces)

View a breakdown of the statuses across your epics, so you can quickly see how your team is progressing towards larger work milestones. For example, how many work items in an epic are done, how many are in progress, and so on. This section is only available on the summary view in software spaces. What is an epic?

Related spaces (for business spaces)

Collaborate with other teams you frequently work with to synchronize your spaces. Here is where you’ll see which other spaces relate to the space you’re working on, so you can understand more broadly how other spaces may affect yours.

If a user from your current space has been active (meaning they performed at least one action) in another space over the last 30 days, that space is considered a related space. This section is only available on the summary view in business spaces.

Filter the space summary

Filtering is available in the summary view, so you can customize your view to show the information that’s most relevant to you.

To filter the data in your summary:

  • Select Filter.

  • Choose a filter and select the data you want to see in your customized summary. You can filter by the following:

  • Date range - view data for all the work items that were created, updated, or due within a particular time period.

  • Assignee - view data for all the work items that are assigned to one or more particular people (or unassigned).

  • Work type - view data for one or more particular work types.

  • Status - view data for all the work items that are in a particular status.

  • Parent - view all summary data for work items that belong to one or more selected parent work items.

  • Priority - view all summary data for work items that have been assigned a particular priority.

What is the “For you” page in Jira?

What is the “For you” page in Jira?

The For you page is designed to bring your most relevant work and updates into one place. It highlights work items that need your attention, conversations you should respond to, and shortcuts back to things you’ve recently worked on.

View the For you page

To get to the For you page, start in Jira and select For you from the sidebar navigation.

At the top of the page, you can view a list of recommended spaces, or select View all spaces to see them all. Select a space to go to it.

If you’re new to Jira, we’ll then show you a list of suggested spaces and teams to join, based on who invited you to Jira or what’s popular.

If you’ve used Jira before, you’ll see a few different tabs with suggestions to help you resume work and stay on top of any recent updates.

What you’ll find on each tab
Recommended

This is a tailored feed of the most relevant updates and suggested next steps for you. It has multiple sections, depending on what kind of work you do in Jira. You might see a combination of the following:

  • Review work due soon: shows incomplete work items with upcoming due dates.
  • Reply to mentions: shows comments that mention you.
  • Reply to comments: shows comments on work items assigned to you.
  • Approve waiting work: shows work items where you are assigned as an approver.
  • Review pull request: shows pull requests assigned to you for review. Hover over a work item in any of these sections and select it to view it in a side panel. From there, you can review its details, make updates, and add comments without losing your place.

If your site has AI features enabled, you might see additional options to help you work faster. On individual work items, you can use Summarize comments to get the context of a thread, or Suggest a reply to draft a response you can refine before posting.

You might also see a Review your agent activity card. This appears when an agent you’ve assigned work to needs your attention, is paused, or has finished. Select the card to open a panel and review the agent session without leaving the For you page. Up to three agent sessions are shown at a time, ordered by urgency and recency.

On Review work due soon cards, you can also hover over a work item and use Select agent to start an agent session and delegate the work without opening the work item.

Assigned to me

Shows work items assigned to you that aren’t done yet. Select a work item to open it in full-page view.

If your site has AI features enabled, you can also invoke an agent directly from this tab. Hover over a work item and use Select agent to start an agent session and delegate the work without opening the work item.

Starred

Shows spaces you’ve starred for quick access. Select a space to view it, or select the star to remove a space from your starred list.

Worked on

Shows work items you’ve recently updated. Select a work item to open it in full-page view.

Viewed

Shows spaces and work items you’ve recently viewed. Select one to open it in full-page view.

Work in Jira Cloud team-managed spaces

Add your team to team-managed boards

Add your team to team-managed boards

This page is for team-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

If you’re in a company-managed space, check out these company-managed space articles instead.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed space.

Add team members to your team-managed board

Your team members must first be added to your Jira Cloud site with access to software spaces before getting access to your board. For more information, see Creating, editing, and deleting users in the Jira admin documentation.

Via a work item on your board

Open a work item and assign it to someone (as long as you’ve already added them to your Jira Cloud site) to add them to your space:

  • Select a card to view the work item’s details.
  • Select the assignee field and select a team member. They will be added to the board and assigned this work item.
From your space

Select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. Select Add people.

Via Space settings
  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.Then select Access.
  • On the page, select Add people.
Assign roles

Roles (also known as permissions) control what each person can see and do on your board.

  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.Then select Access.
  • When you click Add people on the page, you’ll be prompted to select each person’s role from the drop-down menu: You can edit their roles (or permissions) at any time by choosing from the drop-down list beside their name. You also have the option of removing people from your board by clicking Remove.
Flag a work item for attention

Flagging a work item informs your teammates that a work item needs extra attention. For example, you could use a flag to indicate that you don’t have capacity to finish a task, or to indicate that a work item is blocked and you’ll work on it later.

On team-managed boards, flagged work items are shaded yellow:

To flag a work item:

  • Hover over a work item and select More actions (). You can also select multiple work items at once by holding Ctrl (Windows) or Command (Mac).
  • Select Add flag.

Get started with team-managed spaces

Get started with team-managed spaces

This page is for team-managed spaces

To check whether your space is team-managed or company-managed, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

If you’re in a company-managed space, check out these company-managed space articles instead.

More about the difference between company-managed and team-managed space.

Create a team-managed space

All users can create a team-managed space, even non-admins. If you’re a Jira admin and you want to restrict this, you’ll need to remove the Create team-managed spaces permission. For more information on global permissions, see Managing global permissions.

To try out a team-managed space:

  • Next to Spaces in the sidebar, select Create space ().
  • In Choose space type, then Select team-managed.
  • Under template, select Change template and choose either Scrum or Kanban. An option to Create space is also available in the top-right corner when you view all spaces.
What is the board?

If you have the Sprints feature enabled, your board won’t show any work items until you start a sprint.

Usually, your board reflects your team’s process, tracking the status of work it makes its way through your team’s process.

To view your board:

  • If not already there, navigate to your team-managed space.
  • From your space’s sidebar, select the board that sits below your company-managed software space. Your space’s board displays your team’s work as cards that you can move between columns. In Jira, cards and the work they represent are called “work items”.

While the roadmap can help you plan and track large initiatives over time, the board is more tactical. It captures the work your team is currently carrying out, usually over the next week or two.

The columns on your board start out with default statuses to represent the state of work. This visual representation of your team’s work helps you discuss and track the progress of your space from start to finish.

What are status categories?

Jira lets you collect many statuses within three categories (or: status categories). These categories help you sort, filter, and report on your space work.

In Jira, your space comes with three default categories:

  • To do
  • In progress
  • Done For example, you might have a “Backlog” status and a “Waiting for approval” status, in the To do category. Or, you might have a “Developing” status and an “In review” status, in the In progress category.

In Jira, your space comes with three default statuses that match the three default categories:

  • To do
  • In progress
  • Done We recommend these statuses when starting a space. As your team progresses, you may need to add more statuses to control the flow of your team’s work.

How to create, edit, and delete statuses in the workflow editor

Understand the relationship between a status and a column

You can edit or rearrange columns so the board accurately reflects your team’s process.

When you first start out, columns and statuses are connected to each other. This means when you create a column, you’re also creating a status.

The relationship between statuses and columns also applies to the order the columns are in on the board.

The leftmost position (first position, from left to right) is associated with the To do category. The rightmost position (last position, from left to right) is associated with the Done category. Everything in between is considered In progress.

Work in the rightmost column is marked as resolved

When you complete your sprint, this work will be cleared from your board, and won’t return to the backlog. If you don’t have the sprints feature enabled, these work items are automatically removed from the board after 14 days.

Resolved work items have a checkmark on them, like this:

Add, edit, rearrange, and remove columns

To add a new column, click the Create column button beside the rightmost column. The newly created column generates a status with the same name, at the same time.

To update a status’s name, click the column’s name. To rearrange your columns, drag and drop the column’s heading.

To delete a column and status, hover over the column’s heading and select More actions (···), then Delete.

If you delete a column containing work items, you must select a column and status to move those work items to. Work items in your backlog will also inherit the status you choose.

Your board always needs a Done status and Done column. If you decide to delete your Done column that contains work items, the column you choose to move the work items to will also inherit the Done status.

If you work in a Kanban-style, you can limit the amount of work you allow in any one column. Hover over the column’s heading and select More actions (···), then Set column limit.

We recommend this lightweight process when starting a space. As your team matures, you may need to rearrange your columns and statuses to better control the flow of your team’s work.

Learn how to configure columns with multiple statuses in your team-managed space

Create work items

Besides the Create button in the navigation bar, you can quickly create work items directly on your team-managed board and in your team-managed backlog.

Create work items on the board

If you have the Sprints feature enabled, you won’t be able to create work items directly on the board; you can only create work items on the backlog, and then add them to the sprint.

Work items represent tasks to be completed. Create work items in any of your board’s columns so your team can track work progress.

To create a work item on your board:

  • Select the Create work item button at the bottom of any column.
  • Fill in the required information that answers What needs to be done?
  • Select the work type icon on the card to recategorize the task.
  • Select Create. We recommend keeping a work item’s summary both short and descriptive so your team can scan the board quickly to get an overview of each other’s work.
Other quick ways to create work items on the board
  • In any position on your board: Add a work item in the middle of a column by hovering your mouse between two work items and selecting . Try to keep a work item’s details both short and descriptive. Team members should be able to scan the board quickly and get an overview of their team’s work.
Create work items in the backlog

Select Backlog in the space menu on the left and hit + Create work item to add a work item to your backlog.

Move work items across columns

As work is completed, you’ll want to move work items across your board, to indicate progress. Drag and drop a work item to move it. You can select multiple work items with either the Ctrl (Windows) or Command (Mac) key. Once you’ve selected multiple work items, you can move them all to a new column, or perform other actions by selecting More actions ().

Customize card covers

To add or change a work item’s card cover on the board:

  • Hover over a work item.

  • Select More actions ().

  • Select Select cover.

  • Choose a color, gradient, photo by Unsplash, or an image attachment to set it as the cover. To hide all card covers on the entire board:

  • On the board, select View settings.

  • In the Show fields section, select (or deselect) Card cover. You can also add card cover images to company-managed software spaces.

Choose the best view for your board

As your team works with the board, you might find that you need to cut through the noise to find exactly the right things to pick up and work on, or see what your team is up to.

Team-managed boards have default filters and grouping that can help you get a better view of your team’s work.

  • Select Filter below the space navigation (or use keyboard shortcut Shift + F) to open the filter panel. Use these filters to display work items that match specific fields and values.
  • Use the search bar to display work items containing a specific search term.
  • Use the assignee filter to display work items assigned to a specific person.
  • Select Group by to display work items in swimlanes based on the chosen category.
Clear done work items from your board

If you work in a kanban style, Done work items are automatically cleared from the board every 14 days. If you’re working with a large number of work items, you can keep your board tidy by manually clearing the work items in your Done column.

If you have the Sprints feature enabled, you won’t be able to manually clear work items from your board.

To manually clear Done work items from your board, hover over the Done column and select More actions (…), then Clear Done work items.

Only space admins and Jira admins can clear Done work items. Work items will be automatically cleared from your board 14 days after being moved to the Done column.

Once a work item is cleared, it will no longer appear on your board. This also applies to the work item’s subtasks. When a parent work item is cleared, its subtasks are also cleared, regardless of each subtask’s status.

To view cleared work items, select See all Done work items in the Done column, or enable the space work item navigator and select the Done filter.

Read more about searching for work items.

Learn more

If you want to learn more or want to ask us about Jira’s team-managed spaces, join the discussion at Atlassian Community.

Add an attachment to a work item

Add an attachment to a work item

We’re rolling out some changes to the work item as an open beta. Some documentation may not yet reflect these updates, and the new experience might not be enabled on your site. Read more about the upcoming changes

Attachments give context to a work item that text can’t provide.

When a work item has over 150 attachments, attachments will be displayed as a list. Find out about viewing attachments in a list.

To add an attachment to a work item:

  • Open a work item.

  • Drag and drop your file onto the work item. Alternatively, you can:

  • Open a work item.

  • Select the Add quick-add button under the summary for the work item and then Add An Attachment. OR scroll down to the Attachments section and select ‘Add Attachment’

  • Select Upload a file or drag and drop your files into the media picker.

Limits on how many attachments you can add to a work item

You can add up to 2000 attachments to a work item.

Once a work item has over 150 attachments, they’ll display as a list.

Some considerations for attached files:

  • Check the list of supported file formats.
  • File names can’t contain any of these characters: '\', '/','\"', '%', ':', '$', '?', '*'.
  • By default, the maximum size of any one file is 1GB, but your Jira admin can change this limit. The Free plans for Jira and Jira Service Management have a file storage limit of 2 GB per app. The Standard plan allows up to 250 GB per app, and file storage is unlimited on Premium plans. Find out more about Premium plans

Archive a work item

Archive a work item

You’ll need to have the relevant space permissions to archive and restore work items. More about space permissions

Archive a work item if you want to remove it from your space without deleting it. If you archive a work item, it will only appear in Archived work items and can no longer be edited. You can restore an archived work item if you need it in the future.

Archive a work item

To archive a work item:

  • Make sure you’re viewing a work item either in the side bar or in full screen.
  • Select More actions ().
  • Select Archive and confirm your changes. You can’t archive a subtask by itself, but you can archive its parent work item. This will automatically archive any subtask attached to that parent work item.
Restore a work item

To restore a work item:

  • Go to Archived work items.

  • Select the work item checkbox next to the work item you want to restore.

  • Select Restore.

  • Once restored, work items will appear in the space, dashboards, backlog and boards again, and you will be able to edit them. To restore a work item when viewing the work item directly:

  • Select Restore from the banner, or select More actions () then Restore.

  • Once you confirm your changes, the work item will appear in the space, dashboards, backlog and boards again, and you will be able to edit it.

Restore a subtask

If you want to restore a subtask, you’ll also need to restore its parent work item. Restoring a parent work item will automatically restore all of its subtasks.

To restore a subtask:

  • Go to Archived work items.
  • Open the subtask you want to restore.
  • Select Restore parent work item from the banner and confirm your changes.
  • Once restored, the parent work item and its subtasks will appear in the space, dashboards, backlog and boards again, and you will be able to edit them.
Restore multiple work items

To restore multiple work items:

  • Go to Archived work items.
  • Select multiple work items. You can either:
    • use the work item checkboxes
    • hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (Mac) while selecting work items
    • hold the Shift key to select a group of adjacent work items
  • Select Restore.
  • Once restored, work items will appear in the space, dashboards, backlog and boards again, and you will be able to edit them.

Automatically assign work items to people

Automatically assign work items to people

If you’re creating or editing a work item and don’t know who to assign it to, you can choose the Automatic option for the Assignee field. This behaves a bit differently depending on whether or not there are components on the work item that have default assignees.

When there are components

If there are component(s) on a work item, the work item will be assigned to the Default assignee of one of the components. Space admins can change the Default assignee of components by doing the following:

  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Components. More about organizing work with components
When there are no components with default assignees

If there are no components with default assignees on a work item, the work item will be assigned to the space’s Default assignee. Admins can change the space’s Default assignee by doing the following

  • Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
  • Select Details.

Classify a work item

Classify a work item

Classify a work item to help people recognize the sensitivity of information they’re viewing or working on.

You can classify a work item once an organization admin has set up classification levels for your organization.

To classify a work item:

  • Go to a work item.
  • Select More actions (), then select Classify work item.
  • Choose a classification level.
  • Select Assign. Why is my work item already classified?

You may find that a work item you’ve just created or work items you’ve worked on have been classified without any action by you or another user. This could be the result of a default classification level set by the space admin. What is an organization default data classification level?

To change the classification level of a work item:

  • Go to a work item.

  • Select the current classification level.

  • Select Update classification level.

  • Choose a classification level.

  • Select Assign. To remove the classification level of a work item:

  • Go to a work item.

  • Select the current classification level.

  • Select Update classification level.

  • Choose Space default. This means the work item will revert to the default classification level of the space, which could be a different classification level, the same classification level, or none. Only a space admin can change the default classification level of a space.

  • Select Assign.

Clone a work item

Clone a work item

We’re rolling out some changes to the work item as an open beta. Some documentation may not yet reflect these updates, and the new experience might not be enabled on your site. Read more about the upcoming changes

If you ever need to create a duplicate of a work item, there’s no need to do everything manually. Cloning enables you to duplicate a work item within the same space, copying over most information from a work item like the Summary and Description fields and more.

Cloned work items exist as a separate entity to the original work item. Their only connection is that, upon cloning, the two work items are linked — though you can unlink them any time.

In the cloning process, some information from the original work item isn’t automatically cloned but can be included:

  • Attachments
  • Subtasks
  • Links
  • Custom fields (if they’re set up to be cloned)
  • Comments
  • Child work items (for Epics). You must have the Create work items space permission to clone a work item.

To clone a work item:

  • Open a work item.
  • Select ··· > Clone.
  • Edit the Summary.
  • Edit the Assignee and Reporter (if required).
  • Choose what to Include (if any).
  • Select Clone. Keep in mind, the prefix Clone is automatically added to the Summary of a cloned work item.

Your space admin can use automation to remove the prefix in bulk. Find out from our Community and see an example of the rule

Automatically clone a work item

With Jira automation rules, you can set a work item to clone automatically on a schedule.

Once the new work item is cloned and created, it inherits the automation rule which will be turned on automatically.

Collaborate in real-time

Collaborate in real-time

This page is for business spaces

To check whether you’re in a business or software space, select More actions (•••) next to the space name in either the header or the sidebar. At the bottom of the menu that opens, your space details will be shown.

Collaborative mode is Jira’s very own multiplayer experience. If your team is working remotely, you’ll be able to see updates made in context and in real-time. You’ll be able to see who’s online and offline at the same time as you while you’re in the board, list, calendar, and timeline views.

In the board view, you’ll be able to see who’s editing which card. The card on the board will be highlighted by who is editing or dragging the card to a different column.

You’ll also be able to see when someone is editing each cell in the list view. The cell will display an outline with your teammate’s name.

Comment on work item action

Comment on work item action

In smart value entries:

  • ‘issue’ refers to a work item. What is a work item?
  • ‘project’ refers to a Jira space. What is a Jira space?
What is this component?

The Comment on work item action allows your rule to automatically comment on a work item.

Smart values

If your rule is triggered by a work item, any smart value related to work item data can be used in your comment by entering {{issue.[field name]}}. For example, {{issue.summary}} will print the work item’s summary. This also works with custom fields, for example {{issue.Team Leader}}.

This also works for user smart values. For example, to print the work item’s assignee, use {{issue.assignee.displayName}}. Similarly, to @mention the assignee, use [~accountid:{{issue.assignee.accountId}}]. Learn more about account IDs

You can also use any other smart values that print values, such as date and time or development smart values.

Date and time formats in different languages

Date and time formats in different languages

Work item fields with dates and times, including Date Picker and Date Time Picker custom fields, are formatted based on your language preferences. Each user can choose their preferred language in their account settings, then fields will display the standard date and time format for that language. Read more about managing your language preferences.

Date values (including Date Picker fields) are displayed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) time zone. If you’re using post functions or automation rules, consider using a Date Time Picker custom field to cater to users spread across multiple time zones.

Delete all attachments in the attachments panel

Delete all attachments in the attachments panel

If you don’t need your attachments anymore, you can delete those in the Attachments section to reduce clutter. To delete attachments in the work item fields and comments, you’ll have to hover them and delete them individually.

You must be an admin to delete all attachments on a work item.

To add deleted attachments back, you’ll need to add them back manually.

To delete all attachments on a work item:

  • Open a work item.
  • Find the Attachments section and select More actions (···).
  • Select Delete all.
  • Read the confirmation message, then select the appropriate option.

Delete an attachment in a work item

Delete an attachment in a work item

We’re rolling out some changes to the work item as an open beta. Some documentation may not yet reflect these updates, and the new experience might not be enabled on your site. Read more about the upcoming changes

Attachments appear in a separate Attachments section in a work item. If you don’t need an attachment anymore, you can delete it to reduce clutter.

Only you or an admin can delete attachments that you’ve added (unless your permissions have been turned off).

To delete an attachment:

  • Open a work item.
  • Find the attachment to delete.
  • Hover over the attachment.
  • Select the bin icon (). Tip: If the bin icon () doesn’t appear or get announced, you may not have permission to delete an attachment. If this happens, contact your admin or whoever added the attachment.
Attachments in comments

If the attachment was added to the work item by a comment or field, you can’t delete it from the attachment panel. If that’s the case, find the field or comment the attachment was added to and delete it from there.

Deleting a comment with an attachment removes the attachment from the whole work item. If someone has copied the attachment from one comment to another, it will also delete from the second comment.

Edit work items via the more actions menu in the backlog

Edit work items via the more actions menu in the backlog

You can perform the following actions on multiple selected work items in the backlog, including:

  • Add or remove flags
  • Add details to, or change the following fields:
    • Parent
    • Assignee (limit of 50 work items at a time)
    • Priority (limit of 50 work items at a time)
    • Estimate (limit of 50 work items at a time)
    • Labels (limit of 50 work items at a time)
  • Move
    • to the top of the backlog
    • to the bottom of the backlog
    • to sprints or spaces within the backlog
  • View selected work items in the All work search view
  • Archive
  • Delete Learn more about archiving work items

To make a bulk change to work items in the backlog:

  • Select work items while holding Ctrl (Windows) or Command (Mac) to select multiple at once.
  • On any of the selected work items, right-click and select an action, or select Bulk change.
  • Select the action you’d like to perform. More about making bulk changes to work items

Some actions may not appear in the menu if they have a limitation, in which case you may need to adjust the number of items you’ve selected. You may also require permissions for some actions to appear (like the delete and archive actions).

Estimate a work item

Estimate a work item

Before you begin

Estimating stories in your backlog helps you predict how long it would take you to deliver certain portions of the backlog. Note that this discussion refers to the best practices we’ve implemented as the main path in Jira Software. You can choose not to use this approach if you feel it’s not suitable for your team.

This page only applies to Scrum boards.

Estimate a work item

Before a sprint starts, you need to enter estimates for your work items.

To enter an estimate:

  • Go to the Backlog of your Scrum space.
  • Select a work item and enter an estimate in the Story points or Original estimate field (depending on the estimation statistic you set).
Log time and adjust the remaining estimate

As you work on work items during the sprint, you can log time and adjust the remaining time estimate if necessary. Logging time provides valuable info you can use for reporting in Jira.

  • Go to the Active sprints of your Scrum board.
  • Select a work item and choose > Log work (or click on the time tracking field).
  • Enter your time spent and time remaining, then click Save. To view and edit work logs for a work item, open the work item, choose Comments, then choose Work log.

When using the Burndown Chart, note that subtask behavior can vary, depending on whether or not remaining estimate and time spent is enabled for your board.

Subtask behavior when remaining estimate and time spent is enabled

Subtask behavior when remaining estimate and time spent is disabled

If you add a subtask to a work item that’s already in an active sprint, the subtask is treated as scope change.

The scope change is also indicated in the Burndown Chart.

If you add a subtask to a work item that’s already in an active sprint, the subtask is also treated as scope change.

However, scope change is not indicated in the Burndown Chart for the subtask.

Time estimates of subtasks are rolled up to the parent task.

This means that the parent task will have the total sum of all remaining estimates of the subtasks.

Time estimates are tracked individually across the subtasks and the parent task itself.

See Burndown Chart for more details.

Concepts about estimation

Here are some concepts to consider when estimating work items in Jira Software.

Estimation is different from tracking

In Scrum, there is a distinction between estimation and tracking. Estimation is typically performed against Primary Backlog Items (PBIs, usually stories), and is used to work out how long portions of the backlog might take to be delivered. Tracking refers to monitoring the progress of a sprint, to be sure that all stories included in the sprint will be delivered.

Tracking is often performed by breaking down stories into tasks, and applying hour estimates to them during sprint planning, then monitoring the remaining time in a burndown during the sprint.

How is estimation done in traditional development environments?

In traditional development environments, estimation is done this way:

  • A team estimates items in ‘man-hours’ – and these estimates are assumed to be accurate.

  • The team then calculates the total number of man-hours for the backlog of a space.

  • The team then divides the total number of man-hours by the number of people on the team, and the man-hours in a week. This becomes the forecast date for the space. These estimates are often inaccurate because they don’t consider the following:

  • The natural estimation characteristics of the team – meaning, over- and under-estimation are not considered

  • Unexpected interruptions during the man-hours allocated to the items

  • The performance of the team members themselves over time When the estimates become inaccurate, the team then exerts time and effort in trying to ‘force’ the estimates to be accurate. This makes the man-hour approach difficult, if not impossible.

Estimation in Scrum world is all about velocity

In the Scrum world, teams don’t try to achieve estimation accuracy. Instead, they aim to achieve ‘reliable velocity’.

Velocity is a measure of the number of estimation units that a team tends to complete from sprint to sprint. After their first few sprints, most teams will achieve a reasonably consistent velocity. Armed with velocity and estimates on the PBIs in the backlog, teams can predict more accurately how long portions of the backlog will take to complete.

The key is, the estimation unit doesn’t matter – as long as it becomes reasonably predictable from sprint to sprint. For example, teams can use ‘ideal hour’ estimates, but it’s neither necessary or expected that those hours will have any relationship to elapsed time. If a team has a ‘man-hour’ capacity of 120h in each sprint but a velocity of 60h, that makes no difference because you can still use the 60h velocity to estimate the number of sprints that portions of the backlog will take to complete — and therefore, the elapsed time.

Many people then start wondering where ‘the other 60 hours’ went, thereby implying that there is something wrong with team productivity. But that’s usually got nothing to do with it: a team’s estimates merely represent their view of how hard items will be, taking into consideration the team’s natural behavior (such as over- and under-estimation), as well as organizational overhead, etc. The velocity is all that matters from a planning perspective.

Since the units are not related to time, most teams now choose to use story points as their estimation unit. A story point is an arbitrary number that measures the complexity of one story relative to others. In effect, story points clearly break the mental link with time.

Inaccurate estimates are good, as long as they are equally inaccurate

For a team’s velocity to reach a stable state, the team must estimate each backlog item with the same level of accuracy. At the risk of repeating the obvious, the goal of velocity is to be able to look at a backlog of not particularly well-understood stories, and understand how many sprints it will take to complete. This requires a similar level of uncertainty for all of the estimates in the backlog.

There is a counter-intuitive implication here — that teams should estimate each item once, and not change that estimate even if they discover new information about the item that makes them feel their Original Estimate was wrong. If the team were to go ahead and update estimates, this ‘discovery of new information’ will happen regularly. This leads to the backlog having some items that have higher accuracy, but most that don’t. This would pollute velocity because sprints with a larger percentage of high accuracy estimates will complete a different number of units compared to those with a lower percentage of high accuracy estimates. As a result, the velocity could not be used for its primary purpose — that is, for estimating the number of sprints it will take for a team to complete a set of not-well-understood stories in the backlog. Therefore, it’s critical to use the first estimates so that the team’s velocity realistically represents their ability to complete a certain number of units of not-well-understood work far ahead into the future.

What about when teams realize they’ve gotten it wrong?

Consider the following scenario:

  • Work item X has an Original Estimate of 5 days.
  • Before the next sprint is planned, the team realizes that the Original Estimate was too optimistic, and that the work item actually takes 15 days. Some people would argue that using the Original Estimate will endanger the sprint’s success, because the team will take in what they think is 5 days of work into the next sprint when it’s actually 15 days of work.

However, the inaccurate estimate of 5 days is unlikely to be an isolated occurrence. In fact, the estimates are always going to be wrong (some very little, some wildly so). This will often be discovered after the sprint has started rather than before. As long as the team estimates the same way across the whole backlog, this will work itself out over time. For example, if they always underestimate, they may find that for a 10-day sprint with 4 team members, they can only really commit to 20 days of their estimation unit. If they have established a stable velocity, then this has no effect. From a planning perspective, we can still reliably estimate how much work we’ll get done in upcoming Sprints.

Doesn’t that break sprint commitment?

When the team is about to start a sprint, they can use the velocity as an indication of items from the backlog that they can realistically complete. The velocity here is based on the number of items they have successfully completed in the past. However, some people may question how this can be right when the Original Estimates won’t include information about work that may have already been done, or information about how hard a particular item of work is.

As an example, consider the following scenario:

  • A work item has an Original Estimate of 10 days.
  • The team works 5 days on the work item in the current sprint.
  • The team discovers a bad bug somewhere else in the space, and they decide that fixing that bug in the current sprint is far more important than completing work item X as planned.
  • The sprint gets finished, and the work item returns to the backlog. In the next sprint, the team would be tempted to update the estimate for the work item to 5 days, and use that to make their decision whether or not to include it in the sprint. The implication is that they might not include enough work in the next sprint if they used the work item’s Original Estimate of 10 days. However, the reason that the task was not completed previously is because of unplanned work — and it’s unrealistic to assume that this won’t happen again in the future, perhaps even in the next sprint. Thus, the 10-day estimate is a realistic number to use in the absence of certainty. As a result, the cost of the unplanned work that may happen is eventually accounted for in the Original Estimate. Even if the work does turn out to be insufficient for the next sprint, the team will correct that by dragging more work into the sprint.

In the same example, consider if this were the only work item in that sprint and will be the only work item in the next. If the work item is completed in the second sprint, and we use the remaining estimate, then the velocity will be (0d + 5d) / 2 = 2.5d. However, the team can clearly complete more work than that in future sprints. If we use the Original Estimate, then the velocity will be (0d + 10d) / 2 = 5d. The use of the Original Estimate accounts for the fact that the team cannot commit to 10d in every sprint because unplanned work will likely make that impossible. It also realistically accounts for the fact that unplanned work will not happen in every sprint.

Why not estimate on subtasks and roll that up for Velocity and Commitment?

Many teams break down stories into subtasks shortly before the sprint begins so they can use the stories for tracking. This raises the possibility of using the sum of the estimates on the subtasks as a way to decide which work items to commit to in the sprint (and potentially for velocity).

As described above, tracking is really a separate process from estimation and velocity. The estimates that are applied to subtasks clearly have higher accuracy than those that were originally applied to the story. Using them for velocity would cause the velocity to have both high and low accuracy estimates, making it unusable for looking further out in the backlog where stories have only low accuracy estimates.

In addition, only items at the top of the backlog are likely to have been broken into tasks. Using task estimates for velocity means that the velocity value could only predict the time to complete the backlog up to the last story that has been broken into tasks.

Lastly, using subtask roll-up to decide sprint commitment is risky because, unlike velocity value, it doesn’t consider the overhead of unplanned work and interruptions.

Story points are highly recommended – but use what works for your team

More and more industry leaders are moving away from hour estimates, and are now using the story point approach. This makes sense because in a sprint, the main questions to be answered are:

  • How much work can we realistically commit to completing this sprint?
  • How long will this part of the backlog take to deliver? The story point approach based on original estimates can deliver the answers to these questions without the anxiety around ‘accuracy’ that teams feel when asked to estimate in hours.

The Jira Software team itself uses the approach described in this article, and has established a reliable velocity that we use to plan work months in advance — even when new work has been encountered during those months. We recommend this approach because while it is sometimes counter-intuitive, it is also powerful, fast, and simple.

All of that said, one of the key precepts of agile is finding the way that works for you. So Jira Software does support the alternatives described above, including the use of remaining estimates for sprint commitment, hours for estimation, and hour estimates on sub-tasks.

Find a field on the work item

Find a field on the work item

Sometimes there are too many fields in too many places and finding a particular one is hard. If you don’t know where a field is, the work item has a quick way for you find it.

You must be an admin to use Find your field on the work item.

To find a field on the work item:

  • Open a work item.
  • Select more actions (···), then Find your field.
  • Search for the field you want to find.
  • Select the field. A table with the field’s status, admin-related settings, and details will display information about where you can find the field or why the field isn’t displayed on the work item. If the field isn’t visible, it may not be scoped correctly for the specific project or issue types.

To resolve this, navigate to the field’s configuration page, edit the field’s context, and include the relevant projects and issue types. Save the changes to ensure the field appears for the intended usage. How to manage field configurations in work items

Some fields, like Time Spent or Σ Time Spent, are part of time-tracking features and can’t be added to the main issue layout. These fields are visible in specific locations, such as the Work Log tab within the Activity section, or as columns in the issue list view, reports, and dashboards. When users log time, the total logged time will reflect in these fields.

Flag a work item

Flag a work item

You can flag a work item to indicate that it’s important or blocked. The card of a flagged work item is displayed in yellow in the scrum backlog, Active sprints of a Scrum board, kanban backlog (if enabled), and kanban board.

To flag a work item:

  • Go to your board or backlog.
  • Select a work item and select More actions (•••), then Add flag. You can also add a comment when you’re adding a flag to or removing a flag from a work item. You may want to do this to indicate your reason for adding or removing the flag.

Flagged work items are visible to all members of a space.

You can perform this action with your keyboard via Jira’s command palette. Use command + K (for Mac) or Ctrl + K (for Windows) to open the command palette while you’re in Jira. Read more about Jira’s command palette

Search for flagged work items

The flag for a work item is stored in a custom checkbox field called “Flagged”, which has only one value: Impediment. Use the JQL query Flagged = Impediment to find flagged work items.

Get AI‑suggested work item updates from Loom meetings in Jira

Get AI‑suggested work item updates from Loom meetings in Jira

After a Loom meeting, Jira can suggest updates to your work items, powered by Rovo AI. Connect your meetings to Jira for instant tracking and ready-to-approve updates.

When you connect a Loom meeting to a Jira space, Rovo analyzes the meeting transcript and recommends updates such as reassigning work items, changing priority or status, or adding a comment.

Rovo nudges are shown to the person who recorded or owns the Loom meeting. If this is you, you’ll see a nudge on a connected Jira board, where you can quickly review and apply the updates.

The quality, accuracy, and reliability of information generated by AI may vary. Find out why

Before you begin

To use this feature, you need:

  • a software or business space in Jira Cloud on a Standard, Premium, or Enterprise plan, with Rovo AI enabled on your site
  • a Loom account with Loom AI enabled
  • permission to view and edit the Jira board you want to connect
Connect a Loom meeting to a Jira space

You can connect a meeting before you record it, or after.

To connect Loom to Jira before the meeting:

  • In your Loom workspace, select Meetings in the left sidebar.

  • Find the relevant meeting and ensure the recording toggle is enabled.

  • Select Connect to Jira space.

  • In the settings modal, use the dropdown to select the Jira space you want to connect. To connect Loom to Jira after recording the meeting:

  • In your Loom workspace, select Library in the left sidebar.

  • Open the relevant recording.

  • If your recap has been generated, you’ll see an option to connect to Jira.

  • Select the Jira space you want to connect. Once the connection is made, you can access the Jira space directly from Loom in the meeting recap.

Review and apply suggested updates

After the meeting, Rovo processes the transcript and prepares suggestions. This may take a few minutes.

Rovo may suggest changes like:

  • reassigning a work item

  • changing the priority or status

  • updating the description

  • adding a comment To review Rovo’s suggested updates based on the meeting:

  • Open a board in the Jira space connected to your Loom meeting.

  • Look for a Rovo nudge about work item updates from your meeting.

  • Select the nudge to open the suggestions in Rovo Chat.

  • Review each suggestion.

  • For each suggestion, select Accept to apply it, or Discard to skip it. You can also choose to Accept all. Once accepted, the board will be updated with the suggestions.

How redaction works

How redaction works

Redaction is the process of selectively deleting sensitive data. Your organization may identify, redact and replace such data with a solid bar. For example, a credit card number may be considered sensitive data.

How does redaction appear?

If sensitive data has been redacted, you will see a solid bar where the sensitive data was. Here’s an example Jira work item where a bank account number has been redacted from the description and department fields.

The solid bar can be deleted from your content if you don’t need to show that data was redacted.

What happens to the work item history

When sensitive data is redacted from fields in your Jira work item, it will also be redacted from the history.

There are some situations where the data cannot be redacted in the history. If this happens, the best way to ensure the sensitive data is completely removed is to clone the work item and delete the original.

Link work items

Link work items

We’re rolling out some changes to the work item as an open beta. Some documentation may not yet reflect these updates, and the new experience might not be enabled on your site. Read more about the upcoming changes

Use linked work items to connect work across teams and spaces in Jira. Linked work items help your team surface, understand, and manage dependencies and related work. You can link work items across different spaces in Jira to streamline collaboration and increase visibility between software and non-technical business teams.

Work items can have the following link types:

  • is blocked by
  • blocks
  • is cloned by
  • clones
  • is duplicated by
  • duplicates
  • added to idea
  • is idea for
  • is implemented by
  • implements
  • merged into
  • merged from
  • is reviewed by
  • reviews
  • is caused by
  • causes
  • relates to Work item link types can be configured by Jira admins. If an admin deletes a link type, it won’t be available to use. Read how admins can configure linked work items
Show linked work items on the board

Linked work items appear in the detail view by default. You can also choose to show linked work items on the board via view settings. Once enabled, work item links will be visible on the relevant work items’ cards.

To show linked work items on the board:

  • Select View settings in the top right of the board view (Active sprints or Board in the space navigation).
  • Select the toggle to switch on Linked work items. Note that view settings are applied per user. You’ll be switching them on for your board, and not anyone else’s.
Link work items

To link a work item directly on the board:

  • Right-click on a work item or hover to select more actions (•••).
  • Select Link work item.
  • Select a link type, then select the work items you want to link. If you want to link a work item that hasn’t been created yet, select Create linked work item.
  • Select Link. Work items can also be linked through the work item detail view by selecting the Add quick-add button under the work item’s summary and then Linked work item.

You can perform this action with your keyboard via Jira’s command palette. Use command + K (for Mac) or Ctrl + K (for Windows) to open the command palette while you’re in Jira. Read more about Jira’s command palette

View linked work items

On a work item, select the linked work items icon to view linked iwork items on the board. You’ll see the link type, work item key, summary, and status for each linked work item.

Unlink work items

To remove the link between work items:

  • On the board, select the linked work items icon on a work item’s card to view its linked work items.
  • Hover over the work item you’d like to unlink, then select the Unlink icon that appears.
  • In the modal that follows, select Unlink to finalize. You can re-link any work item again if you need to.

You can perform this action with your keyboard via Jira’s command palette. Use command + K (for Mac) or Ctrl + K (for Windows) to open the command palette while you’re in Jira. Read more about Jira’s command palette

Link work to goals on a work item

Link work to goals on a work item

Align your team’s work to higher-level goals directly on a work item. Goals help your team understand how their efforts drive impact and help leaders manage dependencies and mitigate risk. All work types can be linked to a goal in software spaces, business spaces, and plans.

Enable the Goals field on work items

If you haven’t linked a work item to a goal before, you’ll need to enable the Goals field for an work type.

To enable the Goals field:

  • Open a work item of the type you’d like to add the Goals field to.
  • Select Configure at the bottom-right of the work item (near the created and updated dates).
  • In the Fields panel, search for Goals.
  • Drag the Goals field to the Context fields section.
  • Select Save changes to finalize.
Link a goal to a work item

To link a work item to the goal it contributes to:

  • Open the relevant work item
  • Check that you have the Goals field enabled.
  • Select the Goals field.
  • There are three ways to link a goal:
    • Create a new goal by selecting + Create, assign a name and owner, then select Create.
    • Search for a goal, then press Enter on your keyboard.
    • Paste a link to a goal, then select Add.
Unlink a goal from a work item

To unlink a goal:

  • Select the Goals field in the work item
  • Hover over the relevant goal, then select X to unlink it from the work item.

Log time on a work item

Log time on a work item

Jira provides flexibility to set estimation and tracking statistics based on your team’s needs.

Time tracking helps with space schedule planning and managing time expectations. Reports show the original and current time estimates for all work items, and whether they are ahead or behind schedule.

Teams often need to estimate how long work will take to deliver, sprint to sprint. As they complete stories, the team develops a cadence. This is also called velocity. The team tracks the estimation units they’ve completed from sprint to sprint to know how much they can do in future sprints, and have confidence the work will be completed.

You can monitor time spent by viewing the time tracking bars on work items.

Before you begin

You must have the following to do the things described in this section.

Role: App admin(to enable or disable time tracking)

Permission: Browse spaces, Work on work items

If you don’t see the time tracking field in your space, contact your Jira admin for help. Read more about configuring time tracking.

Time tracking appears in the details panel of a work item. It shows the time logged so far and the time remaining.

If a work item has more than 100 child work items, you can’t include them in time tracking. We recommend keeping a limit of 100 child work items per work item. More about parent and child work items

Estimate a work item

Before you start work on a work item, you can set a time, or other type of estimate, to calculate how much time or effort it will take to resolve. The field you set your estimate in depends on your chosen estimation method.

This could be Original estimate, Work item count, or a custom method. Story points (for story and the epic work type) are also available in software spaces.

To set an estimate for a work item:

  • Select the work item and choose the Original estimate, Story points or custom estimation field.
  • Enter the amount of time or number of story points you think it will take to finish the work item. You can use the time tracking report to compare the original and current time estimates for work items in the current space.

You can enter time estimates and log time in weeks (w), days (d), hours (h), and minutes (m). For example, you could estimate 3w or 2d 4h 30m.

If you type a number without specifying a time unit, for example “2” instead of “2h”, the default time unit set by your Jira admin will apply.

Log time on a work item

Once you start work on a work item, log time to keep a record. This lets you compare your original estimate with the actual time taken.

To log time on a work item:

  • Open the work item and select More actions (), then Log work. Or, select the Time tracking field.
  • Fill in the Log time fields, then select Save.
Edit a time log entry

You need the Edit own work logs or Edit all work logs permission to edit work logs.

To edit a work log:

  • Open a work item, and navigate to the Work log found in the activity section of a work item.
  • Find the time log entry, then select Edit.
  • Complete any relevant fields, and select Save. When you edit or delete a time log entry, the previous values don’t change and are used to calculate the time remaining. If the time remaining isn’t what you expect, manually update it in the Edit work log modal.
Delete a time log entry

You need the Delete own work logs or Delete all work logs permission to delete work logs.

To delete a work log:

  • Open a work item, and navigate to the Work log found in the activity section of a work item.
  • Find the work log entry and select Delete. You can adjust the remaining time estimate. You can get Jira to automatically adjust the time remaining by adding back the deleted time, or you can manually set a new time.

You can perform this action with your keyboard via Jira’s command palette. Use command + K (for Mac) or Ctrl + K (for Windows) to open the command palette while you’re in Jira. Read more about Jira’s command palette

To view your team’s velocity, consider using a sprint burndown or time tracking report. More on reports

Markdown and keyboard shortcuts

Markdown and keyboard shortcuts

Edit and create with markdown

The Atlassian editor supports markdown formatting for rich text fields. This makes it quick and easy to add headings, lists, code blocks, and more to your descriptions, comments, and other rich text fields. You can copy raw markdown into the Atlassian editor but you can’t convert content from it into raw markdown.

Rather than remembering different shortcuts for different types of content, you can remember just one: the slash command. Type / to add code, emoji, images, and more to your rich text fields.

For those of you who prefer using markup languages, you can type in markdown and it will convert to fully formatted content as you go.

Navigate work items in a list with your keyboard

Navigate work items in a list with your keyboard

You can search for and progress work items in the List view using your keyboard.

From your space navigation, select List.

To navigate using your keyboard, you can:

  • Use tab to quickly move through different elements of the view.

  • Use arrow keys to move between cells.

  • Use home and end keys to jump to the start or end of a row.

  • Use page up and page down to quickly move through your list. When editing a cell:

  • Use arrow keys to move between elements.

  • When editing a single value, press enter to confirm your input.

  • When editing multiple values, press tab to confirm your input. You can also use command + return on Mac, or Ctrl + Enter on Windows.

  • When editing values, press delete to remove a selection.

Pin a field to the top of a work item

Pin a field to the top of a work item

Scrolling through long lists of fields can be frustrating, especially when you only use a few of them. Pin your most important, useful, and frequently used fields to the top of a work item. Your pinned fields will appear on all work item within a space.

For example, if you pin the Due date field on a bug, Due date will be pinned for all other work types with that field (like stories and tasks) in a given space.

Your pinned fields are completely personal. Only you can see the fields you’ve pinned, and your teammates will only see the fields they’ve pinned.

To pin a field:

  • Open a work item.
  • Hover over the name of the field you want to pin.
  • Select the pin icon that appears. The pinned field should now appear at the top of your work item. If you pin more than one field to the top of your work item, you’ll be able to re-order them. If you want to copy information from any of your pinned fields, you’ll need to hold the ctrl key if you’re using a Windows device or the command key if you’re using an Apple device.

You can drag and drop pinned fields to reorder them.

To unpin a field, hover over the pin icon and select it the same way you pinned it.

You can’t pin fields from Marketplace apps.
